DESIGN ACCEPTANCE - Revision 4 of the adapter-boundary design, 2026-09-19, owner Dhar Rawal.

DECISION. Revision 4 is ACCEPTED, subject to two named conditions that must be satisfied before the F1 interface is frozen. This supersedes the Revision 3 review's "not yet accepted for implementation" status. The structural-equivalence gate that previously blocked this work has passed: fix-iq53.1.5 is closed and capability devreview-structural-candidate has shipped. Design document: /home/drawal/rl/devreview-artifacts-20260919/adapter-boundary-report-rev4.md. Independent review: /home/drawal/rl/devreview-artifacts-20260919/REV4-REVIEW-BRIEF.md. The two conditions are tracked as fix-iq53.2.3 and fix-iq53.2.4, both of which block this task.

WHY IT WAS ACCEPTED. Revision 4 is the first revision that removes machinery rather than adding it. The descriptor drops from 14 fields to 6, SourceRequest from 5 fields to 4, _reconcile (~83 lines) is deleted outright, and result_handle_walks loses a column. Revisions 1 through 3 were rejected for overreach; this one shrinks the surface it touches.

It answers all three Revision 3 demands. First, the unenforceable cooperative "allowance" is deleted and replaced by a framework-issued terminal callback fired at the exact call site _reconcile occupies today, so the placement and the maximum count of the reconciliation call become facts of the framework's own control flow rather than a promise the adapter makes - the framework does not call, therefore the call does not happen. Second, it produced the traces that were demanded. Third, it settles both conservative defaults instead of carrying them as provisional.

The traces show the current work profile is preserved at N+1 across all nine walk shapes, where the Revision 3 contract permitted up to 2.00x inflation. The two 2.00x cases are exactly the two capped shapes - which are precisely the shapes where today's code makes zero reconciliation calls, so a per-callback allowance would have authorised a reconciliation on every callback of a walk that never reconciles at all. That is a sharper argument against Revision 3 than the Revision 3 review itself made.

LIMIT OF THE EVIDENCE, ACCEPTED KNOWINGLY. The traces are fixture-driven, not live. They establish the framework's callback discipline, which is a property of paging.py's control flow and independent of what sits behind the resolver. They do not establish real portal latency, the relative cost of a countOnly against a batch read, or the per-callback behaviour of the adapter that F4/I4 will actually write - the "one backend operation per callback" claim is read off listing.py:613-619 by inspection, not executed. That gap closes only at I6, which is last in the dependency order.

CONDITION 1 (blocking, before F1 is frozen) - preserve the real filter column names on the page. Tracked as fix-iq53.2.3.

Revision 4 replaces filter_columns: Sequence[str] on the descriptor with filterable: bool and moves the actual column names into opaque adapter state. A boolean is sufficient for plan selection but not for display, and the names are agent-visible: they are read from the descriptor at paging.py:1906, carried onto the ResultPage at paging.py:2206, printed into the page header by rendering.py:72-73, and named in prose by _zero_message, whose call site is paging.py:2070. A boolean cannot reconstruct them. The consequence is that a complete-zero page degrades from naming the fields that were searched to saying "the rendered rows" - on precisely the page whose job is to stop a zero being over-read. Revision 4's ownership map asserts "rendering.py: no change - page format preserved". That assertion is false as written and must be corrected.

Additionally, the read-site inventory in section 6.2 ("7 fields across 11 sites"), carried forward unchanged from Revision 2, still omits the display consumer at paging.py:2206. That is the same undercount already flagged once as revision-1 correction 7; the inventory has now been wrong in the same way twice. Correct it before F1.

CONDITION 2 (blocking, before F2 is frozen) - an empty batch terminates the walk regardless of any continuation offered. Tracked as fix-iq53.2.4.

Revision 4 moves terminal recognition from "empty batch" to "absent continuation", which removes what the source at paging.py:1656 calls "THE stop condition, and the only one". Section 3.6 specifies four failure modes but does not specify an adapter that returns an empty batch while still offering a continuation. Such a walk never terminates: the purse bounds it within a fetch, but across fetches nothing does, so it burns up to 8 backend calls per fetch indefinitely while every page looks like legitimate progress. One explicit sentence in the contract fixes it, preserves today's behaviour exactly, and costs nothing.

OPEN QUESTION RESOLVED - read-only store opens and the -shm sidecar policy.

The question Revision 4 raised and declined to decide was which repository owns the immutable=1 / -shm sidecar policy for ResultHandleStore.open_readonly. The context is that a plain mode=ro SQLite connection to a WAL-mode database still creates an -shm sidecar - which is how 17 sidecars once appeared under the frozen EXP-028 v4 evidence root - while immutable=1 suppresses the sidecar but can silently read a truncated database when an uncheckpointed WAL is present. The safe/unsafe judgement is therefore per-file.

OWNER'S DECISION: none of Revision 4's three options. Instead, mirror ReadOnlyObservabilityStore - give ResultHandleStore.open_readonly an overridable _connect seam and let IDO subclass it. This is exactly the pattern IDO already uses at evaluation/observability.py:204-227. It adds no new framework parameter, which is the objection that got two prior revisions rejected, and both the precedent and its written rationale already live in the very file Revision 4 cited. This is recorded as a decision, not carried forward as an open question.

REVISION 3'S OPEN QUESTION - confirmed settled. An adapter that returns neither a continuation nor a completeness claim is handled by serving the stored rows and reporting incomplete; traversal is never silently restarted. Revision 4 correctly found that this needs no new machinery, because the existing renderer already produces exactly that page: walk_can_continue is a positive allowlist, so any stop reason outside it falls through to continuation=source-incomplete with no cursor. Restart and refuse-by-name are recorded as rejected, not carried as options, and the put_declaration redeclaration-identity interaction Revision 3 worried about does not arise under the settled answer.

Both acceptance conditions (fix-iq53.2.3 filter_columns, fix-iq53.2.4 empty-batch terminal) are closed. title: Strip agent-memory feedback table; rename human_feedback HTTP to /post_feedback
description:
## Owner request (verbatim)

Owner: Dhar Rawal. Date: 2026-09-14. Source: Cursor.

Table 1 functionality is obsolete.

Remove /api/feedback (read table 1). Delete the current /post_feedback implementation. Then rename /human_feedback as /post_feedback since the table 2 implementation takes feedback from both humans and coding agents. Legacy support is not a requirement.

## What to remove (table 1 — agent-memory `feedback`)

This is the old one-row-per-turn upsert used as live-agent conversation memory, not the Observability review notes.

- Table `feedback` (`turn_key`, `feedback_json`, `updated_at`) and store APIs: `upsert_feedback`, `get_feedback`, `list_feedback`.
- FastAPI/MCP **current** `POST /post_feedback` (`run_fastapi_mcp/__main__.py` ~2160) plus `save_last_turn_feedback` (`run_fastapi_mcp/utils.py`).
- run_chatbot **GET `/api/feedback`** and **GET `/api/feedback/<turn_key>`** (`run_chatbot/server.py` ~2613–2628). Debug UI does not call these; IDO store has 0 rows.
- Join of `feedback` into `get_memory_window` / `dspy.History` (`conversation_history_io.py` `feedback` key on memory turns).
- Tests that exist only to cover that table/API.

No dual-read, no migration, no compatibility shim. Legacy support is not a requirement. IDO `feedback` table is empty.

## What to keep and rename (table 2 — `human_feedback`)

Keep the `human_feedback` table and `add_human_feedback` / `list_human_feedback`. Provenance already distinguishes `human`, `coding_agent`, `distillation_agent`. Observability UI Feedback card uses this.

- Delete the table-1 `/post_feedback`.
- Rename the table-2 HTTP surface currently named `/api/human-feedback` (run_chatbot) to **`/post_feedback`** (owner wording). Align FastAPI/MCP if a human_feedback write path exists there, or add `/post_feedback` as the single write for table 2.
- Update UI `api("/api/human-feedback?...")` callers to the new path.
- Do not invent a second table or a provenance detector on table 1.

## Acceptance

- No `feedback` table or table-1 read/write APIs remain.
- No GET `/api/feedback`.
- One `/post_feedback` exists: it appends table 2 (`human_feedback`), not an upsert of table 1.
- Observability UI still lists/saves review notes (human and coding-agent provenance).
- Focused tests updated; no dual-stack leftover.

Parent: fix-9eg. Related: IDO store table 1 unused (0 rows); table 2 is the review loop.

2026-09-19 plan clarification: Specify POST /post_feedback as the sole table-2 write surface and retain/document a distinct GET read surface for listing notes; do not rename GET into an ambiguous write operation. Update UI and coding-agent docs/examples together. Preserve formal multi-rater review sidecar APIs and existing feedback provenance. Sealed evidence must remain immutable. This task does not add automatic memory injection, scoring or training.
Human UI and coding-agent structured reads/actions must share semantics and stable store/experiment/task/attempt/turn/span references. Reuse existing stores, workspaces, benchmarks and APIs. Include focused real-component integration tests and relevant browser interaction checks; no paid experiments are required to implement this work. No mandatory upfront scores, numeric targets, rubric, hypothesis, pre-registration ceremony, or reproducibility snapshots.

Multiple-run optimization amendment (owner discussion, 2026-09-19):
The proposed coding-agent feedback recording API retains the three categories Observations / Analysis, Conclusions, and Recommendations (see owner-confirmed enum contract below), together with their previously proposed subcategories and free-form comment content. This amendment does not replace or rename that taxonomy. Carry category/subcategory explicitly through the API; do not require humans to write structured syntax or infer mandatory metadata from agent comment headings. Single-evidence comments stay valid. Paired execution/step references and task-wide aggregation are owned by fix-9eg.19.1 using this same API, not a competing write route. Distillation observations, suggested lessons, disagreement and later verification are ordinary comments, with human/coding-agent/distillation-agent provenance.

OWNER-CONFIRMED FEEDBACK CONTRACT (supersedes earlier three-question shorthand):
Categories and allowed subcategories, represented as API enum values:
- observations_analysis (UI: Observations / Analysis): observation, analysis.
- conclusions (UI: Conclusions): what_went_right, what_went_wrong.
- recommendations (UI: Recommendations): what_to_do, what_not_to_do.
The owner confirmed these six meanings explicitly in this implementation session. UI category/subcategory selectors and watermark guidance facilitate free-form human comments; the coding-agent recording API carries category and subcategory explicitly as enums and accepts arbitrary structured text within the comment. Validate category/subcategory pairing. No parsing headings to infer required metadata for NEW writes. Preserve existing historical text without rewriting frozen evidence; uncategorized legacy comments remain readable and visibly legacy/unclassified rather than guessing a new subcategory. Comparison comments can link both recorded executions/pass/step anchors through the same API. No separate insight schema, review layer, or mandatory verdict workflow.
acceptance_criteria:
Original owner acceptance above plus: UI/agent reads and writes are documented and tested together; table-1 memory integration removed without deleting formal review functionality; human/coding-agent provenance preserved; sealed workspace evidence remains unchanged.
Category/subcategory and free-form content round-trip for human and agent callers through the existing proposed feedback API. No separate insight table, mandatory verdict workflow or automatic prompt/training injection is introduced. Existing formal review records remain unaffected.
notes:
Triage (2026-09-19): priority=P1; cost=medium; risk=medium. Owner-requested cleanup touches memory, store and routes; medium regression risk.
Updated triage: P1 / cost medium / risk medium. Scope includes the multiple-run amendment; existing delivery order is unchanged.
Taxonomy corrected from owner clarification. Previous worked/went_wrong/should_change headings are legacy presentation, not the new API category enumeration.
2026-09-19 feedback worker (awaiting reviewer acceptance; NOT closed). Agent-memory feedback removed: the feedback table is gone from the schema literal, upsert_feedback/get_feedback/list_feedback are gone, get_memory_window no longer joins feedback (two-key window), GET /api/feedback and /api/feedback/<turn_key> 404, and conversation_history_io.py no longer emits the feedback key. SCHEMA_VERSION 6 -> 7; MIN_READABLE_SCHEMA_VERSION 6 keeps existing v6 evidence readable. Review-note write surface renamed to POST /post_feedback on both the chatbot and FastAPI/MCP, with distinct reads GET /api/feedback-notes, GET /api/task-feedback, GET /api/feedback-taxonomy (FastAPI: GET /feedback, GET /feedback_taxonomy). Category/subcategory/target_kind/provenance are Literal enums, so they appear as enumerations in the OpenAPI schema. Removed-API tests were converted to removal/replacement coverage, not deleted. Cross-file gap reported as fix-24da (append_conversation_turn still writes feedback: None).
Accepted by root reviewer: independent feedback/comparison/source-switch run194 passed, revised feedback worker190 passed, implementation and owned tests now Ruff clean. Categorized enum API and free-text UI contract validated; full pair identity remains stable; archived notes roundtrip through sidecars with both evidence stores unchanged; read paths create no sidecar; anchors scrub presentation labels. Navigation race corrected with real delayed-HTTP regression. Workspace pair composer UI remains separately assigned P1 integration fix-x9cn; do not infer parent .19 complete. WEC legacy feedback:None key is separately tracked eligible P2 fix-24da.

title: ExperimentRunner archival never lands: evidence_run(archive_dir) runs while the runner's own sink is open, so archive_to raises WriterStillOpen
description:
Found during the fix-49m.3 review (2026-09-06), pre-existing on feat/experiment-observability-3.3.

ExperimentRunner._prepare_process (experiment.py ~:693) takes the process-wide sink BEFORE evidence_run() opens, deliberately (one writer per DB). ExperimentRunner._execute (experiment.py:922) then calls evidence_run(workflow, archive_dir=self.archive_dir). At exit, evidence_run (evidence_run.py:410) calls ObservabilityStore(db_path).archive_to(target); archive_to (observability_store.py ~:4534) raises WriterStillOpen while sink_for_db_path(source) is open. The exception is caught and appended to run.extra_problems ("evidence archival failed"), so an in-process runner with archive_dir set NEVER produces an archive and every such run is marked with a problem. No 3.3 test covers the in-process archive path (the ported tests/test_evidence_run.py had to drain and close the writer inside the block to pass).

Options: (1) evidence_run closes/flushes the sink it can see before archiving (breaks the one-writer contract only at the end of the run); (2) ExperimentRunner closes its sink before the evidence_run block exits; (3) archive_to checkpoints the WAL through the live sink instead of refusing. Decide with the owner; add a test that runs ExperimentRunner with archive_dir in-process and asserts an archive file.
notes:
Additional symptom 2026-09-06: tests/test_evidence_run.py::test_the_archive_is_immutable_and_its_digest_verifies failed once under a 2-minute full union run with SourceChangedDuringArchive('source DB/WAL bytes changed while taking the snapshot') and passed 3/3 in isolation. The ported test drains the writer queue but leaves the sink open, so the sink's periodic writer-health persist can land between the two digests. Same root cause: archiving while a live sink exists. Fixing the sink lifecycle for archival (this bead) should also make the test deterministic; until then treat that test as load-sensitive.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-07 (awaiting review).

Lifecycle chosen: the writer is HELD STILL, not killed. New SQLiteTraceSink.quiesced() context manager (observability_store.py:5727) does flush -> park the writer thread at the top of its loop (_park_if_quiescing, :5810; park point wired at _writer_loop :5880) -> _settle_for_snapshot (:5822) which force-persists health and runs PRAGMA wal_checkpoint(TRUNCATE) once, deliberately, so the two writes that used to land between archive_to's before/after digests are part of what is archived instead of a change to it.

archive_to (:4902) is now archive_to(destination, *, quiesce_live_writer=True): a sink this process's factory owns is quiesced; with quiesce_live_writer=False it refuses as before (seal_workspace_evidence passes False, experiment.py:667, because the seal has already stamped capture_complete). A writer this process CANNOT reach still refuses, via the new durable incarnation marker: _refuse_if_an_unreachable_writer_holds (:4944) reads writer_health.writer_incarnation and raises WriterStillOpen when it says open, the host matches and the pid is still alive; a dead pid is treated as a stale crash marker so an open marker cannot wedge a store forever.

Second, independent cause of SourceChangedDuringArchive fixed too: _snapshot_to (:4998) holds one idle 'pin' connection open for the whole snapshot, because SQLite checkpoints a WAL database when its LAST connection closes -- an unrelated reader letting go mid-snapshot rewrote -wal and was reported as a source change nobody made. That is the tier-2 TestWorkspaceRoutes shape (its seeded_db has no sink at all).

evidence_run.py:423 gains the comment explaining why the sink is deliberately open at the archive step; no behaviour change there.

Tests: tests/test_evidence_run.py -- _drain_writer() deleted and all 7 call sites removed, so every archiving test now runs with its writer OPEN (the shape the bug lived on and no test took). tests/test_experiment_container.py TestHarness gains test_an_in_process_run_with_an_archive_dir_produces_one (end-to-end: status complete, evidence_problems == [], segment valid, archive digest verifies, 0444, no -wal, ReadOnly reader sees the experiment and its turns, sink still open), test_archiving_a_live_store_does_not_change_its_bytes (10 back-to-back snapshots of a live store, writer resumes and accepts a turn afterwards), test_a_writer_this_process_cannot_reach_still_refuses (out-of-registry sink -> WriterStillOpen, and archivable again once it closes).

test_experiment_sealing.py: one-line stub signature fix (boom(destination, **archive_options)).

Flake: test_the_archive_is_immutable_and_its_digest_verifies 10/10 under 6 CPU burners; test_archiving_a_live_store_does_not_change_its_bytes 10/10 under the same load. The tier-2 TestWorkspaceRoutes fixture was out of bounds for this session (tests/test_run_chatbot_* reserved for a concurrent agent) -- not run.

Focused: 226 passed, 1 skipped over test_evidence_run/test_experiment_sealing/test_observability_store/test_experiment_container/test_experiment_controller/test_fastapi_experiment_binding. Wider sweep of every observability-touching test file except test_run_chatbot_*: 658 passed, 111 skipped. No commit made.
close_reason: Reviewed 2026-09-07. Archive quiesces a same-process writer (flush -> park -> settle: forced health persist + wal_checkpoint TRUNCATE) for the snapshot; an unreachable writer (durable incarnation marker) is still refused; a pin connection is held across the snapshot so an unrelated reader closing cannot checkpoint the WAL mid-copy (second, independent flake cause). Seal keeps unconditional refusal. ExperimentRunner with archive_dir now produces a valid archive in-process (end-to-end test); _drain_writer removed from every evidence test. Orchestrator re-run: focused set 226 passed 1 skipped; tier-2 TestWorkspaceRoutes 10/10 under 4 CPU burners; implementer's 10/10 on the two archive tests. Cross-process cooperative quiesce remains refusal (bead-worthy only if a two-process harness needs mid-run archives).

title: Reject non-JSON-native benchmark payload values
description:
## Why

IDO smoke tests (ido-tsq.3) showed write_version accepts Python tuples inside payload objects because json.dumps coerces them to arrays. That is silent type-shifting: a driver can pin a digest of lists while believing it stored tuples. Architecture §21 says payload is an opaque JSON object, not a Python object.

## What

In benchmark_catalog, recursively require JSON-native values in task payload (and analysis JSON): object/array/string/number/boolean/null; string keys; finite floats. Refuse tuple, Enum, bytes, dataclass, NaN/Inf with BenchmarkManifestError. Do not schema-check payload keys. Add focused tests. Do not import IDO types.
acceptance_criteria: Focused catalog tests refuse tuples/enums/non-string keys/NaN; existing payload dict/list fixtures still pass. No IDO imports.
close_reason: Recursive JSON-native validation on task payload and write_analysis; focused catalog/analysis tests pass.

title: Trainer must not abort a run over a thin intent label or missing generation provenance
description:
Two publication gates treated advisory/structural-mismatch conditions as fatal.

1. split_training_data raised TrainingDataError when any intent label had fewer than MIN_TRAINING_ROWS_PER_LABEL rows. The persona holdout already rescues starved labels into train and records them as unmeasured. The class-aware split should do the same: train the thin label, skip its evaluation row, warn. Abort only when no label can form an evaluation set.

2. _classify_status marked commands MISSING (blocking) when generate_diverse_utterances was never called, even when context provenance showed real trained rows. UtteranceProvenance is a generation record written only from that helper; hand-written generate_utterances never produces one. MISSING must require no generation record AND no included context. Thin hand-written commands still fail the row floor.

Also: label names in messages must be plain text, not a list-repr of numpy strings, because Rich treats [np.str_('cmd')] as markup and drops the name.

Acceptance: a one-row label trains unmeasured with a named warning; a hand-written command with rows>=floor is not MISSING; all-singleton datasets still raise; tests in test_training_report.py and test_heldout_evaluation.py cover both.

title: Concurrent module hydration race: a sibling's ordinary import sees a half-built module
description:
Found by the first G2B generation losing 12 of 16 attempts (ido-2l0.28's 'recovered module-import failures', which were never actually fixed).

DEFECT. python_utils.get_module loads a module by calling spec.loader.exec_module directly - necessary, because workflow command modules live outside any importable package root - and publishes it to sys.modules BEFORE executing it so relative imports inside it resolve. Both are required. Together they race: thread A publishes an EMPTY module and starts executing it; thread B's sibling module does an ordinary 'from .that_module import Thing', which is a plain sys.modules lookup taking none of our locks, finds the empty module, and raises 'cannot import name Thing' naming a class that is plainly in the file.

Second failure amplifying the first: a half-built module was LEFT in sys.modules after a failed exec, so every later import of that name in the process failed identically - which is how one racing failure became a whole generation of them.

MEASURED on the IDO tree, 8 concurrent cold loads: 5/3/3/3/7 failures before, 0/0/0/0/0/0 after.

FIRST FIX WAS WRONG and is worth recording: a per-module lock. The two threads load DIFFERENT modules, so they take different locks; the collision is between one thread's get_module and another thread's ordinary import statement. Only serializing hydration closes it. Caught by the regression test rather than by the empirical run, which had passed by luck.

FIX: a single re-entrant _hydration_lock around publish-and-execute (re-entrant because a module body can import a sibling through the same function), plus retracting the module from sys.modules when exec_module raises. Cost is bounded: hydration is once per module per process and get_module is lru_cached, so this contends only at cold start.

TESTS: tests/test_concurrent_module_hydration.py - the sibling race driven directly with a barrier, eight concurrent loads of one module all getting the same object (not merely not raising), and a failed import not poisoning the name.
close_reason: Fixed and verified: single re-entrant hydration lock plus sys.modules retraction on failed exec. 8-way cold loads of the IDO tree: 5/3/3/3/7 failures before, 0/0/0/0/0/0 after. Three regression tests.

title: Measurement mode: allow disabling the DSPy caches without disabling the memory-policy proof
description:
The server keeps the DSPy memory and disk caches ON by policy. server_memory.py line 57 states the intent: "Disk cache stays ON for repeat-prompt performance", and install_policy() hardcodes enable_memory_cache=True / enable_disk_cache=True with no environment override.

That is a reasonable production default. It is wrong for MEASUREMENT, and there is currently no way to turn it off.

WHY IT MATTERS, measured rather than argued. A downstream evaluation corpus (the IDO complex-task G2A baseline) runs each task utterance 10 times, and three of them 60 times, to estimate reliability and an irreducible variance floor. Identical prompt in, cached completion out. Same case, same commit (89ba8ba / g2a-baseline-2), same environment, only the cache policy changed:

   cache ON  : 60 attempts -> 1 DISTINCT final answer
   cache OFF : 10 attempts -> 10 DISTINCT final answers
   cache-off answer lengths: 270 279 282 286 294 330 332 350 765 4610

Across that whole collection, 310 attempts carried 54 distinct answers - an effective sample size of 17 percent of nominal. The variance floor computed from it was 0.0000, which is what a cache guarantees rather than what the workflow earns. Every reliability interval derived from those runs has been withdrawn.

Note the second column too: with the cache off, 10 of 10 attempts on that case came back PARTIAL and 0 succeeded, where the cached single answer had been scored as a stable result. The cache was not only collapsing the variance, it was pinning the corpus to one lucky trajectory.

WHAT IS NEEDED

1. An opt-out that install_policy() honours - env var (e.g. FW_DSPY_CACHE=off) or a launch flag - disabling both the memory and disk caches. The production default should stay ON.

2. _assert_policy_structurally() must keep working when the cache is disabled. Today it fails: it checks the memory cache reports its configured maxsize, and a disabled cache reports None. So the only way to disable the cache right now is to neutralise the assertion, which also disables the proof that DSPy honours its memory bounds - an unacceptable trade for a measurement run, which is exactly the kind of run that most needs its evidence to be citable.

3. The readiness probe / startup log should report the cache state as asserted fact, the way it already reports dspy_disk_cache=ON, so a harness can record what it actually ran under rather than what it requested.

INTERIM WORKAROUND, for reference only: a launcher that intercepts dspy.configure_cache before the server calls it, plus a no-op on _assert_policy_structurally. It is diagnostic-only for the reason in (2). Two incidental notes for whoever implements this: dspy 3.2.1 has no enable_litellm_cache kwarg (configure_cache takes enable_memory_cache / enable_disk_cache / memory_max_entries / disk_size_limit_bytes), and configure_cache REBINDS dspy.cache, so it must run before any LM is constructed.
acceptance_criteria: A documented opt-out disables both DSPy caches; _assert_policy_structurally still proves the memory bounds with the cache off; startup reports the cache state as asserted fact; production default stays ON.
close_reason:
WITHDRAWN 2026-08-30 after testing the alternative. The blanket flag was the wrong shape and it is not needed.

WHAT I CHECKED. dspy.LM.forward does `cache = kwargs.pop("cache", self.cache)`, so DSPy supports a per-call override, and dspy_utils.get_lm(**kwargs) forwards to dspy.LM. But no runtime caller passes kwargs - workflow_execution_context.py:1616 and workflow_agent.py:712 both call get_lm with none - and there is no env or config path to inject them. So the kwargs route is not reachable without editing fastworkflow.

THE ROUTE THAT NEEDS NOTHING. DSPy resolves its disk cache directory from DSPY_CACHEDIR (dspy/clients: DISK_CACHE_DIR = os.environ.get("DSPY_CACHEDIR") or ~/.dspy_cache), and install_policy() calls configure_cache WITHOUT passing disk_cache_dir, so it inherits that. A server started with a fresh empty DSPY_CACHEDIR therefore has a COLD disk cache, and a fresh process has a cold memory cache.

VERIFIED, not assumed: two servers, each with its own empty DSPY_CACHEDIR, one attempt of the same case each - 3930-character answer versus 258-character answer, different hashes, and each cache directory populated with 48 files afterwards, proving the cache was live and had started empty.

WHY THIS IS BETTER THAN WHAT I ASKED FOR, and this is the part that changes my mind rather than just my mind being changed. Disabling the cache breaks _assert_policy_structurally, because it checks the memory cache reports its configured maxsize and a disabled cache reports None. So the feature I requested would have forced a measurement run to give up the proof that DSPy honours its memory bounds - on precisely the runs whose evidence most needs to be citable. Cold-cache-per-replicate keeps the cache ENABLED and the assertion intact, and gets the same independence.

NO ACTION NEEDED IN FASTWORKFLOW. The defect was cache hygiene in the measuring harness, not a missing affordance here. Recorded rather than deleted so the next person who reaches for a cache flag finds the alternative first.

title: Citations are write-ordered behind their divergence rows; an orphan is suppressed, not written
description:
RECONSTRUCTED 2026-08-29 from shipped code and tests. Landed in 3351f92 (merged 7a0340e) but was never filed as a bead; ~8 code and test references pointed at a non-existent issue. Filed retroactively and closed so the citations resolve.

THE PROBLEM. A citation in distillation_insight_citations names a divergence row. If the citation is written while its divergence row never landed -- the record queue is lossy under pressure -- the result is an ORPHAN: section 15's provenance recipes join through that table and would read the orphan as evidence that an insight was drawn from a divergence which does not exist. Silent, and in the direction of overstating support.

THE FIX. Ordering, not just loss detection. A citation is only written once the divergence row it names is IN THE TABLE. Divergence records are enqueued ahead of the citations drawn from them and the record queue is FIFO, so by the time the citation write runs the row is either present or it was genuinely lost. In the lost case upsert_distillation_row raises OrphanedCitation and the writer COUNTS the suppression rather than writing a citation that points at nothing.

WHERE IT LIVES: observability_store.py -- the OrphanedCitation class (~650), the citation branch of upsert_distillation_row (~1856), the docstring contract (~1817), and the writer's warning path (~4660, logged with a [fix-sb8.16] tag). Also distillation.py ~1027 (idempotent upsert on re-emission).

TESTS: tests/test_distillation_observability.py ~2818 onward -- "write ordering, not just loss detection", including the case where finalize_pass_metrics returned before re-emitting.
close_reason: Closed

title: Flush barrier settles on per-barrier watermarks, not global sink quiescence
description:
RECONSTRUCTED 2026-08-29 from shipped code and tests. This work LANDED in 3351f92 (merged 7a0340e) but was never filed as a bead, so ~10 code and test references pointed at a non-existent issue. Filed retroactively and closed, so the citations resolve.

THE PROBLEM. The flush barrier used to settle on GLOBAL queue quiescence -- "both queues are empty". One SQLiteTraceSink is shared by every channel on a workflow DB (get_observability_sink caches one sink per DB path), so another channel's steady span emission can prevent that condition forever. A distillation run waiting for its evidence to be durable could be starved indefinitely by unrelated traffic.

THE FIX. Per-barrier watermarks. _span_enq/_record_enq count everything ever accepted onto each queue, bumped by producer threads under _seq_lock; _span_done/_record_done count what the writer has dequeued and are touched only on the writer thread. A barrier settles when the writer has reached THIS barrier's work, not when the queues happen to be empty.

WHERE IT LIVES: observability_store.py -- _FlushTicket (~3843, with the starvation rationale in its docstring), the watermark fields (~3897), the enqueue counter (~4268), the dequeue advance (~4489), and the shared-sink note (~4235, ~4579). Also distillation.py ~513 and ~1365 (the barrier is scoped to this turn's trace).

TEST: tests/test_observability_store.py ~2037 -- "the barrier must not require GLOBAL sink quiescence."

NOTE ON THIS ID: a bead numbered fix-sb8.15 was briefly filed on 2026-08-29 for a different purpose (cleaning up the dangling fix-sb8.N citations). title: Restored turn raises AttributeError: WorkflowExecutionContext has no attribute _execution_recorder
description:
Found 2026-08-29 while running a regression sweep for fix-ajv.18/.19. NOT caused by that work: verified by stashing all working-tree changes and re-running at clean HEAD (7b1f413), where it fails identically.

FAILURE
tests/test_turn_result_capture.py::TestConversationMemoryStamping::test_restored_turn_baselines_on_the_restored_history

  AttributeError: WorkflowExecutionContext object has no attribute _execution_recorder
  fastworkflow/workflow_execution_context.py:1173

The site reads:
    self._execution_recorder.records() if self._execution_recorder is not None else ()
The guard checks for None but the attribute does not EXIST on this instance, so the
guard itself raises. The path is a RESTORED turn, so the likely cause is that the
restore/deserialize path constructs the context without going through whatever
initializes _execution_recorder on the live path.

Reproduce:
    python -m pytest "tests/test_turn_result_capture.py::TestConversationMemoryStamping::test_restored_turn_baselines_on_the_restored_history" -q

Fails in isolation, so it is not cross-file test pollution.

Sweep context: 287 of 288 passed across test_observability_store, test_capture_policy,
test_capture_policy_wiring, test_capture_policy_error_namespace, test_turn_result_additive,
test_turn_result_capture, test_tracing_phase1, test_execution_record_capture,
test_no_capture_control_flow, test_evidence_run, test_react_suspend_resume,
test_command_executor_errors, test_label_encoder_isolation. This was the only failure.

SUGGESTED: initialize _execution_recorder to None in the restore path (or on the class,
so no path can omit it), rather than converting the read to a getattr default -- a
getattr default here would hide the next path that forgets to initialize it, and this
attribute is what joins outcomes to their execution records.
acceptance_criteria: test_restored_turn_baselines_on_the_restored_history passes; _execution_recorder is guaranteed to exist on every construction path, not defaulted at the read site.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-29. Confirmed a PRODUCTION bug, not just a test artifact: _serialize_turn_accumulator's own docstring says "Resume continues the same logical turn rather than starting a new one (_begin_turn is deliberately skipped)", and _begin_turn was the only place _execution_recorder was ever bound. So every cross-process resume that finalized a turn hit the AttributeError.

TWO PARTS, both following the file's existing conventions:
1. Bound in __init__ alongside the other turn-accumulator state, so no construction path can omit it. Taken instead of the getattr-default the bead warned against: a default at the read site would hide the next path that forgets to bind it, and this attribute is what joins outcomes to their execution records.
2. Minted in the restore path, sink-gated exactly as _begin_turn gates it, so a RESUMED turn can still record the commands it is about to run. Without this the fix would stop the crash and leave every post-resume outcome carrying a command_call_id with no ExecutionRecordRef to join to -- the gap fix-ajv.16 closed for failures, reopened for resumptions. The restore block already rebuilds _turn_history_baseline, _turn_key, _turn_outputs and _turn_started_at the same way.

The pre-suspension process's records are deliberately NOT carried across: they went durable with that process's spans, and the ledger is per-process.

TESTS: tests/test_execution_record_capture.py, 3 new (attribute bound before any turn begins; a resumed turn finalizes instead of raising; a resumed turn still records). Negative control: reverting both bindings fails those 3 plus the originally-reported test_restored_turn_baselines_on_the_restored_history.
close_reason: Closed

title: Naming a failed command moves its record under command.<name>.* and can UNDO withholding under the evidence profile
description:
Introduced by the fix-ajv.16 fix, documented in a code comment at workflow_agent.py but not mitigated. Latent today; a deployment that declares per-command field policies gets the exposure.

MECHANISM
_apply_capture_policy (observability_store.py:492-535) derives EVERY field path for a command output from its command_name, defaulting to the literal 'unknown':
  command.<name>.response
  command.<name>.parameters.<field>
  command.<name>.artifacts.<key>

Before fix-ajv.16 a failed command's output carried command_name='' so all three resolved to command.unknown.* . After the fix they resolve to the real routed name.

CapturePolicy.apply (capture_policy.py:349-374) short-circuits:
    declared = self.policy_for(field_path)
    if declared is not None:
        gated = declared.redact_before_prompt if for_prompt else declared.redact_before_trace
        if not gated:
            return value          # WHOLE, whatever the disposition would have been
Only when NO policy is declared does it fall through to the profile default, which under the evidence profile is what withholds user-text.

CONSEQUENCE, and it runs toward LESS withholding
A policy declared for a command's HAPPY path -- e.g. command.ControlsMonitor/open_finding.response with redact_before_trace=False, entirely reasonable because that command's normal response is benign -- now also governs its FAILURE records. Failure records do not carry normal output: command_response is "Execution error: {e!r}" truncated to 500 chars, and artifacts.error_message is str(e) or repr(e) truncated to 1000 (workflow_agent.py). Exception reprs carry whatever the command was handling. So a field that was an omit envelope under command.unknown.* comes back as a raw string under the routed name.

Second, quieter effect: a blanket command.unknown.* rule written to catch unattributed failures silently stops matching them.

Severity is currently bounded by FW_OBS_CAPTURE_TRACEBACKS (default '0', observability_store.py:179), which replaces the real stack with a sentinel at :702-703. That caps the 4KB-traceback case but not the error_message/response case.

SUGGESTED FIX -- separate the namespace, do not weaken the contract
In _apply_capture_policy, when a command_output has success False, derive its paths under an error segment:
  command.<name>.error.response
  command.<name>.error.artifacts.<key>
A policy declared for command.<name>.response (written for success) then no longer matches failures, and a deployment that genuinely wants error text whole must say so explicitly. Fails safe by construction and leaves "declared policy wins" intact -- which matters, because forcing an override on failure records instead would break that contract everywhere else it is relied on.

VERIFY BEFORE IMPLEMENTING: that the success field is present on the model_dump()ed command_output dict this function walks. It is asserted on the LIVE object in tests/test_command_executor_errors.py, which is not the same thing.

REJECTED: reverting fix-ajv.16 (reintroduces 130 unattributable failures); forcing a classification override on failure records (breaks the declared-policy-wins contract); capping error_message at persist time (partial, does not address the general case -- worth doing as a belt, not as the fix).

TEST: under the evidence profile with a declared non-gated policy for command.X.response, a FAILED X must still be withheld while a SUCCESSFUL X is returned whole.
acceptance_criteria: A declared non-gated policy on command.<name>.response does not un-gate that command's failure records under the evidence profile; test covers success-whole/failure-withheld under one declared policy; the workflow_agent.py comment is updated to point at the fix rather than describing an open risk.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-29. _apply_capture_policy now derives a failed command's response and artifacts paths under command.<name>.error.*; parameters deliberately stay on command.<name>.parameters.* (a failure's parameters are the same values the success path carries, so a rule that gates them must keep applying -- moving them would stop the rule matching and fall through to the profile default, which under debug returns the value whole). ask_user excluded: success=False there means unanswered [A7], not failed.

VERIFICATION NOTE the bead asked for: the discriminator is NOT command_output['success']. CommandOutput.success is a PROPERTY delegating to command_response.success, and model_dump() emits no top-level success key at all (dumped keys: command_response, workflow_name, context, command_name, command_parameters, started_at, duration_ms, command_call_id). The implementation reads command_response.success, which is present in the dump. Had this been taken on trust the branch would have been dead code that silently never fired.

Tests: tests/test_capture_policy_error_namespace.py, 7 cases. Negative control confirmed: the 4 that pin new behaviour fail against the old paths; the 3 that pin preserved behaviour (success whole, ask_user, parameters gated) pass either way, which is what they are for.
close_reason: Closed

title: Tests: tests/test_experiment_container.py
description:

title: Harness: run a task set as an experiment, one conversation per attempt
description:
The thing that actually produces an experiment. Today a task is executed by a human typing into the chatbot; nothing runs a SET.

Behaviour:
- input: a task set (list of task_id + the message(s)/startup action that drive it) and a repeat count k
- create the experiment row first, with its hypothesis, BEFORE any task runs (pre-registration is worthless if written afterwards)
- wrap the whole thing in evidence_run() so the run gets zero-drop assertion, prune suppression, archival and provenance - and mark the experiment status='invalid' if it comes back invalid
- one conversation per (task_id, attempt), on its OWN channel, so attempts can run concurrently without hitting leased_session's 409 and without sharing a SessionStateStore pending slot
- resume/partial: a crashed harness must leave the experiment status='running' and be resumable or explicitly markable invalid, never silently half-scored

Concurrency is the whole reason for one-channel-per-attempt; a shared channel would serialise the run by construction.

Ordering note: task independence is a methodological requirement here. Conversations in the SAME channel share a topic namespace and get cross-linked; separate channels per attempt gives independence for free. Do not 'optimise' this into one channel.

Consumers: the tau2 15-task hard set at k=3 is the motivating case, but the harness should not know anything tau2-specific - a task set is data.
acceptance_criteria: Running a task set produces one experiments row, N*k conversations correctly labelled, an evidence bundle, and a status that is complete or invalid but never silently partial. Attempts demonstrably run concurrently.
notes: Shipped fastworkflow/experiment/runner.py: ExperimentTask/AttemptRun/Grader/ExperimentHarness. Creates the experiment row (with hypothesis) BEFORE any task runs; wraps the sweep in evidence_run() and records each segment; one channel + one WEC + one unique workflow_id_str per attempt so attempts run concurrently (test asserts wall-clock overlap, not just distinct ids); resume() selects on finished_at IS NULL and restarts via restart_attempt. Defeats BOTH determinism contaminants ([XR16]): FW_LM_CACHE=0 through get_lm, and FW_UTTERANCE_CACHE_SCOPE=workflow sharding ___convo_info/cache.sqlite3, which was keyed on nothing and would have correlated attempts AND leaked the baseline arm into the treatment arm. Cache posture recorded in the evidence segment. NOT ChatSession (write-once chat_session global + blocking Topology-A ask_user). DSPy memory policy is opt-in: install_policy claims the config-owner thread process-wide with no uninstall.

title: Plumbing: carry experiment/task/attempt from the runtime to the turn record
description:
Getting the labels onto the rows, without touching channel semantics.

The write path today: WorkflowExecutionContext produces a TurnResult carrying channel_id and conversation_id; run_chatbot/server.py ~L693-740 builds the turn record from it; SQLiteTraceSink writes it. The experiment labels must ride the same path rather than being stitched on afterwards by a query.

Work:
- carry experiment_id/task_id/attempt on the same object that already carries channel_id/conversation_id, and set them where the conversation is minted
- record EvidenceRun.run_id against the experiment row, closing the gap where run_id exists only in the bundle JSON (evidence_run.py as_record)
- DistillationResult should likewise carry its run id so the CLI summary can point at the record (this is fix-sb8.2's ask; make sure the two ids do not collide in naming)

EXPLICIT NON-GOAL: channel_id semantics do not change. It stays the session key - the leased_session(channel_id) concurrency lease and the SessionStateStore pending-blob key. One channel remains one live session, which is what lets attempts run concurrently. Anything that makes channel_id mean 'experiment' reintroduces the 409 serialisation and the shared ask_user pending slot this design exists to avoid.

Related but separate: fix-9eg.8 (identity beyond the hard-coded developer channel) unpins run_chatbot's channel_id='chatbot' (server.py:427). That is orthogonal - it is about WHO, this is about WHICH EXPERIMENT - but both touch the same field, so land them aware of each other.
notes: Shipped. TurnResult += experiment_id/task_id/attempt (appended, defaulted). WEC: _bind_experiment_labels validates the triple at bind_observability_identity (all-three-or-none, isinstance int, positive - the type check is load-bearing because SQLite INTEGER is affinity not constraint); labels stamped at the single TurnResult construction site; mint_conversation_id called with them; serialize_state/apply_serialized_state carry them through cross-process ask_user resume. serialize_turn_result projects them into turn_row. [XR10]: EvidenceRun default id prefix run- -> evr-. THIRD BULLET WAS ALREADY SHIPPED: DistillationResult.run_id exists at distillation.py:627 (fix-sb8.2) and is printed by run/__main__.py:288-296 - verified, not re-implemented.

title: Schema: experiments table + experiment_id/task_id/attempt on conversations and turns
description:
The additive schema change. Follows the existing store conventions in fastworkflow/observability/store.py: _SCHEMA_STATEMENTS, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, explicit secondary indexes, short-lived WAL connections.

experiments(
  experiment_id TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
  label TEXT NOT NULL,              -- identifier: scrub-only under redaction (Phase 0 decision)
  hypothesis TEXT,                  -- WRITE-ONCE, enforced at the store layer
  notes TEXT,                       -- freely editable
  arm TEXT,                         -- e.g. 'baseline', 'treatment'; NULL for unpaired experiments
  baseline_experiment_id TEXT,      -- what this arm is compared against
  status TEXT NOT NULL,             -- running | complete | invalid
  created_at TEXT, completed_at TEXT,
  provenance_json TEXT)             -- EvidenceRun.as_record() observability block

conversations += experiment_id, task_id, attempt
turns         += experiment_id, task_id, attempt   -- denormalised for filtering, as channel_id already is
CREATE INDEX idx_turns_experiment ON turns(experiment_id, task_id, attempt)

All new columns NULLABLE. NULL experiment_id means 'not part of an experiment', so every existing row and every ordinary chatbot turn stays valid with no backfill.

WRITE-ONCE hypothesis is a real constraint, not a convention: enforce it in the store's update path (reject a non-NULL -> different-value transition) the way apply_label_txn is the single enforcement point for labels. A UI-only guard is not enough - the point is that the record is trustworthy later.

status='invalid' is set when the evidence run reports drops or the run never completes; a crashed run must not be silently scoreable. See EvidenceRun.valid, which already refuses to call an unfinished run valid.

Blocked on fix-bn1.1: the version bump must be coordinated with fix-sb8.1 before this lands.
acceptance_criteria: Tables and columns created idempotently; write-once hypothesis enforced at the store layer with a test; existing DBs open unchanged with NULL experiment_id; version bump matches the fix-sb8.1 decision.
notes: Shipped. observability_store.py: FEATURE_EXPERIMENTS_V1 marker (no SCHEMA_VERSION bump, [DR28]); experiments / experiment_attempts / experiment_evidence_runs tables; experiment_id/task_id/attempt on turns+conversations in BOTH the CREATE TABLE literals and a guarded ALTER before the statement loop; 5 indexes incl. UNIQUE idx_conv_experiment_attempt. Store API: create_experiment (declared_tasks/attempts required+positive), set_experiment_hypothesis (write-once, store-enforced), record_evidence_segment, start_attempt/finish_attempt/restart_attempt, complete_experiment (STORE computes the verdict; invalid is terminal via AND status<>'invalid'), experiment_scores/compare_experiments, list/get. Erasure: forget_channel invalidates + deletes attempt rows; clear_conversations deletes all three; prune exempts. list_turns gains experiment/task/attempt filters + projection. New exceptions ExperimentNotFound, HypothesisIsWriteOnce.

title: Phase 0: experiment identity model and capture-policy classification (schema-version question settled by fix-sb8)
description:
UNGATED 2026-08-29: fix-sb8 shipped in merge 7a0340e and DECIDED the schema question unilaterally. This bead's first item is therefore settled, not pending. What remains is the bn1-only half.

WHAT SB8 DECIDED, verified in code and now the precedent to follow:
 - SCHEMA_VERSION stays 1. Six new tables (distillation_runs, distillation_passes, distillation_divergences, distillation_insights, distillation_insight_citations, distillation_verdicts) were added additively via CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS with NO version bump.
 - The reason is recorded as [DR28] at observability_store.py ~1392: the old premise ("schema v1 was never shipped") expired at v3.2.0, so two released builds already disagree about shape at the same user_version. Version-gating was therefore ABANDONED as the compatibility mechanism.
 - The replacement is a schema_features marker in the diagnostics table, merged not overwritten (_merge_schema_features, ~1439), which readers FEATURE-DETECT. sb8 registers FEATURE_DISTILLATION_V1.
 - Columns on EXISTING tables use an ALTER TABLE block guarded by PRAGMA table_info, since CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS cannot add columns. Two live examples: "ALTER TABLE spans ADD COLUMN distillation_pass TEXT" and "ALTER TABLE conversations ADD COLUMN updated_at TEXT".

CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS EPIC: there is no coordinated version bump to negotiate and no shipping-order constraint. fix-bn1.2 follows the established pattern directly and should register its own schema_features marker (e.g. FEATURE_EXPERIMENTS_V1) rather than touching user_version.

STILL OWNED BY THIS BEAD, and unaffected by sb8:

1. IDENTITY.
 - is experiment_id the EvidenceRun.run_id, or a separate id the run_id is recorded against? (an experiment may span more than one run if a run is resumed after a crash)
 - task_id: caller-supplied stable string (tau2 task name, corpus message id) -- NOT derived from the conversation topic, which is LLM-generated and channel-uniquified
 - attempt: a separate counter, since conversation_id is per-channel and not stable across channels
 - denormalisation: conversations only, or conversations AND turns? Precedent says both -- channel_id is already denormalised onto turns, spans and artifacts so filters need no join.

2. CAPTURE-POLICY CLASSIFICATION for the new text fields. Under the evidence profile a user-text field degrades to a digest badge. channel_id is scrub-only BECAUSE it is an identifier. Decide: label = identifier (scrub-only, so WHERE experiment_id=? keeps working and the label stays readable); hypothesis/notes = ? They are developer-authored prose rather than customer data, but policy classifies by content type, not author. Getting this wrong means the first evidence-grade run comes back with an unreadable hypothesis.
   NOTE: fix-ajv.18 has since added a related precedent -- a failed command's response/artifacts move to command.<name>.error.* so they do not inherit the success path's declared policy. The same "separate the namespace rather than weaken the contract" reasoning applies if experiment text needs different treatment from turn text.

3. DE-CONFLICT THE URL NOUN with fix-sb8.6: /api/distillation serves "runs" (one row per compared MESSAGE) and fix-bn1.5 serves /api/experiments (a labelled SET of tasks). A distillation sweep run inside an experiment must be reachable from both directions without two competing "run" concepts in the URL space.

Deliverable: an ADR or design-doc section recording items 1-3. The version-bump negotiation that used to be item 1 is closed -- record the decision above as inherited, not re-litigated.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc/ADR section merged recording: the shared version-bump decision with fix-sb8.1, the experiment/task/attempt identity model, and the capture-policy classification for label/hypothesis/notes. fix-sb8.1 updated to reference it.
notes: Delivered: docs/experiment_container_design.md, revision 2 (post adversarial review). Rulings [XR1]-[XR20]. Identity, capture-policy classification and the /api/distillation vs /api/experiments noun split are all decided. Review: 46 findings raised across 6 lenses, 38 survived independent refutation, 8 blocking; two rulings reversed ([XR7] task_id policing, [XR8] provenance_json) and one table added (experiment_attempts).
