title: Failed commands lose an identity the frame already had
description:
From the IDO ido-2l0.19 investigation, 2026-08-29. 133 command outputs across a 310-attempt collection carry an empty command_name. The comment claiming the identity is unknown is FALSE for 130 of them.

THE PRODUCER, and it is the only one in the package: workflow_agent.py:223-247, the except Exception around CommandExecutor.invoke_command, builds CommandOutput(command_name='', ...) at :232 with the comment 'unknown at this point (failure pre-empted routing)'. workflow_name, context and command_parameters are never passed and take model defaults (__init__.py:90-93).

THE COMMENT IS WRONG. Every error fw.command.execute span has exactly one fw.nlu.intent child (133/133), and 130 of those closed STATUS_OK with resolved:true and a canonical command_name (intent_detection.py:337-352). Recovered: 60 ControlsMonitor/open_finding, 32 Directory/find_identity, 14 Directory/find_organization, 10 EntityLookup/find_application, 9 ControlsMonitor/list_findings, 4 ControlCatalog/list_controls, 1 Directory/find_permission. Routing HAD completed; the exception came out of the response generator invoked at command_executor.py:225/:227, by which point command_name (:195), workflow_name (:199) and context (:200) were bound LOCALS. They are lost only because _invoke_command_impl has no except and the assignments sit at :229-232, past the raise. THE IDENTITY WAS KNOWN AND DISCARDED.

THREE COMPOUNDING ERASURES, all measured:
 1. NO JOIN KEY. command_call_id is stamped only on the success path (command_executor.py:116); the except BaseException at :82-96 re-raises before it. 0 of 133 failure outputs carry one, while 133 of 133 of their error spans do.
 2. SPAN COLUMNS EMPTY. The error end_span at :86-95 passes only error_type, so 0 of 133 error rows have a non-null command_name or context column.
 3. TRACEBACK DISCARDED AT PERSIST TIME. The real stack IS captured (workflow_agent.py:240) and replaced by a sentinel at observability_store.py:702-703, gated by FW_OBS_CAPTURE_TRACEBACKS read at :678, default '0' (:179).

SUGGESTED, in value order:
 FW-1 STAMP THE CALL ID. At command_executor.py:82-96, before re-raising and only when exc is not a control signal (CommandCancelledError, AskUserSuspend), set exc._fw_call_id first-writer-wins so nested dispatch keeps the innermost; read it at workflow_agent.py:231-247. MUST also call record_execution in that except block (today only at :152) or you create the first outcome carrying an id with no ExecutionRecordRef, silently violating the three-way identity pinned by tests/test_dispatch_path_conformance.py:116-124. Public shape unchanged - command_call_id already exists as Optional[str]=None (__init__.py:96-102).
 FW-2 ANNOTATE THE ROUTED IDENTITY at the frame that has it: wrap the response-generator call at command_executor.py:225-227 in try/except BaseException setting exc._fw_command_name/_fw_workflow_name/_fw_context, first-writer-wins, re-raising unconditionally. Fixes 130/133 at source.
   CAPTURE-POLICY WARNING: _apply_capture_policy derives field paths from command_output.get('command_name') or 'unknown' (observability_store.py:493, used :498/:509/:517/:532). Populating the name moves these records from command.unknown.* to command.<name>.*. Under debug nothing changes; under evidence a deployment's per-command rules start applying - more withholding, correct direction, but it can withhold the error_message an operator needs, and a blanket command.unknown.* rule stops matching. Belongs in the changelog.
 FW-3 ERROR-PATH end_span PARITY: pass command_name and context at command_executor.py:86-95.

STILL UNKNOWN: whether 133 outputs are 133 distinct failing tool calls. execute_workflow_query retries once (workflow_agent.py:567-568) and each attempt appends its own row; with no command_call_id the true count of distinct logical calls cannot be recovered from the existing store. FW-1 is what makes it recoverable in future.
acceptance_criteria: A command that fails after routing records its name, context and workflow_name; the failure output and its error span share a command_call_id; a test covers the post-routing exception path.
close_reason:
Landed, then repaired: the first pass introduced a regression that both reviews caught.

WHAT LANDED: FW-1 stamps command_call_id onto the in-flight exception first-writer-wins and pairs it with record_execution so an outcome carrying an id always has an ExecutionRecordRef to join to (the three-way identity test_dispatch_path_conformance pins). FW-2 annotates the routed identity at command_executor's response-generator call, where it is a bound local, and workflow_agent reads it - fixing the 130 of 133 failures whose identity was KNOWN AND DISCARDED. FW-3 gives the error end_span command_name and context parity. 66 tests green across the executor, dispatch-conformance, execution-record, additive-turn-result, public-shape and no-capture-control-flow suites.

THE REGRESSION, found by adversarial review and now fixed. _annotate_exception guarded the setattr and left getattr OUTSIDE the try, and the error end_span called getattr(exc, ...) directly. An exception whose __getattr__ raises anything but AttributeError therefore escaped and DESTROYED THE COMMAND'S REAL EXCEPTION - the precise failure that function's own docstring says must never happen, reintroduced by the probe meant to avoid it. Fixed: the read is inside the guard, and a new _annotation() helper is used everywhere an annotation is read, in both files. tests/test_command_executor_errors.py::test_a_hostile_getattr_cannot_mask_the_real_exception, VERIFIED TO DISCRIMINATE - it fails against an unguarded variant and passes against the fixed one, checked by swapping the file both ways.

ALSO FIXED: record_execution was called BARE inside the except handler while every sibling observation site on that path is wrapped precisely so it cannot mask. Now wrapped. Recording is best-effort; unwinding is not.

A CLAIM IN THE CODE WAS BACKWARDS AND IS NOW CORRECTED. The capture-policy comment said naming the command means 'more withholding, which is the correct direction'. A reviewer ran it: capture_policy short-circuits and returns a value WHOLE when a declared policy is not gated for the sink, so a field that was an omit envelope under command.unknown.* can come back as a RAW STRING under the routed name - including a 4KB traceback in artifacts.error_message. The direction is toward LESS withholding. Latent only because observability_store passes no field policies today. The comment now says so.

TWO THINGS RECORDED, NOT FIXED:
 - CONTROL-SIGNAL SPANS CHANGED SHAPE. except BaseException stamps CommandCancelledError and AskUserSuspend too, and the error end_span reads those annotations outside the is_control_signal guard, so a cancelled span goes from command_name=None context=None to the routed values. Probably the right outcome; nothing pins it either way, so it is stated rather than asserted.
 - CommandOutput.is_ask_user is command_name == 'ask_user'. A failure output now carries the real routed name AND success=False, which is the pattern complete_ask_user_entry scans for. Unreachable today because ask_user is a DSPy pseudo-command and not routed - but root-context command names are unqualified and ido has several. Filed as fix-ajv.17.

title: Blinded review mode: suppress every system verdict in the review view
description:
Its own bead rather than a flag inside the review view, because this is the requirement that fails SILENTLY and therefore needs its own tests.

WHAT IT SUPPRESSES when an assignment declares itself blind: turns.status and turns.success, any pass/fail chrome, any prior reviewer's answers, and anything else that tells the reviewer what the system already concluded. The trace itself stays - the reviewer is meant to read what happened.

WHY IT IS NOT COSMETIC. A reviewer who can see that the system scored a turn successful is being asked to CONFIRM rather than to JUDGE, and their agreement then measures deference, not agreement. The failure leaves no trace: ratings still arrive, an inter-rater figure is still computable, and it reads as strong agreement. Nothing looks wrong.

THE LEAK IS USUALLY HELPFULNESS. A success badge in a corner, a red row, a 'previous reviewer said' hint, a default pre-selected from the system's own verdict - each one is an obvious kindness in a debugging UI and each one destroys the measurement. Worth a test per surface rather than a single flag check.

ALSO WORTH DECIDING: whether a blinded assignment should hide ORDERING signals too. If rows arrive grouped by outcome, a reviewer who notices the boundary has recovered the verdict from the sequence, and the view is blind only in its markup. The first consumer shuffles under a declared seed before handing the assignment over, so this may be the consumer's job - but the view should not RE-SORT into a revealing order.
acceptance_criteria: With a blind assignment, no rendered surface carries status, success, a system verdict, or another reviewer's answers; a test per surface, and one asserting the view does not re-sort rows.
notes: Implemented server-side blinded review mode in commit 1ace85b (worktree /home/drawal/rl/fastworkflow-observability). Progress payload exposes assignment rows in declared order and only the presenting rater's latest answers. Review-pane turn payload now uses a capability-gated row endpoint and strips turn status/success/answer plus nested system answers, outcomes, scores/rewards, evaluation results, machine predicate results/verdicts, and rater answer/verdict fields before JSON serialization. Review trace endpoint preserves span structure/status, plans, commands, observations, and failures while stripping outcome/verdict/default-answer attributes. Non-blinded projections retain those fields. Multi-rater export now requires an explicit adjudicator capability; missing/rater capabilities receive 403. Tests: .venv/bin/pytest -q tests/test_review_ingest.py tests/test_review_sidecar.py tests/test_review_export.py tests/test_observability_workspace.py tests/test_blinded_review.py => 39 passed. Remaining for fix-rj2.6: integrate this commit with sibling observability beads and run the parent-level aggregate checks (not run here by isolation). Risk: blinding is enforced on review-context endpoints via a conservative recursive field-name projection; future outcome-bearing schema keys must be added to the projection, and generic operator workspace endpoints remain outside the rater review projection. Bead intentionally left open.
close_reason: Server-side blinded projections @ 1ace85b. Progress/turn/trace review payloads strip status/success/outcomes/other raters; assignment order preserved; traces keep observations/failures. Independent tests: 39 passed. CSS-only hiding not used.

title: Review view: one rubric row beside its trace
description:
The reason to host this in run_chatbot at all. Everything else could be a script; the trace viewer could not.

ONE ROW AT A TIME: the turn's trace on one side, that row's questions on the other, answers captured as the reviewer reads. Progress and resume, because an assignment is not finished in one sitting and a reviewer who loses four hours of judgements does not start again.

WHY THE TRACE IS THE POINT. The IDO stopgap (evaluation/rate_cli.py) shows a reviewer only the final ANSWER. That is sufficient for judging what the operator was shown, and useless for judging WHY a run failed - which needs the plan, the commands and the observations. So the stopgap can collect presentation verdicts and cannot collect attribution, and attribution is half of what the review is for. The progressive-disclosure trace debugger already in run_chatbot is exactly the missing surface.

REUSE RATHER THAN REBUILD: the existing turn -> plan/execution -> step -> tool call -> command -> NLU -> LLM view is the thing; this bead adds a question pane beside it and a way to move to the next row, not a second viewer.

DEPENDS ON fix-9eg.11 for what to render and fix-9eg.10 for where answers go.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewer can work an assignment end to end from the browser, see each turn's full trace beside its questions, leave and resume without losing answers.
notes: Implemented in isolated worktree commit 06e4813. Added capability-gated GET /api/review/assignments/<id>/progress and POST /api/review/assignments/<id>/answers using X-Review-Capability; SPA renders row questions beside existing scoped trace viewer with next/prev and latest-revision resume. assignment.blinded is exposed only as a hook; server-side suppression remains for fix-9eg.14. Validation: 64 passed, 7 skipped across requested review/workspace/feedback tests plus test_run_chatbot_test_mode.py. Bead intentionally left open.
close_reason: Capability-gated review pane beside existing trace viewer @ 06e4813. GET progress + POST answers require X-Review-Capability; launch token alone 403. Resume loads latest revision. Independent tests: 37 passed. Blinding deferred to fix-9eg.14. Capability in URL fragment is a resume tradeoff.

title: Review rubric: a declared question set attached to turns, as data
description:
The contract that lets run_chatbot host structured human review WITHOUT knowing what is being reviewed. No UI in this bead; this is the document shape and its validation.

A RUBRIC IS: a list of rows, each naming a turn_key and the questions to ask about it; each question carries an id, prompt text, and a CLOSED answer vocabulary. Plus assignment-level metadata (an id, a rater slot, and the blinding flag the sibling bead consumes).

WHAT FASTWORKFLOW KNOWS: 'a rubric is questions with closed vocabularies, attached to turns'. WHAT IT MUST NEVER KNOW: what any question means. The first consumer's questions are about task-contract predicates and a failure taxonomy; a different workflow's would be about something else entirely, and neither belongs in this repo.

WHY CLOSED VOCABULARIES ARE PART OF THE SCHEMA RATHER THAN THE CALLER'S PROBLEM: a free-text verdict cannot be aggregated, and the aggregation is the point - inter-rater agreement is computed by comparing answers, so two raters typing 'not shown' and 'not-shown' have disagreed as far as any arithmetic can tell. Validating at capture is the only place it can be enforced cheaply.

DELIBERATELY NOT IN SCOPE, because it is the consumer's: what the answers mean, how they are scored, who rates, inter-rater agreement, adjudication. This bead defines a question and an allowed answer; it draws no conclusion from either.

REFERENCE CONSUMER, useful as a shape check rather than a requirement: ~/rl/ido/evaluation/g2a_worksheet_run1_stratified.json - 60 rows, per-row question lists, closed vocabularies, produced by evaluation/worksheets.py.
acceptance_criteria: A rubric document validates or is rejected with the reason; an answer outside a declared vocabulary is refused at capture; the schema carries no domain vocabulary of its own.
notes: Implemented on feat/experiment-observability-3.3 in d1ed885. fastworkflow/review/sidecar.py validates domain-neutral assignment documents: scoped turn refs, metadata/rater slots/blinding, single-select and multi-select vocabularies, and bounded notes. Capture rejects out-of-vocabulary and over-bound answers. Assignment rows bind canonical workspace-manifest digest, workspace identity, and per-store evidence digests. No IDO/EXP vocabulary is embedded. Bead intentionally left open.
close_reason: Domain-neutral assignment/rubric validation in review_sidecar.py: single-select, multi-select, bounded-note; out-of-vocab refused; no IDO vocabulary in schema.

title: feedback table is write-only: no read API and no HTTP route
description:
Found while building the IDO dual-rater path (ido-2l0.8), verified against the 3.2.x tree.

upsert_feedback(turn_key, feedback_json) writes (observability_store.py:1521). NOTHING READS IT BACK. There is no get_feedback, no list_feedback, and no HTTP route that serves it. The only path to a stored verdict is the LEFT JOIN inside get_memory_window (:1399-1400), which requires a conversation_id AND only returns turns passing _USABLE_TURN_FILTER - status completed/failed with a non-NULL conversation_summary. A verdict on any other turn is unreachable through the public API.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THIS ONE CONSUMER. The IDO architecture (section 15.1) commits to exactly this storage: 'evaluator verdicts land in the store's feedback table keyed by turn_key, so a reviewer sees the verdict beside the trace with no new storage machinery'. That design is currently unimplementable - the verdict goes in and cannot come out. The same applies to fix-9eg.1 (Feedback panel: render feedback-table rows beside traces), which cannot be built without a read path.

SUGGESTED: get_feedback(turn_key) and list_feedback(channel_id=..., limit=...) on ObservabilityStore, plus GET /turns/{turn_key}/feedback. Read-only, no interpretation - the caller decides what the payload means.
acceptance_criteria: A verdict written by upsert_feedback is retrievable by turn_key through both the store API and an HTTP route, for a turn with no conversation_summary.
notes: Implemented on feat/experiment-observability-3.3 in f5b039e. ObservabilityStore now has direct get_feedback(turn_key) and list_feedback(channel_id, limit) reads with no conversation-summary/usable-turn filter. Debug HTTP exposes GET /api/feedback/<turn_key> and filtered GET /api/feedback. Focused tests pass; bead intentionally left open for orchestrator.
close_reason: Agent-feedback read path on feat/experiment-observability-3.3 @ f5b039e: get_feedback/list_feedback and GET /api/feedback/<turn_key> retrieve upsert_feedback without conversation_summary. Formal review is not stored in feedback. Independent tests passed; claim-race flake under large parallel run reproduced green in isolation.

title: Prune suppression is unverifiable across processes; the startup prune does honour FW_OBS_SUPPRESS_PRUNE
description:
Found while wiring the IDO evaluation harness (ido-2l0.9), alongside the evidence_run cross-process defect.

Requirements 12.4 requires that pruning shall not run mid-evaluation. Two things stop that being achievable from a harness today:

1. suppress_pruning() (observability_store.py:196) is an IN-PROCESS counter. A harness that enters it suppresses pruning in the harness and not in the server that is actually writing. FW_OBS_SUPPRESS_PRUNE is the only cross-process switch, and NOTHING in the fastworkflow tree ever sets it - only tests/test_evidence_run.py:349 does, for a subprocess case.

2. SQLiteTraceSink.__init__ runs an opportunistic store.prune() at observability_store.py:2064. So the variable has to be in the server's environment BEFORE the server starts; setting it afterwards is too late for the startup prune.

Neither is a defect in isolation - the combination means the documented way to suppress pruning does not work for the documented evidence topology.

SUGGESTED: document the env var as the cross-process contract and have run_fastapi_mcp surface it (a flag, or at minimum a startup log line stating whether suppression is in effect), so a harness can assert it rather than hope.

IDO WORKAROUND IN PLACE: evaluation/observability.py ServerEnvironment puts FW_OBS_SUPPRESS_PRUNE=1 in the launch environment and records it into provenance, so the value the bundle cites is the value that was set rather than one read back from the wrong process.
acceptance_criteria: A harness can determine from the running server whether prune suppression is in effect; the startup prune honours the variable.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-29. The bead asked for the env var to be documented as the cross-process contract and for run_fastapi_mcp to surface it "so a harness can assert it rather than hope". Both, and the surfacing is assertable rather than a log line.

1. GET /probes/readyz?observability=true now returns {"observability": {"config": {...FW_OBS_* in effect...}, "pruning_suppressed": bool, "enabled": bool}}. Opt-in like the existing ?memory flag, since probes are frequent. This is what makes it ASSERTABLE: a harness reads the value in effect in the SERVER process instead of assuming its own environment reached it, and can cite the answer in its bundle.

2. Startup log line reporting enabled / profile / pruning_suppressed with the raw FW_OBS_SUPPRESS_PRUNE value, wrapped so a logging failure can never stop the server. It makes a silent mis-setting visible at the one moment it can still be corrected -- before the recorder's construction-time prune.

3. README env table now documents FW_OBS_SUPPRESS_PRUNE, stating explicitly that it is the cross-process contract, that suppress_pruning() only covers the calling process, that the variable must be in the SERVER's environment BEFORE it starts because the recorder prunes once on construction, and pointing at the probe for confirmation.

TESTS: tests/test_probes.py::TestObservabilityRegimeIsAssertable, 4 cases -- absent unless asked for, suppression in effect, suppression NOT in effect (the answer a harness most needs: it asked and it did not take hold), and the capture profile riding along so a bundle can cite the profile the server actually used.

NOT CHANGED, deliberately: suppress_pruning() stays an in-process counter. Making it cross-process would mean shared mutable state in the DB, and the env var already crosses the boundary correctly -- the defect was that nothing reported whether it had.
close_reason: Closed

title: Concrete ContextHandles are blocked: no framework identity for a context instance, and handle_projector is dead
description:
From fix-ajv.3/.1. Every ContextHandle the runtime projects today is TYPE-ONLY
(concrete=False), which arch 6.7 permits only as feature-off legacy behavior and
which explicitly CANNOT contribute to G2A/G2B. So FW-REQ-002's two context-handle
acceptance criteria currently hold at the TYPE level only.

WHY: there is no framework-level identity for a context instance.
Workflow.current_command_context is an arbitrary application object;
current_command_context_displayname is just the class name again on the test
workflows; id() is a reusable memory address. capture_policy.project_context_handle
therefore degrades to type-only rather than inventing a key, and
tests/test_context_handle_capture.py::test_the_handle_is_type_only pins that so it
cannot quietly be assumed away.

ALSO FOUND: runtime_manifest.ContextDeclaration.handle_projector is DEAD. It is
parsed and merged (runtime_manifest.py:653, 798-804, 1087) and nothing anywhere
resolves it, so a workflow that names a projector today gets nothing.

TO CLOSE: a projector registry that actually resolves handle_projector, plus a
workflow-side hook that yields an instance key. Both are design decisions, which is
why this is not a patch. Until then, no G2A/G2B claim may rest on context handles.
notes:
2026-08-28 OWNER DECISION (Dhar): DEFERRED THROUGH G2B, not merely deferred. Do not close this before the G2B bundle is assembled, even if the design work becomes cheap.

Reason: G2A and G2B are a paired comparison and must be instrumentation-identical. Landing concrete context handles between the two bundles would give G2B an evidence axis G2A does not have, so any difference on that axis would be unattributable — lens change or system change, indistinguishable. Deferring symmetrically through both keeps the pair honest. Fixing this BEFORE G2A, or AFTER G2B, are the only safe windows; between them is the one option that is actively wrong.

Consequence accepted: FW-REQ-002's two context-handle acceptance criteria hold at the TYPE level only for both bundles, and no G2A or G2B claim may rest on context handles. Recorded as a declared limitation in ido-2l0.10.

Scope confirmed in code: the projection machinery is complete and tested (capture_policy.py:549, keyed HMAC, stable handle_id, honest degradation). Three separate design gaps block concrete handles, which is why this is not a patch: (1) no framework identity for a context instance; (2) ContextDeclaration.handle_projector is dead — parsed at runtime_manifest.py:655, validated on merge at 800-806, merged at 1089, resolved nowhere; (3) no security scope — tracing.py uses UNSCOPED_SECURITY_SCOPE because there is no SecurityContext (FW-NFR-010, arch 12.4).

title: Write paths no redaction or capture policy reaches: feedback_json, train metrics, diagnostics, span scalar columns, sync-path labels
description:
Found while wiring the capture policy for fix-ajv.1. Five persisted surfaces are
touched by NEITHER the credential Redactor NOR the new CapturePolicy, so they are
verbatim under every profile including `evidence`:

1. feedback_json  - upsert_feedback (observability_store.py:919)
2. train_runs.metrics_json - record_train_run (:931)
3. diagnostics values - set_diagnostic (:961)
4. span SCALAR columns command_name / context / name / channel_id
   (upsert_span_rows:589-615). Span ATTRIBUTES are redacted; the scalars beside
   them are not, and a context display name can carry entity content.
5. conversation labels written through the SYNC store path
   (run_fastapi_mcp/utils.py:1738 -> ObservabilityStore.record_conversation_label
   -> apply_label_txn:529). Only labels QUEUED through
   SQLiteTraceSink.record_conversation_label reach the redacting _apply_label, and
   the production path is the sync one - so in practice conversation topics and
   summaries are persisted unredacted.

Item 5 is the one worth doing first: it is a live path, not a latent one, and the
label text is LLM-generated from user conversation.

Distinct from fix-cj4 (session-state redaction) - that is a different store. The
evidence-profile promise of FW-REQ-002 clause 3 ("every captured field shall have
sensitivity, size, retention, and redaction policy") is not true while these five
exist, so an evidence bundle cannot yet be claimed default-deny end to end.
close_reason:
Five surfaces closed in observability_store.py + tests/test_redaction_coverage.py
(36 tests). 826 pass across the whole EXP-003 surface.

Protection was applied at the STORE, not at the callers, so a third caller cannot
bypass it - run_fastapi_mcp/utils.py needed no change at all.

  5. sync-path conversation labels -> apply_label_txn, scrub + policy (user-text)
  4. spans.context   -> scrub + policy (user-text)
     spans.name/command_name -> scrub + policy (controlled-vocabulary)
     spans.channel_id -> scrub ONLY, see below
  2. train_runs.metrics_json -> scrub + policy (opaque-payload)
  1. feedback_json   -> scrub ONLY, see below
  3. diagnostics.value -> scrub ONLY, see below

THREE DELIBERATE SCRUB-ONLY DECISIONS (each would otherwise change behavior)
- feedback_json is the AGENT'S MEMORY of being corrected: get_memory_window parses
  it and restore_history_from_turns feeds it to dspy.History. A badge still parses,
  so under `evidence` the agent would silently receive an envelope where its
  feedback used to be. Behavior change, not exposure reduction -> fix-cj4.
- diagnostics.value holds writer_health, which health_delta and evidence_run read
  to decide whether a run is valid evidence AT ALL. Withholding it blinds the
  evidence gate under the only profile that makes the gate mean anything, and would
  digest the very turn keys problems() prints for the operator.
- spans.channel_id: forget_channel erases with DELETE ... WHERE channel_id=?, so
  digesting it narrows first-class erasure to whatever the trace_id fallback still
  covers. Buying exposure reduction with weaker erasure is not a Phase 0 trade.

CORRECTIONS TO MY OWN ISSUE TEXT
- Every line reference I filed was ~380 lines stale (the file grew when fix-ajv.1's
  capture-policy wiring landed). Findings themselves were all correct.
- I filed the four span scalars as ONE item; they are three different decisions.
  `context` genuinely carries entity content - current_command_context_displayname
  calls a workflow-supplied get_displayname(instance), and the bundled
  simple_workflow_template/_commands/WorkItem/_WorkItem.py:15-16 returns the item's
  absolute PATH from it. `name`/`command_name` are closed vocabularies.
  `channel_id` cannot be policed at all without breaking erasure.
- train_runs.metrics_json is worse than "unclassified numbers":
  heldout_evaluation.EscalationScore.failures records the verbatim utterance of
  every failing case and metrics_persistence.py:168-172 copies the whole escalation
  block through, so that column carries free text today. Hence opaque-payload.

Two ordering facts are load-bearing and commented at the site: policing runs AFTER
_unique_topic_in_txn (policing first would glue the collision suffix outside the
envelope's closing brace and leave a column that no longer parses as JSON), and the
scrub runs BEFORE the policy so the queued and sync label routes produce
byte-identical envelopes (asserted by digest comparison).

Cost: ~3 us added per span (9.3 -> 12.3 us debug, 16.9 us evidence), on the writer
thread rather than the turn path.

NOT TRUE YET, and this was the claim the bead was filed to make true: an evidence
bundle is still not default-deny end to end, because feedback_json is verbatim by
the decision above. That last step is fix-cj4's.

title: Runtime provenance capture API for evaluation harnesses (arch 6.3)
description:
Unblocks ido-07y.1 (EXP-002 evaluation/ package scaffold, P0 open), which must
assemble arch 6.3 EvaluationProvenance. About 15 of its fields originate in
fastWorkflow and today have no single producer, so the harness would hand-roll
the assembly. Three concrete hazards if it does:

1. command_surface_fingerprint vs workflow_fingerprint. The only thing named
   like a fingerprint today is compute_commands_source_fingerprint, which hashes
   absolute paths + (size, mtime_ns). It is right for cache invalidation and
   WRONG for identity, and it is already mislabeled "workflow_fingerprint" in
   checkpoint.py:95 and metrics_persistence.py:221. A harness copying that
   pattern records a value that changes when a file is touched or the tree is
   copied -- the exact O3 defect fix-i6h.2 just closed.
2. importlib.metadata.version("fastworkflow") returns 2.30.1 on this machine
   while pyproject says 3.2.0: the editable install's dist-info froze on 8 Aug
   and does not track version bumps. A single-accessor answer is silently five
   minor versions stale.
3. resolve_current_version returns None for a workflow on the pre-versioning
   layout even though it IS trained (both hello_world workflows are in this
   state). Recording None alone reports a trained workflow as untrained;
   legacy_layout_in_use carries the difference.

Deliver fastworkflow/observability/provenance.py as a leaf (stdlib + Pydantic +
runtime_manifest only, arch 22) exposing the fastWorkflow-origin half of 6.3 and
leaving the harness-owned axes (corpus, contracts, evaluators, tenant/principal/
dataset/timeslot, backend attestation) to ido. Values that need a heavy or
non-leaf import -- trained-artifact id, dspy cache state, per-call LM kwargs --
are caller-supplied rather than reached for; artifact_versioning alone costs
2.1s and pulls the package root plus dspy/litellm.

Also needs the first LLM role registry in the codebase (11 roles, all referenced
ad hoc today) with two documented traps: LLM_COMMAND_METADATA_GEN pairs with
LITELLM_API_KEY_COMMANDMETADATA_GEN (no underscore, so deriving the key name
from the role name silently misses), and LLM_RESPONSE_GEN is an orphan present
in every env file and read by no code.

API keys: fingerprint only, never the value.
close_reason: fastworkflow/observability/provenance.py landed: EngineProvenance / WorkflowProvenance / ModelProvenance under RuntimeProvenance, plus capture_runtime_provenance() as the one-call entry point. Leaf per arch 22, enforced structurally by a test that AST-parses both leaf modules and fails on any non-leaf fastworkflow import. Verified end to end against the live ido workflow: fingerprint_verified True, 6 roles captured, no secret in the serialized record. Three traps the API now handles that a hand-rolled assembly would not: both version answers are recorded because the editable install's dist-info says 2.30.1 while pyproject says 3.2.0; trained_artifact_legacy_layout distinguishes a legacy-layout trained workflow from an untrained one (resolve_current_version returns None for both, and both bundled hello_world workflows are in that state); command_surface_fingerprint is named for what it is so nobody records the mtime/path hash as workflow identity the way checkpoint.py:95 and metrics_persistence.py:221 already do. Independent review found one critical and seven major issues, all fixed with regression tests: reproducible returned True when the cache state was unknown (the default) -- it now requires cache known-off, matching how the engine half already refuses source_dirty=None; proxy basic-auth credentials were recorded verbatim from LITELLM_PROXY_API_BASE and are now stripped to a fingerprint; config_hash had a newline delimiter collision and now routes through canonical_content_hash; git_revision validated neither the ref nor the result, so a hostile .git/HEAD was an arbitrary file read published as source_revision; a broken gitdir pointer climbed to the enclosing repo and returned its revision; the trained tri-state and two docstring overclaims were corrected. 143 tests across the two suites, 235 passing with adjacent suites. Full suite deferred to pre-commit per instruction.

title: workflow_content_hash includes generator bookkeeping files; decide whether load_manifest should verify the declared fingerprint
description:
Found from the ido side while verifying cross-repo agreement on the arch 7.1 recipe (ido bead ido-ylw.4). Good news first: canonical_content_hash in runtime_manifest.py and canonical_fingerprint in ido's gen_ido_scaffold.py agree byte-for-byte on identical inputs (verified on three cases incl the b'b\0c\0d' framing case), and load_manifest('ido_workflow') accepts the manifest ido emits unmodified - 18 contexts, 63 commands, 14 occupiable, schema 1, all features off. The two sides interoperate on first contact.

TWO ISSUES, both about scope rather than recipe.

1. workflow_content_entries hashes every .json under the workflow root, which picks up files a generator writes for its own bookkeeping. ido writes .generated_manifest.json (the list of paths its last run emitted, used to tell a stale generated artifact from an unaccounted-for one). That file used to carry a generated_at timestamp, which made workflow_content_hash TIME-DEPENDENT on an ido workflow - measured 27 Aug: same tree, two different hashes across a simulated regeneration. That is precisely the property arch 7.1 says the hash must not have.

I have already removed the timestamp on the ido side, so the acute bug is gone and fw's hash is now stable there. But the class remains: any generator's bookkeeping file under the workflow root is in scope by default, and the next one may not be as easy to make content-stable. Suggest excluding dot-prefixed files by convention (a leading dot is the usual signal for 'tool bookkeeping, not source'), which fixes the class without core needing to know any specific workflow's filenames.

2. workflow_fingerprint is declared in the manifest and carried through to merged metadata (runtime_manifest.py:895) but never verified against workflow_content_hash. Today ido's declared value and fw's computed value DIFFER, and after fix 1 the difference is exactly the one file above: fw sees 135 files, ido's generator scopes 134. Both are stable now, so nothing is broken.

The decision to make: if load_manifest is ever meant to verify the declared fingerprint - which is the natural next step and what makes the field worth carrying - then the two file-selection rules must be reconciled first, or a healthy workflow will fail startup conformance. If it is never verified, consider dropping the field or documenting that it is advisory, because two functions that both compute 'the workflow fingerprint' with the same recipe and different scopes is a trap.

Reference: ido's scope rules are FINGERPRINT_SUFFIXES / FINGERPRINT_EXCLUDED_TREES / FINGERPRINT_EXCLUDED_FILES in gen_ido_scaffold.py; recipe recorded in the comment above canonical_fingerprint; tests in ido tests/test_workflow_fingerprint.py.
close_reason: Both issues fixed. (1) workflow_content_entries now skips dot-prefixed files and directories at any depth, which closes the class rather than the instance -- no bookkeeping file a generator invents can make the hash time-dependent again. (2) verify_workflow_fingerprint + FingerprintVerification compare declared against computed as a tri-state (matches / stale / not declared, where not-declared is not a failure since 7.2 makes the field optional); check_startup_conformance gained an opt-in verify_fingerprint flag, off by default because Slice 0 changes no behavior and it costs a full tree read. The scope question resolved in favour of verifying: with the dot rule, fastWorkflow selects the same 134 files ido's generator does and computes exactly ido's declared sha256:326aec98..., so strict startup conformance on the live ido workflow PASSES. Two further defects found in review and fixed here: a missing workflow folder used to hash to the empty tree (a confident sha256 every wrong path shares) and now raises; a malformed manifest used to escape as a raw JSONDecodeError past the ManifestConformanceError the CLI catches, and now arrives as a conformance error naming the file. Follow-up fix-ijf filed: the two scope RULES are structurally different and agree on today's tree rather than by construction. tests/test_context_runtime_manifest.py 104 tests; 235 passing across adjacent suites. Full suite deferred to pre-commit per instruction.

title: Tests: tests/test_distillation_observability.py
description:
Integration tests against real workflows, per .cursor/rules/testing_rules.mdc
(no mocks). Extends the existing tests/test_distillation_core.py (199 lines)
and tests/test_distillation_action_log.py (249 lines).

Coverage:
* Pass separation: a --generate_insights turn produces two traces per the

* Grouping row written with both pass ids, model identity, and rolled-up cost.
* Fingerprint equality on a clean run; a deliberately perturbed pass entry is
  flagged NON-COMPARABLE and its divergences are excluded from aggregates.
* Alignment: repeated identical calls survive (the set-semantics bug); a
  single differing parameter yields ONE same-command-different-params pair,
  not two unmatched entries; reordering is classified as reordered;
  same-end-state-different-path is flagged non-material.
* Provenance round trip both ways: insight -> divergence -> spans -> insight.
* Negative outcomes recorded: EMPTY extraction and no-divergence runs.
* Retention: a pinned trace survives a prune that removes an unpinned one.
* Replay: a stored run replays student-only and reports divergence-removed.
* Overhead: distillation observability off (or absent sink) costs nothing —

title: Insight ledger: extractor span, stable insight ids, bidirectional provenance, and negative outcomes
description:
Make the final artifacts traceable to their evidence, in both directions.

Extractor observability: the LLM call that decides what the rule is
(extract_insights() L592 and extract_planning_insights() L719) is currently
unobserved. Emit it as a span carrying its inputs — user query, both formatted
trajectories, the divergence summary, and the existing_insights corpus it was
deduping against — plus the raw output before parsing.

Insight ledger rows: stable insight id, kind (planning | execution), text, the
run and divergence record(s) cited, the extractor span id, and the file plus
entry number it was appended to. The id must NOT be the file entry number:
_append_numbered_insights() continues numbering by regex over the file
(L665-693), so renumbering or a hand edit would orphan every reference.

Reverse index: from a line in planning_agent_insights.md or
execution_agent_anti_patterns.md, get the runs that produced it.

Negative outcomes, which are evidence and are currently invisible:
* diverged but the extractor returned EMPTY — record whether it judged the
  difference context-justified or a duplicate. This is how you tell whether
  the extractor is too conservative or too eager.
* no divergence at all — the 'student was already correct' set, which is the
  counter-evidence pool for any candidate rule.

title: Phase 0: design doc + adversarial review gate for distillation observability
description:

platform.

Produce docs/distillation_observability_design.md and put it through an
adversarial review. It must settle:

1. IDENTITY. How two passes of one message are represented. trace_id ==
   turn_key is assumed by root_span_id(), deterministic_span_id(),
   GET /api/spans/{trace_id}, GET /api/turn/{turn_key}, and the turns PK.
   Candidates (a) derived per-pass trace ids '{turn_key}#teacher', (b) shared
   trace_id + spans.pass discriminator, (c) real per-pass logical turn keys.

   invariant that the choice breaks.
2. Whether the schema is N-pass-capable (>2 students) even though we ship 2.
3. De-conflict 'evidence streams' with fix-35m.3 (EXP-013), which already
   promises distinct distillation accumulators and evidence streams. 35m.3
   owns the isolation guarantee; this epic owns recording and review. Write
   the boundary down so it is not built twice.
4. Record the reversal of design-doc ruling [R24] ('insights distillation is
   explicitly out of Studio scope') in
   docs/fastworkflow_observability_studio_design.md as an amendment, with the
   reason.
5. Storage budget: --generate_insights roughly triples span volume. State the
   expected per-run cost and whether it changes the default retention.
notes:
COORDINATION (2026-08-29, filed with fix-bn1): this Phase 0's SCHEMA_VERSION decision is no longer this epic's alone. fix-bn1 (Experiment container) adds a second set of tables and columns to the same observability.sqlite3 — experiments, plus experiment_id/task_id/attempt on conversations and turns.

SCHEMA_VERSION is PRAGMA user_version, readers FAIL CLOSED on a forward version (IncompatibleObservabilityDB), and there is no numbered migration chain. Two independent bumps would put two mutually incompatible DB versions in flight with no way to read either from the other's build.

So: decide ONE bump covering both epics' tables, or explicitly decide a shipping order and record it. fix-bn1.1 is the counterpart gate and must be settled jointly with this one.

Also de-conflict the URL noun: fix-sb8.6 serves /api/distillation 'runs' (one row per compared MESSAGE) and fix-bn1.5 serves /api/experiments (a labelled SET of tasks). A distillation sweep run inside an experiment must be reachable from both directions without two competing 'run' concepts in the URL space.

title: distillation_runs grouping record: one row per compared message, linking both passes
description:
The row that makes two traces one comparison. Keyed by the user-visible turn,
holding at minimum: the two pass trace ids (per the Phase 0 identity choice),
per-role model identity (teacher agent/planner, student agent/planner,
extractor), both pass-entry state fingerprints, planning_diverged and
exec_diverged booleans, insight counts, per-pass wall time, and per-pass token
and cost totals rolled up from fw.llm.call spans.

Cost/latency is not decoration: distillation exists to make the small model
good enough to replace the big one, so 'what did each pass cost' is the
benefit side of the ledger and belongs on the run row where the UI and
aggregate queries can reach it without walking spans.

DistillationResult currently carries two ints and is discarded; it should
carry the run id so callers (and the CLI summary) can point at the record.

Follow the existing store conventions in fastworkflow/observability/store.py
(_SCHEMA_STATEMENTS, CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS, explicit secondary indexes,
short-lived WAL connections).
notes:
Schema-mechanics findings (2026-08-27):

SCHEMA_VERSION = 1 lives in PRAGMA user_version, and readers FAIL CLOSED on a
forward version (IncompatibleObservabilityDB). There is no numbered migration
chain — _ensure_schema runs idempotent CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plus one
ad-hoc column patch. So the version-bump decision is a compatibility break,
not a formality; it is escalated to fix-sb8.1.

Good news for the cost/latency rollup: fw.llm.call already carries model,
usage, cost, and cache_hit as span attributes (dspy_logger.py ~L420-431). The
per-pass rollup is a query over existing data, not new instrumentation.

Precedent for a store-level read helper: ObservabilityStore.list_train_runs()
exists with no HTTP route. Do not repeat that — fix-sb8.6 must expose the new
tables or they will be as invisible as train_runs is today.

title: Comparability evidence: pass-entry state fingerprints, restore assertion, model identity, DSPy cache hit/miss
description:
A divergence is evidence of a student mistake ONLY if both passes started from
identical state. Nothing currently proves that, so every diff is deniable and
so is every insight derived from it. This is the credibility layer — rank it
above the UI work.

Record, per run:
* A stable fingerprint (hash) of pass-entry state — workflow context, cme
  context, conversation-history tail — captured at teacher entry AND at
  student entry, then compared. distillation.py snapshot_workflow_state()
  (L197) already captures exactly these three; restore_workflow_state() (L209)
  writes them back and verifies nothing.
* An explicit restore-succeeded assertion: today a partial or failed restore is
  silent, and anything outside those three fields is never restored at all.
* Per-role model id and parameters, so runs are not silently compared across a
  model change.
* Per-LLM-call DSPy cache hit/miss. A cache hit in one pass and a miss in the
  other is a silent confound that looks like a behavioural difference.

Downstream contract: a run whose two fingerprints differ is marked
NON-COMPARABLE, and every consumer (UI, aggregate queries, replay) must treat
its divergences as unusable rather than as evidence.
notes:
CORRECTION (2026-08-27) — scope is smaller than filed on one
point and unchanged on the rest.

DSPy cache hit/miss is ALREADY captured: fw.llm.call carries cache_hit
(dspy_logger.py ~L429), alongside model, usage, and cost. So this task does
NOT need to instrument it. What is missing is the rollup and the
interpretation: per-pass aggregation, and flagging the asymmetric case (a
call cached in one pass and live in the other) as a confound that makes the
divergence non-comparable. Same for model identity — the per-call model
attribute exists; what is missing is the per-ROLE record on the run row so
runs are not silently compared across a model change.

Still genuinely absent, and the substance of this task: the pass-entry state
fingerprints and the restore-succeeded assertion. Nothing in the tree computes
or stores those today.
close_reason: Closed

title: Structured divergence record: sequence alignment, divergence taxonomy, materiality flag
description:
Replace the prose divergence summary with a persisted structured record. This
is the piece most likely to be underestimated: a trajectory diff is not a text
diff, it needs a correspondence between the two sequences.

What is wrong with compare_trajectories() today (distillation.py L315-407): it
is set-difference over _action_signature() = (command_name, sorted-params
json). Set semantics collapse repeated identical calls; a single differing
parameter renders as two unrelated 'only by teacher' / 'only by student'
entries instead of one same-command-different-params pair; the ordering check
only inspects the intersection; and the fallback branch emits the literal
string 'Action sequences differ (unclassified difference)'.

Deliver:
* A canonical step key per comparable unit (executed action; plan step).
* A real sequence alignment (LCS / edit script) producing MATCHED PAIRS.
* A per-pair kind: identical | same-command-different-params |
  param-value-only | extra-in-student | missing-in-student | reordered |
  different-answer-same-actions.
* A materiality flag derived from post-pass state fingerprints: two different
  paths that reach the same end state are not a mistake, and the current code
  cannot express that. This is the main source of spurious insights.
* Do the same for plan-level comparison (compare_planning_traces(), L413,
  which today only reports positional 'Step i: Teacher planned X, Student
  planned Y').

Persist the structured record and RENDER the prose summary from it for the
extractor prompt, so the extractor, the UI, and aggregate queries all read one
source of truth. Better extractor input is a side effect, not the goal — this
epic does not re-tune extraction.

title: Compare recorded executions: winner/candidate, best/other runs and teacher/student
description:
Reuse existing experiment scores/comparison and provenance views. Add a shared structured comparison projection and browser view for matching task/attempt/turn evidence, answers, feedback, timings, recorded cost and execution sequences. Support qualitative inspection even when scores are absent or runs differ. Show unmatched tasks/calls and missing evidence explicitly; never force alignment by list position. Start with deterministic matching on existing task/call/context identities; ambiguous matches remain side by side. Distinguish exploratory inspection from existing formal score-comparability checks. No statistical-significance or fixed-target gate.
Human UI and coding-agent structured reads/actions must share semantics and stable store/experiment/task/attempt/turn/span references. Reuse existing stores, workspaces, benchmarks and APIs. Include focused real-component integration tests and relevant browser interaction checks; no paid experiments are required to implement this work. No mandatory upfront scores, numeric targets, rubric, hypothesis, pre-registration ceremony, or reproducibility snapshots.

Multiple-run optimization amendment (owner discussion, 2026-09-19):
Use one comparison projection and UI for (a) winner versus candidate task executions, (b) best attempt versus other attempts of the same task/experiment, and (c) recorded teacher versus student passes. The unit is a scoped recorded execution: store/workspace, experiment/task/attempt when applicable, logical turn(s), optional recorded pass selector and step/span anchors. Teacher and student may share a trace ID; pass identity must separate them and exclude extraction activity. A multi-turn attempt remains navigable in full. Use small adapters to existing evidence rather than forcing every teacher/student record into a new experiment or changing its producer.
Reuse a stored structured alignment where available; otherwise produce a shared deterministic alignment from recorded steps. APIs, browser and agent/extractor consumers use that result, not independent browser diffs. Repeated, inserted and missing calls remain explicit; cross-run call IDs alone are not a correspondence rule. Preserve comparability/materiality evidence when recorded, label unavailable evidence unknown and allow exploratory inspection. Difference does not automatically mean error; reference/teacher/best labels do not claim infallibility.
Extend the existing task page with Runs / Compare / Feedback views. Pin the selected best/reference on the left, display another run on the right and offer Previous/Next and a compact full run list. Default to answers and artifacts, then planning/execution drill-down. Offer Differences only and jump to first difference; reuse failure/navigation/loop markers. Do not create n parallel panes or a separate Distillations navigation tab. Display lightweight per-reviewer reviewed/not-reviewed progress keyed to the EXACT reference/compared execution pair; zero comments does not imply unreviewed. Selecting a new reference changes the review pairs without relabeling prior reviews or feedback.
Feedback actions use the existing recording API and categories/subcategories, with stable anchors to one or both sides. No new insight or adjudication layer.

OWNER-CONFIRMED FEEDBACK CONTRACT (supersedes earlier three-question shorthand):
Categories and allowed subcategories, represented as API enum values:
- observations_analysis (UI: Observations / Analysis): observation, analysis.
- conclusions (UI: Conclusions): what_went_right, what_went_wrong.
- recommendations (UI: Recommendations): what_to_do, what_not_to_do.
The owner confirmed these six meanings explicitly in this implementation session. UI category/subcategory selectors and watermark guidance facilitate free-form human comments; the coding-agent recording API carries category and subcategory explicitly as enums and accepts arbitrary structured text within the comment. Validate category/subcategory pairing. No parsing headings to infer required metadata for NEW writes. Preserve existing historical text without rewriting frozen evidence; uncategorized legacy comments remain readable and visibly legacy/unclassified rather than guessing a new subcategory. Comparison comments can link both recorded executions/pass/step anchors through the same API. No separate insight schema, review layer, or mandatory verdict workflow.
acceptance_criteria:
Candidate opens against current winner by default. Human and agent obtain equivalent references/differences. Inserted/repeated/removed calls and unmatched tasks are visible; ambiguous alignment is labeled. Existing aggregate comparison is reused. Scoreless experiments can be inspected and selected; formal refusal reasons remain visible.
Three runs can be reviewed against a selected best run without leaving the task: pin reference, advance through both others, mark each pair reviewed even with no comment, and resume. Switching best run preserves original pair review/feedback history. A recorded teacher/student fixture sharing a turn/trace projects separate passes through the same comparison view. UI and machine projection show equivalent alignment/evidence references; absent scores do not prevent review. Full attempts and all artifacts remain reachable.

title: Retire legacy dual-write per-channel conversation DBs (Phase 7 completion)
description:
COMPLETED in v3.2.0. The per-workflow observability.sqlite3 is the single source
of truth for conversations, turn records, memory rebuild and feedback. Nothing
under fastworkflow/ imports run_fastapi_mcp/conversation_store.py any more.

WHAT LANDED IN THIS PASS

Gate 2 / §2.4 + rulings I1,I6,C8,C9 (observability_store.py):
 - emit_turn_record is ack-returning and synchronous-first. True = the row is
   durable before the call returns; False = queued and not yet durable; the
   tracing shim returns None when there is no sink at all, which is a distinct
   third state so a caller gating on durability does not defer forever.
 - ALL emissions take the same path (awaiting_user and terminal), so one logical
   turn can no longer split across the sync and queued paths (I6).
 - Degraded path reserves the ordinal synchronously before enqueueing, so a
   record written while the DB was wedged still sorts chronologically (I6).
 - Bounded pending-retry ring (_PENDING_RETRY_MAX=64) keyed by turn_key, retried
   on the writer heartbeat and drained at close (I1).
 - Circuit breaker: FW_OBS_SYNC_WRITE_TIMEOUT_S busy timeout on its own
   connection, FW_OBS_SYNC_BREAKER_COOLDOWN_S cooldown, re-arms ONLY after an
   off-turn-path write probe succeeds (C9).
 - Writer health gained sync_writes, sync_fallbacks, sync_write_ms_max,
   pending_retry_depth, sync_breaker_open.
 - record_conversation_label now returns the topic it actually stored.

Ruling I3 (WEC): last_completed_turn_key, set at terminal finalize only for a
turn that contributed a memory entry, serialized with session state, cleared by
clear_conversation_history, and re-bound from the store on activation. Feedback
keys off it instead of max(ordinal). Also last_turn_record_stored and
last_turn_added_memory for the trim gate and the label schedule.

§2.1 correction: an awaiting_user emission now leaves the memory columns NULL
and the terminal upsert fills them, as the design says.

Gate 1 / step 4 (run_fastapi_mcp): restore reads get_memory_window with
step-back binding (I7) plus reuse of a reserved-but-empty conversation so an
idle channel stops leaking a conversation row per cold start; feedback via
upsert_feedback by turn_key; labeling reads conversation_label_state /
conversation_summaries and writes through the store synchronously; /conversations
uses list_conversation_summaries (phantom exclusion, C7); /activate_conversation
uses the memory window and 404s on zero usable turns; admin dump reconstructs
from the store with a legacy_stores_present marker (C7); trim gated on the emit
ack (I2); turns_appended from the ack (I10); durable_turn_count is a dead field
kept for checkpoint compat (C5); finalize_conversations_on_shutdown deleted.

§2.5: topic generation moved to fastworkflow/conversation_labeling.py;
conversation_store re-exports it so its retained tests use one implementation.

DELIBERATE DEVIATIONS (recorded in the design doc's status block)
 - legacy_floor at mint and the one-shot topic dedupe are NOT ported: both
   reconciled two live stores, and nothing reads the legacy files now.
 - A suspended-then-resumed exchange is ONE conversation turn, not two.
 - FW_OBSERVABILITY=0 means no conversation persistence at all.

TESTS: ported the legacy-mechanism suites to obs-store equivalents rather than
deleting them (ruling C5) - test_conversation_lazy_labeling,
test_manager_shutdown_matrix, test_fastapi_memory_bounds,
test_conversation_topic_generation_bounds. Added gate-2 coverage
(TestSyncFirstTurnRecords), cold-restore/step-back/empty-reuse coverage, and
I3 coverage including the activation case where feedback would otherwise land
on the conversation the user navigated away from.

FOLLOW-UP: fix-gxr (physical deletion of conversation_store.py and its tests)
needs explicit approval.

title: Turn viewer: progressive-disclosure drill-down over fastWorkflow abstractions
description: The chatbot debug turn viewer renders every span as a flat waterfall row, discarding the parent_span_id hierarchy the store already persists. Each level shows its own information first, then a waterfall scoped to its direct children as the drill-down control. title: Distillation teacher/student passes pollute the live turn's span trace
description: Epic-review observation (fix-kw7.2/kw7.8). distill_message runs inside the open logical turn, so teacher AND student passes emit fw.agent.tool_call / fw.command.execute / fw.planner.* spans under the same trace_id with nothing distinguishing pass from real execution — a --generate_insights turn's waterfall shows roughly double the tool calls. Fix direction: a 'distillation_pass' span attribute (teacher/student) plumbed through the distillation entry points, and a chatbot filter/badge.
notes:
Reparented from fix-kw7 to fix-sb8 (distillation observability epic), 2026-08-27, and raised P3 -> P1.

Under fix-kw7 this was a polish item: a --generate_insights waterfall looks
wrong. Under fix-sb8 it is the foundation — separating the two passes is what
makes a teacher/student DIFF possible at all, and every other task in the epic
reads whatever identity scheme this establishes.

Scope change that follows: the original fix direction (a "distillation_pass"
span attribute plus a chatbot filter/badge) is now only ONE of three
candidates, and it is the weakest of them for diffing, because a shared
trace_id leaves the two passes interleaved in the parent/child structure and
pushes partitioning onto every consumer. The alternatives are derived per-pass
trace ids ("{turn_key}#teacher") and real per-pass logical turn keys. The
choice is made in fix-sb8.1 (Phase 0 design + adversarial review) because it
touches the trace_id == turn_key invariant assumed by root_span_id(),
deterministic_span_id(), GET /api/spans/{trace_id}, GET /api/turn/{turn_key},
and the turns primary key. Do not start this task before fix-sb8.1 closes.

The extraction pass (the insight-extractor LLM call) is a third pass to
account for, not just teacher and student — see fix-sb8.5.
Runtime constraint found 2026-08-27, load-bearing on the
identity choice: _execute_message calls _begin_turn(message) exactly ONCE
before entering distillation, and _run_agent_pass does not re-enter it. Any
scheme wanting per-pass turn identity must therefore either re-open a turn per
pass or tag spans without minting new turn keys — the middle ground does not
exist. Related: only ONE turn record is written at finalize and the teacher
output wins, so the student pass currently leaves no durable turn row.

Also note fw.train.* is reserved in tracing.py and never emitted; fix-sb8.1
decides whether distillation gets its own reserved prefix rather than
borrowing it.
close_reason: Closed

comments.author: Dhar Rawal
comments.text:
FINAL PRE-PR REVIEW (2026-08-26/27): three parallel adversarial reviewers over the FULL working tree (both work streams merged) + orchestrator verification. Everything found was fixed on the tree the same session, with regression tests.

CODE FIXES:
1. _compute_context_mutations could RAISE THROUGH FINALIZE (TypeError sorting mixed-type removed context keys) — the one hole in the never-fails-a-turn contract. Body now wrapped + key=repr sort. Test: TestContextMutationEdgeCases.
2. fw.agent.step span LEAKED on non-ValueError reasoning failures (AdapterParseError, provider errors) and on CommandCancelledError from a tool — the retried attempt's whole subtree then parented under a phantom never-emitted span. Both react.py exits now close the span (error/cancelled) before propagating. Tests: TestStepSpanExceptionSafety.
3. FW_OBSERVABILITY=0 was NOT free: observe_dspy_host bound the DSPy callback unconditionally, so every LM call JSON-projected its full prompt before discovering there was no sink. Now inert without a live sink (one get_sink check per turn). Test: TestDisabledObservabilityDspyCost.
4. WEC conversation self-mint (R17 amendment) could fire on FastAPI's DEGRADED eager-mint path: floor-less (C2 bypass, legacy-id aliasing) and later double-minted by reserve_conversation_id. bind_observability_identity gained additive embedder_owns_conversations=True (FastAPI passes it); bare embedders keep self-minting. Test: TestEmbedderOwnedConversationSuppression. (Both the FastAPI-slice and core-slice reviewers found this independently.)
5. Train pid-file staleness/PID-reuse could block training globally forever (files never cleared; kill-0 liveness only). Pid files now record the kernel process start time; a live pid with a different start time is a recycled number; stale files are unlinked on sight. Tests: TestPidReuseHardening.
6. configure_env refused for bundled examples (writing a passwords file into site-packages / the un-gitignored examples dir); GET /turns/{key} + /trace store reads moved off the event loop (run_in_executor; a locked DB stalls one worker, not every channel).

DOC FIXES (docs<->code now consistent; verified claim-by-claim incl. executing every SQL recipe in the shipped skill): README quick-reference CLI block rewritten (four invocations no longer parsed), README + shipped-skill span trees corrected to the real agent-mode chain (fw.agent.execute/step added; fw.llm.call nesting; deterministic-mode note), fw.agent.tool_call kind corrected to 'tool', design doc gained amendments for POST /api/train (4th control-plane write), retired --prune/--forget-channel flags, FW_OBS_SYNC_WRITE_TIMEOUT_S row, schema additions note, keep_dspy_history, and a Decision-Log preamble covering the studio->run_chatbot rename; parity doc channel/train/launch sections corrected; skill reference gained agent-loop spans, ask_user/tool_call/llm.call attribute completions, read-API corrections (get_spans positional, list_train_runs, Phase-7 reads, inherited-writer-names caveat), envelope/index details; run_prune/run_forget_channel re-docstringed as library utilities (kept with their tests per the no-test-deletion rule); launcher docstring aligned with amended R19; tracing.py reserved-v2 comment corrected; stale links fixed (forge spec, team-skill passwords.env rows — root passwords.env deletion verified safe: 0-byte stub, gen-env merges by glob).

VERIFIED SOUND (high-confidence, cross-checked): all four chatbot control-plane writes correctly gated (token+host/origin, constant-time), env picker sends file CONTENT one-way over loopback and writes 0600 workflow-local, clear_conversations preserves train_runs/diagnostics/counters, CSP/textContent/sandbox discipline intact, [A39] indistinguishable 404s on both GETs, --cors_loopback_only regex bypass-tested, keep_dspy_history genuinely bounded (probe fails startup if not), merge of the two work streams emits a coherent span tree with no double emission, fix-kw7.13 acceptance criteria all met.

TESTS: 318 green across every touched suite after the fixes (chatbot 127, FastAPI 163-batch incl. shutdown/labeling, observability core 137+1skip) + the earlier full-suite run. RECOMMENDATION: one final full-suite run on the quiesced tree immediately before the PR (serialize with any other active agent).

BEGIN IMMEDIATE for every state transition; compare-and-set on record_version. Tables: operations (UNIQUE(scope_digest, logical_call_key)), attempts, events, reconciliation_events, compensation_links, reconciliation_gates, logical_call_tombstones, journal_owner. JournalScope is an HMAC'd keyed digest with a key version, and every API requires one - an operation id alone never grants access, and 'no such operation' and 'not yours' give the same answer. Durable owner epoch bumped on every open, so a restart makes every live prior permit unspendable. The arch 14.4 transition matrix is a table the code consults, not prose.

title: command_contract.py: declared adapter effect keys, idempotency/reconciliation declarations, effect kinds
description: Absent/invalid contract = unknown = write-capable. Contracts feed StrictWriteGate and consequence assessment.
close_reason: command_contract.py: CommandEffectContract with effect_kind (unknown by default, never read_only), the adapter effect_key, IdempotencyGuarantee (backend_deduplicated / naturally_idempotent / unknown) and a ReconciliationDeclaration carrying strategy id+version, authoritative source, consistency window and whether the receipt is recoverable. may_dispatch_writes requires all three of a declared write, an effect key, and a reconciliation strategy - a command that can fail into an unresolvable state cannot be permitted to fail. binding_digest covers target+parameters+scope; logical_call_key deliberately excludes non-target parameters so a retry of the same step derives the same key, with the binding digest catching a caller reusing a key for a different call.

title: StrictWriteGate + dispatch invariant: create_or_get operation, durable unknown premark, permit-bound single dispatch, CAS transitions
description: Arch §14.3: no backend call before durable premark; joined existing operations replay bounded results or raise reconciliation-required; WEC never calls journal or backend directly.
close_reason: strict_write_gate.py: StrictWriteGate is default-deny per command (plan 6) and additionally refuses on an insufficient contract, on journal capacity pressure, and on a set reconciliation gate; WriteDenied is a ControlSignal so it halts the turn instead of becoming an observation. ExternalOperationRunner implements the arch 14.3 dispatch invariant in order: create_or_get (a replay joins), join semantics per outcome (succeeded replays and never dispatches; unknown/partial raise reconciliation-required unless the contract declares backend deduplication; partial never retries), begin_attempt's durable outcome-unknown premark + single-use permit bound to operation/attempt/version/epoch, exactly ONE adapter invocation, then CAS transition. An adapter that raises leaves unknown and sets the gate. A 'succeeded' receipt that is not recoverable records outcome-unknown instead, because it cannot support the claim it makes.

title: ReconciliationGate + versioned strategy registry; retention, tombstones, capacity fail-closed
description: Gate checked at admission/startup/resume/dispatch/finish; strategies are versioned code registrations — callers cannot submit free-form retry_safe (arch §6.9, §14.6, §14.8).
close_reason: ReconciliationStrategy protocol + StrategyRegistry: versioned code, not a flag. Determination AND retry eligibility both come from the strategy's rules - callers cannot submit a free-form retry_safe value (arch 14.6). An unregistered strategy id and a source outcome the strategy does not accept are both refusals. Gates: set_gate/clear_gate/gate_is_set, and clear_gate refuses while any operation it blocks on is still protected, because clearing it early is the forbidden unknown-to-known conversion performed by omission. Retention: compact() writes a logical-call tombstone per compacted operation and skips protected records and anything in a compensation link; a tombstoned key cannot be recreated. health() reports protected count and oldest unresolved age and turns dispatch_enabled false on protected-record pressure - capacity pressure disables new dispatch rather than deleting a protected record.

title: Tests: full crash matrix rows 1-12 on fake backend + owner-epoch, receipt recovery, replay suppression, retention

close_reason: tests/test_operation_journal.py: 30 tests over the crash matrix at all four FW-REQ-008B injection points. Before dispatch: not-dispatched, replay joins, different binding conflicts, restart leaves nothing to reconcile. After dispatch: the premark asserted FROM INSIDE the adapter (if that ordering ever inverts a crash leaves no evidence), a crashing adapter leaving outcome-unknown with the gate up, no retry without evidence, same-id retry only under declared deduplication, partial never retried. After acknowledgement: an unrecoverable success receipt not certifying success, a succeeded operation immutable with the refusal itself recorded, and publication failure after backend success leaving unknown with the backend called exactly once. Ownership: epoch increments on restart, a prior-epoch permit cannot transition, a stale epoch cannot begin an attempt, a scope cannot read another scope's operation. Plus reconciliation with evidence, unregistered/unaccepted strategies, compensation as a linked new operation that erases nothing, gate-clearing refusal, default-deny, capacity refusal, tombstoned compaction, and key/binding derivation. Found and fixed a real defect while writing them: the CAS-loss diagnostic event was being written inside the transaction that then rolled back, so a refused late result vanished instead of being recorded.

  'Ada Lovelace'      -> 'Wall Clock'           d=0.636   (product list)
  'Ozymandias Shelley'-> 'Cycling Helmet'       d=0.647   (product list)
5 of 10 non-member names and 4 of 10 non-member products are rewritten to a real record. On a retail workflow that means the turn proceeds against the wrong customer's orders. At auto_apply_threshold=0.2 every one of these becomes a suggestion instead, which is the correct outcome.

Cross-domain legal values are also rewritten: 10/40 retail user_ids -> product names (e.g. 'aarav_santos_2259' -> 'Garden Hose', d=0.667) and 7/40 product names -> user_ids ('Backpack' -> 'daiki_jackson_4362', d=0.500).

THE TWO DISTRIBUTIONS ARE SEPARABLE, which is what was missing before. Sampling 160 one-edit typos of real members across names/products/emails/user_ids, versus the cross-domain sets:
  typos that SHOULD apply:        max distance 0.200
  cross-domain that must NOT:     min distance 0.222
Sweep over both sets combined:
  threshold   typos applied   cross-domain applied
  0.15        152             0
  0.20        154             0
  0.30        154             30
  0.40        154             40
  0.50        154             42
  0.70        154             57   <- current default
So 0.2 keeps every typo and rejects every cross-domain match.

KNOWN COST, and the one judgement in this issue. Normalized distance is edits/length, so a one-edit typo on a SHORT value scores high and would be downgraded from applied to suggested at 0.2:
  'Ltd'  -> 'Ltx'  0.333    'IT'   -> 'Ix'   0.500
  'USD'  -> 'USx'  0.333    'high' -> 'higx' 0.250
  'medium', 'pending', 'Bicycle' and longer are unaffected (<= 0.167)
A realistic order-status enum (pending/processed/delivered/cancelled/exchange requested) is entirely unaffected. A 3-char enum like low/medium/high loses auto-correction on 'lox' and 'higx', which become 'did you mean high?' -- one extra turn, and arguably the right answer, since one edit on a 3-char code is genuinely ambiguous between legitimate codes.

The deeper observation, NOT proposed for this issue: no single normalized threshold can express 'is plausibly a typo' across all value lengths, because the metric conflates edits with length. An absolute edit-distance cap (<= 2 edits) would express it directly. That is a larger design change and should be its own issue if wanted.

FIX: change the auto_apply_threshold default from 0.7 to 0.2. The parameter already exists from fix-86c, so this is a one-line default change plus tests.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-20. auto_apply_threshold default changed 0.7 -> 0.2 in DatabaseValidator.fuzzy_match (utils/signatures.py). One-line default change; the parameter itself came from fix-86c.1.

The docstring now records WHY it is strict, the Batman figure, and the edits/length length-dependence, so the next person to loosen it sees the cost first.
