title: intent_detection fuzzy pre-match takes best_matched_commands[0] without handling ties
description:
At _workflows/command_metadata_extraction/intent_detection.py:114-120 the Levenshtein pre-match takes the first element of a list that find_best_matches explicitly documents as 'ALL entries tying for the minimum distance':

    best_matched_commands, _ = find_best_matches(
        command.replace(" ", "_"), command_name_dict.keys(), threshold=0.3)
    if best_matched_commands:
        command_name = best_matched_commands[0]

On a tie this picks by candidate order, which is dict insertion order over command names and plain utterances, and it then bypasses the classifier entirely. Compare DatabaseValidator.fuzzy_match, which treats a tie as ambiguity and returns suggestions.

LATENT, not currently biting, for two reasons: leading-window scoring makes exact ties uncommon, and fix-d28 measured this pre-match firing on 0 of 95 probe utterances. It becomes load-bearing the moment this call site moves to best_window=True, because under best-window EVERY candidate containing the input ties at exactly 0.0 -- so a fragment like 'product' would tie across every utterance containing it and route to whichever came first.

Guarded for now by test_bare_fragment_does_not_match_a_longer_utterance in tests/test_fuzzy_match.py, which pins this call site to leading-window behaviour. Anyone changing that test should fix the tie-break in the same change.

Fix direction: on len(best_matched_commands) > 1, fall through to the classifier rather than guessing, since the ambiguity machinery downstream already knows how to prompt.

Split out of fix-86c.
notes:
PRIORITY RAISED p3 -> p1 on measurement, 2026-08-20. The issue as filed said 'latent, not currently biting'. That was wrong: the tie is reachable TODAY with leading-window scoring and real command names, and the outcome is nondeterministic across processes.

MEASURED against the 15 real retail_workflow command names, at the call site's own 0.3 threshold:
  'modify_pending_order'  -> d=0.000, 3-way tie:
       modify_pending_order_address / modify_pending_order_items / modify_pending_order_payment
  'modify pending order'  -> same 3-way tie (a plain user utterance, not just agent output)
  'find_user_id'          -> d=0.000, 2-way tie:
       find_user_id_by_email / find_user_id_by_name_zip
Sibling commands sharing a prefix tie at EXACTLY 0.0 under leading-window truncation, because the shared prefix is all that gets compared. Prefix-sharing siblings are the normal shape of a generated command set, so this is not an edge case.

NONDETERMINISTIC. command_name_dict is built by iterating a SET of command names (intent_detection.py:58-73) and Python randomizes str hashing per process, so [0] is not stable. Eight fresh processes, identical input 'modify_pending_order':
  modify_pending_order_payment  x5
  modify_pending_order_items    x2
  modify_pending_order_address  x1
Three distinct outcomes for one input. The same turn can route differently between runs, which also means it cannot be reproduced from a transcript.

BLAST RADIUS is worse than the generic case: all three targets MUTATE, and they mutate different things (address / items / payment). The route bypasses BOTH the classifier (intent_detection.py:122-123 only consults it when command_name is unset) and the top-k ambiguity prompt, which is the mechanism that exists precisely to ask which of the three the user meant. Retail's three commands all have required parameters, so the immediate consequence is a parameter prompt for the WRONG command rather than a silent mutation -- the user asks to change a delivery address and is asked for a payment_method_id. A zero-required-parameter mutating command reachable this way would be a silent wrong write; unsurveyed.

Reachability confirmed by reading the path: tentative_command_name = command.split(' ')[0] ('modify') is not a command name, so the dict hit at :109 misses and control reaches the fuzzy branch at :114 with the full string.

FIX now has two parts, not one:
  a) INTENT_DETECTION: on len(best_matched_commands) > 1, leave command_name unset and let the classifier and its ambiguity prompt handle it. Clean, and the downstream machinery already exists.
  b) The clarification stages (INTENT_AMBIGUITY_CLARIFICATION / INTENT_MISUNDERSTANDING_CLARIFICATION) have NO classifier fallback -- fuzzy is the only mechanism -- so a tie there currently falls to 'what can i do?' at :156. Decide deliberately whether that is the wanted behaviour when a user's reply is ambiguous between two offered suggestions.
Sorting command_name_dict would make the pick deterministic without making it correct; determinism is the smaller half of this bug.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-20, INTENT_DETECTION half only. The clarification half remains open by design; see below.

intent_detection.py:112-131. When the fuzzy pre-match returns more than one candidate AND the stage is INTENT_DETECTION, the command name is left unset so the classifier and its top-k ambiguity prompt decide, and the discarded tie is logged at warning level. A unique match still short-circuits the classifier exactly as before.

Scoped to INTENT_DETECTION for a reason found while implementing: the clarification stages have no classifier to defer to, and their fall-through at :156 sets command_name = 'what can i do?', which is only a resolvable key at INTENT_AMBIGUITY_CLARIFICATION (where what_can_i_do's plain utterances are added to command_name_dict at :78-83). At INTENT_MISUNDERSTANDING_CLARIFICATION that literal is NOT in the dict -- only the short name 'what_can_i_do' is -- so routing ties into that fall-through would risk a KeyError in resolve_fully_qualified_command_name. Widening the guard is therefore not a one-line change and needs the clarification-stage decision made first.

TESTS: tests/test_intent_detection_fuzzy_tie.py, 8 cases, real RoutingDefinition + real predict path with only the classifier result injected (the seam test_wildcard_escalation.py established).
- test_prefix_sharing_commands_tie_at_distance_zero / _from_a_spaced_utterance: the precondition, on tests/todo_list_workflow's real add_child_todoitem / add_child_todolist pair.
- test_tie_defers_to_the_classifier_rather_than_picking_one: classifier confident about a THIRD command wins, proving the tie no longer commits.
- test_tie_reaches_the_ambiguity_prompt_when_the_classifier_is_unsure: the prompt is restored.
- test_tie_is_logged: the previously invisible discard is now visible.
- test_unique_fuzzy_match_still_routes_without_the_classifier / test_exact_command_name_still_routes: positive controls proving the guard did not disarm the pre-match.
- test_clarification_stage_tie_still_resolves_to_one_of_the_tied_commands: pins the OPEN half at INTENT_MISUNDERSTANDING_CLARIFICATION so the remaining decision is made on purpose. This is the test to change when it is decided.

Reaching the clarification stages in a test needs cme_workflow.context['command'] set and a None modelpipeline, because those stages write to the clarification cache and store_utterance_cache only embeds when the pipeline is not None.

Targeted runs green: the 8 new cases, plus test_wildcard_escalation / test_you_misunderstood_command / test_workitem / test_fuzzy_match / test_workflow_serialization_hooks = 173 passed. Full suite running.
QUALITY GATE: full suite green. 1846 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed in 3003.37s (50:03), 2026-08-20. Covers all four changes in this batch (fix-0xn tie guard, fix-11r auto_apply default, fix-63k difflib default, fix-07b docs). Previous run on this tree was 1825 passed; the 21-test increase is the new tie-guard and default-threshold cases.

title: find_best_matches scores the leading window only, so a contained candidate loses to an unrelated one
description:
find_best_matches truncates each candidate to len(input) before measuring distance (utils/fuzzy_match.py:46-51), so a candidate matching anywhere other than the START is scored as though it did not match at all, and can lose to an unrelated candidate sharing leading characters.

Measured for 'Garrison' against ['Aaron Garrison', 'Barry Jones']:
  Aaron Garrison  compared as 'aarongar'  distance 0.750
  Barry Jones     compared as 'barryjon'  distance 0.375  <- unique minimum, under 0.7

so fuzzy_match returns (True, 'Barry Jones', []) and validate_parameters applies it with setattr (signatures.py:636-637). Nothing is reported to the caller or the user: the command runs against a value the user never supplied and the response looks like a normal success. Same mechanism turned 'Ltd' and 'e Ltd I' into 'IT Division' on the IDO dataset.

FIX: score against the best window rather than the leading one. Preserves the partial-input behaviour the truncation was added for (Fred -> Fred Flintstone). Measured over the IDO catalogues: wrong answers 56 -> 0, unharmed fragments 457 -> 545, one-edit typo recall unchanged at 577/577. Ambiguous barely moves (588 -> 556), which is the intended outcome — a fragment that legitimately matches several candidates SHOULD come back as suggestions.

*** MUST BE OPT-IN, NOT A GLOBAL CHANGE TO THE HELPER ***
find_best_matches has a second consumer at _workflows/command_metadata_extraction/intent_detection.py:114 (threshold 0.3), on the routing hot path. Best-window scoring can only LOWER distances, so at a fixed threshold it admits strictly more matches; that call site bypasses the classifier entirely when it fires and takes best_matched_commands[0] without handling ties, while under best-window every candidate CONTAINING the input ties at exactly 0.0.

Measured out-of-tree with the fix applied, against representative command names and seed utterances at that site's 0.3 threshold — new matches that do not exist today:
  'product' -> 'list all the product types you carry'
  'types'   -> 'list all the product types you carry'
  'shipped' -> 'cancel the order that has not shipped yet'

Bare fragments would start hijacking routing ahead of the classifier. fix-d28 records that this pre-match fired on 0 of 95 probe utterances, i.e. it is near-dead today, and nothing in tests/ covers it — so a global change would likely pass the full suite while silently altering routing. Add best_window as an opt-in flag (or a separate function) and have DatabaseValidator opt in; leave intent detection on today's semantics and pin it with a test.

ALSO IN SCOPE: log the substitution. signatures.py:636-637 rewrites the parameter with no record; a logger.info when corrected_value != field_value makes this class of bug diagnosable from a trace instead of from a reproduction script.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-20.

utils/fuzzy_match.py
- Added best_window_distance(normalized_input, normalized_candidate): smallest normalized distance between the input and any equal-length window of the candidate.
- find_best_matches gained best_window: bool = False. Default (leading-window) behaviour is byte-for-byte unchanged, so intent_detection.py:114 is untouched. Docstring records WHY it is opt-in: best-window can only lower distances, so it admits strictly more matches at a fixed threshold, and callers that route on the first match rather than treating ties as ambiguity depend on the narrower behaviour.

utils/signatures.py
- DatabaseValidator.fuzzy_match now calls find_best_matches with best_window=True.
- The silent-substitution path logs when it changes a value: 'db_lookup substituted <command>.<field>: <old> -> <new>' at logger.info, guarded on corrected_value != field_value.

VERIFIED against the patched tree:
  fuzzy_match('Garrison', ['Aaron Garrison', 'Barry Jones']) -> (True, 'Aaron Garrison', [])   was (True, 'Barry Jones', [])
  fuzzy_match('Ltd', ['IT Division', 'Acme Ltd'])            -> (True, 'Acme Ltd', [])         was 'IT Division'
Intent-detection call site re-probed at its 0.3 threshold: 'product', 'types', 'shipped' still match nothing; 'add' and 'list' match exactly what they matched before.

TESTS: tests/test_fuzzy_match.py, 29 cases. Includes test_bare_fragment_does_not_match_a_longer_utterance, which pins the intent-detection pre-match so a future refactor cannot quietly flip it to best-window, and test_never_exceeds_leading_window_distance, which asserts the monotonicity property the opt-in decision rests on. Existing consumers re-run green: test_workitem.py + test_workflow_serialization_hooks.py + test_param_example_cache.py, 166 passed.

title: R6+R7+R8+R9: Lazy topic/summary fill — call site off the turn's critical path, status gating, and refresh policy
description:
The lazy-fill policy from gh-65, with four corrections. Blocked on fix-dzs.3
(blank sentinel must be reliable), fix-dzs.4 (the call must be bounded), and
fix-dzs.5 (there must be something worth summarizing).

R7 — THE CALL SITE PUTS THE LLM BACK IN THE DRAIN WINDOW. gh-65 implementation
note 3 says to call the helper "after incremental persist of a completed chat
turn, still under runtime.lock". That location is inside _run_turn, before DONE:

    turns.py:487-491
        # Persist BEFORE DONE so a poller never sees "done" with unsaved state.
        save_conversation_incremental(...)
        _persist_after_turn(...)
    turns.py:511
        execn.exec_state = ExecState.DONE

While that runs the channel is still in busy_channel_ids(), so
wait_for_active_turns_to_complete waits on topic generation — the LLM call lands
in the exact 30 s window this epic exists to protect. It also adds the full LLM
latency to a user-facing turn (200 or 202), and widens the window in which a
concurrent request on that channel gets 409 from _reject_if_busy. Put the generate
AFTER exec_state=DONE and outside the turn's critical path.

R8 — "COMPLETED CHAT TURN" IS NOT DISTINGUISHABLE THERE. _run_turn persists
unconditionally after work_fn returns, including when the result is
AWAITING_USER (the lock is released on suspension, but persistence has already
happened). So an ask_user clarification would trigger generation on a
half-finished exchange, and under "generate once, never refresh" that title is
permanent. Gate on TurnStatus explicitly — see _is_awaiting_user_output
(utils.py:616-627) and _build_turn_result (workflow_execution_context.py:796-834)
for the authoritative signal. Also honor gh-65's kind gating: invoke_agent,
invoke_agent_stream, invoke_assistant yes; perform_action and
initialize_startup no.

R6 — GENERATING AT TURN 1 AND NEVER REFRESHING CONTRADICTS A DOCUMENTED
INVARIANT. _conversation_turns_for_summary (__main__.py:313-320) exists
specifically so summarization reads the whole durable conversation rather than the
20-turn memory window, because summarizing the window "would silently produce
'topic of the last N turns'". Generating on the first chat turn and never
refreshing produces "topic of the FIRST turn" — permanently, for a 40-turn thread.
Same class of error, reached from the other end. Today's shutdown/rotate labeling
at least sees the whole conversation.
  Resolve with one of: (a) defer the first generation to turn 2 or 3; (b) refresh
under a cheap policy, e.g. when appended_turn_count has doubled since the label
was written, which needs one extra field on the conv record and no extra reads;
(c) refresh on rotate and activate only. Pick one and record why. Note (b) costs
LLM calls on long threads — weigh against guiding principle 2.

R9 — THE CONCURRENCY MODEL IS MIS-DESCRIBED, AND THE GUARANTEE IS SMALLER THAN
CLAIMED. gh-65 says the runtime lock is what prevents activate and a first chat
from double-generating. The actual guard on /new_conversation and
/activate_conversation is _reject_if_busy, whose docstring is explicit that the
lock is NOT a busy signal:

    __main__.py:851-857
        Keyed off the registry active-execution pointer (NOT runtime.lock.locked()):
        the lock is released while a request defers and across AWAITING_USER, so it
        is not a reliable "busy" signal.

So gh-65's test "concurrent activate + first chat: exactly one generate" will
usually observe a 409 instead, and should be written to accept that. A lock-scoped
check-and-set is still correct for the blank->set transition, but runtime.lock is
an asyncio.Lock (utils.py:1300) and is therefore in-process only. Per the ratified
single-writer-per-channel invariant (R27 of the TurnResult review,
docs/turn_result_design_review.md:1272-1285), two pods serving one channel can
both generate. State the guarantee as "exactly one generate per writer", and do
not document it as an absolute.

SCOPE. The ensure_topic_and_summary helper as gh-65 describes it, plus:
- call site after DONE, not before;
- TurnStatus and kind gating;
- a decided refresh policy;
- check-and-set under runtime.lock, with the scope documented honestly.
Keep /new_conversation's existing force behavior routed through the same helper.

ACCEPTANCE (adapted from gh-65's list, with the corrections above).
- Initialize-only x N then shutdown: zero topic-gen LM calls.
- Initialize then invoke_agent: one generate, AFTER the turn reaches DONE, and the
  turn's own latency is not extended by it.
- Bounce then same channel_id invoke_agent: generate once on that first chat turn.
- Bounce then POST /activate_conversation: generate once from stored turns.
- A turn that suspends at ask_user does NOT trigger generation.
- /perform_action does not trigger generation.
- Concurrent activate and first chat: at most one generate; a 409 is an acceptable
  outcome for one of them.
- Generate timeout or failure: the chat turn and the activate still return 200 and
  the topic remains blank (retryable, per fix-dzs.3).
- A channel whose turn is still running at SIGTERM is not held open by topic
  generation.
close_reason: Lazy fill shipped. Helper ensure_topic_and_summary/try_ensure_topic_and_summary in utils.py (turns.py already imports it; generate injected so each caller's test seam stays local). R7: hook runs as the last act of the turn's own task, after DONE/clear_active/done_event - verified by moving it to the issue's location and watching 3 tests fail. Eviction race resolved by touching only the durable store (retirement closes execution_context only), not by pinning the runtime, so drain and safety are both satisfied. Both _run_turn and run_owned_turn hooked. R8: allow-lists - kinds invoke_agent/invoke_agent_stream/invoke_assistant, statuses COMPLETED/FAILED, so AWAITING_USER and future statuses opt out. R6: unbounded geometric refresh at turn counts 1,4,16,64 (no new store field), O(log n) calls; blank-retry deliberately not milestone-gated. R9: new per-channel label_lock, guarantee documented as at-most-one-per-writer with the multi-pod limit stated on the lock. 12 new tests in test_conversation_lazy_labeling.py; 175 pass across the affected suites.

title: R1: 'conversation summary' is a constant literal on the deterministic and action paths, so there is nothing to summarize or preview
description:
THE BLOCKER OF THIS EPIC. Both gh-65's preview field and its lazy-labeling policy
assume every turn's "conversation summary" carries meaningful text. On two of the
three paths it carries a hardcoded constant, and the motivating workload uses
exactly those two.

EVIDENCE. Only the agent path puts real text in the field:

    workflow_execution_context.py:696-703  (summarize_and_record_turn)
        conversation_summary = message                  # raw user text, or
        ... = self._extract_conversation_summary(...)   # LLM extraction if actions

The other two hardcode it:

    workflow_execution_context.py:1212-1214  (_process_message, assistant mode)
        self.append_conversation_turn("assistant_mode_command", json.dumps(record))
    workflow_execution_context.py:1276-1278  (_process_action, perform_action)
        self.append_conversation_turn("process_action command", json.dumps(record))

/initialize routes through precisely those: _run_startup_sync (utils.py:340-353)
calls ctx.process_action_turn(startup_action) or ctx.process_turn("/" + command),
and the "/" prefix forces deterministic mode. So for the talk_to_ido
unique-channel /initialize workload, turn 0's "conversation summary" is the string
"process_action command".

CONSEQUENCE 1 — gh-65's preview design is dead on arrival. The issue states "for
initialize it tends to be the English defect summary; for chat, the user-visible
turn text". The second half is true (agent path). The first half is false. A
picker built on turn 0's "conversation summary" renders the identical constant for
every initialize-only conversation.

CONSEQUENCE 2 — and this is the strongest argument FOR gh-65's main proposal,
which the issue never makes. generate_topic_and_summary reads ONLY that field
(conversation_store.py:456-461). So those 50 shutdown LLM calls in the 3.0.1 soak
were not "paying for a title on a transcript nobody will open" — they were paying
an LLM to title the constant string "process_action command". There is zero
information in the input. The same applies to generating on
/activate_conversation for an initialize-only channel, which gh-65 proposes to
add.

WHAT IS ACTUALLY AVAILABLE. conversation_traces on those paths holds
json.dumps({"command", "command_name", "parameters", "response"}) — a structured
record. gh-65 says there is "no separate raw-command field on the durable turn",
which is true of the top-level keys (extract_turns_from_history keeps only
"conversation summary", "conversation_traces", "feedback") but misses that the
command IS in traces. command_name plus a truncated response would make both a
usable preview and a summarizable input. The 450 KB defect XML is in
parameters inside that same blob, so anything reading it must project, not
hydrate.

SCOPE. Decide and implement what "conversation summary" should hold on the
deterministic and action paths. Minimal candidate: the command name plus the
response text, truncated, built from the same record already being serialized into
traces — no new data, no extra store reads, no LLM. Keep the agent path unchanged.

CONSTRAINTS (guiding principles 1 and 2).
- This field is written on every turn of every path, so the change must be O(1)
  and allocation-cheap; do not add an LLM call or a store read here.
- The field is also read by _refine_user_query (workflow_execution_context.py:1291,
  last 5 turns) and is fed to the intent/agent path as history. Changing its
  content changes what the model sees. Check that before choosing a format — this
  is not a display-only field.
- Existing stored turns keep the old constants. Any consumer must tolerate both.

ACCEPTANCE.
- An /initialize-only conversation's turn 0 has a "conversation summary" that
  identifies what ran.
- generate_topic_and_summary given that turn produces a title a human would
  recognize.
- _refine_user_query behavior with the new content is checked, not assumed.
close_reason: conversation summary now names the turn on both deterministic and action paths (message/command_name -> response, each half sliced to 200 chars and newline-collapsed, <=404 total), so a 450 KB payload can never reach the field. conversation_traces unchanged. 8 tests in new tests/test_conversation_turn_summary_content.py.

title: R3: Bound topic generation at the LLM client — asyncio.wait_for cannot stop the executor thread and exit can block 300s
description:
CORRECTS gh-65 implementation note 4, which says "Executor + timeout on remaining
generate sites. Do not call DSPy sync on the event loop. Per-call timeout (e.g.
2-5s)." Moving the call to an executor is right. The timeout, as specified, does
not bound anything that matters.

MECHANISM. asyncio.wait_for around loop.run_in_executor(None, ...) cancels the
AWAIT, not the thread. The blocking litellm call keeps running in the default
ThreadPoolExecutor. On loop close, asyncio.Runner.close does:

    loop.run_until_complete(loop.shutdown_default_executor(constants.THREAD_JOIN_TIMEOUT))

VERIFIED IN THIS ENVIRONMENT (2026-08-13):

    python 3.13.14
    THREAD_JOIN_TIMEOUT 300

So a design intended to bound shutdown to the 30 s drain can block process exit
for up to five minutes waiting on an orphaned LLM thread — strictly worse than
today's in-loop sequential call, and a direct regression of the goal in gh-65's
motivation section. The same trap applies to any future "timeout" placed on the
generate sites; note that the repo already uses the DEFAULT executor everywhere
(turns.py:475, __main__.py:444), so there is no isolated pool to abandon.

SCOPE. Bound the work, not the wait. In order of preference:
1. Pass an explicit client-side timeout to the LLM call itself, so the thread
   returns on its own. get_lm("LLM_CONVERSATION_STORE", ...) is the seam
   (conversation_store.py:464); check what litellm/DSPy timeout knob is reachable
   through it and whether a per-role default belongs in fastworkflow.env alongside
   the model strings.
2. If (1) is not reachable, use a DEDICATED executor for topic generation that can
   be shut down with wait=False, so an orphaned thread cannot hold the interpreter.
   Do not put this work on the default executor, which turn execution shares.
3. Only then add asyncio.wait_for on top, as a response deadline for the caller.

APPLIES TO EVERY REMAINING GENERATE SITE, which after fix-dzs.1 is
/new_conversation today (__main__.py:1519 — currently a sync DSPy call made while
holding runtime.lock, inside an async endpoint) plus whatever the lazy-fill work
adds.

RELATED DECISION TO MAKE EXPLICIT (gh-65 raises it and leaves it open):
/new_conversation currently fails the rotate with HTTP 500 if generation fails.
Decide and record whether rotate stays strict. Recommendation: keep it strict —
rotate is an explicit user action and a silently unlabeled archived thread is
worse than an error — but with a bounded timeout it now fails fast instead of
hanging.

ACCEPTANCE.
- A generation that hangs cannot extend process exit beyond its own bounded
  timeout plus the drain.
- No topic-generation work runs on the default executor, or if it does, it is
  bounded at the client.
- The chosen timeout value is recorded with its reasoning, not just a magic
  number.
close_reason: Bounded at the client, not the await: generate_topic_and_summary passes timeout (new LLM_CONVERSATION_STORE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, default 12s) and num_retries=1 into dspy.LM, verified reaching dspy's litellm boundary. Worst case ~25s fits inside the 30s drain, asserted by test. /new_conversation now awaits it in an executor (253k concurrent-coroutine turns vs 1-3 on-loop) and stays strict with an actionable 500. 9 tests in new test_conversation_topic_generation_bounds.py.

title: R4: An empty generated topic is stored as ' 1', poisoning the blank sentinel the lazy design depends on
description:
BLOCKS the lazy-fill policy (R6+R7+R8+R9), because that design makes topic == ""
mean "needs generation" and writes exactly once.

MECHANISM. If generate_topic_and_summary returns an empty topic — a DSPy
JSONAdapter partial parse, a truncated completion, or a model that simply emits
nothing for that field — the empty candidate is fed to _ensure_unique_topic, which
finds it colliding with every unlabeled conversation's blank topic and appends a
suffix to it.

VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY (2026-08-13, v3.0.1, real store): with two blank-topic
conversations present,

    update_conversation_topic_summary(1, "", "some summary")
    -> stored topic is ' 1'      (a space and a one)

CONSEQUENCE. ' 1' is not blank. Under "generate once, blank -> written", that
conversation is now permanently considered labeled and will never be retried, and
a picker renders ' 1' as its title. gh-65 is careful to redefine what a blank
topic means ("no successful LLM title yet") but never notices that its own store
can leave a third state that is neither a real title nor the retry sentinel.

SCOPE. Two changes, both small:
1. Refuse to write an empty or whitespace-only topic. Treat it as a failed
   generation: leave the record blank, log at WARNING once, and let the next
   eligible trigger retry. Decide whether the summary should still be written when
   the topic is empty (probably yes — a summary with no title is still useful and
   the blank topic keeps the retry).
2. Guard _ensure_unique_topic against an empty candidate regardless, so no future
   caller can reintroduce this.

DESIGN QUESTION TO RESOLVE HERE, not later. Is "blank" a sufficient state, or does
this need an explicit attempted/failed marker? Blank-means-retry is fine for the
lazy triggers (a chat turn or an activate will come around again) but it gives no
way to stop retrying a conversation whose content the model cannot title, and no
way to distinguish "never tried" from "tried and failed" in
/admin/dump_all_conversations. Recommendation: keep blank-means-retry for v1 (it is
the minimal change) and record the limitation, since the triggers are
user-initiated and therefore self-limiting.

ACCEPTANCE.
- A generation returning "" or "   " leaves the stored topic exactly "".
- The conversation is retried on the next eligible trigger.
- No stored topic is ever a bare numeric suffix.
- Test drives the real store with an empty topic, per the integration-tests-only
  rule.
close_reason: update_conversation_topic_summary declines to write a blank topic (one WARNING, summary and updated_at still written); _ensure_unique_topic returns '' for any blank candidate before scanning, so no caller can reintroduce the ' 1' suffix. Declining to write rather than assigning '' also protects an already-labeled conversation from a failed refresh. Blank-means-retry kept; limitation recorded in docstring. 7 tests appended to test_conversation_topic_labeling.py.

title: R5: _ensure_unique_topic collides a conversation with itself, corrupting the topic on refresh
description:
PRE-EXISTING BUG, reachable on main today, independent of the rest of this epic.
Small self-contained fix in conversation_store.py.

MECHANISM. _ensure_unique_topic (conversation_store.py:124-145) scans conv:1
through conv:last_conversation_id and collects every stored topic, INCLUDING the
record about to be updated. update_conversation_topic_summary (:255-278) reads the
record, then calls _ensure_unique_topic before writing, so the old topic of the
very conversation being updated is in the collision set. Regenerating an unchanged
topic therefore collides with itself and gets a numeric suffix.

VERIFIED EMPIRICALLY (2026-08-13, v3.0.1, real store, no mocks):

    first write        -> 'Order Status Question'
    idempotent refresh -> 'Order Status Question 1'
    refresh again      -> 'Order Status Question'

It oscillates. Every refresh either adds or removes the suffix.

REACHABLE TODAY. POST /activate_conversation on an already-labeled conversation,
then POST /new_conversation. new_conversation (__main__.py:1517-1526) generates for
the active conversation and calls update_conversation_topic_summary on it. If the
LLM returns the same topic it returned last time — which for a conversation whose
content has not changed is the likely case — the stored topic is corrupted.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE AFTER THIS EPIC. gh-65's helper keeps force=True for
/new_conversation and adds a generate on /activate_conversation, which makes the
activate-then-rotate sequence more common, not less.

SCOPE. Exclude the conversation being updated from the collision scan. Options:
pass conv_id into _ensure_unique_topic and skip i == conv_id, or short-circuit
when the candidate equals the record's current topic. Prefer the former: it also
fixes save_conversation's reuse of the same helper if a conversation_id is passed
explicitly.

PERFORMANCE NOTE (guiding principle 2). _ensure_unique_topic is O(number of
conversations for the channel) SQLite reads per topic write. That cost is on the
shutdown/rotate path today. Any lazy-fill design moves it onto a user-facing
request, so do not make it worse here; excluding one id does not change the
complexity, but this is the place to note the ceiling if a channel ever
accumulates thousands of conversations.

ACCEPTANCE.
- Writing the same topic twice to the same conversation is idempotent: no suffix
  appears and none disappears.
- A genuine collision with a DIFFERENT conversation still gets suffixed (do not
  regress the feature the helper exists for).
- Regression test written against the real store, per the repo's
  integration-tests-only rule.
close_reason: _ensure_unique_topic takes exclude_conversation_id, passed from update_conversation_topic_summary and save_conversation; rewriting a conversation's own topic is now idempotent instead of oscillating. 9 integration tests in new tests/test_conversation_topic_labeling.py.

title: Conversation topic/summary lifecycle: bound shutdown and fill labels lazily (gh-65, R1-R12)
description:
Adversarial review of https://github.com/radiantlogicinc/fastworkflow/issues/65
("Defer conversation topic/summary generation off process shutdown"), verified
against the working tree at v3.0.1, commit caf2e45. Findings are numbered R1-R12
and each is one child of this epic, in the style of fix-vof.

VERDICT. The proposal's direction is correct: process shutdown must not call
LLM_CONVERSATION_STORE. But the issue understates its own case, one of its
designs rests on a false premise about the data, its timeout mechanism cannot do
what it claims, and three of its policy choices reintroduce the cost they were
meant to remove.

WHAT THE ISSUE GETS RIGHT (verified, no action needed): DEFAULT_MAX_LIVE_SESSIONS
= 50 (utils.py:43); the 30 s drain (__main__.py:540); no per-call timeout or
overall budget in finalize_conversations_on_shutdown (:407-429); a sync DSPy call
made from an async shutdown function (:418); busy channels skipped; turns
persisted before exec_state=DONE (turns.py:487-491); blank topic/summary
placeholders (conversation_store.py:309-310, 351-352); /activate_conversation
does not generate; GET /conversations is LLM-free; bounce restore works via
_create_user_runtime plus checkpoint (utils.py:516-527, 583-587).

TWO SUPPORTING FACTS THE ISSUE DOES NOT CITE, both of which strengthen it.

1. Shutdown labeling is already LRU roulette, not a contract being removed. In
the soak's shape (600 unique channel_ids, max_live_sessions=50), ~550 sessions
were retired mid-run by _retire_one_candidate (utils.py:1227-1271), which
checkpoints, pops and closes with no topic generation anywhere. So ~92% of those
conversations were already never labeled, and which <=50 get a title is decided
by LRU residency at SIGTERM. That is a much stronger compatibility argument than
"clients already did not get this under SIGKILL".

2. The test suite already works around the shutdown LLM call in three places and
nothing asserts it. tests/test_manager_shutdown_matrix.py:292-297 tears down
every session before exiting the lifespan because "generate_topic_and_summary is
a live LLM call", and :480-482 clears conversation history mid-test for the same
reason. The two tests that call steps.finalize assert only on closing and
logging. So removing the pass breaks no existing test and lets those workarounds
go.

TIERING (guiding principle 3). Children carry the label must-have or
nice-to-have.

MUST-HAVE, in dependency order:
  R2+R11  bound shutdown: checkpoint before labeling, drop the LLM pass, keep
          the durable-save fallback. This alone captures most of the value and
          is the smallest diff in the epic.
  R5      _ensure_unique_topic collides a conversation with itself on refresh.
  R4      an empty generated topic is stored as ' 1', poisoning the blank
          sentinel the whole lazy design depends on.
  R3      bound the LLM call at its client; asyncio.wait_for cannot.
  R1      conversation summary is a constant literal on the deterministic and
          action paths, so for the motivating workload there is nothing to
          summarize and nothing to preview. Blocks the lazy-fill policy and the
          preview field.
  R6+R7+R8+R9  the lazy-fill policy itself: call site, turn-kind and status
          gating, refresh policy, and the real scope of the dedupe guarantee.

NICE-TO-HAVE:
  R10     preview on ConversationSummary, denormalized at write time.
  R13     /activate_conversation and cold session create hydrate whole
          conversations before windowing (adjacent memory defect).
  R12     ensure_topic_and_summary spec gaps.

GUIDING PRINCIPLES FOR EVERY CHILD (from the developer, 2026-08-13):
1. Keep code changes modular and minimal. Prefer the smallest edit at the right
   chokepoint over a redesign; do not bundle findings.
2. Keep performance, latency, memory consumption and reliability in mind always.
   At 450 KB turn payloads every extra read of a turn record is measurable, and
   any work added to a turn's critical path is user-visible latency.
3. Must-have fixes ship before nice-to-have enhancements.
close_reason:
All eleven review findings of GitHub issue #65 resolved: ten fixed, one (fix-dzs.7 preview) closed won't-do-now with its research preserved in that issue's notes.

WHAT SHIPPED. Process shutdown no longer calls LLM_CONVERSATION_STORE at all; it makes unsaved turns durable through the same save_conversation_incremental chokepoint and leaves blank placeholders. Labels are filled lazily instead: on the first completed chat turn (after the turn reaches DONE, off its critical path and out of the shutdown drain), on activate, and on rotate, refreshed geometrically at turn counts 1, 4, 16, 64 so a long thread costs O(log n) calls rather than one or n. Generation is bounded at the LLM client (LLM_CONVERSATION_STORE_TIMEOUT_SECONDS, default 12s, num_retries pinned to 1) because asyncio.wait_for bounds the wait and not the thread, and Python 3.13 then joins default-executor threads for up to 300s at exit. 'conversation summary' now carries real content on all three paths - it was a hardcoded constant on the deterministic and action paths, which is why topic generation had nothing to work with. The blank-topic sentinel is sound: an empty generated topic used to be stored as ' 1' and count as labeled forever. Two pre-existing store defects fixed along the way (topic self-collision, oscillating on every refresh; update_conversation carrying the same defect). The restore paths no longer hydrate whole conversations to keep the newest 20 turns. Streaming EOF no longer waits on the label, which matters because invoke_agent - the MCP-exposed tool - is the streaming endpoint.

THREE CORRECTIONS TO THE ORIGINAL GITHUB ISSUE, all verified against code: its preview design rested on a field that was a constant literal; its per-call timeout could not bound the process; and its call site would have put the LLM call back inside the 30s drain it was written to protect. The issue also understated its own case - shutdown labeling was already LRU roulette (~92% of conversations in the motivating soak were evicted and never labeled), and the real harm was that up to 50 untimed LLM calls sat in front of the load-bearing checkpoint write.

EVIDENCE. 188 tests pass across the affected suites, 37 new across 5 new files. Four fixes were verified by falsification - reverting the fix and confirming the intended test fails and nothing else: the shutdown call count, the windowed read (20 turn reads vs 100, identical turns returned), persist-then-label (500 with ValueError), and streaming EOF.

description:

title: Migrate cache_matching to float32 BLOB utterance_cache schema
description:
Design §4 Step 3 — MUST NOT be a mechanical KVStore/JSON swap (measured 3–6x regression).

Own table:
  CREATE TABLE utterance_cache (
    k TEXT PRIMARY KEY,
    meta TEXT NOT NULL,  -- JSON: command_mapping, feedback dates
    vec BLOB NOT NULL    -- numpy float32 embedding .tobytes()
  );
Write: np.asarray(embedding, dtype=np.float32).tobytes()
Read: np.frombuffer(vec, dtype=np.float32)

One row per utterance (no whole-cache blob rewrite). Perf gate: 1000 utterances match+store cycle << 238ms speedict baseline (target ~1.8ms).

title: Add fastworkflow/kvstore.py (SQLite WAL JSON KVStore)
description:
Implement KVStore in fastworkflow/kvstore.py per design §3.

API: __setitem__, __getitem__, __delitem__, __contains__, get, keys, close, context manager.
Values JSON-serialisable only. PRAGMA journal_mode=WAL, synchronous=NORMAL, busy_timeout.
check_same_thread=False (sqlite3.threadsafety==3).
keys() must materialise via fetchall() before iterating (conversation_store mutates while iterating).
__delitem__ raises KeyError on missing key (dict semantics).

No callers yet — pure additive.

title: Replace speedict with stdlib sqlite3
description:
Replace abandoned speedict/RocksDB with stdlib sqlite3 (WAL). Unblocks Python 3.13+ installs, removes pickle RCE surface, and fixes process-exclusive lock concurrency failures.

Design of record: /home/drawal/rl/fastworkflow-speedict-to-sqlite-migration.md (analysed against fastworkflow 2.30.1, 2026-08-08).

Decision: go straight to sqlite3 — do NOT route through rocksdict or sqlitedict. No data migration; abandon existing .rdb stores.

Why: speedict has no 3.13 wheel and no sdist; upstream abandoned (Speedb acquired by Redis); pickle on disk; RocksDB exclusive LOCK fails/hangs under multi-process.

Scope modules: workflow.py (enablecache), intent_detection.py, cache_matching.py (BLOB schema required), conversation_store.py. New module: fastworkflow/kvstore.py.

Acceptance: pip install works on 3.11–3.14; no pickle markers on disk; 4-process ConversationStore concurrency succeeds; cache_matching match+store @1000 utterances << 238ms baseline; speedict removed from pyproject; requires-python widened to at least <3.15.

- No speedict import or dependency remains
- requires-python allows 3.13 (and preferably 3.14)
- KVStore (JSON) used for enablecache, intent_detection, conversation_store
- cache_matching uses float32 BLOB + JSON meta schema (not all-JSON)
- Verification checklist in design doc §6 passes
- Release notes mention abandoned .rdb files and downstream shim deletion
notes:
Landed: kvstore.py (KVStore + UtteranceCacheStore), all four call sites migrated, speedict removed, requires-python >=3.11,<3.15.

- Follow-up issue fix-snl for enablecache key collision

title: Apply PR #56: context-aware command visibility (with review fixes)
description:
Apply https://github.com/radiantlogicinc/fastworkflow/pull/56 locally onto current main, incorporating Sourcery review feedback, then verify.

## PR summary
Two related fixes that make the command lists shown to the agent and the planner context-aware:
- Executor: re-scope the ReAct agent's available_commands to the current context whenever it changes (set_current_*, go_up, reset_context) via a context-change observer on the Workflow, so the agent never acts on a stale command list after a mid-trajectory switch.
- Planner: build_query_with_next_steps now uses get_all_contexts_command_display_text so the planner sees every available context's commands.

## Files changed in PR
- fastworkflow/command_metadata_api.py (+67)
- fastworkflow/utils/react.py (+5)
- fastworkflow/workflow.py (+19)
- fastworkflow/workflow_agent.py (+15/-1)
- fastworkflow/workflow_execution_context.py (+10)

Head commit: 8937222895e12206ac4526365bad580ff0666cdb
Branch: sanchit056:agentic_enhancements_v2

## REQUIRED review fixes (must apply, not just cherry-pick)
1. Context-change listeners on Workflow: add remove/unsubscribe API and/or weakrefs so short-lived workflows/agents do not leak via long-lived listener lists that only append.
2. In _notify_context_change: log with exc_info=True (or full traceback), not just `{exc}`, while still never breaking context switching.
3. In command_metadata_api.py get_all_contexts_command_display_text fallback except: log warning with exc_info=True before returning base_text; use existing module logger conventions (import logging / getLogger if needed).

## Acceptance
- PR changes applied and review comments addressed
- Targeted tests for this PR's behavior (context-aware command visibility / listener refresh / planner all-contexts display)
- Full pytest regression suite green (do NOT run two full suites at once; suite ~24 min; activate .venv)
- Close this bead and export: bd export -o .beads/issues.jsonl
- Do NOT commit/push unless asked

## Notes
- Local remote: origin=dharrawal/fastworkflow, upstream=radiantlogicinc/fastworkflow
- Use mgrep for searches, not Grep/WebSearch
- Conservative beads profile: no commit/push without approval

title: Direct actions run validate_extracted_parameters
description:
Direct actions (CommandExecutor.perform_action and every caller: /perform_action, /initialize startup_action, MCP tool calls, ChatSession Action) silently skip Signature.validate_extracted_parameters because they construct InputForParamExtraction with the bare constructor instead of create(). The NLU path uses create() and runs the hook.

Design of record: docs/fastworkflow_direct_action_validation.md (re-verified on 2.29.2).

Fix: use InputForParamExtraction.create() in perform_action and always call validate_parameters (including when action.parameters is empty/falsy). Keep ValueError failure shape for this release; structured TurnOutput rejection is a follow-up.

Ship as minor 2.30.0 — behaviour change for callers that relied on the gap.
acceptance_criteria:
- perform_action resolves INPUT_FOR_PARAM_EXTRACTION_CLASS and runs validate_extracted_parameters
- Empty/absent parameters still run the hook
- Regression tests prove direct-action and create() paths agree on the hook message
- Full pytest suite green
- Doc updated from Not fixed to Fixed
- Version bumped to 2.30.0
notes: All children closed. Ship: perform_action uses InputForParamExtraction.create() and always validates; regression tests in tests/test_direct_action_validation.py; doc marked Fixed; version 2.30.0. Full suite 1696 passed / 14 skipped / 0 failed. Failure-shape (ValueError→500 vs structured TurnOutput) deferred as follow-up, not in this epic.
close_reason: Closed
