title: R5: selective training of a command, context, or subtree, with upward closure
description:
Adds `fastworkflow train <workflow> [--command C] [--context X] [--changed-only]`.

THE NON-OBVIOUS PART (spec R5, decision D5): retraining a single command is NOT local. "Only this command changed" is never only one context.
- A context's classifier must be retrained if ANY of its own commands changed.
- A context must ALSO be retrained if any of its ANCESTORS' commands changed, because those utterances form its `wildcard` class (F6). This is the dependency that makes naive per-command retraining silently desync wildcard classes across the hierarchy.
- Contexts that inherit a changed command through the `base` axis must be retrained.
- --changed-only computes the dirty set from command-file fingerprints plus the R6 utterance cache, then CLOSES IT UPWARDS over the hierarchy.
- The output must STATE which contexts were retrained and which were carried forward, so the developer can see the closure that was computed rather than trusting it.

DEPENDS ON: R6 (fingerprints for --changed-only) and R4 (D8 — merging new per-command work into a live artifact set with no rollback is the same hazard class as F5).

CONTEXT MODEL: the inheritance semantics here are load-bearing and already specified elsewhere — consult the fastworkflow-architecture-contract skill on context_inheritance_model.json / the context hierarchy before deriving the closure rule from scratch.
notes:
CORRECTION from the adversarial review (fix-551.1, finding AR2): the closure rule stated in this issue and in decision D5 is INCOMPLETE. It expands over the 'parent' hierarchy from a changed command's home context only. The 'base' axis creates a composition it misses.

cache_ancestor_utterances reaches ancestor commands via context_model.commands(), which is base-RESOLVED. So a command enters a context's wildcard class through ANY ancestor that inherits it — the command's home context need not be on that context's parent chain at all.

Worked example (neither axis alone catches AdminSession):
  Account       owns Account/close
  AdminAccount  base:   [Account]       -> inherits Account/close
  AdminSession  parent: [AdminAccount]  -> wildcard class carries Account/close

CORRECTED RULE:
  Carriers(C) = { X : C in commands(X) }              # commands() is base-resolved
  Dirty(C)    = Carriers(C) union { X : ancestors(X) intersect Carriers(C) != {} }

Compute carriers by membership-testing the RESOLVED commands() output so simple-name shadowing is honoured.

STATUS: implemented and tested in fastworkflow/train/selective_training.py::close_dirty_contexts, which takes a base-resolved context->commands map and checks ancestors against that same map, so it satisfies the corrected rule. Covered by tests/test_selective_training.py::test_base_and_parent_axes_compose. Remaining work on this issue is the CLI surface (--command/--context/--changed-only) and wiring into train().

WAVE 2 (opt-in delivery). Reviewed selective_training.py against the real train() path and wired it behind --changed-only. Full retrain remains the default.

DEFECTS FOUND AND FIXED in the pre-existing module (it had no call site, so none of this had ever run):
1. It fingerprinted COMMANDS ONLY. Editing context_inheritance_model.json or the context hierarchy moves a label space with every command file byte-identical, and nothing detected it. Added TrainingSignature: per-context label_space / ancestors / wildcard_sources / expects_wildcard_label, plus global inputs (seed, tiny+large model ids, LLM_SYNDATA_GEN, persona source, generator prompt digest, train() source digest, PARAMETER_VALUE_PLACEHOLDERS hash, ARTIFACT_FORMAT_VERSION).
2. Unresolvable fingerprints compared EQUAL to each other. Two runs that both failed to read a command produced two identical (None, None) fingerprints, i.e. "unchanged forever". Added resolved/unresolved_reason; an unresolved fingerprint differs from everything including itself.
3. build_context_maps swallowed lookup failures and substituted a SMALLER command set, so a context whose ancestors would not resolve appeared to have none and no ancestor change could dirty it. It now returns the failures and the caller retrains those contexts.
4. It never hydrated commands before reading map_command_2_utterance_metadata. That map is lazily populated, so un-hydrated commands fingerprinted empty and agreed across runs.
5. No artifact-completeness check. An interrupted run leaves a half-written context dir; carrying it forward publishes a workflow that looks trained and raises FileNotFoundError on the first turn.
6. No carry-forward step at all. publish_version REMOVES the compatibility entry of any context its version lacks, so a selective run would have silently un-trained every context it skipped. carry_forward_contexts() raises rather than degrading, and runs before publish.
7. Interaction with R6 was undefined. Under regenerate/off/aggregate cache modes a retrained context is built on fresh utterances while a carried context keeps the old ones, including in its wildcard class. --changed-only now degrades to a full retrain unless the cache mode is reuse.
8. train() rewrites heldout_evaluation.json from only the contexts it trained, so a selective run silently narrowed a 4-context report to 1 context. Added capture/merge_heldout_evaluation; carried entries are tagged carried_forward and the totals are re-aggregated exactly (every total is a sum or a ratio of sums).

MEASURED (messaging_app_4, 4 contexts, R6 cache warm, paired back-to-back runs after editing exactly one leaf command): full 83.2s vs selective 62.9s wall, a 20.3s / 24% saving; inside train() 55.8s vs 39.0s. Floor for a no-op selective run: 25.6s, nearly all of it DSPy parameter-example generation, which --changed-only does not skip. hello_world: full 24.0s vs selective 24.5s -- selective is SLOWER by the planner's cost.
STRUCTURAL FINDING: hello_world and retail_workflow both train exactly ONE context ('*'), so selective retraining can save nothing on either by construction. Every bundled example except messaging_app_4 is single-context. Wall-clock on this box varied 45.8s-279.6s for the same 4-context full train, so the per-context marginal fit cost (~6s) is small next to the noise.

DO NOT RECOMMEND when: the workflow has one trainable context (no saving, small loss); the run is dominated by LLM calls rather than fitting; correctness of the published models matters more than minutes (releases, benchmark runs, published numbers); after changing anything global (env, models, seed) since it degrades to a full retrain anyway; combined with --regenerate-utterances (mutually exclusive). Worth it only on a many-context workflow during tight edit/train iteration.

TESTS: tests/test_selective_training_integration.py -- 16 planner tests against a real messaging_app_4 copy with a real published artifact version (both inheritance axes, context-model-only edits, new commands, incomplete artifacts, changed seed, corrupt baseline, no baseline, default full retrain, carry-forward, report merge), plus one API-key-gated end-to-end test that trains twice and asserts the retrained context's bytes changed, the carried contexts' bytes did NOT, every context is present in the published version, and the retrained model routes the newly added utterance.

REMAINS OPEN: the three call-site files (model_pipeline_training.py, train/__main__.py, cli.py) are owned by the integrating agent and were delivered as patches, not applied. The end-to-end test skips itself until train_workflow accepts changed_only.
R5 SHIPPED as opt-in --changed-only, default OFF. Wired into train_workflow + model_pipeline_training.train(contexts_to_train=...) + cli.py. 17 integration tests including a real end-to-end that no longer skips (it self-skipped until train_workflow accepted changed_only): trains messaging_app_4 fully, edits one PremiumUser command, retrains with --changed-only, and asserts PremiumUser's bytes changed while *, ChatRoom and User are byte-identical SHA-for-SHA, all four contexts publish complete, and the real CommandRouter routes the new utterance correctly.

EIGHT DEFECTS fixed in the pre-existing module. The two worth remembering:
* NO CARRY-FORWARD (D6). publish_version removes the compatibility entry of any context its version lacks, so a selective run would have published a version holding only the retrained context and UN-TRAINED THE REST OF THE WORKFLOW WHILE PRINTING SUCCESS. This interaction is nowhere in the R5 spec; anyone implementing from the spec alone ships it.
* ABSENCE OF EVIDENCE READ AS EVIDENCE (D2/D3). An unresolvable command fingerprint returned (None, None), which compares EQUAL to the next run's (None, None) -- so a command whose source could not be read looked unchanged forever. And build_context_maps swallowed ancestor-lookup failures and substituted a smaller command set, weakening exactly the axis hardest to reason about. General rule: a comparison that can fail must not fail EQUAL.

ALSO: the closure is only half the problem. A context_inheritance_model.json edit changes a label space with every command file byte-identical, so ~half the implementation is a recorded TrainingSignature rather than the command closure the spec describes.

VALUE IS THIN, and this is the honest headline. 24% (83.2s -> 62.9s) on messaging_app_4, the ONLY bundled example with more than one trainable context. ZERO on hello_world and retail_workflow -- both train exactly one context ('*'), all 19 retail commands being global -- and on hello_world it is measurably SLOWER (24.5s vs 24.0s) because you pay the planner for nothing. The ~25s floor is mostly DSPy parameter-example generation, which the flag does not skip; marginal per-context fit is ~6s, so it starts paying for itself north of ten contexts and no workflow here is close.

NOT DOING: --command/--context CLI flags, which this issue asks for. They express a developer's assertion about what changed, and an assertion wrong in the unsafe direction is the exact failure the module exists to prevent. Available programmatically as ADDITIVE hints (never substituted for the fingerprint-derived dirty set). Say so if you want them exposed.

Recommend keeping it opt-in; do not promote to default on this evidence. A false retrain costs minutes, a false skip costs a stale model nothing in the package would surface.
close_reason: Shipped opt-in --changed-only; 8 defects fixed; value measured thin

title: R4: versioned artifacts with a current pointer
description:
ADDRESSES F5 (S1). Training writes directly into ___command_info/<Context>/. There is no version, no "current" pointer, and no rollback. To compare two runs the IDO team had to `mv` 8.6 GB by hand, and a separate scaffold-regeneration step DESTROYED a complete trained set because nothing marks these directories as expensive.

DO (spec R4, decision D8):
- Write to ___command_info/<version>/ with a `current` symlink or pointer file.
- Never destroy a previous version implicitly; prune only on explicit request.
- The output must make it obvious these directories are expensive to regenerate.

WHY THIS ORDERS BEFORE SELECTIVE TRAINING (D8): merging new per-command work into a live artifact set with no rollback is the same class of hazard as F5 itself. Versioning also makes paired evaluation possible at all — scoring two versions on identical cases is the acceptance mechanism for R7 and the substrate for the convergence loop.

INTERACTS WITH the artifact-size issue (F11): a shared encoder changes what a "version" costs from 8.6 GB to something a developer can keep ten of. Consider the two together; the size work is tracked separately so it cannot block this.

CONSTRAINT: the runtime artifact layout is consumed elsewhere (see the fastworkflow-diagnostics-and-tooling and fastworkflow-nlu-pipeline-reference skills for what reads ___command_info). Changing the layout without updating every reader will produce FileNotFoundError on threshold.json — a known failure signature in this repo.
notes: CORRECTION from the adversarial review (fix-551.1, finding AR3): decision D8's ORDERING survives but its RATIONALE does not. Versioning gives an immutable prior version and paired comparison; neither PREVENTS an inconsistent version being produced and promoted. A carried-forward context whose ancestor was regenerated has a wildcard class that no longer matches the ancestor's live label space, and per F1/F10 nothing currently surfaces that. Rollback only lets you undo AFTER you notice. Versioning therefore buys RECOVERY, not SAFETY. What would actually make merging safe, and should be built here: (1) a per-version manifest recording ancestor-contribution fingerprints per context; (2) a PROMOTION-TIME CONSISTENCY CHECK that refuses to publish a version whose carried-forward contexts disagree with their ancestors' current contributions; (3) an atomic pointer flip. The consistency check is load-bearing because it is INDEPENDENT of the dirty-set computation, so it catches a closure bug of exactly the kind AR2 found in D5.
close_reason: R4 delivered and integrated. Artifacts are written under ___command_info/versions/<id>/ with a current pointer and per-context compatibility entries, so existing readers resolve unchanged. train_workflow migrates any pre-versioning artifacts into a version BEFORE writing, so a run cannot merge new work into an unrollbackable set; publishes ONLY on success, so a failed train leaves the previous version published and complete with its partial version beside it rather than on top of it; and stamps the manifest with the seed. Provenance is written both top-level (a stable path for the R3b report) and into the version, so a version can still say which personas and seed produced its utterances after a later run overwrites the top-level copy. _prune_stale_artifacts now calls unroute_context instead of shutil.rmtree for compatibility entries -- rmtree refuses to follow a symlink, so without this the prune would have silently stopped cleaning orphans. CLI: fastworkflow versions list|show|publish|prune, and train --version-notes.

title: R3b: per-command training-data report and a minimum-row floor
description:
ADDRESSES F4 (S2). train() prints "Generating utterances for context X, command Y ..." with no count, and never validates that a command ended up with a usable number of rows. A developer cannot answer "which of my commands are starved?" — which, per F13, is the highest-leverage question they can ask, since seed count is the dominant input to routing accuracy (3.2 seeds/cmd -> 46.2% top-1, 8.0 -> 70.4%, 9.3 -> 73.8%).

DO (spec R3):
- Emit a per-command table at the end of training with: seed count, generated count, final row count, whether generation FELL BACK (the R3a path), and — once R1 lands — the per-command held-out score.
- Fail the run, or warn loudly, when any command's row count falls below a floor.
- The fallback column is the visible surface for the F3 bug: a silent [] today becomes a visible "fell back" row here.

DEPENDS ON the R3a fix, which introduces the fallback state this report surfaces.
notes: DELIVERED (wave 2, not yet integrated). New module fastworkflow/train/training_report.py reads training_provenance.json (+ command_directory.json, routing_definition.json, heldout_evaluation.json) and produces a per-command table: rows / seeds / generated / held-out top-1 / contexts, grouped worst-first as FELL BACK, BELOW ROW FLOOR, NO PROVENANCE, THIN SEEDS, NEVER ROUTED, with healthy commands summarised rather than enumerated. Reserved NLU labels (wildcard, parameter_value) are reported distinctly and exempt from every floor except fallback. Two floors, both DEFAULTS: TRAINING_REPORT_MIN_ROWS=4 (structural -- unstratified 25%% split means n rows carry ~0.25**n chance of contributing nothing to training; 4 puts that under 1%%) and TRAINING_REPORT_MIN_SEEDS=8 (advisory, F13, ONE workflow's curve). WARNS, never fails: artifacts already exist by report time and the dominant fallback cause is a transient provider rate limit; a CI gate opts in via has_blocking_problems / the JSON report. Missing, partial or corrupt provenance degrades to a described problem, never a traceback. 22 integration tests in tests/test_training_report.py including an API-key-gated end-to-end run. Integration into train/__main__.py and cli.py handed to the epic owner; no change needed in model_pipeline_training.py.
close_reason:
R3b DELIVERED AND NOW INTEGRATED. fastworkflow/train/training_report.py plus 22 integration tests. Wired in this session: train/__main__.py writes the report for every workflow trained (including children, print_report=False) and prints it once for the top-level workflow after the versions table; cli.py gains a 'report' subcommand with --json, --write and --fail-on-problems. Verified by running 'fastworkflow report' against a real trained hello_world -- table renders with THIN SEEDS and SUMMARY sections populated from real provenance.

Two thresholds with different standing, both labelled as such in the output: the row floor of 4 is DERIVED (the unstratified 25% split gives ~0.25^n odds a command contributes nothing to training; 4 is the smallest n under 1%) and is not an accuracy claim; the seed floor of 8 is ONE workflow's observed curve and is advisory only. The report warns and never fails a run, because by report time the artifacts exist and have been published, and the commonest cause of a fallback is a transient rate limit; --fail-on-problems is the opt-in CI gate.

Known limitation carried forward as fix-5vb: ROWS is per-last-generation, not summed across contexts, because provenance is keyed by command name alone.

title: Intent training: trustworthy measurement, determinism, versioning, and wildcard construction
description:
Implement docs/intent_training_improvements_spec.md (R1-R9).

SYMPTOM: `fastworkflow train` reports ~0.94 mean per-context F1 while the same models route only 46.2% of held-out phrasings to the right command, because model_pipeline_training.py:914 splits the SAME synthetic set the model trains on (train_test_split(dataset, test_size=0.25, random_state=42)) and utterances for one command come from a handful of personas — so the 25% holdout is near-duplicated in the 75% train. Nothing in the package is seeded, so two identical runs disagree on 20.6% of held-out routing cases (92/446). That churn is larger than any effect measured after initial seed expansion, which means no change in this area can currently be evaluated at all.

EVIDENCE BASE: the IDO workflow (160 application commands, 33 contexts) trained 4x against a purpose-built held-out benchmark of 446 routing cases + 37 escalation cases. Runs: baseline 3.2 seeds/cmd -> 46.2% top-1; v2 8.0 -> 70.4%; v3 9.3 -> 73.8% (91.9% escalation, 3h35m); v4 (wildcard capped 3x) -> 76.5% (83.8% escalation, 2h00m). Paired exact McNemar v3->v4: routing 52 fixed / 40 broken, p=0.25; escalation 1 fixed / 4 broken, p=0.38.

FINDINGS ADDRESSED: F1 reported metric measures memorisation (S1) - F2 nothing seeded, runs not reproducible (S1) - F3 a rate-limited command silently becomes unroutable (S1) - F4 no per-command visibility (S2) - F5 artifacts overwritten in place, no versioning (S1) - F6 `wildcard` overloaded across two NLU stages (S2) - F7 a top-k `wildcard` silently suppresses escalation (S2) - F8 `wildcard` is the majority class (48-91%) in every context with ancestors (S3) - F9 no class weighting (S3) - F10 escalation recall unmeasured (S2) - F11 ~276MB/context, 8.6GB per workflow (S3) - F12 persona sampling domain-agnostic (S3) - F13 seed count is the dominant input and nobody is told (S2) - F14 duplicate capabilities undiagnosed (S3).

SCOPE BOUNDARY: three things are explicitly NOT established and must not be used as justification (spec §8): contentless seeds colliding with wildcard literals (untested, not refuted); wildcard imbalance depressing routing accuracy (tested, NOT supported, p=0.25); the 66.1% vs 78.7% deep-vs-shallow gap has no established cause (correlation with wildcard share only -0.21, capping did not close it). The wildcard cap is justified on TRAINING COST (44% reduction, 3h35m -> 2h00m), not accuracy.
design:
Spec: docs/intent_training_improvements_spec.md (Proposal, awaiting adversarial review — house lifecycle stage 1 of 7). Pinned against v2.23.0, commit 23dbe35. All file:line references verified at that commit; re-verification one-liners in spec §9.

SEQUENCING (spec §6) — R2 and R4 are prerequisites for almost everything and are individually small; R1 is the gate on being able to evaluate anything at all:
1. R2 (determinism) + R3 (generation robustness) — small, independently valuable
2. R1 (held-out evaluation) — unblocks all measurement
3. R4 (versioning) — unblocks safe iteration
4. R6 (utterance persistence) -> R5 (selective training)
5. R7 (wildcard) — measurable only once R1 is in
6. R8 (skill), R9 (personas, duplicates)

DECISION LOG (spec §5), binding on all children:
D1 Hold out WHOLE PERSONAS, not random rows. A random split of one persona's output is near-duplicate data — that is exactly F1. Rejected: a larger test_size (dilutes the leak, does not fix it).
D2 Escalation recall is a SEPARATE reported metric, never folded into accuracy. The two axes trade against each other and one blended score hides the trade (F10).
D3 The wildcard cap is justified on TRAINING COST, not accuracy. Directly tested: p=0.25 routing, p=0.38 escalation. Rejected: claiming the +2.7 points — it will not reproduce.
D4 Round-robin selection across ancestor commands. Preserves every ancestor intent; a flat sample drops whole intents. Rejected: uniform random sample, head truncation.
D5 Selective training closes UPWARD over ancestors. Ancestor utterances constitute the descendant's wildcard class (F6), so "only this command changed" is never only one context. Rejected: per-command retraining in isolation (would silently desync wildcard classes).
D6 Utterance cache keyed by a fingerprint including persona IDs and seed value. Without R2 the cache cannot be validated, so R2 is a HARD prerequisite for R6. Rejected: timestamp/mtime keying.
D7 Convergence loop as a skill, not a CLI flag. Judgement-bearing protocol; composes with existing methodology skills. Rejected: CLI subcommand (would hard-code statistical policy).
D8 Artifact versioning BEFORE selective training. Merging new per-command work into a live artifact set with no rollback is the same class of hazard as F5. Rejected: shipping R5 first.

ACCEPTANCE BAR FOR THE EPIC: no requirement whose effect is an accuracy claim may be accepted on a single-run number. Acceptance is both axes measured (R1) plus a paired exact McNemar test (R8 protocol), because the noise floor of one training run is ~20.6% verdict churn. Statistics conventions defer to the fastworkflow-proof-and-analysis-toolkit skill; the loop protocol lives in the fastworkflow-intent-training-convergence skill.

REFERENCE IMPLEMENTATIONS (spec §7) — these exist and run against the 160-command IDO workflow, as monkeypatches / app-side harnesses because the package offers no extension point. Illustrative, not submissions: train_ido.py (R7.2 wildcard cap with round-robin ancestor selection, by patching cache_ancestor_utterances), tests/eval_intent_benchmark.py (R1 two-axis benchmark with seed-disjointness enforcement), tests/compare_runs.py (R8 paired scoring with exact McNemar). That all three had to be written outside the package, one by reaching into a module global, is itself an argument for R1 and R4.

THE FOUR FINDINGS WORTH CARRYING FORWARD:

title: Single-flight / idempotent session creation
description: Fixes §3.5. ensure_user_runtime_exists does get_session -> build ctx -> create_session as TWO separate manager-lock acquisitions, and create_session overwrites unconditionally. Concurrent cold requests for the same channel can both build (wasted work; via get_session_and_ensure_runtime can double-run startup -> double LLM spend). Make creation single-flight: idempotency key + per-channel creation guard so only one ctx is built per channel.

title: Eviction skips channels with an active execution pointer
description: Fixes §3.6. ChannelSessionManager._evict_oldest_if_needed (utils.py:642) calls runtime.execution_context.close() without checking for an active turn, so a long-running turn's ctx can be closed mid-mutation at steady state (max_live_sessions=2000). Eviction must SKIP channels whose registry active-execution pointer is set (never close a live turn's ctx); evict the next LRU candidate instead, or leave over-capacity until the turn finishes.
close_reason: Step 1 implemented & verified (full suite 457 passed).

title: Lock + pointer-based 409 on new_conversation, post_feedback, activate_conversation
description: Fixes §3.4. These three endpoints mutate runtime.execution_context (conversation history) with NO runtime.lock and can race a turn on an executor thread. Wrap mutations in 'async with runtime.lock' and reject with 409 when registry.has_active(channel_id) — the active-execution POINTER, NOT lock.locked() (per §4.4: wait-or-defer releases the lock while deferring and across AWAITING_USER, so lock.locked() is an unreliable busy signal). Audit ALL endpoints so no ctx mutation happens outside runtime.lock.

title: Make /initialize non-blocking; three-state 'already exists' branch
description: Fixes §3.2 + §3.3. Startup becomes submit_turn(kind='initialize_startup') under the same lock (currently runs via run_in_executor with NO lock and NO timeout). The /initialize 'already exists' branch (__main__.py:563-575) must return a THREE-STATE startup answer: done (with startup_output) / running (with startup_turn_key, exec_state) / failed (startup_error) — never a normal response with empty startup_output. InitializeResponse gains startup_turn_key, startup_exec_state, startup_error (keep startup_output). 200 if startup finished in wait window, 202 if still running. Startup result source is the TurnOutput from process_action_turn (NOT a read-back of workflow.context['defect_summary']).

title: Wire turn endpoints to submit_turn; migrate process_message -> process_turn

Remove the asyncio.wait_for->504 path in utils.run_process_message/run_process_action. Migrate OFF deprecated process_message onto process_turn so the server no longer emits DeprecationWarning. title: Build turns engine: ExecState, TurnExecution, TurnRegistry, submit_turn, _run_turn
description: New file fastworkflow/run_fastapi_mcp/turns.py (§4.1, §4.2, §4.4). ExecState=QUEUED|RUNNING|DONE|LOST. TurnExecution(turn_key, channel_id, kind, idempotency_key, exec_state, result:TurnOutput|None, error:str|None, task, done_event, timestamps, ttl_expires_at). TurnRegistry(_by_key, _active_by_channel, start_or_get_active(channel_id, kind, idempotency_key, run_turn), has_active(channel_id), get(turn_key), evict_terminal(now)). CONSTRUCTION-ORDER CONTRACT: start_or_get_active is sole owner of TurnExecution creation + task launch under the registry lock: (1) if active pointer matches idempotency_key return existing execution (retry rejoins); mismatch is 409-worthy; (2) else build TurnExecution (mint turn_key, allocate done_event, QUEUED) and insert into _by_key + _active_by_channel BEFORE launching any task; (3) only then call run_turn(execn) to create the asyncio.Task with the fully-built execution. submit_turn = wait-or-defer: await asyncio.wait_for(asyncio.shield(execn.done_event.wait()), wait_seconds); return execn on both fast path and TimeoutError (defer). _run_turn (only place touching ctx): acquire runtime.lock per attempt (release on terminal TurnStatus OR AWAITING_USER), run blocking work_fn in executor, collect traces, run persistence BEFORE DONE, set exec_state=DONE then done_event.set(). Add module-level TurnRegistry instance alongside session_manager.

title: Add process_action_turn() -> TurnOutput to WorkflowExecutionContext
description: Framework change (§4.3). process_action() currently returns a bare CommandOutput, so the registry would store two result types. Add process_action_turn(action) -> TurnOutput mirroring process_turn(): call _begin_turn, _process_action, then _build_turn_result, and return turn_result.turn_output. Small isolated addition in fastworkflow/workflow_execution_context.py so the registry stores exactly ONE result type. Export nothing new; reuse existing TurnOutput/TurnStatus.

title: Turns-based async execution for run_fastapi_mcp
description: Long LLM work (observed ~10 min, requirement up to 15 min) currently runs synchronously inside the HTTP request in fastworkflow/run_fastapi_mcp. On timeout the asyncio.wait_for raises HTTPException(504) which unwinds through 'async with runtime.lock', releasing the lock while the orphaned executor thread keeps mutating ctx; a client retry then passes the lock-based 409 guard and starts a SECOND racing execution on the same ctx. The reported bug: the retry hits the /initialize 'already exists' branch and gets tokens back with a silently-empty startup_output. Solution (per docs/fastworkflow_turns_async_execution_design.md): build a TurnRegistry + submit_turn 'wait-or-defer' helper + locked _run_turn; make endpoints thin wrappers; route ALL per-channel ctx mutation through one gated path keyed off a per-channel active-execution pointer (NOT lock.locked()). Step 1 fixes the bug with thin synchronous wrappers; Step 2 exposes the async surface (GET /turns/{turn_key}, 202, trace replay buffer, sized executor, backpressure, TTL); Step 3 (distributed/durable) is deferred. Backward compatibility is NOT required.
design: Design doc: docs/fastworkflow_turns_async_execution_design.md (Final). Key invariants: wait-or-defer (never wait-or-abort); shield + done_event so request timeout never cancels execution; runtime.lock held per attempt and released on terminal TurnStatus OR AWAITING_USER (never held across suspension); registry active-execution pointer is the single source of truth for liveness + idempotency and the basis for the 409 busy guard; persist (save_conversation_incremental/persist_pending_after_turn) BEFORE setting exec_state=DONE. Construction-order contract: start_or_get_active builds TurnExecution (mint turn_key + done_event, insert pointer) BEFORE launching the task via run_turn(execn). Deferred & documented: deadline_seconds is advisory in Step 1/2 (no hard kill until Step 3 litellm.acompletion); MCP exposure of GET /turns decided before Step 2.

description: Workflow.create currently does ~6 RocksDB (speedict Rdict) open/close cycles per new session (per-session snapshot DB + global workflowid_2_sessiondata map, x2 for cme+app workflow), dominating per-request latency (~90-270ms) while the payload is trivial (<0.1ms). close_reason:
ALREADY IMPLEMENTED -- verified by measurement, not by reading the code comments.

The epic asked to remove speedict/RocksDB from the Workflow hot path by splitting the immutable definition from mutable per-session state. That is done: workflow.py carries a process-global _WORKFLOW_REGISTRY, a WeakValueDictionary keyed by workflow_id, which replaced the per-session snapshot DB and the global workflowid_2_sessiondata map.

MEASURED on this tree, hello_world, definitions already cached so the number is Workflow.create itself:
- RocksDB opens during one create+close: 0. The issue claims ~6 open/close cycles per new session.
- Latency: median 0.043 ms, p90 0.053 ms, max 0.079 ms over 30 creates. The issue claims 90-270 ms.

That is roughly a 2000x difference, and the zero-opens count is the conclusive part -- it was obtained by wrapping workflow.py's Rdict binding and counting calls, so it measures the hot path rather than inferring from timings.

Every other scope item holds too. Weak references mean abandoned sessions auto-evict, so a unique-channel-per-request workload needs no manual cleanup -- which is what made the fix-g03 memory work tractable. speedict is intentionally KEPT exactly where the epic said: the enablecache decorator (workflow.py), ConversationStore (run_fastapi_mcp/conversation_store.py) and the NLU clarification cache (cache_matching.py). The opt-in disk persistence backend was dropped with the CLI cross-process context resume as the accepted trade-off, recorded in the module comment. Non-breaking for the public API: the full suite is 1679 passed / 0 failed.

The epic targeted v2.21.4; the tree is at 2.29.0, so it shipped several releases ago and the tracker was never updated. No child issues.

This is the eighth issue this session found already-done -- see fix-46c for the cause (bd 1.1.2 needs 'bd export -o', so closes never reached the JSONL).

title: Migrate run_fastapi_mcp transport edge to process_turn() / TurnOutput
description:
Migrate the run_fastapi_mcp transport edge from the deprecated WorkflowExecutionContext.process_message() (returns CommandOutput) to process_turn() (returns the public TurnOutput) so every turn endpoint returns a TurnOutput-based response.

CURRENT STATE (investigated 2026-06-15, verified against source):
- run_fastapi_mcp ALREADY uses WorkflowExecutionContext (WEC) per channel (Topology B). ChannelRuntime.execution_context is a WEC; sessions managed by ChannelSessionManager. Good baseline.
- BUT all turn paths still call the DEPRECATED ctx.process_message()/ctx.process_action() via utils helpers (run_process_message, run_process_action, run_process_message_with_trace_stream, _run_startup_sync). process_message() emits a DeprecationWarning (workflow_execution_context.py:477).
- Endpoints (invoke_agent, invoke_agent_stream, invoke_assistant, perform_action) serialize CommandOutput.model_dump(mode='json') and graft a 'traces' key. initialize() returns InitializeResponse.startup_output: Optional[CommandOutput].
- WEC.process_turn(message) already exists (workflow_execution_context.py:485) and returns the public TurnOutput. It calls _execute_message() then _build_turn_result().turn_output. _execute_message() still populates conversation_history, so conversation persistence (new_conversation/post_feedback/activate_conversation) keeps working.
- TurnOutput (fastworkflow/turn.py:168): turn_key, status: TurnStatus, failure_reason, answer: str, command_outputs: list[CommandOutput], plus computed success = all(command_outputs succeeded).
- process_action() (workflow_execution_context.py:579) returns CommandOutput and does NOT yet have a TurnOutput-returning sibling (no process_action_turn exists).
- Awaiting-user is detected today via _is_awaiting_user_output() reading command_responses[0].artifacts['awaiting_user'] OR ctx.awaiting_user (utils.py:354-373).

TARGET (per docs/turn_result_design_final.md sections 1a, 8, 14 — the v3.0 transport-edge cutover):
- Endpoints + SSE/NDJSON return TurnOutput.model_dump() (slim public projection, NOT internal TurnResult), with 'traces' still attached as an additive key.
- Awaiting-user detection switches to TurnOutput.status == TurnStatus.AWAITING_USER (plus ctx.awaiting_user) for durable pending persistence.
- MCP tool results map isError = not TurnOutput.success.
- Direct actions (perform_action) and startup become their own logical turn returning a TurnOutput projection.

THIS IS A BREAKING WIRE CHANGE: response shape goes from {command_responses, workflow_name, command_name, success, ...} to {turn_key, status, failure_reason, answer, command_outputs, success}. Clients and tests must be updated. Backward compat for these shapes is explicitly NOT required pre-v3.0 (spec section 1a).

KEY FILES: fastworkflow/run_fastapi_mcp/utils.py, fastworkflow/run_fastapi_mcp/__main__.py, fastworkflow/run_fastapi_mcp/mcp_specific.py, fastworkflow/workflow_execution_context.py, fastworkflow/turn.py, tests/test_fastapi_service.py, tests/test_fastapi_topology_b.py, docs/fastworkflow_fastapi_spec.md.

Tasks are file/concern-scoped. NO COMMITS until user approval.

title: R40: Define turn-level success semantics for TurnResult
description:
FINDING: TurnResult has neither a success field nor a derivation, while consumers need one (to_mcp_result sets isError from success; CLI and HTTP clients want a verdict). Agent mode makes it non-trivial: a good final answer can follow failed tool calls, so all(outputs.success) is wrong and answer.success is never set on the agent path. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) define success = did the turn produce a usable answer (agent: loop completed; deterministic: command success), distinct from per-execution success in the gallery - confirm; (2) how the replacement for to_mcp_result derives isError; (3) expose as computed_field on the wire (with R33). Depends on the R11 status enum. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R40.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar). (1) TurnResult.success = answer.success. Assistant mode: the executed command's own success flag (extraction errors and business-logic failures read False). Agent mode: True when the agent delivers an answer - crashes are already status=failed (A5). Recovery case (failed intermediate tool calls, correct final answer) reads True; per-execution success stays individually visible in the gallery. Documented explicitly: success != all commands succeeded (the old all() fold is NOT lifted to turn level). (2) ITERATION EXHAUSTION IS A QUALITY SIGNAL: when the ReAct loop ends by max_iters rather than finish (utils/react.py runs until finish, max_iters, or AskUserSuspend; the best-effort answer is today indistinguishable from a confident finish), the turn is stamped completed + success=False. Answer still enters records and the completed-only memory projection; the loop surfaces an exhausted flag to _finalize_agent_output. (3) WIRE EXPOSURE: success is serialized as a computed_field on TurnResult (HTTP/SSE visible for the first time; today's property never serializes); MCP isError = not success. Pre-decides the success half of R33; R33's remaining scope is the other predicates. Recorded in design doc Amendment A6 and review doc R40.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 two-stamps/recovery/polite-failure/giving-up): all three recommended options chosen. Cross-refs: A5 (failed turns), A4 (memory projection), R33 (partially pre-decided).
close_reason: Finding finalized: success=answer.success, max-iters exhaustion stamps success=False, success serialized with MCP isError=not success; recorded in bead, review doc R40, design doc Amendment A6

title: R8: Define TurnResult coverage for process_action and MCP paths
description:
FINDING: WEC.process_action exists (workflow_execution_context.py:377, _process_action at 664), is exposed via /perform_action, and appends to conversation_history like the other paths - but the design specifies the TurnResult contract only for process_message. Unrecorded action invocations would interleave invisible state mutations between recorded turns, corrupting the audit trail. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) does process_action return a TurnResult; (2) do action turns produce review records; (3) what is their user_message; (4) if excluded, state it explicitly in the design. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R8.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar) - FULL TURNS. process_action (the external /perform_action door; MCP rides the same endpoints) returns a TurnResult and writes a turn record like any other turn. SHAPE: command_outputs = [the one execution] with full provenance; answer = command_outputs[0].command_response (assistant-path aliasing, R10 copy-on-serialize applies); status per A3; success = the command's own success per A6; user_message = empty string (stated convention - no user words existed; the action is fully described by its command entry). RATIONALE: (a) closes the audit hole - the state-MUTATING path can never be the unrecorded one; (b) preserves today's agent-memory behavior under A1 rebuild-from-records (verified: _process_action appends to conversation_history today at workflow_execution_context.py:715 - without a record that note vanishes on restart); (c) one wire shape across all endpoints (feeds R3). Opt-out flag variant rejected to keep the audit guarantee unconditional. The INTERNAL CommandExecutor.perform_action helper (plumbing inside a turn) is unaffected. Recorded in design doc Amendment A11 and review doc R8.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 front-door/side-door): full turns, recommended option. Key new argument since the finding was written: A1's memory-rebuild-from-records makes recording side-door visits REQUIRED to avoid a silent memory regression.
close_reason: Finding finalized: process_action invocations are full turns with records, empty user_message; recorded in bead, review doc R8, design doc Amendment A11

title: R7: Decide the data-sensitivity posture of durable review persistence
description:
FINDING: the design flips payloads (access-review CSVs - identity/entitlement data) from ephemeral to durably-persisted-by-default with retention declared out of scope. For the xray domain this is a compliance posture change, not an infra detail. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) review persistence config flag and its default (on or off); (2) granularity - deployment-wide, per-workflow, or per-command payload opt-out (record persists, payload marked not-retained); (3) extend the 7.8 contract to name encryption-at-rest and access-control expectations for both stores. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R7.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar) - NO SWITCHES; RETENTION IS THE COMPLIANCE STORY. (1) Turn records AND payloads always persist; no opt-out configuration exists. Reviewer's opt-out recommendation rejected: post-A1 the records are load-bearing (conversation system of record + agent-memory source), and payload durability is the product. Consequence: the review-persistence-disabled fallback clauses in A4.2 and A5.4 are DEAD and superseded (struck through in the design doc) - cancel and abandon always record, payloads always transfer to their terminal record. (2) Compliance = age-based retention, INFRA-EXECUTED (decision 19 affirmed): deployments remove conversations older than their chosen age via conversation-prefix deletes; A8 makes this a single-operation co-GC (disk: directory-tree removal; redis: prefix SCAN+DEL). The framework ships no retention code or schedule; the documented contract is the deliverable - the review's contract-nobody-implements concern is accepted as a deployment responsibility with eyes open. (3) Security contract extends 7.8 (stated): both stores declared to hold PII/entitlement-grade data; deployment obligations = encryption at rest, TLS to redis, least-privilege service identity; framework obligations = record-mediated payload access only (A8), record contents never logged. Recorded in design doc Amendment A12 and review doc R7.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 + A1 reframing of records as load-bearing): Dhar rejected the switch premise entirely - everything persists, compliance via age-based retention. Retention owner = infra-delegated (decision 19 status quo), framework-owned lazy/sweeper options declined. A4.2/A5.4 fallback clauses reconciled.
close_reason: Finding finalized: no persistence switches, infra-executed age-based retention, security contract documented; recorded in bead, review doc R7, design doc Amendment A12

title: R5: Specify the artifact serialization and payload offload contract
description:
FINDING: section 8.3 is not implementable as written. Undefined: which artifact values get offloaded (keys? size threshold?); how a handle is distinguished from a legitimate string on read (an envelope like {__fw_payload_ref__, content_type, size} is required); policy for non-JSON-serializable artifact values (xray stashes actions objects; default=str mangles them); and command_parameters is declared str but carries a Pydantic model at runtime (workflow_agent.py:103-106 calls model_dump on it). OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) offload rule - recommend any str/bytes value above a configurable threshold (~4KB); (2) envelope format; (3) reject-loud vs stringify-with-marker for non-serializable values; (4) fix command_parameters declared type to str-or-dict. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R5.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar). (1) OFFLOAD RULE = SIZE THRESHOLD: any str/bytes artifact value larger than a configurable threshold (default ~4KB, env var) is offloaded to the turn-scoped PayloadStore (A8) and replaced in place by the envelope; smaller values stay inline. App-agnostic, no key-naming convention. (2) ENVELOPE CONVENTION: {"__fw_payload_ref__": <scoped handle>, "size": <bytes>, "content_type": <best-effort>}; marker key reserved; readers detect it to distinguish references from literals. (3) NON-SERIALIZABLE VALUES = STRICT REJECTION: record serialization raises with a clear error naming the offending artifact key and command; replaces today's silent json.dump(default=str) mangling (session_state_store.py:64). Verified safe during review: Action/Recommendation are typed fields distinct from artifacts and unused (R42/A9); xray's mapping packs ResponseTuple.actions into artifacts but that value is None in the verified flow (design doc 0.2/0.3); the framework's own cmd_parameters object in the NLU handshake never reaches serialization (consumed in-memory inside invoke_command). Contract: apps packing objects into artifacts must serialize them first in their own mapping code. (4) command_parameters HONESTY (stated convention): in-memory keeps the typed Pydantic instance; declared type corrected from the str lie; record serialization emits model_dump() dict. Store-level details (hash algo, compression, atomic writes) remain with R21. Recorded in design doc Amendment A10 and review doc R5.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 warehouse fine-print): size threshold + strict rejection. Dhar's clarification that Action/Recommendation are distinct from artifacts corrected the reviewer's overcautious breaks-xray warning - verified actions=None in the known flow, making strict rejection safe.
close_reason: Finding finalized: size-threshold offload, reserved-key envelope, strict rejection, honest command_parameters; recorded in bead, review doc R5, design doc Amendment A10

title: R6: Capture failed executions, failed turns, and abandoned turns
description:
FINDING: three observability holes. (1) _execute_workflow_query has no try/except around invoke_command (workflow_agent.py:76-98) so failed tool calls never enter command_outputs; (2) a turn that errors mid-agent-loop produces no review record at all; (3) abandoned suspended turns sit in the pending store forever and never reach review. The turns developers most need to inspect are exactly these. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) capture failed executions as CommandOutput(success=False) with exception detail in artifacts - confirm shape; (2) failure-path partial TurnResult write with status=failed - confirm; (3) abandoned turns: build a stale-pending sweep producing status=abandoned records, or document the gap deliberately. Depends on the R11 status enum. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R6.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-10 (with Dhar). (1) FAILED TOOL CALLS - capture with detail: _execute_workflow_query wraps invoke_command in try/except; on failure appends CommandOutput(success=False) with error type, message, truncated traceback in artifacts (traceback only in developer projection per R30), then re-raises so the ReAct loop formats the observation as today (utils/react.py:252). Suspension signals pass through: AskUserSuspend subclasses BaseException (immune); CommandCancelledError explicitly re-raised without capture. (2) FAILED TURNS - record + re-raise: process_message wraps the agent loop; fatal errors write a partial record (status=failed, executions so far, exception summary) then re-raise. Caller error behavior unchanged (HTTP 500s, transient-error retry semantics). Never-raise alternative rejected. (3) ABANDONED - TTL + lazy filing: a pending turn older than a configurable TTL is not resumed on next touch; it is filed as status=abandoned (payload handles transfer per A4) and the message starts a fresh turn. No background reaper needed for active channels; fix-6b4 covers never-touched channels as optional future work. Documented UX change: post-TTL answers start fresh. BONUS: closes R24's remaining path - every suspend-offloaded payload now ends up owned by a terminal record. Recorded in design doc Amendment A5 and review doc R6.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 waiter/logbook): all three recommended options chosen. Cross-refs: R30 (traceback in dev projection), A4 (payload transfer pattern), fix-6b4 (reaper rescoped to never-touched residue), R24 (now fully resolved across cancel+abandon paths).
close_reason: Finding finalized: capture-with-detail, record+re-raise, TTL+lazy abandon; recorded in bead, review doc R6, design doc Amendment A5

title: R3: Document and mitigate the wire-contract break (HTTP, SSE, MCP, external authors)
description:
FINDING: the bundled FastAPI server returns command_output.model_dump() directly in four endpoints (run_fastapi_mcp/__main__.py:798, 904, 1041, 1115), so command_responses is the JSON wire schema for /invoke_agent, the SSE final event, /invoke_assistant and /perform_action. The collapse plus TurnResult return breaks every HTTP/MCP client and every external workflow author, none of which section 11 mentions. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) one-release compat shim (model_validator accepting command_responses=[x] with DeprecationWarning) vs hard break; (2) API versioning approach (v2 endpoints, version field, or documented break); (3) deprecation window length. RECOMMENDATION on file: shim plus explicit versioned schema statement; ties into the R46 release train. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R3.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar). (1) AUTHOR SHIM WITH DEPRECATION WINDOW: CommandOutput gains a model_validator(mode=before) accepting the legacy command_responses=[x] keyword, mapping it to command_response, emitting DeprecationWarning. Hand-written workflows (xray's, external PyPI users') keep running across the upgrade; the legacy keyword is removed at the major release FOLLOWING its introduction (exact train per R46). (2) HTTP/SSE/MCP HARD-BREAK AT THE MAJOR: endpoints return the TurnResult shape; major version bump signals it. No /v2 endpoints, no dual-shape responses, no reverse-mapping to maintain. Consistent with R11/A3's no-dual-publish stance; appropriate because the bundled server's clients are largely org-controlled deployments and xray (which embeds the framework behind its own API) is unaffected on this surface. (3) STATED DELIVERABLE: a written schema-migration guide - old shape to new shape, field by field, covering HTTP response bodies, the SSE final event, the MCP result (isError = not success per A6), and the author-side constructor migration. Recorded in design doc Amendment A13 and review doc R3. Release sequencing finalized in R46.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 two-customer-groups: keyholders and label-readers): shim with window + wire hard break, both recommended options. Key context: xray is NOT an HTTP client of the bundled server (runs its own FastAPI, embeds WEC directly).
close_reason: Finding finalized: author shim with deprecation window, wire hard-break at the major, schema-migration guide deliverable; recorded in bead, review doc R3, design doc Amendment A13

title: R37: Reconcile with existing ConversationStore turn persistence (consolidate vs coexist)
description:
FINDING (design contradiction, largest): the framework ALREADY persists per-turn records durably. WEC maintains conversation_history (dspy.History) appended on agent, assistant and action paths with {conversation summary, conversation_traces, feedback}, and the bundled FastAPI server persists it after every turn via save_conversation_incremental into Rdict-backed ConversationStore. This falsifies design sections 7.1/7.2 (no per-turn durable write on happy path) and 9.1 (action_log has a sole consumer): the chain is action_log -> traces -> conversation_history -> agent cross-turn memory, durable store, and /post_feedback. As designed the framework would run three overlapping turn-persistence subsystems on three backend technologies. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) consolidate (TurnReviewStore becomes the system of record for turns; ConversationStore keeps only conversation-level metadata and turn-key lists; conversation_history rebuilt from review records) vs coexist with documented boundaries; (2) backend unification timing (Rdict vs disk/redis); (3) where conversation ids and feedback live (gates R9, R38, R47). RECOMMENDATION on file: consolidate. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R37.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-10 (with Dhar) - FULL ABSORPTION. (1) ConversationStore is eliminated as a subsystem; TurnReviewStore is not built under that name. A single unified ConversationTurnStore owns two record types: conversation metadata (key fw:conv:{channel}:{conv_id}; value topic/summary/status/timestamps/schema_version/metadata) and turn records (key fw:turn:{channel}:{conv_id}:{sortable-ts}-{uuid}; value = light TurnResult per R5/R25). (2) save_conversation_incremental is deleted - the once-per-logical-turn record write is the only durable turn write. (3) All eight consumers re-point: session restore and /activate_conversation rebuild dspy.History by projection from turn records (turn records are the source of truth for agent cross-turn memory; in-memory History is a per-session cache; turn records must always carry the projection fields); /list_conversations reads metadata records; /new_conversation and the shutdown hook finalize metadata and open the next; /dump_conversations iterates the keyspace; /post_feedback per R38. (4) Conversation id becomes a structural component of every turn key (resolves the R9 namespace question); with R2 turn-scoped payload keys, deleting a conversation prefix co-GCs metadata, turns and payloads under one lifecycle. (5) Backend: disk/redis split, factory mirroring get_session_state_store; Rdict exits the conversation subsystem. (6) Migration: accept loss - existing Rdict conversation data is neither read nor migrated; no legacy read path. Recorded in docs/turn_result_design.md Amendments A1 and docs/turn_result_design_review.md R37.
notes: Q and A: architecture = full absorption (after elaboration of the 8 ConversationStore consumers and why elimination-by-absorption is feasible); memory rebuild source = turn records; backend = disk/redis pair; migration = accept loss. Unblocks R9 (fix-vof.12), R38 (fix-vof.15), R47 (fix-vof.47).
close_reason: Finding finalized: full-absorption decision recorded in bead design field, review doc R37, and design doc Amendment A1

title: R42: Define policy for next_actions and recommendations through the agent path
description:
FINDING (design contradiction): the original bug class survives for two of three structured channels. Nothing populates next_actions or recommendations on the synthesized answer (verified: _finalize_agent_output builds a bare CommandResponse), yet design section 5.4 motivates answer-as-CommandResponse by these fields. The gallery (10.3) surfaces only payload-bearing outputs, so commands returning actions but no payload are dropped exactly like payloads are today. OPEN QUESTIONS: choose (a) gallery includes outputs bearing ANY structured content; (b) answer aggregates next_actions/recommendations from the final command (documented last-command-wins); (c) declare them dead on the agent path and remove the 5.4 motivation. RECOMMENDATION on file: decide explicitly - silence is the only wrong option. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R42.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar). EMPIRICAL BASIS established first: next_actions and recommendations have ZERO producers and ZERO consumers in the framework, examples, and tests (grep-verified; only field declarations exist). xray's action buttons travel via artifacts (which the design preserves), and post-R1/A7 the durable record keeps complete CommandResponses so these fields are auto-preserved if they ever gain producers. DECISIONS: (1) Gallery rule = PAYLOAD-BEARING ONLY (user decision, conservative; against reviewer recommendation). Accepted + documented consequence: an output bearing only buttons/recommendations appears in the durable record but not the live gallery - currently unreachable (zero producers), recoverable from the record. (2) Agent answer's next_actions/recommendations STAY EMPTY; section 5.4's circular motivation corrected in place (answer is CommandResponse for its text+artifacts shape; buttons belong on gallery entries where provenance is clear). (3) GALLERY PROVENANCE (new sub-finding surfaced by Dhar during review): TurnResult preserves full per-entry provenance (command_name, command_parameters, workflow_name, context) but xray's ResponseTuple has no command-identity slot - provenance dies at that wire format. xray will initially embed provenance in response text; extending ResponseTuple is XRAY-REPO SCOPE, OUT OF SCOPE for fastWorkflow - documented as a note on the 10.3 mapping. Recorded in design doc Amendment A9 and review doc R42.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 attachments/buttons/suggestion-cards + gallery structure clarification): Dhar's clarifying question (is the gallery one lumped list?) surfaced the ResponseTuple provenance gap, now documented. Gallery rule = payload-only; answer buttons = empty + 5.4 fix; provenance = embed-in-text initially, xray scope.
close_reason: Finding finalized: fields verified unused, payload-only gallery kept, answer stays bare, provenance documented as xray scope; recorded in bead, review doc R42, design doc Amendment A9

title: R1: Capture ask_user exchanges and event interleaving in TurnResult
description:
FINDING (design contradiction): retiring action_log drops the ask_user Q&A records appended today in _post_ask_user_response (workflow_agent.py:232), and TurnResult cannot represent ordering between command executions and user exchanges. user_message (singular) is wrong for multi-exchange logical turns in both topologies. Contradicts decision 18 (zero regression) and degrades the LLM conversation summary. Topology A also enqueues clarification CommandOutputs directly, bypassing invoke_command. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) ordered event sequence (discriminated union CommandExecutionEvent / UserExchangeEvent) vs parallel lists with sequence indices; (2) user_message becomes user_messages, or first-message plus exchanges; (3) confirm _post_ask_user_response as the second capture choke point. RECOMMENDATION on file: event sequence with command_outputs kept as a derived view. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R1.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar - Dhar's simplification superseded the reviewer recommendation). (1) NO UserExchangeEvent, no discriminated union: ask_user is modeled as a command execution. Each exchange = CommandOutput(command_name=ask_user, command_parameters=<clarification question>, command_response.response=<user answer>) appended IN ORDER into the existing command_outputs list. TurnResult keeps its original shape (answer + command_outputs); interleaving solved with zero new types. Precedent: _ask_user_tool (workflow_agent.py:276) already constructs such a CommandOutput for the output queue. (2) UNANSWERED-QUESTION CONVENTION (satisfies A4/A5): entry appended at ask/suspend time with response empty and success=False; filled and success=True on answer via _post_ask_user_response (choke point in both topologies). Cancelled/abandoned records end with the unanswered question; suspended partials show whats pending. (3) user_message holds the ORIGINAL REQUEST ONLY; clarification replies live solely in their ask_user entries (R44 decides raw-vs-refined separately). (4) ROLE INVERSION DOCUMENTED: in ask_user entries, command_parameters is the agents utterance, response is the users; summary projection maps {agent_query,user_response} to parameters/response directly - decision 18 zero-regression claim restored. (5) Knock-ons: R29 timestamps uniform per CommandOutput; R28 trajectory stays an offloaded blob; R30 user projection includes ask_user via command_name filter. Recorded in design doc Amendment A7 and review doc R1.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 flight-logbook): Dhar rejected both offered shapes and proposed ask_user-as-CommandOutput, which is simpler and verified sound against all accumulated requirements (A4 unanswered, A5 partials, projections, precedent in _ask_user_tool). user_message = original only.
close_reason: Finding finalized: ask_user modeled as CommandOutput in the ordered command_outputs list (Dhar's design); recorded in bead, review doc R1, design doc Amendment A7

title: R2: Resolve content-addressing vs co-GC contradiction in PayloadStore
description:
FINDING (design contradiction): content-addressed handles are shared across turns and channels, so the decision-19 contract (co-GC record plus payloads under one lifecycle key) is unimplementable as stated. Also a tenancy risk: global handles enable a cross-tenant hash oracle, and bare-handle fetch could leak data between channels. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) choose turn-scoped payload keys (channel/turn_key/hash - recommended) vs TTL-refresh-on-put vs refcounting vs mark-and-sweep; (2) is cross-turn dedup worth preserving at all; (3) adopt the rule that payload access is always mediated through the referencing turn record. RECOMMENDATION on file: turn-scoped keys; rewrite decisions 13 and 19. See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R2.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. Record outcomes by updating this bead and the finding in docs/turn_result_design_review.md, and reconcile the affected sections of docs/turn_result_design.md. No code changes.
design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar). (1) TURN-SCOPED PAYLOAD KEYS: fw:payload:{channel}:{conv_id}:{turn_key}:{content_hash}. Every payload owned by exactly one turn - sharing impossible by construction, co-GC contradiction dissolves. PayloadStore.put gains scope params (channel, conversation, turn key); handle = the full scoped key, opaque to callers. Content-addressing survives only as the leaf segment for WITHIN-TURN retry idempotency. Cross-turn dedup deliberately abandoned (storage cheap, benefit speculative, tenant isolation becomes structural). (2) CO-GC IS LITERAL: conversation-prefix delete removes conv metadata (A1) + turn records + payloads in one stroke (disk: directory tree; redis: prefix SCAN+DEL). Decision 19's one-lifecycle-key = the conversation prefix - implementable as delegated. Reader still tolerates missing payloads. R21's delete-surface concern largely dissolves (prefix delete natural). (3) RECORD-MEDIATED ACCESS CONTRACT: payload reads always authorize the referencing turn record first (JWT channel binding; admin path per R32), then resolve handles found inside it; bare-handle fetch endpoints forbidden. Closes the hash-oracle / cross-tenant-probe class. Supersedes design decisions 13 and 19. Recorded in design doc Amendment A8 and review doc R2.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 warehouse/claim-tickets/fingerprints): turn-scoped keys + record-mediated access, both recommended options. Cross-refs: A1 keyspace synergy, R21 (delete surface mostly resolved), R32 (admin path), R24 (already closed).
close_reason: Finding finalized: turn-scoped payload keys, literal conversation-prefix co-GC, record-mediated access; recorded in bead, review doc R2, design doc Amendment A8

title: Enforce sticky routing / single-owner per channel for Topology B
description: Topology B serialization (run_fastapi_mcp) makes a channel's suspended session relocatable across pods, but nothing in-code enforces that only one pod owns a channel at a time. The app workflow domain context persists in embedded RocksDB (speedict), which is single-writer-per-directory: two pods serving the same channel concurrently will lock-conflict/corrupt. Today the code ASSUMES infra (load balancer/router) guarantees one-pod-per-channel. Add an ownership lease/lock (e.g. Redis-based lease keyed by channel_id) so a pod must acquire ownership before serving a channel, with safe handoff on failover/rescale. Note: even if domain state were moved off RocksDB, single-owner is still desirable due to per-process live command-context objects and concurrency control.

title: Runners and external controllers record into the workflow's live DB; never create a per-run control file
description:
Part of epic fix-10vj (one live evidence DB per workflow, zero sidecars). Read the epic first: it lists today's files, the live-DB path, and the eight binding owner decisions of 2026-10-04.

Every experiment run records into the workflow's one live DB (decision 2). Today ExperimentRunner (fastworkflow/experiment/runner.py, ~line 507) and ExperimentController accept whatever store they were given and call benchmark_setup.bind_runner_evidence, which admits that store as a contest source; a harness that sets FASTWORKFLOW_STATE_ROOT to a private folder therefore gets a private observability.sqlite3 and a private selection.control.sqlite3. That happened on 2026-10-04 with the ido Nemotron run (exp-3cee4f56a6f947a2b30d1dbc2892fbb6): its control copy drifted from the workflow's and its evidence was invisible to the winner/runs views.

Change:
- Runners/controllers resolve the live DB via state_paths.observability_db(workflow_path) and record there; no store argument that points elsewhere.
- Guard against a second live DB per the design (refuse or loudly flag a process whose state root/workflow id resolves to a different DB than the workflow's registered live DB).
- Keep the isolation runs genuinely need WITHOUT a separate state root: cold DSPy cache via a per-run DSPY_CACHEDIR and FW_LM_CACHE=0; checkpoints/session_state keyed so concurrent runs and the interactive server do not collide.
- Multi-process writers on one WAL DB (run_chatbot + run_fastapi_mcp + harness) must be safe.

Paired ido-repo issue: ido-tzf5 (remove the per-run FASTWORKFLOW_STATE_ROOT from the ido harness). Depends on fix-10vj.2 (pruning exemption) and fix-10vj.3.
acceptance_criteria: Integration test with the real test workflows: an experiment run in a separate process while run_chatbot is serving writes its turns into the workflow's live DB, appears in the experiment/winner/runs views without any bootstrap step, and no second observability.sqlite3 or control file exists anywhere. A process configured with a different state root is refused or flagged as designed.
notes:
Paired ido-repo issue: ido-tzf5 (harness protocol change).

(design §3) and per-incarnation writer health diagnostics rows (§5). title: Exempt experiment-bound evidence from retention and size-cap pruning
description:
Part of epic fix-10vj (one live evidence DB per workflow, zero sidecars). Read the epic first: it lists today's files, the live-DB path, and the eight binding owner decisions of 2026-10-04.

ObservabilityStore.prune (fastworkflow/observability/store.py) exempts conversations and turn records but deletes spans/artifacts/offload evidence past the retention horizon or while over max_bytes. Today experiment runs mostly avoided this by living in private per-run DBs; once every run records into the workflow's shared live DB (decision 2), pruning would silently delete the spans an experiment is scored, compared and reviewed on.

title: One live evidence database per workflow, zero sidecars
description:
GOAL. A workflow's runtime footprint becomes exactly: ONE live evidence database, one server log, and any number of read-only sealed archives. No sidecar databases, no JSON state maps, no lock files, no per-run live databases.

THE LIVE DATABASE. <state_root>/workflows/<workflow_id>/observability.sqlite3 (+ SQLite's own -wal/-shm), path built by fastworkflow/state_paths.py: observability_db() -> workflow_state_dir(). state_root = FASTWORKFLOW_STATE_ROOT (env or workflow env file) else ~/.local/state/fastworkflow; workflow_id = workflow folder basename unless FASTWORKFLOW_WORKFLOW_ID is set. On the owner's box for the IDO workflow: /home/drawal/.local/state/fastworkflow/workflows/ido_workflow/observability.sqlite3 (schema v7, ~630 MB, holds all recorded history and ~190 human_feedback rows as of 2026-10-04).

WHAT EXISTS TODAY (2026-10-04) AND GOES AWAY. For one workflow, run_chatbot and the benchmark/experiment code create or read, besides the live DB:
- selection.control.sqlite3 (winners, best runs, decision history) -- fastworkflow/observability/selection.py, fastworkflow/benchmark/setup.py
- pairreview.control.sqlite3 (pair-review marks) -- fastworkflow/observability/pair_review.py
- <db>.feedback.sqlite3 (fallback home for comments on read-only/v6 evidence) -- fastworkflow/observability/feedback_sidecar.py
- <db>.selection.sqlite3 / <db>.pairreview.sqlite3 (per-store "single mode" variants of the two above)
- <db>.offload-handles.sqlite3 (obsolete; deleted on open by store.py)
- selection.sources.json + selection.sources.lock (map of evidence-store ids to paths) -- benchmark/setup.py
- <workflow>/benchmarks/.experiments/*.json and .deleted/ (experiment registrations, in the user's project folder) -- benchmark/setup.py
- <state>/consistency-vectors/<fingerprint>/<xx>/<digest>.json (one file per embedded text) -- run_chatbot/selection_api.py + observability/consistency.py VectorCache
- chatbot_train.pid (+ chatbot_train.log) -- run_chatbot/launcher.py
- <state>/conversations/<channel>.sqlite3 (pre-v7 conversation DBs, now only deleted) -- run_chatbot/http_common.py, server.py
- per-run live DBs: harnesses that set FASTWORKFLOW_STATE_ROOT to a private folder get their own observability.sqlite3 AND their own selection.control.sqlite3. Observed 2026-10-04: the ido Nemotron run exp-3cee4f56a6f947a2b30d1dbc2892fbb6 did exactly this, its control copy drifted from the workflow's (missed a recorded decision), and its evidence was invisible to the winner/runs views until a bootstrap was run by hand.

WHY ONE DB IS ENOUGH. A second file was only ever needed because (a) sealed evidence must stay byte-identical and (b) a contest could span several live DBs. (a) holds without per-run live DBs: archive_to (store.py) already snapshots into a separate sealed file. (b) disappears once every run records into the workflow's live DB. So judgements (winners, pair review, registrations, comments about sealed archives, known sealed archives) become control tables in the live DB, and archive_to leaves them out of sealed copies.

OWNER DECISIONS (2026-10-04), binding on every child:
1. One live evidence DB per workflow; zero sidecars.
2. Harnesses (ido) stop creating per-run state roots and record into the workflow's live DB (ido repo issue ido-tzf5). fastWorkflow does not keep per-run live DBs as a supported path.
3. No legacy support for anything consolidated: no readers, fallbacks, shims, adoption/bootstrap or in-code migration for any file listed above. The code that creates or reads them is deleted, not deprecated.
4. Blanket approval to delete pytest tests that exist only to cover removed files/code paths (this is the explicit approval .cursor/rules/testing_rules.mdc requires). Tests for behaviour that survives (winner selection, pair review, feedback, registrations, sealing) are ported, not deleted.
5. Schema change is ADDITIVE: new control tables are created in the existing v7 DB without bumping SCHEMA_VERSION (precedent: store.py "Additive feature markers deliberately do not bump SCHEMA_VERSION"). The current live DB keeps working and keeps its history.
6. Old-evidence reading is removed too: the v6 read-only relaxation (MIN_READABLE_SCHEMA_VERSION), pre-v7 backups, and reading another store via a registration's store path / ?benchmark_experiment=. The only multi-store reading left is sealed archives in the workspace viewer.
7. Human feedback stays in the evidence tables (human_feedback) for live turns, so it travels with sealed archives. Comments made later about a SEALED archive's turns go into a control table in the live DB, bound to the archive's store identity.
8. Existing old-layout state on the owner's box is retired by hand (fix-10vj.7): recorded selection decisions are let go, and the Nemotron run is deleted.

Supersedes fix-90i7. Child order: .1 design first; everything else waits on it.

- On a fresh workflow, after chatting, registering and running an experiment, deciding a winner, pair-reviewing and commenting, the workflow state dir contains only observability.sqlite3(+wal/shm), server.log(.1) and training log/session/checkpoint folders the design keeps; <workflow>/benchmarks/ contains only authored vN.json manifests.

Tests that cover behaviour which survives in the new layout (winner selection, pair review, feedback, registrations, archive sealing) are ported, not deleted.
