title: Selection recovery elects a newer registration over an older history-only experiment
description: When the selection control file is rebuilt from scratch while an evidence store is temporarily unreadable, recovery elects a newer registration over an older experiment that exists only in the evidence history. Causes: the older-unadopted check skips experiments that are already members (selection.py ~1382); _seed_registrations (setup.py ~627) runs before history adoption (~655). Repro: /tmp/d1/claim_b.py scenario 3. Fix option (b): elect the oldest member, not the caller.
close_reason: Initial election picks the oldest group member (_order_key), selection.py _register; tests in test_experiment_registration_and_repeat.py

title: A sole automatic winner can never be deleted; a winner-less group cannot be promoted
description: Found 2026-10-02 while reviewing fix-jfy5. (1) retire_experiment refuses the current winner, including the automatic first winner, and record_decision offers no decision that clears the pointer (keep/undecided leave it unchanged). An experiment created by mistake as the first in its group can only be replaced (create B, promote B, delete A), never removed. (2) record_decision raises NoCurrentSelection when the group has no pointer, and promote is a compare-and-set on the current selection_id. So a group left winner-less (an incomplete bootstrap today, or a future 'withdraw winner' decision) cannot have any member promoted until a later automatic initial election. Developer's preferred direction: a client 'withdraw winner' decision. That also needs a compare-and-set promotion from 'no pointer', plus a rule for whether automatic election may fire after a human withdrawal. Learning doc: docs/learning/non_ui_changes_checklist.md D1.

comments.author: Dhar Rawal
comments.text: Done (uncommitted): (a) sole-member winner can be deleted (retire_experiment allow_sole_winner; delete_empty_experiment; can_delete in handler_benchmark) and (e) clearer ExperimentSelected / NoCurrentSelection messages. Remaining: (c) let a client promote into a winner-less group (CAS on 'no pointer') so a permanently lost evidence store no longer leaves every new group unpromotable (repro /tmp/d1/claim_b.py scenario 2, claim_b_live.py).

title: Replace per-verb if-chains with one route table and one auth chokepoint; make 'clear conversations' an explicit route
description: do_POST is 261 lines (server.py 2283-2543): an allowlist built from seven predicates plus a literal set (2286-2327), then a separate dispatch that re-tests the same paths. Anything allowlisted that no earlier branch matches falls into the final block, which is the destructive clear-all-conversations (2524-2536), guarded only by the confirm string. Host/Origin and token gates are copy-pasted into do_GET, do_POST, do_PUT, do_DELETE and do_PATCH; do_PATCH's docstring says so itself: 'no shared chokepoint ... A do_PATCH written without them would be an ungated cross-origin write' (2630-2636). Routing elsewhere is string prefix/suffix matching (_handle_api 188 lines, _handle_workspace 187; selection_api.owns_write admits any best-run/* suffix and 404s later). Error envelopes differ ({error} vs {error, **payload}; 500 bodies differ by verb).
acceptance_criteria: Declarative (method, pattern) -> handler table with write/live-only/workspace-allowed flags; one entry point applies Host/Origin, token and body parsing; the allowlist is derived from the table; explicit POST /api/clear_conversations; one error envelope {error, code, details}. A test enumerates the table and asserts every route is gated; unknown write paths -> 405; existing route tests pass unchanged.
notes:
Triage (2026-09-29): priority=P2; cost=medium; risk=medium. P2 because the current shape makes an ungated verb or an accidental destructive fall-through a one-line mistake. Medium cost; medium risk (wide surface, but well covered by route tests).
Design options (2026-09-29, from read-only survey): current = 5 verb methods each repeating Host+token; non-allowlisted writes 405 BEFORE auth; POST allowlist (2578-2619) duplicated by dispatch; clear_conversations is the POST fallthrough. ~90 routes; no test enumerates routes. Lower-risk plan: (0) characterization test first - generated status matrix (method x sample path x {no token, bad host, ok}) pinned as golden, so any behaviour change is visible; (1) one _gate() chokepoint called once per request, preserving today's order (405-before-auth) - tiny diff; (2) route table for WRITE verbs only (~15 routes); allowlist derived from the table so 405 and dispatch cannot diverge; clear_conversations gets an explicit entry; GET router (_handle_api, already one function) and selection_api internal dispatch untouched. Estimated: cost medium->low, risk medium->low. Changing 405-before-auth to auth-first is a separate behaviour decision.
Owner decision (2026-09-30): Option B - auth first for every request (Host, then token, then routing/405). Do it as a separate step AFTER the behaviour-neutral route-table refactor, so the characterization matrix shows exactly which cells move (405 -> 401/403 only for requests lacking a valid token or with a bad Host).
close_reason: One _gate() chokepoint (Host/Origin then token) used by GET and every write verb; 18-row write route table (13 POST, 1 PUT, 2 DELETE, 2 PATCH) from which the 405 set is derived; clear_conversations is an explicit row; workspace refusals encoded per row (allowed_in_workspace). Owner decision Option B applied as a separate step: unknown writes without a valid token / from a bad Host or Origin now 401/403 instead of 405 (60 cells). tests/test_run_chatbot_route_matrix.py pins 198 routes x 4 conditions (live, workspace, cold servers); step-1 matrix unchanged. HEAD/OPTIONS stay 501 (answered by BaseHTTPRequestHandler before any verb). Targeted files + browser gate 42/42 green; full suite not run (user instruction).

title: /api/navigation ships every turn's full row and is rebuilt and fully re-rendered on every entry to debug mode
description: navigation.read_source pages ALL experiments, conversations and turns (_pages, 500 at a time, no cap), and build_navigation keeps the full row dict as `info` on every node. Measured on the ido store: 1,356,427 bytes for 165 turns (~8 KB per turn; ~80 MB at 10k turns), 0.05 s server-side. SPA: setTopMode('debug') -> refreshAll -> refreshConvs -> renderHierarchy, which clears and rebuilds the whole rail (index.html 2770-2772, 10922); openTurnInDebug from chat takes this path every time; findHierarchy is a full DFS called once per experiment row (8353-8357), O(rows x nodes).
design: Design review. Options: (a) slim turn/conversation node info to the keys the SPA reads from hierarchy nodes (grep node.info usage) and fetch the rest on selection (already happens via /api/turn); (b) ETag of the body + If-None-Match -> 304, and the SPA skips re-render when unchanged; (c) index hierarchy by key/experiment_id client-side instead of per-row findHierarchy DFS; (d) lazy/paged children: high cost/risk, deferred. Chosen a+b+c. Acceptance: ido-store payload < 150 KB; unchanged refresh -> 304 and no rail rebuild; browser_validation gate green.
acceptance_criteria: Navigation payload < 100 KB on the ido store (node detail fetched on selection; turns lazily paged under their conversation); unchanged refresh answers 304 via an ETag derived from store state; rail render bounded with 10k synthetic turns in a browser check.
notes: Triage (2026-09-29): priority=P2; cost=medium; risk=medium. Fast today only because the store is small; linear growth in bytes and DOM. Medium risk: the rail's selection/alignment logic is intricate and race-tested.
close_reason: Navigation: turn-node info slimmed to status/started_at (other node kinds keep full info shown in the detail pane), ETag/304, SPA skips rail rebuild on 304, hierarchy index replaces per-row walk. ido payload 1,356,427 -> 371,485 bytes (rest is conversation summaries, benchmark manifests, experiment rows). Verified with targeted test files only; full suite not run (user instruction, 2026-09-29).

title: run_chatbot hides its own failures: access log suppressed, no logger.exception, 500 bodies carry only the exception class name
description: server.py:2100 `log_message` -> pass. `rg 'logger\.(exception|error)|exc_info|traceback'` finds nothing in server.py or selection_api.py. do_GET/do_POST/do_PUT/do_PATCH answer `internal error: {type(exc).__name__}` (e.g. 2192-2196, 2539-2542); do_DELETE answers a fixed sentence with no type (2625-2626); selection_api._guard maps known errors but unexpected ones bubble to those handlers. So a developer sees 'internal error: KeyError' in the UI and nothing in the terminal -- in the tool whose job is observability. There is also no request timing anywhere, which is why the turn-list latency went unnoticed.
design: Design review: logger.exception in every outer do_* handler with method + path (token query param redacted) + short error id also returned in the 500 JSON; opt-in access log (env FASTWORKFLOW_CHATBOT_ACCESS_LOG=1) with status + duration, off by default so the terminal banner stays quiet. No behaviour change for success paths. Cost low, risk low. Done together with fix-hzux.9 (same plumbing).
acceptance_criteria: An injected exception in a GET, POST and DELETE handler each logs one traceback with method, route and an error id; the 500 JSON carries the same error id; an opt-in access log records status and duration; the bearer token never appears in any log line (test).
notes: Triage (2026-09-29): priority=P2; cost=low; risk=low. Low cost (outer handlers only), low risk, high diagnostic value.
close_reason: logger.exception with token redaction + error_id in 500 JSON; opt-in access log FASTWORKFLOW_CHATBOT_ACCESS_LOG=1 (token redacted). Verified with targeted test files only; full suite not run (user instruction, 2026-09-29).

title: Spawned FastAPI server and train logs are unreachable from the UI; messages point at 'the terminal' or 'the workflow state directory'
description: launcher.spawn_server (launcher.py:147) Popens the server with the chatbot's inherited stdio, so its logs interleave with the chatbot's terminal. UI copy: index.html 11237-11239 'check the chatbot's terminal for its logs', 12652-12653 (server not ready), 11079-11081 'Training failed -- see the train log in the workflow state directory.' with no path, although start_train already returns log_path (server.py:2061-2067). When the chatbot was launched from an IDE task, via wslview/powershell, or its terminal was closed, the evidence for 'why did my server die' is gone.
acceptance_criteria: Spawned server output goes to a bounded log under the workflow state dir; token-gated GET /api/logs/{server,train}?tail=N returns bounded, secret-redacted text; server-stopped / not-ready banners and the picker's training status offer 'View log' plus the absolute path. Integration test: kill the spawned server and read its tail through the API.
notes: Triage (2026-09-29): priority=P2; cost=medium; risk=low. Medium cost (new endpoint + UI + redaction); low risk (additive).
close_reason: Spawned server output -> <workflow state dir>/server.log (previous spawn kept as server.log.1); token-gated GET /api/logs/{server,train}?tail=N (default 200, max 2000, last 1 MiB, {path,exists,lines,truncated}), redacted via store.Redactor + token/Bearer/secret KEY=value masking; View log + absolute path on server-stopped, not-ready, spawn-failure and training-failure UI. Test kills a real spawned child and reads its tail via the API. Verified with targeted test files + browser gate (42/42); full suite not run (user instruction).

title: Spawned FastAPI server is orphaned when run_chatbot exits uncleanly (SIGHUP, SIGKILL, crash); next launch silently moves ports
description: spawn_server uses start_new_session=True (launcher.py:147), so terminal signals never reach the child; run_chatbot_main handles SIGTERM only (server.py:4549-4555), and SIGHUP (closing the terminal or WSL window) or SIGKILL/OOM skip the finally that calls terminate_server. No pid file is written for the server (only for train), and run_fastapi_mcp has no parent-liveness check (rg getppid/PDEATHSIG: none). The orphan keeps the workflow's API keys loaded, keeps serving unsigned dev JWTs on loopback, and holds ~700 MB (the live child on this box: 695 MB RSS). The next launch finds 8000 busy and _free_server_port moves to an ephemeral port with only a log line, so orphans accumulate unseen.
design: Design review. Options: (a) handle SIGHUP like SIGTERM in run_chatbot_main: trivial; (b) parent-death watch in the spawned server: hidden --parent_pid arg on run_fastapi_mcp; a daemon thread exits the server when os.getppid() changes or the pid disappears (portable; avoids preexec_fn/prctl, which is unsafe in the threaded chatbot); (c) server pid file + reaping stale servers on next activate. (b) covers SIGKILL/OOM/crash, so (c) is redundant. Chosen: (a)+(b); (c) dropped to cut cost. Risk low: arg is additive and hidden.
acceptance_criteria: Tests: SIGHUP and SIGKILL of the chatbot leave no run_fastapi_mcp child within 10 s (parent-pid watch or PR_SET_PDEATHSIG); a stale server pid file (pid + start time, same format as the train pid file) from a dead chatbot is reaped on the next activate.
notes:
Triage (2026-09-29): priority=P2; cost=low; risk=low. Low cost (signal handler + parent watch + pid file), low risk.
Follow-up (2026-09-29): the test-shaped time.sleep branch is gone; tests skip the wait via spawn option startup_probe_seconds=0. Retry path now uses _spawn_and_probe/_child_exited_message instead of a duplicated nested block. The close reason's 'left as-is' remark is superseded.
close_reason: FastAPI child gets --parent_pid and self-terminates when the chatbot dies (parent_watch.py); SIGHUP handled like SIGTERM; one ephemeral-port retry on startup collision. Left as-is (readability, out of scope): _child_survived_startup has a branch shaped around tests patching time.sleep. Verified with targeted test files only; full suite not run (user instruction, 2026-09-29).

title: [review] Adversarial review of run_chatbot observability UI/UX (2026-09-29)
description:
Adversarial review of `fastworkflow run_chatbot` (run_chatbot/server.py 4,565 lines, selection_api.py 2,836, navigation.py 153, launcher.py 504, static/index.html 13,042) across seven concerns: functionality/UI/UX, performance, latency, reliability, modularity/reuse, readability, and deployment for its intended audience (product/dev/test only, never serving the workflow to end users; so auth hardening beyond loopback+token is out of scope, but lifecycle, logs and operability on dev boxes are in scope).

Measured 2026-09-29 on the working tree of feat/experiment-observability-3.3 against the owner's real store ~/.local/state/fastworkflow/workflows/ido_workflow/observability.sqlite3 (615 MB: 165 turns, 50,807 spans, 505 MB of span attribute JSON), through an in-process ChatbotServer opened read-only.

Headline: the debug rail's turn list costs O(all span bytes in the store) per request (6 s at 165 turns; 49-59 s each under 4 concurrent requests), and the tool hides its own failures (no server-side exception logging; spawned server/train logs unreachable from the UI). Children carry evidence, fix direction and acceptance; each records priority, cost and risk.
acceptance_criteria: All children closed or explicitly deferred with a reason.
notes: Triage (2026-09-29): priority=P2; cost=high; risk=medium. Aggregate of the children; the P1 child is the only one blocking daily use on real stores.
close_reason: All 18 review issues resolved (17 fixed, fix-hzux.18 decided 'no'). Verified with targeted test files and the browser gate throughout; the full suite was not run at the user's instruction.

title: Move chat input tip into Tip tooltip beside Send

title: Cold resume: offload archive opened from an empty workflow path (database named after the cwd)
description: Found 2026-09-28 by the fix-hfbr implementer; affects the DEFAULT path. build_tool_agent ran inside apply_serialized_state before any app workflow was active, so state_paths.observability_db('') resolved to <state_root>/workflows/<cwd basename>/observability.sqlite3. After a cold resume, pre-suspension evidence was invisible (search_memory misses, rehydration can't resolve labels) and post-resume evidence went to the stray DB (erasure never reaches it). Unaffected when FASTWORKFLOW_WORKFLOW_ID is set. Fixed: agent.py build_tool_agent reads the session's bound app_workflow.folderpath first, falling back to the active workflow; covered by tests/test_plan_resume.py test_a_context_resuming_a_suspended_turn_archives_in_the_workflows_own_database.

The agent ReAct loop (and intent clarification) use CommandsSystemPreludeAdapter with DSPy's default use_json_adapter_fallback=True; on a parse failure DSPy retries with a plain JSONAdapter that does not inject the available-commands prelude (fastworkflow/utils/chat_adapter.py ~58-61; dspy 3.3.0 chat_adapter.py:76-94; agent adapter at workflow_execution_context.py ~1813). title: Close integration-test gaps for the planner, plan lifecycle, real SDK errors and listing edge cases
description:
Found in adversarial review of 01b0d64 (fix-ufot follow-up) and 43e42a2 (fix-4dsr). Priority P2 | Cost medium | Risk medium (risk = impact of leaving it unfixed). Not fixed yet.
Review item: E53. Commits: 01b0d64, 43e42a2. Concerns: reliability, robustness, code-org. Related: fix-4dsr (43e42a2, finish-time plan check); fix-ufot (01b0d64, search_memory follow-up).

Evidence: no test calls build_query_with_next_steps structured/fallback, _turn_plan clear/keep logic (workflow_agent.py:765-827), workflow_command_names, or checker_from_env returning a real checker; no assertion of finish_check_note on step spans; loop tests monkeypatch internals (test_react_suspend_resume.py:243-252 _FixedChecker/_BrokenChecker); test_finish_check.py uses _ScriptedClient + unittest.mock.patch (:16,51-69,250-256) and plain TimeoutError, never SDK exception types — mock-like, against the no-mocks policy; listing tests cover only a 3-row ido fixture, basic markdown/tab, and one ambiguity case that passes by accident (tests/test_observation_search.py:545-663); served_rows bounds tested only with 1-digit totals (:560-565). E34–E38 all pass current tests.
Fix direction: todo_list_workflow integration test with check on/off, a local HTTP stub of the Jev endpoint, ask_user resume; planner fallback tests; listing edge-case tests (wrapped/empty-cell/single-space rows, groups, footers, E35 case, ≥100 rows at every budget, oversized preamble, timing guard).
notes: 2026-09-27 design (owner accepted all recommendations): Work package WP1 slice 1 (TypeSafe/Jev client hardening + loopback Jev stub fixture; with fix-oivq, fix-conv, fix-2so9, fix-qgeu, fix-em0l) and WP6 slice 3 (plan/ledger survive cross-process resume + not-run steps; with fix-ju1v, fix-lnzw). Recommended design: slice 1: loopback Jev stub fixture (ThreadingHTTPServer on port 0 speaking POST /v1/systemone with scriptable answers, error envelopes and delays, recording request bodies; must swallow client disconnects) + 4 tests: note fires; timeout fails open with reason="error"; request body contains only redacted text; E14 envelope as strict xfail. No production code, ~150 LOC. Slice 2: dspy DummyLM planner tests + _turn_plan lifecycle. Slice 3: cross-process + E16 dispatch tests on a real WorkflowExecutionContext on todo_list. Slice 4: listing edge cases with E34/E35/E37 (or strict xfails until then). Cost low (slice 1; slice 3 medium), implementation risk low, residual risk medium for E53 overall after slice 1, low after slice 3. Accepted decisions: E53: loopback HTTP stand-in for TypeSafe and dspy DummyLM for planner tests are acceptable under the no-mocks rule; E29: validated FW_JEV_BASE_URL with loopback http allowed (the harness binds through it). Evidence/measurements: partly addressed (test_jev_client.py, test_turn_plan.py are new); every build_query_with_next_steps caller in tests is monkeypatched away; no coverage of the _turn_plan lifecycle, real SDK error types, or the note on step spans; _ScriptedClient and patch remain in test_finish_check.py. Prototype /tmp/e53_jev_stub.py with the real SDK and FinishChecker: happy path fires a note; slow response raises real TypeSafeAPITimeoutError and fails open; a 400 with a message raises TypeSafeBadRequestError whose str() lacks max_tokens_exceeded (E14 reproduced live). The error envelope is a guess; one real capture should pin it. Test plan: the slices above. Dependencies/merge: slice 1 lands with WP1; slice 3 with fix-ju1v and fix-lnzw (WP6); slice 4 with the WP8 listing series.
close_reason: Implemented per the accepted 2026-09-27 design (work packages WP1-WP11), uncommitted in the working tree. Verified by an independent adversarial verifier (two rounds): meets design; ido replays unchanged (refers_to 0/5,056 rows differ; strict listing parser: 494 ido listings still served, all 1,974 new refusals legitimate). Targeted test files only (39 files, all passing, network blocked); full suite not run per owner instruction. See CHANGELOG 3.4.0.

title: Cap the search evidence bound and add an override independent of FW_MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS
description:
Found in adversarial review of 01b0d64 (fix-ufot follow-up) and 43e42a2 (fix-4dsr). Priority P2 | Cost low | Risk medium (risk = impact of leaving it unfixed). Not fixed yet.
Review item: E42. Commits: 01b0d64. Concerns: performance, scalability, deployability. Related: fix-ufot (01b0d64, search_memory follow-up).

Evidence: search.py:78-84 fraction=Fraction(1,4), override_env=None; search.py:118-119 FW_MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS takes precedence over the search model's window; search call timeout=120 (:883-884); justification only ido data (:73-75).
Failure: 1M-token search model → ~1 MB (~260k tokens) per search, repeated per call (tens of seconds, real $); a large agent window declared via FW_MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS with a small search model makes large searches hit the over-window refusal ~10× more often; digit-dense text can fill the window.
Fix direction: absolute ceiling (e.g. 128 KB) + override env var; resolve the search window independently.
notes: 2026-09-27 design (owner accepted all recommendations): Work package WP10 (Evidence-bound ceiling; standalone). Recommended design: option A + B in context_budget.py. A: cap the derived value in search_observation_max_bytes at a ceiling of 131,072 B; add FW_SEARCH_OBSERVATION_MAX_BYTES as the spec's override_env (spec at :213-219, override_env=None at :216; budget_bytes already handles parsing, the floor and warnings); an explicit override may exceed the ceiling; report it in budget_provenance overrides; docs and an env-template line. B: window = min(FW_MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS, search model metadata) when both are known (today the setting wins, :317-318). ~25 LOC. Cost low, implementation risk low, residual risk after fix low. Accepted decisions: E42: ceiling 131,072 B + FW_SEARCH_OBSERVATION_MAX_BYTES override (may exceed ceiling); window = min(FW_MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS, search model metadata). Modify (not remove) the tests pinning 'no override' / window scaling. Evidence/measurements (real litellm metadata): mistral-small-latest (example config) window 262,144 -> bound 262,144 B, twice the documented 131,072; gpt-4.1 1,047,576 -> ~1 MB; FW_MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS=1M with gpt-4o-mini search -> 1,000,000 B sent to a 128k-token model. Default path gets cheaper: with the example model the bound halves, so 128-256 KB observations are searched as a prefix with the existing bounded-evidence marker; no recorded ido observation exceeds 5.4 KB. Search call timeout still 120 s (search.py:972). Test plan: modify tests/test_observation_search.py:262-284 (no tuning override; 4x and 2x window scaling) and the 'no tuning override' docstring; tests/test_context_budget.py:240-252 (gpt-4o-mini 128,000 stays under the ceiling); add ceiling, override-above-ceiling and min-window cases. Dependencies/merge: none; note the listing parser reads the full archived text regardless of this bound (fix-n4z9).
close_reason: Implemented per the accepted 2026-09-27 design (work packages WP1-WP11), uncommitted in the working tree. Verified by an independent adversarial verifier (two rounds): meets design; ido replays unchanged (refers_to 0/5,056 rows differ; strict listing parser: 494 ido listings still served, all 1,974 new refusals legitimate). Targeted test files only (39 files, all passing, network blocked); full suite not run per owner instruction. See CHANGELOG 3.4.0.

title: Enforce the answer bound in served_rows
description:
Found in adversarial review of 01b0d64 (fix-ufot follow-up) and 43e42a2 (fix-4dsr). Priority P2 | Cost low | Risk medium (risk = impact of leaving it unfixed). Not fixed yet.
Review item: E38. Commits: 01b0d64. Concerns: features, scalability. Related: fix-ufot (01b0d64, search_memory follow-up).

Evidence: listing.py:126 head joins preamble + columns with no size limit; :135-136 reserves only max(closing(0), closing(total)); callers search.py:818-826. Reproduced: 5 KB preamble, 3,000 B budget → 5,162 B output ending "rows 1-0 of the 2 rows … rows 1-2 are NOT shown"; intermediate closings like "1-99 … rows 100-100" overran 2,792 budgets by up to 4 B; a single oversized row yields a zero-row answer with no model fallback. Search observations are never offloaded (search.py:39-43), so the overrun persists in every later segment.
Fix direction: bound/trim preamble; reserve widest closing; fall back to the model path when zero rows fit.
notes: 2026-09-27 design (owner accepted all recommendations): Work package WP8 (Listing parser series; step 3 together with fix-k56c (E36), after fix-zoup + fix-n4z9 and fix-36gv, before fix-1593 widening). Recommended design: option A. After the row loop in served_rows, drop rows until head + rows + the real closing line fits the budget; return None when zero rows fit or the head alone exceeds the budget, so search.py:900 falls through to the search-model path. ~15 LOC in listing.py + ~5 in search.py. Cost low, implementation risk low (the fallback is today's default path), residual risk after fix low. Default path: none (router-on only). Accepted decisions: no E38-specific owner decision was needed; WP8 order: E35+E37, then E34, then E36+E38, then E46 widening. Evidence/measurements (/tmp/medrisk_e38.py): preamble unbounded (listing.py:128): a 5 KB preamble against a 3,000 B budget produced 5,410 B with 'rows 1-0 of the 2 rows'; closing reservation (:135-137) takes max(closing(0), closing(total)) but intermediate closings are wider, worst overrun 3 B over a sweep; a single row larger than the budget produced 130 B with 0 of 2 rows and no fallback. served_over_bound telemetry (search.py:910) records an overrun but does not prevent it. title: Remove the quadratic parse_table cost from every search (and skip it when the router is off)
description:
Found in adversarial review of 01b0d64 (fix-ufot follow-up) and 43e42a2 (fix-4dsr). Priority P2 | Cost low | Risk medium (risk = impact of leaving it unfixed). Not fixed yet.

Evidence: search.py:814 parse_table runs unconditionally; result used only `if (router and table)` (:815-816); listing.py:104-106 rescans following rows from every index. Measured: 26 KB 0.79 s, 52 KB 3.4 s, 104 KB 13.2 s CPU on the agent thread; reachable given the ~131 KB evidence bound.
Failure: default deployments (router off) pay seconds of CPU per search on large observations.
Fix direction: skip when router is None; single-pass parse or cap input; stop at first ambiguity (E35).
notes: 2026-09-27 design (owner accepted all recommendations): Work package WP8 (Listing parser series; step 1 together with fix-zoup (E35); then fix-36gv, then fix-k56c + fix-3zxk, then fix-1593 widening). Recommended design: option A plus the cheap half of B. Make a refusal final: a candidate that refuses after accepting at least one row ends the whole parse with None, via a REFUSED sentinel in the three _*_at helpers handled in parse_table (listing.py:106-110). ~15 LOC, listing.py only. Also move table = parse_table(...) below the short-observation check (search.py:882 vs :883). Cost low, implementation risk low (only turns wrong accepts into refusals), residual risk after fix low. Default path: ~3 ms of telemetry parsing. Accepted decisions: E37: done together with E35 (refusal-final parser) + parse after the short-observation check. Evidence/measurements: timings at 26/52/104 KB: well-formed listings ~1/2/3 ms; aligned listing refused at its last line 0.22/0.81/2.97 s; short 2-cell lines refused at the end 1.1/4.0/14.2 s; refusal-final prototype 1.5/1.6/3.8 ms. The parser reads the full archived handle['text'], not the 131 KB read bound (with mistral-small-latest the bound is already 262,144 B), so cost is unbounded; a 512 KB pathological observation extrapolates to minutes of CPU on the agent thread. Over 4,000 random listings: 3,843 identical, 157 differ, all where the current code picked a header inside an earlier candidate's row span (the E35 bug). Without the 'at least one accepted row' condition, 545 differ (a legitimate 'Account  Alan' preamble is refused). On the router-off path the result is used only for telemetry (listing_parsed, listing_shape). Test plan: extend the ShortObservationsAndServedRows test class at this step, including the pathological inputs. Dependencies/merge: same change as fix-zoup (E35), first in the WP8 series. The skip-when-router-off stopgap is not needed since E35 lands together.

title: Budget and cap the total vendor latency added per turn
description:
Found in adversarial review of 01b0d64 (fix-ufot follow-up) and 43e42a2 (fix-4dsr). Priority P2 | Cost medium | Risk medium (risk = impact of leaving it unfixed). Not fixed yet.
Review item: E23. Commits: 01b0d64, 43e42a2. Concerns: performance, scalability. Related: fix-4dsr (43e42a2, finish-time plan check); fix-ufot (01b0d64, search_memory follow-up).

Evidence: router runs on every search_memory over a parsed listing with no per-turn cap (search.py:805-816); finish check once per turn (react.py:554) but see E06; FastAPI turns run on the default executor (run_fastapi_mcp/turns.py:625).
Failure: worst case ≈ +8.4 s first plan (+3.7 s fallback) + N×≥2 s routing + ≥8 s check + replan cost (E07), each holding a shared worker thread, reducing concurrency; docs give only per-call numbers.
Fix direction: one per-turn vendor time budget shared by all calls; cap routing calls per turn; record added latency in the turn record.
notes: 2026-09-27 design (owner accepted all recommendations): Work package WP3 (One per-turn vendor budget with hard cutoff; with fix-i94q). Recommended design: option B. Add jev_client.TurnBudget tracking remaining vendor seconds (time actually spent in calls, not wall-clock since turn start) plus a routing count; slice(cap) returns a deadline of now + min(cap, remaining) and the time used is subtracted afterwards. The budget lives on the agent and is replaced when the continuation scope changes (scope-binding path in continuation.py ~318); a resume after ask_user keeps the scope and budget. The router closure (agent.py:322) and FinishChecker.note reach it. After the routing cap, record listing_skip_reason="router_budget" and use the search model (default-path behaviour). Record cumulative vendor_ms on the router verdict and the finish_check event. ~50 LOC across jev_client, search.py, search_router, finish_check, agent.py, continuation.py. No budget created when router and checker are both off. Cost medium, implementation risk low, residual risk after fix low. Accepted decisions: E06/E23: hard cutoff via bounded worker pool of 4; router cap 3 calls/turn; finish check 8 s; per-turn vendor total 10 s; cumulative vendor_ms on events. Evidence/measurements: the router runs on every search_memory over a parsed listing with no per-turn count (search.py:897-898); one router per agent (agent.py:310); turns run on the default executor (run_fastapi_mcp/turns.py:625); each feature has only its own per-call/per-check limit. Test plan: same local server; five searches over listings produce at most 3 fw.search.route spans and router_budget skip reasons after that; a slow router plus a check does not exceed the turn total. Dependencies/merge: built together with fix-i94q (shares its budget object).

title: Route decision-model features through a provider interface / LLM role instead of hard-wiring one vendor
description:

Review item: E22. Commits: 01b0d64, 43e42a2. Concerns: generalizability, code-org. Related: fix-4dsr (43e42a2, finish-time plan check); fix-ufot (01b0d64, search_memory follow-up).

Evidence: direct vendor SDK imports and types (search_router.py:35,91-92,152; finish_check.py:52,187-230,268); only accepted value "jev" (search_router.py:44, finish_check.py:65); planner behaviour gated on the vendor (workflow_agent.py:790). Everywhere else models are LLM_<ROLE> + LITELLM_API_KEY_<ROLE> with litellm_proxy routing.
Failure: cannot use LiteLLM proxy, self-hosted models or approved-vendor lists; users who cannot send data to TypeSafe lose both features and the structured plan.
Fix direction: small decision-provider interface; Jev as one implementation; LiteLLM/DSPy implementation under an LLM_DECISION role; decouple structured planning from provider.
notes: 2026-09-27 design (owner accepted all recommendations): Work package WP12 (Provider interface stages 1-2; standalone, after WP1). Recommended design: stage 1: new decision.py (~60 LOC) with neutral YesNo(instructions, true, false) and OneOf(instructions, criteria) questions and ask(state, questions) -> {key: p | (choice, probs)}; neutral errors StateTooLarge (E14 logic moves into the adapter) and ProviderFailure(status, request_id, code) reusing E20's describe_failure; a Jev adapter in jev_client (~40 LOC) building byte-identical Noul/Choice objects; ~60 LOC of mechanical changes in finish_check and search_router. Stage 2: register_decision_provider(name, factory) called from code only (no module path in an env var); the flag accepts registered names (~30 LOC). Stage 3 (LiteLLM/DSPy provider under an LLM_DECISION role) deferred. Cost low-medium (stage 1 about a day; stage 2 low; stage 3 would be high), implementation risk low given the golden test, residual risk medium after stage 1 alone, low after stage 2. Accepted decisions: E22: stop at stage 2 (DecisionProvider interface with Jev adapter + golden request-body test; then register_decision_provider from code only); defer LiteLLM stage 3. Evidence/measurements: vendor question types built directly (finish_check.py:60, 202-245; search_router.py:37, 82-89); results read as .noul/.choice/.probabilities; only 'jev' accepted as a flag value (jev_client.py:70); planner mode depends on the vendor (workflow_agent.py:810). Decoupling structured planner mode alone is not worth it (no consumer without a check, ~3x planner latency). Docs caveat: FLAG_MIN/ASK_MIN and precision/recall are Jev-calibrated; stage 3 needs re-measurement on the 910 step-subject pairs and 180 router questions. Test plan: golden request-body test: capture the bodies the loopback fixture receives for fixed inputs before the refactor and assert identical afterwards. Dependencies/merge: build after the WP1 jev_client hardening PR so E14/E20 move into the adapter without rework. A provider should declare whether it is third-party so E05's gate (fix-7tz5) can skip self-hosted providers later.
close_reason: Stages 1-2 implemented (WP12) and verified: decision.py protocol + JevProvider + code-only registration; golden request-body tests prove byte-identical Jev requests. Stage 3 (LiteLLM provider, recalibration) split out to fix-jwce.

title: Persist _turn_plan across cross-process ask_user resume, or record distinct no-plan reasons
description:

Recommended design: option B (includes A). Declare _turn_plan and _turn_plan_status in WorkflowExecutionContext.__init__ (:159-166) with causes planner_empty, plan_unreadable, lost_on_resume, not_planned; the event keeps reason "no plan" and adds no_plan_cause. In import_suspended, seed current_trajectory from the stash when the mirror is empty and a checker is attached. title: Bound finish-check question count and ledger size so large multi-subject turns are still checked
description:
Found in adversarial review of 01b0d64 (fix-ufot follow-up) and 43e42a2 (fix-4dsr). Priority P2 | Cost medium | Risk medium (risk = impact of leaving it unfixed). Not fixed yet.
Review item: E09. Commits: 43e42a2. Concerns: performance, scalability. Related: fix-4dsr (43e42a2, finish-time plan check).

Evidence: scope questions = steps × (1 + subjects × (1 + parts)) (finish_check.py:323-329), execution similar (:333-347); QUESTIONS_PER_REQUEST=100 resends the whole ledger with every chunk (:279-282); ledger halving multiplies calls (:289-292). 6 steps × 40 subjects → 492 questions, 6 requests.
Failure: audits over dozens of subjects hit OutOfTime and fail open — exactly the turns most likely to have missed steps; tokens grow with chunks × ledger.
Fix direction: cap subjects/pairs, settle scope deterministically where possible, bound ledger by bytes, record a "too large" reason.
notes: 2026-09-27 design (owner accepted all recommendations): Work package WP5 (Subject cap with step-level fallback; standalone). Recommended design: option B in finish_check.py. Above SUBJECTS_MAX = 12, check with subjects dropped: only 'does step k need a command?' and 'was step k executed at all?' (2 x steps questions; both wordings are in the measured set and caught every wholly-missed step); record reason "subjects capped" with the count. Add a ledger byte cap trimming head, then refers_to, from the oldest rows first. Allow at most one split. ~30 LOC. Cost low-medium, implementation risk low (deterministic, measured wordings only, affects only turns over the caps), residual risk after fix low-medium (per-subject misses on large turns not caught; option C would reach low). Accepted decisions: E09: SUBJECTS_MAX = 12; above it check step-level only (reason 'subjects capped'); ledger byte cap; at most one split. Option C (per-subject for least-traced subjects) only if data shows many large turns. Evidence/measurements: questions = steps x (1 + subjects x (1 + parts)) (:346-354, :356-373), sent in chunks of 100 each resending the whole ledger (:76, :300-303), splits multiply (:305-313). 6 steps x 40 subjects: 492 questions in 6 requests; the fallback: 12 questions in 2 requests. The 118 recorded attempts (cache_v7) all had 9 subjects and up to 27 steps: at most 2 requests, median 0.5 s, max 0.72 s, max 54k input tokens; latency tracks input tokens (r=0.84, ~13 us/token), not question count (r=0.29). Main real impact is token cost; ~1.5-2.5 s expected for 40 subjects vs 8 s (unverified; no data above 9 subjects). One live check on a 30+-subject recorded turn would settle time vs cost. Test plan: local-server integration test with a 40-subject plan; assert question count <= 2 x steps, reason == "subjects capped", completion within budget, ledger no larger than the byte cap. Dependencies/merge: must use E06's deadline (WP3, fix-i94q). Interacts with E02/E04 (fewer subject names leave); does not touch E15's recall gap.

title: Enforce real wall-clock bounds on vendor calls (router 2 s, finish check 4 s/call, 8 s/check)
description:
Found in adversarial review of 01b0d64 (fix-ufot follow-up) and 43e42a2 (fix-4dsr). Priority P2 | Cost medium | Risk medium (risk = impact of leaving it unfixed). Not fixed yet.
Review item: E06. Commits: 01b0d64, 43e42a2. Concerns: performance, reliability. Related: fix-4dsr (43e42a2, finish-time plan check); fix-ufot (01b0d64, search_memory follow-up).

Evidence: finish_check.py:265-267 deadline checked only before each call; TypeSafeClient(timeout=4.0) (finish_check.py:448-450) and search_router.py:189-193 pass a scalar to httpx (per-phase connect/read/write/pool, read resets per chunk, DNS not covered; typesafe_sdk _core/client/sync/client.py:87, _core/transport.py:154-156); build_ledger (finish_check.py:389-390) runs before the deadline starts. Simulation: budget 0.8 s / 0.39 s per call took 1.17 s (scaled ≈11.7 s). docs/observation_search.md:524 states 8 s as the whole-check budget.
Failure: slow/trickling endpoint or DNS stall holds the turn thread well past the documented bounds; fail-open path can add >12 s per turn; router can do so on every search.
Fix direction: per-call timeout = min(4 s, remaining budget); start budget before ledger build; httpx.Timeout with overall deadline or hard wall-clock cutoff; correct docs.
notes: 2026-09-27 design (owner accepted all recommendations): Work package WP3 (One per-turn vendor budget with hard cutoff; with fix-sotm). Recommended design: option B (includes A). A: per-call timeout = min(cap, time left) via system_one(timeout=...), and start the deadline before build_ledger. B: hard cutoff jev_client.call_within(client, seconds, **kw): run the request on a small process-wide worker pool, wait future.result(timeout=seconds), on timeout abandon it and fail open; a non-blocking semaphore makes a saturated pool fail at once ('vendor busy') instead of queueing. ~40 LOC in jev_client plus call-site changes in FinishChecker._call and SearchRouter._decide (~15 + ~5 LOC). Cost low-medium, implementation risk low (opt-in paths only, fail-open, httpx2 client already shared across threads), residual risk after fix low. Accepted decisions: E06/E23: hard cutoff via bounded worker pool of 4; router cap 3 calls/turn; finish check 8 s; per-turn vendor total 10 s; cumulative vendor_ms on events. Evidence/measurements (typesafe_sdk 0.7.2, httpx2 2.9.1, 1.0 s budget, local slow server): httpx2 Timeout has only connect/read/write/pool limits. Server silent 3 s -> 1.00 s; body in 12 slices 0.5 s apart -> 6.00 s and succeeds (also with per-call Timeout(0.8)); DNS stall -> 3.00 s; real FinishChecker with 0.45 s calls -> 1.45 s, 0.9 s calls -> 1.89 s, trickle -> 6.01 s. Prototype held every case, trickle and DNS included, to 0.99-1.00 s. Known side effect: an abandoned request still finishes vendor-side and is billed. docs/observation_search.md:588-591 still understates the bound. Test plan: ThreadingHTTPServer fixture in stall/trickle/delay modes; assert FinishChecker.note() and SearchRouter.route() return within budget + 0.2 s and fail open with the right error_type. Dependencies/merge: one change with fix-sotm (time left comes from the turn budget). Tests bind the SDK to the local server via the explicit/validated base URL from fix-2so9 (WP1), not TYPESAFE_BASE_URL.

description:

Evidence: with FW_OBS_CAPTURE_PROFILE=evidence, capture_record_for returns {"__fw_capture__": true, "classification": "opaque-payload", "disposition": "omit", …} (store.py:820-826); neither search_router.py nor finish_check.py detects this.

Fix direction: detect withheld fields, fail open with reason `policy_withheld`; warn once at client construction.
notes: 2026-09-27 design (owner accepted all recommendations): Work package WP2 (Outbound filter; with fix-hu4f). Recommended design: option C (A + B). Asking the policy directly (not via capture_record_for) also trips when FW_OFFLOAD_EVIDENCE_REDACTION=off. B: jev_client.egress(text) -> str | None returning None for any badge; the router returns error="policy_withheld" and the check fails open with reason policy_withheld. ~40 LOC. title: Finish check: decide what happens to user-gated plan steps when the user never answers
description: From fix-9gy8: the fix-4dsr finish check skips optional and user-gated plan steps by design. In the GTE runs the operator never answers questions, so skipped steps are never done: 16 of the 33 arm-N turns certified 'every step executed' had skipped user-gated steps. Options to evaluate: (a) after an ask_user that was declined or unanswered, re-classify the step as agent-owned and check it; (b) name skipped user-gated steps in the note so the agent either does them or the answer marks them unresolved; (c) leave as is and rely on fix-emzj. Interacts with fix-emzj (fewer user-gated steps) and with the exhaustion-honesty rule (no fabricated fills). Also observed: the agent ignored 11 of 21 fired notes (0 further commands), which bears on the still-open gate-vs-note question. Not started.

title: Finish check: judge whether each plan step was satisfied, not only whether its command ran

Measure offline first on the fix-9gy8 arm-N stores (60 turns, judged). Not started.

title: Offload label and agent instructions promise full restoration at answer time, which the rehydration budget does not guarantee
description:
Found reviewing commit 01b0d64 (fix-ufot follow-up). The offload label (labels.offload_label: 'It is restored in full when the final answer is written, so search it with search_memory only for a value you need for your next step'), the WorkflowAgentSignature docstring ('every observation of this turn is restored in full when the final answer is written ... never to collect rows for the final answer'), the search_memory tool docstring, and served_rows' closing line ('Every row of O<n> is restored in full when the final answer is written') all state full restoration as a guarantee.

answer_rehydration.rehydrate is still a hard byte budget: most recent first, it stops at the first label that does not fit and leaves older observations as labels named in answer_rehydration_note. fix-k6w3 measured the budget binding in 4 of 79 recorded attempts (5.1%, Wilson 95% 2.0-12.3%). In those turns the new wording also tells the agent not to search for report rows, so evidence the agent was told would come back may not.

Options: (1) weaken the wording to 'normally restored' plus a pointer to the note; (2) make it true -- e.g. the fix-k6w3 split/synthesis design, or have the finish step search dropped labels; (3) measure first: re-run fix-k6w3's binding-rate analysis on runs recorded with the new wording, since agents told not to search may produce fewer inline search answers and different trajectory sizes.
notes:
2026-09-28 rating (owner-requested): cost low (wording fix, option 1), risk medium (budget binds in ~5.1% of recorded turns; in those the agent was told evidence returns and not to search for report rows). Making the promise true (option 2) would be high cost.
2026-09-28 decision (orchestrator, under owner's 'fix all low cost/low risk' instruction): options A+B. Agent-visible default-path wording changed WITHOUT re-measurement: label mark 'Normally restored for the final answer.', search_memory description, signature docstring (the 'search only for a value you need next; never to collect rows' instruction restored verbatim), rehydration note prefix telling the extractor to state omitted rows. Residual: in ~5% of turns the answer is still incomplete but says so. A fix-k6w3 re-run would measure the wording's effect.
close_reason: Honest restoration wording (A) + extractor told to state omitted rows (B). Verified by an independent adversarial verifier plus a follow-up fix round; targeted test files only (network blocked), all passing; full suite not run per owner instruction. Uncommitted in the working tree; see CHANGELOG 3.4.0.
