title: Study answer rehydration on recorded runs: is splitting over-budget evidence into parallel extractor trajectories + synthesis worthwhile?
description:
Raised in PR 84 review. Today fastworkflow/answer_rehydration.rehydrate walks offload labels most recent first and STOPS at the first replacement that would exceed the extraction budget (context_budget.answer_rehydration_max_bytes, 250,000 B at the reference window). Everything older stays a label and is named in one answer_rehydration_note line ('Not rehydrated for the answer (evidence exists under these observations): ...'), so the extractor can only report those slots as unresolved.

Proposal (owner): do not stop. When not every label fits, continue into another extractor trajectory, and another, until every archived observation behind a label has been rehydrated in exactly one of them. No observation is rehydrated in more than one trajectory; in each trajectory, observations rehydrated elsewhere stay as their labels with a note like today's naming where their evidence went (e.g. 'Rehydrated in another partial answer: O5, O9'). Run the extract call on each trajectory in parallel to get partial answers, then one synthesis call merges them into the single final answer. When everything fits in one trajectory, behaviour is exactly today's single extract call (no synthesis).

Design points to settle:
- Partitioning: keep most-recent-first order; pack greedily per trajectory under the same budget; the non-label part of the trajectory (thoughts, args, inline observations, search answers) is repeated in every trajectory, so it is paid N times and must be subtracted from each budget. An observation larger than a whole budget on its own still needs the existing overflow/truncation path.
- Notes: each trajectory must say which evidence it holds and which lives in other partials, so a partial reports 'not in my evidence' rather than 'does not exist'. Keep today's note semantics for evidence that is truly unavailable (unresolved).
- Synthesis: a separate signature over the partial answers (and the user query); it must merge rather than paraphrase, sum or union list-style deliverables, surface conflicts between partials, and never present one partial's subset as exhaustive. It is model text over model text, so it must not add facts absent from every partial.
- Output shape: the extract signature may have several output fields; decide how partials map to them and how the synthesiser fills each.
- Cost/latency: N extract calls + 1 synthesis instead of 1; parallel to bound latency; cap N (a deployment setting or derived) and fall back to today's note when the cap is hit.
- Failure: a failed partial must not lose the answer -- synthesise from the rest and name the evidence that went unread, like rehydration_failed today.
- Observability: extend rehydration_finished (partials count, aliases per partial, synthesis tokens/duration); keep the loop's own trajectory untouched as today.
- Evaluation: paired benchmark against the single-trajectory extract on tasks whose evidence exceeds the budget (fastworkflow-research-methodology).

Shared design: this is the same map-reduce shape as design (B) in fix-ufot (split one large observation into chunks, search in parallel, synthesise). Build one shared partition/fan-out/synthesise helper for both rather than two, and settle chunking, note and synthesis rules once.

Wiring: fastWorkflowReAct._rehydrate_for_extract / _extract_prediction (react.py) and StructuredContinuationReAct._finish_prediction (continuation.py) are the single extract path; the copy is built there today.

Risk: medium-high -- changes the final answer path for every long turn; needs the paired benchmark before it ships.
notes:
Correction to the framing above (owner, 2026-09-26): this is RESEARCH, not implementation. Decide, using data from recorded runs, whether the split / parallel-extract / synthesise design is worthwhile, and use the same data to answer the design points listed above. Nothing is to be implemented under this issue; if the data supports it, the outcome is an experiment card (or a documented retirement). fix-ufot is being researched in parallel by another agent; coordinate on the shared map-reduce helper question rather than settling it unilaterally.
FINDINGS 2026-09-26 (research, recorded runs only, $0, no code changed).

DATA. Every IDO benchmark attempt store with answer rehydration on: /home/drawal/rl/ido/evaluation/collections/result-search/*/attempt-*/ (events.jsonl rehydration_finished + the offload-handles archive), 79 attempts in 16 cells, 2026-09-15..16, framework builds 4832b3c..9e5e9d9, cerebras/gpt-oss-120b at the 131,072-token reference window, budget 250,000 B. Slot-level answer judgements from ido/evaluation/artifacts/result-search/*/attempt-N-judgement.json. No other store on this machine holds a real rehydration event (the /tmp/fw-offload-* hits are test fixtures). Demand per attempt = bytes_before + recorded added_bytes of rehydrated aliases + archived size of dropped aliases.

1. HOW OFTEN THE BUDGET BINDS: 4 of 79 attempts (5.1%, Wilson 95% 2.0-12.3%). Demand/budget median 61%, p90 89%, max 127%. Every binding attempt needs exactly 2 partitions; none needs 3. Each attempt has exactly one extract call.

2. WHAT WAS DROPPED, AND WHAT IT COST. Always the oldest observations: navigation lines (open_*, find_* uid lookups, 18-300 B, whose uids the agent restates later) and early enumeration page walks (fetch_result_page / who_has_access_to holder pages, whose conclusion, the count, sits on the last page, which is recent and was rehydrated). Slot-level judgements (3 of 4 binding attempts judged; routing-pinned a3 unjudged): 0 deliverable slots attributable to dropped evidence.
 - rehydrate-pinned a2 (O1..O12 dropped): the two slots fed by dropped O7/O8/O12 (publishing system, feed) were answered CORRECTLY from later restatement; its 18 unresolved slots were never retrieved (judgement: 'a retrieval-time failure, not an answer-time one').
 - scope-neutral-v2 a2 (O1..O5 dropped): O1-O4 are navigation; O5 (23,088 B holder listing) is byte-identical to O13, which was rehydrated. The missing slots were never retrieved.
 - coverage-pinned a1 (O1..O20 dropped): dropped range = Cloud Administrator holder page walk; the holder count slot was correct. Its 'count only, no right named' misses are over O59/O72, which WERE rehydrated -> writer failure, not budget.
So in the recorded runs the proposal's only possible benefit (answers over evidence that was dropped) has zero observed instances.

3. REPEATED (NON-LABEL) PART, the cost every extra partition pays again: bytes_before median 88,601 B (35% of budget), p90 46%, max 66%. In the 4 binding attempts it is 95-165 KB (38-66% of budget), i.e. a second partition re-sends ~40-69k tokens.

4. BYTES PER TOKEN AT EXTRACT TIME: median 2.74 B/token (2.33-3.20), not 4. The 250 KB budget is ~91k tokens median and the largest extract prompt was 103,967 tokens of the 131,072 window. Raising the budget instead of splitting is not safe at this window. (Also relevant to fix-ufot's 4 B/token window-minus-overhead estimate.)

5. COST IF BUILT: extract call median 4.5 s / 55k prompt tokens (p90 8.8 s / 83k). A 2-way split on the ~5% of binding turns adds one parallel extract (~40-69k tokens repeated base + the dropped labels) plus one synthesis call over two partials.

6. CHEAPER DETERMINISTIC ALTERNATIVE: dedupe by archived text digest, not only by alias. 47 of 79 attempts carry byte-identical observations under different aliases (median 1.9 KB, max 30.4 KB); digest dedupe alone would have kept 1 of the 4 binding attempts (scope-neutral-v2 a2) inside the budget. No model call, no synthesis.

DESIGN POINTS, answered where the data reaches:
- Partitioning: N=2 covers every observed case; a cap of 2 loses nothing in this corpus. The repeated base is large (up to 66% of budget), so partition 2's room can be as small as ~85 KB.
- Notes: the dropped half is navigation + superseded page walks, so a second partial would mostly answer 'not in my evidence'. That is exactly the ido-8ps.19 risk of a later round overwriting a correct value with a plausible one from less relevant content.
- Synthesis / output shape / failure: no data. No partial has ever been produced, and the 4 natural cases give no slot on which a synthesiser could have helped.
- Evaluation: a paired benchmark on the current card is underpowered by construction (only ~1 in 20 attempts binds, and those bound at 107-127%); it would need a purpose-built over-budget task.

PRIOR ART: this is ido-8ps.19's multi-round refinement over dropped content, filed 2026-09-15 as conditional on 'whether the budget binds at all on this task'. The same data answers that condition.

RECOMMENDATION: NOT worthwhile now; retire, or defer with explicit re-open triggers: (a) binding rate above ~15% on a task family, or (b) any judged slot lost to a dropped alias, or (c) deployment on a smaller-window model (at 32k the budget would be ~62 KB, below the median 88 KB base, so each partition would repeat a base that alone exceeds the budget and splitting could not help; that regime needs a different fix). Consider the digest-dedupe change as a separate small fix. Also: the shared map-reduce helper argument should not drive fix-ufot's design (B), since this issue supplies no demand for it.

LIMITS: one task family (privilege audit, pinned + neutral phrasings), one model, one window; FW_TRAJECTORY_MAX_BYTES pinned at 28000; 1 of 4 binding attempts unjudged. Owner decision pending: close as retired/deferred, or keep open.
FOLLOW-UP FINDINGS 2026-09-26 (same corpus, $0, no code changed). Recorded here only; nothing written to fix-4dsr.

A. CHEAPER FIX ASSESSED: dedupe rehydration by archived text digest (handles already carry text_sha256), not only by alias.
- Cost: ~20-40 lines in answer_rehydration.py plus offline tests (T0); no model call, no added latency.
- Return: small. Duplicates are ~1% of rehydrated demand (median ~1.9 KB, ~700 tokens; max 30.4 KB, 11.4% of demand). It would have kept 1 of the 4 over-budget attempts in budget (scope-neutral-v2 a2: 30 KB duplicate vs 16 KB overshoot); the other three overshoot by 36-68 KB against 1-25 KB of duplicates. No measurable answer gain, since the rescued attempt had lost nothing.
- Risks: (1) the skipped older alias stays a label, so it needs a mapping note ('O5 is identical to O13, shown above'), NOT the 'not rehydrated' wording, or it invites a new pointer/false-absence answer; (2) identical text can carry different context clauses (same listing reached from two subjects), so dedupe only when the clauses match, or print both; (3) compare raw-vs-raw or stored-vs-stored digests under redaction, or it silently never matches (harmless but inert).
- Verdict: hygiene, not a quality fix. Not filed.

B. WHERE UNRESOLVED ANSWERS ACTUALLY COME FROM. 118 judged attempts with archives (74 with rehydration on: 465 unresolved + 438 missing slots of 26 per attempt). Strict classification (an item counts as held only if the command that produces that axis ran and its output contains the expected identifiers):
- producing command never ran: 163 unresolved / 193 missing
- it ran, but only for other subjects: 162 / 42
- value held in the archive, not reported: 0 / 10 (~1%)
- unclassifiable (right-level items with no identifier in ground truth: feed, publishing system, conferring collection, finding-to-identity; spot checks read 'not addressed'): 140 / 193
A looser 'any identifier anywhere in the archive' test over-counts (a person's uid appears in other people's holder listings) and was discarded after spot checks.
So unresolved slots are a retrieval-coverage problem in the loop, not an answer-time visibility problem; no extract-step change (rehydration, splitting, dedupe) reaches them.

C. LOOP BEHAVIOUR.
- Only 5 of 115 attempts exhausted their iterations; the rest finished voluntarily with work left.
- Attempts with >=15 enumeration commands (fetch_result_page / who_has_access_to) left median 13/26 unresolved+missing vs 10/26 for <=5 (correlation, not shown to be causal).
- Roster nudge (20 attempts with roster_nudge events): fired 12, declined 8 (7 'every named item was already a subject', 1 'no room to act'). After a fired nudge 10 of 12 agents ran more commands (2-30), yet those attempts still ended with 7-22 gaps. All 7 'already a subject' attempts still had 7-13 missing+unresolved slots: subject presence is a poor proxy for coverage.

D. OPTIONS FOR FEWER UNRESOLVED SLOTS (not filed):
1. Finish-time coverage check per (named subject x requested item type), deterministic from the execute ledger (command + context clause), with commands declaring what they produce; nudge names the missing pairs. Same goal as fix-4dsr (which uses plan steps + a Jev judge instead).
2. Bounded repeat / one-time finish refusal while gaps remain (110 of 115 attempts finished with steps left); measure exhaustion and fabrication with it (ido-8ps.23 honesty rule observed at n=1 only).
3. Automatic follow-up round over the still-unresolved retrievable items via the existing continuation machinery: the useful part of this issue's idea (spend the second round retrieving new evidence, not re-reading old).
4. Cheaper steps per item on the IDO side (per-person composite command; count-only/filters instead of page walks).
5. Writer-side checks matter for incorrect slots (premise copying, ido-8ps.28), not for unresolved (~1%).
Target caution: 'zero unresolved' invites fabrication (pre-honesty-rule exhausted runs filled 13 slots from queries never issued). Target instead: no unresolved item that was retrievable within budget, every gap named, and measure unresolved and fabrication together.

E. INPUTS RELEVANT TO A FINISH-TIME EVALUATOR (recorded for whoever designs one):
- Per-subject granularity is required: a step like 'list groups for each person' can pass on partial coverage.
- Existence questions ('was list_groups run with X as subject?') are answerable from offload labels (command + context clause); value questions are not needed since held-not-reported is ~1%.
- Unrehydrated trajectory is median 88.6 KB ~ 32k tokens at 2.74 B/token (p90 ~42k): about half of turns exceed a 32k-token state limit. A compact execute ledger (command, subject, alias per step; ~6 KB for 60 steps) fits easily.
- Offline replay corpus exists: 20 roster-nudge attempts plus ~115 judged attempts with archives under ido/evaluation/{collections,artifacts}/result-search.

LIMITS: one task family, one model/window; B's classification is heuristic (30-45% unclassifiable); C is correlational.
RE-EXAMINATION WITH fix-ufot (01b0d64) AND fix-4dsr (43e42a2) IN PLACE, 2026-09-26 ($0, no code changed, no new runs).

DATA. GTE corpus (ido GTE, 12 tasks, cerebras/gpt-oss-120b, 131k window, budget 250,000 B): arm C gte-cleanup-candidate-20260923 (60 attempts, judged: blind 0-2 completeness by two judges), gte-cme-pinned-ablation-20260920 arms T/B/R (180, judged), gte-list-owns-paging-20260920 (12), and the fix-ufot live cells in ~/rl/ufot-offline/live/runs (26 attempts with rehydration, tasks 04/08/09, fw 563de1c + the uncommitted 01b0d64 changes; NOT judged). fix-4dsr has NO recorded run (its notes: live ido benchmark not done), so its effect is projected, not measured.

1. BUDGET WITH fix-ufot: 0 of 26 attempts over budget; demand median 38%, p90 57%, max 68%. Arm C (pre-ufot, same design otherwise): 0 of 60, median 36%, max 62%. Matched tasks, max demand C -> ufot: task 04 56% -> 46%, task 08 56% -> 55%, task 09 62% -> 68%. Searches fell (median 2 vs 5-6 on the same tasks), as the new label/instruction wording intends ('search only for a value the next step needs, never to collect rows for the final answer'); so the final answer now depends on rehydration alone, but there is >=32% headroom in every recorded attempt. Only the Sep-20 ablation ever dropped evidence (5 of 180).

2. PROJECTION FOR fix-4dsr + MAX_FORCED_REPLANS 3 (loop ceiling 4 segments x 25 = 100 decisions). The finish-check note fires once, only with >=2 iterations left, so it cannot push a turn past the ceiling. Fit over arm C + ufot: demand ~= 16.3 KB + 1.46 KB per execute -> 65% of budget at 100 executes. Every recorded attempt could add >=33 executes at its own rate before binding (median 91). The edge case is task 09: its largest attempts (69-74 executes, 150-170 KB) reach 85-91% if they add 25 more executes. Expect the budget to start binding occasionally on task-09-like turns, and rarely elsewhere.

3. DOES DROPPED OR LARGER EVIDENCE HURT COMPLETENESS? No sign of it.
- Ablation's 5 dropped-evidence attempts scored at or above their same-arm/same-task siblings on both judges (e.g. B/12/a3 dropped 17 aliases at 111%: J1 0 vs siblings 1,0,0,1; J2 1 vs all-1).
- Within arm x task (completed runs), completeness vs rehydrated demand / extract tokens: ablation n=142, rho +0.21 (p~0.05) on BOTH judges, i.e. more evidence goes with MORE complete answers; arm C n=49, rho -0.08 to -0.13 (p 0.41-0.64), no detectable effect across 32-51k extract tokens.
- No output cap is in play: complete (score 2) answers are no longer than partial ones (median 6.8 KB vs 7.5 KB), max 24 KB.

4. WHAT MAKES GTE ANSWERS INCOMPLETE (arm C, judge 1, 44 answers scored < 2; keyword-classified rationales, heuristic): a branch never done (skipped alert branch, 3 of 5 identities, login never walked) in 28 (64%); compression (counts, 'first entitlement', samples instead of the full list) in 20 (45%); both in 13; other 9. Compression is new relative to the privilege-audit corpus. It happens with the evidence present (arm C had 0 drops), so it is a writer choice. The writer's only instruction is 'Comprehensive final answer with supporting evidence', and the judges' 'absence of noise' score pulls the other way.

5. WHAT EACH FIX REACHES. fix-4dsr targets the not-done class (the majority); its effect needs the live paired run. Neither fix reaches compression. Since 01b0d64 the agent no longer copies rows via search, so the writer is now the only path to a full list: an answer-side instruction (list every row the request asks for, from the rehydrated evidence) is the natural next experiment for that class. Budget splitting / map-reduce (this issue) still has nothing to fix: 0 drops under the current design, and drops that did happen cost nothing measurable.

UPDATED RECOMMENDATION: unchanged, retire or defer. Add a re-open trigger: rehydration_finished with dropped_aliases on more than ~5% of turns in the fix-4dsr live benchmark (watch task 09). Measure completeness on the fix-ufot cells with the same blind judges before crediting them with anything (completion 23/26 vs arm C 10/15 on the same tasks is not completeness).

LIMITS: one workflow family (ido), one model/window; ufot cells unjudged and small (n=26, three tasks); fix-4dsr unmeasured; section 4 classification is keyword-based.
LIVE CHECK 2026-09-27 (fix-9gy8, GTE 12x5x2 with fix-ufot + router, finish check on/off, 120 cells): re-open trigger NOT met. 0 of 120 turns dropped evidence, 0 overflows, largest rehydration 74% of budget (arm U), 63% in arm N; median extract prompt ~29-30k tokens in both arms. Longer runs from both fixes did not bring the budget into play. Completeness gaps observed are plan/retrieval gaps (see fix-9gy8), not answer-time visibility.
SUMMARY OF FINDINGS 2026-09-27 (kept OPEN at owner request).
1. Is splitting over-budget evidence into parallel extractor trajectories + synthesis worthwhile? NOT NOW. The rehydration budget binds rarely: privilege-audit corpus 4/79 attempts; GTE Sep-20 ablation 5/180; GTE arm C 0/60; fix-ufot live cells 0/26; fix-9gy8 live benchmark with both fixes 0/120 (max 74% of budget). Where it did bind, 0 judged answer items were lost, and dropped-evidence attempts scored at or above their siblings.
2. Larger answer prompts do not reduce completeness: within task, more rehydrated evidence goes with slightly MORE complete answers (ablation rho +0.21, both judges); arm C shows no detectable effect.
3. Unresolved/incomplete answers come from the loop, not the extract step: ~all unresolved items were never retrieved (~1% held but unreported), plus writer compression (counts/samples instead of full lists) with the evidence present.
4. fix-4dsr's finish check (fix-9gy8) did not move completeness (N-U judge 1 -0.05, judge 2 -0.12, within noise): plan-step execution is not task satisfaction, and user-gated plan steps are skipped while the benchmark operator never answers. Follow-ups filed, not started: fix-3xts, fix-emzj, fix-fvxu.
5. Cheaper alternative (digest dedupe of rehydrated observations): hygiene only, not filed.
6. Re-open triggers for building the split: dropped aliases on >5% of turns on any task family; any judged item lost to a dropped alias; deployment on a smaller-window model (a different fix is needed there).
Open items the owner may still decide: close as retired/deferred; whether to file the digest-dedupe fix; a writer-side 'list every requested row' experiment for the compression class.
Owner decision 2026-09-27: NO on the content-dedupe (digest) fix; do not file it. GO on the writer list-completeness experiment, both approaches (prompt instruction and deterministic row appendix), tracked separately.

title: Replace the roster nudge with a finish-time check that every plan step was executed
description:
Split out of fix-jnoz (owner ruling, PR 84 review). The roster nudge (fastworkflow/answer_coverage.py build_nudge, fired from fastWorkflowReAct at agent-selected finish) decides 'covered' by entity presence: a regex over the request (names, uids, emails) tested against recorded context clauses. Even after the fix-jnoz stopgaps (silent when no clause names an instance; wording limited to 'never the subject of any command') it stays brittle: it depends on the request's surface form, on workflows declaring instance_label/instance_label_attr, and on 'was a subject' as a proxy for 'was covered'.

Goal: a more robust design that evaluates whether the task was completed against the requirements the request actually states, using what the turn retrieved, and returns the agent to the loop (bounded) when a requirement is unmet.

Scope questions to settle before building:
- How requirements are derived from the request (planner output already exists: build_query_with_next_steps; reuse vs a dedicated extraction), and how to keep that from inventing requirements.
- What evidence the check reads (archive via rehydration-style copy, subjects, search answers) and its byte budget (context_budget).
- Whether a model call is acceptable at finish (cost/latency per turn; determinism; the current nudge is model-free by design).
- Gate vs note: current nudge is a once-per-turn note, never a gate; keep that property or justify changing it.
- Evaluation: paired benchmark against the current nudge (fastworkflow-research-methodology), measuring completed cells, exhausted turns, false 'could not retrieve' answers.
- Migration: remove answer_coverage's regex extractor once the replacement is accepted; FW_EVAL_FINISH_REMINDERS semantics.

Risk: high -- changes finish behaviour for every workflow; must not ship without a paired benchmark.
design:
Owner decisions, 2026-09-26:

- Requirements: each step of the planner's plan (build_query_with_next_steps) is one requirement. No separate extraction; the evaluator judges only steps that exist, so it cannot invent requirements. Limit: a step the plan omits cannot be checked.
- Evidence: the complete, UNREHYDRATED trajectory (what the agent actually saw). Offloaded results appear only as labels, so a step whose proof sits behind a label may read as unmet -- count these separately in evaluation.
- Model: a model call at finish is acceptable if it is a Jev call (TypeSafe System One, https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction). Natural shape: state = the trajectory; one Noul per plan step ("is step k satisfied by the trajectory?"), all in one request, evaluated in parallel and in isolation; threshold nouls in code. Constraints from the jev-1.13 docs: 32k tokens for state + longest question (64k total), so the trajectory needs a budget/truncation rule; accuracy drops with large irrelevant state and with indirection, so step questions must be literal and self-contained; pin a versioned model id (not jev-latest) once thresholds are tuned.
- Gate vs note: STILL OPEN. Current nudge is a note (replaces the finish observation, agent may finish again immediately) that fires at most once per turn and only with iterations left. Benchmark should measure how often agents ignored the current nudge to decide whether a bounded gate is warranted.
- Evaluation: paired, offline, over trajectories already in the observation store -- replay both the Jev evaluator and the current nudge on the same turns and compare verdicts against outcomes. Measures detection only; the effect of returning the agent to the loop needs live runs.
- Migration: current design has not shipped. If the replacement is accepted, remove all traces of it (answer_coverage.py, roster-nudge wiring in utils/react.py, NudgeReport, roster_nudge events, FW_EVAL_FINISH_REMINDERS semantics as they stand). Test deletions still need explicit owner approval.
notes:
Jev findings, 2026-09-26 (sources: https://docs.typesafe.ai/introduction, https://docs.typesafe.ai/models.md, https://docs.typesafe.ai/concepts/state.md, https://docs.typesafe.ai/primitives/noul, https://docs.typesafe.ai/model-jaggedness/jev-1.13.md):

- Fit: Jev evaluates typed questions against a state and returns probabilities, not generated text. One Noul (yes/no, returns P(yes)) per plan step, all in one request; questions are evaluated in parallel and in isolation, so adding steps barely adds latency and does not add context rot. The unmet/met cut is a threshold in our code -- no output parsing, deterministic finish-time decision given the probabilities.
- Model/limits (jev-1.13.0): POST /v1/systemone; 32k tokens for state + longest question, 64k for state + all questions; text only (string, JSON object, or array). Priced per input token ($0.042/Mtok), output free. Rate limits 250k tok/s, 1,200 req/min, subject to change; SDKs retry 429 with backoff. Aliases jev-latest/jev-preview move on release -- pin the versioned id once thresholds are tuned.
- State shape: pass the trajectory as a JSON object/array with named fields (thought_i, tool_name_i, tool_args_i, observation_i) rather than one flat string, so each step question can point at named parts of the state.
- Jaggedness to design around:
  * Large state with irrelevant detail lowers accuracy. Long trajectories with many unrelated tool calls are the risk case; the offline replay must report accuracy vs trajectory size. Filtering the trajectory per step is the documented mitigation, but it conflicts with "read the complete trajectory" -- decide after measuring.
  * Literal reading and indirection: plan steps must become literal, self-contained questions. Steps that refer to other steps ("look up the user found in step 2") need rewording before being asked.
  * No counting, arithmetic, or date comparison: any plan step whose satisfaction hinges on numbers or dates must be checked in code, or split so Jev only makes the semantic judgment.
  * Adversarial content: the trajectory contains tool output (external data) and Jev does not treat state as hostile. Injected text in an observation could sway a verdict; test for it.
  * Noul thresholds do not transfer to Choice questions or across model versions.
- Evaluation doubles as calibration: replaying Jev over the stored trajectories yields, per plan step, P(satisfied) alongside the known outcome -- that is the data to tune the threshold against. The same replay should count how often agents ignored the current roster nudge (finished again immediately), which is the evidence for the open gate-vs-note question.
- Open: behaviour when the trajectory exceeds the 32k budget (truncate which parts?), and when the Jev call fails or is rate-limited (must fall through silently, like the current nudge's never-fail rule).
See fix-k6w3 (FINDINGS / FOLLOW-UP FINDINGS 2026-09-26, sections C-E): recorded runs show unresolved slots are a loop retrieval-coverage problem, not an answer-time one, and 'was a subject' is a poor proxy for coverage (all 7 'already a subject' attempts still had 7-13 gaps) -- reinforcing a finish-time completion check such as the Jev-based evaluator here. Note its caveat: the median unrehydrated trajectory is ~32k tokens, so about half would exceed Jev's 32k state limit.
Evidence revision, 2026-09-26 (supersedes 'complete unrehydrated trajectory' in the design field; owner accepted the ledger alternative from fix-k6w3 section E, with the refinements below):

- Jev state = a compact execute ledger, one row per step: step index, tool/command name, subject (the recorded context clause, via context_clause_of), alias, and an OUTCOME field. fix-k6w3 sizes the ledger at ~6 KB for 60 steps, far under the 32k-token state limit, whereas the median unrehydrated trajectory (~88.6 KB, ~32k tokens at 2.74 B/token) would exceed it about half the time. Fewer irrelevant bytes also avoids Jev's documented large-state accuracy loss.
- Refinement 1, outcome per row: command + subject alone would mark a step done when the command ran but errored, returned nothing, or hit the wrong subject. Derive a short outcome in code (error / empty / result) plus a bounded head of the observation (for example the first ~200 B, or the offload label line). The ledger step->ordinal numbering already exists (execute_ordinal_pairs in observation_offloading/continuation.py); outcome and head still have to be assembled.
- Refinement 2, per-subject expansion in code: coarse plan steps ('list groups for each person') pass on partial coverage (fix-k6w3 E). Expand such steps into one Noul per (step x named subject) before asking. Subject names come from the plan step or request, so nothing is invented; if a step cannot be expanded, ask it once.
- Refinement 3, evaluate the choice in the replay: on the ~half of recorded turns whose full unrehydrated trajectory fits 32k tokens, run both states (ledger vs full trajectory) and compare verdicts against the judged slots. Ship the ledger unless the full trajectory is materially better where it fits. Do not mix the two states at runtime: the per-step thresholds are calibrated to one state shape and would not transfer.
- Not needed: observation values. Held-but-not-reported is ~1% of unresolved slots (fix-k6w3 B), so existence-plus-outcome questions carry the signal.
OFFLINE REPLAY RESULTS 2026-09-26 (no agent runs; recorded IDO attempts only; ~$0.27 of Jev; scripts + cached responses in /home/drawal/rl/4dsr-offline, outside the repo).

SETUP. 118 judged attempts (privilege-audit task family, 3 phrasings; ido/evaluation/{collections,artifacts}/result-search). Requirements = the initial fw.planner.plan steps (median 17). Evidence = ledger rebuilt from fw.agent.step spans + context_line events (command, context clause, outcome, 200 B head; median 20 KB, max 34 KB -- fits every time). Subjects = the 9 named in the request (5 people, Christopher Hubbard, 2 rights, 1 control; taken from the judgement for scoring). Jev jev-1.13.0, two requests per attempt: (a) state=request+plan: per step 'does it need a command?' + per (step x subject) 'does it apply?'; (b) state=ledger: per (step x subject) 'was the step's goal achieved for S, by any command, with a result?'. Unit score = max over steps of P(action)*P(applies)*(1-P(done)). Ground truth per (attempt, subject): any judged slot unresolved/missing (g_gap) or not correct (g_notcorrect). Baseline = the roster nudge's presence test computed with the repo's own answer_coverage helpers at end of turn (matches 11/20 recorded nudge events; all 9 differences explained: 8 agents acted after the nudge, 1 'no room to act').

PROMPT ITERATION (on 2 pilot attempts, both inside the 118): v1 asked 'was this step carried out for S' -> flagged every reasoning step (intersect/compare) and every goal reached by a different command. v2 added the per-step 'needs a command?' question and asked about the step's GOAL; used for all results below.

RESULTS (threshold 0.5 unless stated; cluster-bootstrap 95% CI by attempt):
- People (n=708, g_gap base 0.74): Jev P 0.91 R 0.45, AUC 0.68 [0.60,0.75]; nudge P 0.96 R 0.30. Of 522 person gaps Jev catches 234, nudge 157; Jev-only 94, nudge-only 17. False alarms on 186 gap-free people: Jev 24, nudge 6. At threshold 0.7 Jev reaches P 0.95 R 0.38, i.e. more recall than the nudge at about its precision. Jev also caught people for whom nothing was retrieved and the answer fabricated values (judged 'incorrect', not 'unresolved'), e.g. scope-neutral-v2/attempt-5 Barbara Sanchez and Brandon Miller.
- Rights (n=236, base 0.85): Jev AUC 0.51 [0.39,0.64] -- uninformative. It flags the portrait step, but the rights' missing axes (publishing system, feed, conferring collection) are largely not retrievable. Nudge fires on 3%.
- Control (n=118): Jev flags 92% (P 0.54 at base 0.51). Cause: indirection -- the agent acts on the control by its code, and no ledger row ties the code to the control's name (a documented jev-1.13 weakness). AUC 0.77, so a higher threshold helps (0.8: P 0.70 R 0.63). The nudge never checks the control (its regex does not extract it).
- Turn level: Jev flags at least one subject in 115/118 turns even excluding the control, the nudge in 62/118; almost every recorded turn really did end with gaps (median 12 of 26 slots).
- Ledger vs full unrehydrated trajectory: only 9 of 118 trajectories fit Jev's limit (Jev counts more tokens per byte than the 2.74 B/token estimate). On those, flag agreement 0.96, AUC 0.81 vs 0.83 (g_gap). The ledger loses nothing measurable; n is small.
- Cost/latency: median 56k input tokens per turn (~$0.0024), 0.7 s wall for the two requests in sequence (they are independent and could run in parallel). Six attempts' longest plans pushed the full-trajectory request over 64k tokens; questions need chunking at around 120 per request.

READING. On the subjects that matter most here (people), the Jev check finds about 50% more gaps than the roster nudge at similar precision, including unretrieved-then-fabricated cases the nudge cannot see. It still misses over half of person gaps; spot checks show the main cause is the plan itself (e.g. the plan never asks for a person's collections), the known limit of plan-as-requirements. Two weak spots to fix before a live experiment: (1) indirection -- add to each ledger row the instance the command resolved to (context after), or name-to-identifier mappings; (2) rights-style gaps that no command can fill -- either accept them or have the note ask the agent to say so rather than retry.

LIMITS. One task family, one agent model, one judge; subjects taken from the judgement (in production they must come from the request/plan); evaluated at end of turn, whereas the live check runs at the agent's first finish; prompt wording tuned on 2 of the 118 attempts. Detection only: whether a flagged agent then closes the gap needs live runs.
Correction to READING above: 'the main cause is the plan itself' rests on one closely inspected attempt (final-confirm-neutral/attempt-4, whose plan never asks for collections), not on a count. Why Jev misses over half of person gaps is not yet measured; the next step is to classify the misses (step missing from plan / step present but judged done / other).
SCOPE CLARIFICATION (owner, 2026-09-26): the check verifies that every plan step was EXECUTED, not that the user's task was completed. Consequences: (1) the v2 'was the step's goal achieved' wording measures completion and must be replaced by an execution question; (2) the OFFLINE REPLAY RESULTS above were scored against judged answer slots, which measure completion, so their precision/recall do not measure this check -- a step can run and still leave a slot unresolved (the rights' portrait step); step-level execution labels are needed instead; (3) 'gaps no command can fill' is out of scope: a step whose command ran is executed regardless of what it returned. Carried over: the per-step 'needs a command?' filter and per-subject expansion.
EXECUTION REPLAY v3 (2026-09-26, after the scope clarification; files in /home/drawal/rl/4dsr-offline: jev_exec.py, sample.py, labels.txt, score_labels.py). Owner rulings: a substitute command counts if it does the same kind of action for the same subject; ground truth = blind hand labels.

METHOD. Execution question per (plan step x subject) over the ledger ("was this step executed for S: the named command or a same-kind substitute ran, not an execution error; what it returned does not matter"), all 118 attempts. Scope reused from the cached 'needs a command?' x 'applies to S?' answers. Flag = P(action)*P(applies)*(1-P(executed)) >= 0.5. Blind sample: 12 random attempts; per attempt up to 5 flagged, 5 in-scope-not-flagged, 3 out-of-scope pairs = 135 pairs, labelled from the ledgers without seeing Jev's scores. Label rules: navigation-only steps (open_directory, reset_context, open_controls_monitor) belong to no subject; conditional steps whose condition excludes the subject are out of scope; multi-part steps are Y only if every command part ran (P = partial). Weighted estimates re-weight each pair by its bucket size in its attempt.

RESULTS (weighted to the 12 attempts' full pair populations; raw sample counts in score_labels.py output):
- Scope: recall 1.00, precision 0.87 -- no in-scope pair was missed; the extra pairs are mostly remediation and finding steps credited to the control, which I labelled as Hubbard's.
- End to end, strict (partial = not executed): precision 0.76, recall 0.89 (sample: 25 TP, 19 FP, 5 FN, 86 TN).
- Excluding the control subject: precision 0.89, recall 0.86 (sample 20 TP, 7 FP, 5 FN).
- Control subject alone: 12 of 17 flags are false (sample precision 0.29, recall 1.00). Cause, as before: the agent acts on the control by its code, and no ledger row ties the code to the name. Hubbard steps run in the ControlFinding context (propose_fix, show_affected_entities) fail the same way (4 of the 7 non-control FPs). 26 of the 135 pairs come from 2 attempts recorded before context clauses existed (empty context column).
- Misses (5 FN): 4 are partially executed multi-part steps (e.g. list_accounts skipped, list_groups never run) that Jev scored as executed; 1 is a borderline substitute (Alan's uid taken from a holder listing, no find_identity; P(executed) 0.49).
- Code reference (backticked command names in the step vs ledger rows mentioning the subject): precision 0.53, recall 0.87 -- much worse than Jev, because it cannot credit substitutes or rows that name the subject only through an identifier.

DESIGN GAPS FOUND. (1) Indirection: each ledger row needs the instance it acted on in plain words (e.g. the context AFTER the command, which carries names, or a code -> name map from listings); this is the main source of false flags. (2) Multi-part steps: ask one question per command part, or have the step split into parts in code, so a partial step is not scored as executed. (3) Subject-less steps (navigation, 'enter X') are never checked by the per-subject expansion; they need one unexpanded 'was this step executed at all?' question.

LIMITS. One labeller (the agent that built the check, labelling blind to scores but not independent of the design); 135 pairs from 12 attempts of one task family; the scope labels for remediation/finding steps (control vs Hubbard) are a judgement call that moves precision by a few points.
V4 FIXES + RETEST (2026-09-26; /home/drawal/rl/4dsr-offline: fixes.py, jev_v4.py, score_v4.py, sample_v4.py, labels2.txt, score_v4_holdout.py, test_mapreduce.py; ~$0.16 of Jev).

IMPLEMENTED. (1) Instance naming, in code: each ledger row gets acted_on (the context the next command ran in), refers_to (every identifier in its command/contexts resolved to the label a retrieved `id  label` listing gave it, plus the listing that produced it, one hop resolved), and names_in_output (request-named subjects found in its full output, from the archive). (2) Multi-part steps: lettered sub-steps that name a command become parts, each with its own 'does this part concern S?' (plan state) and 'was this part executed for S?' (ledger state); a step is unmet if any applicable part is. (3) Subject-less steps: one unexpanded 'was this step executed at all?' per step. Map/reduce: questions sent in chunks of 100; on max_tokens_exceeded the ledger is halved recursively and answers reduced with max. With a 0.3 prefilter no real attempt needed a split; forced test (ledger padded to 182 KB) split 3 times, 4 requests, 19/21 verdicts equal to the unsplit run, both differences borderline control cases moving toward 'executed'.

RESULTS.
- Design sample (the 135 v3 pairs, whose errors motivated the fixes -- optimistic): weighted precision 0.76 -> 0.95, recall 0.89 -> 0.94.
- FRESH HOLDOUT (8 attempts not used for design, 90 pairs + 12 subject-less steps, labelled blind): v3 precision 0.73 recall 0.78; v4 precision 0.69 recall 0.90 (weighted). Excluding the control: v3 0.79/0.74, v4 0.75/0.89. Control only: v3 0.54, v4 0.49 precision (recall 1.00 both). Subject-less steps: all 12 executed, v4 flagged none (no negatives in the sample, so recall there is unmeasured).
- Reading: on unseen attempts the multi-part split is what generalises (recall +12 points); the instance-naming fix did not fix the control (precision still ~0.5), and overall precision is flat to slightly down.

HOLDOUT ERRORS, by cause (13): optional parts/steps counted as required, 5 (e.g. 'e. Optionally run open_portrait', '(Optional) apply remediation after approval'); control still unrecognised in list_controls steps, 3 -- the listing labels it 'Contractor whom manager left', not the request's 'Active contractor identities whom manager left', so names_in_output misses it; scope judgement calls (remediation credited to the control, per-holder step credited to the permission, portrait-as-holders substitute), 4; one partial step scored executed, 1.

NEXT (v5, needs a THIRD fresh holdout because this one has now been looked at): drop optional/after-approval parts and steps in code or in the action question; fuzzy name matching for names_in_output (token overlap) so a listing row naming the control is linked. Remaining 98 unlabelled attempts are enough for one more holdout.
V5 + THIRD HOLDOUT (2026-09-26; /home/drawal/rl/4dsr-offline: jev_v5.py, fixes.py is_optional/step_optional/name_in_text, verdicts.py, sample_v5.py, labels3.txt, score_holdout3.py; ~$0.17 of Jev).

V5 = v4 + (a) optional / after-approval steps and parts dropped in code (title or opening words say optional / 'if needed' / approval-gated; sub-parts also when approval-gated anywhere; sub-step letters extended to a-l) and (b) names_in_output matched by word overlap (a line holding >= max(2, 60%) of the subject's words), with the row rule telling Jev that a listing containing S counts for a 'list to locate S' step.

THIRD HOLDOUT: 8 attempts in neither earlier sample, 86 pairs + 17 subject-less steps, labelled blind, stratified by v5's verdict. Weighted: v3 P 0.69 R 0.80; v4 P 0.87 R 1.00; v5 P 0.85 R 0.83. v5 lost recall: word-overlap names let Jev credit two unexecuted steps (open_finding for the control; Alan's multi-part step), and the optional filter missed '(only after user confirmation)' placed after the step title, so approval-gated remediation steps were still flagged. On holdout 2 (which v5 was designed on, so not a fair test) v5 had cut false flags 22 -> 10; that did not replicate.

POOLED FRESH ESTIMATE (holdouts 2+3, 16 attempts, 176 pairs; fresh for v3 and v4): v3 P 0.71 R 0.79; v4 P 0.77 R 0.95. Excluding the control: v3 0.84/0.73, v4 0.83/0.93. Control only: v3 0.50, v4 0.62 precision (recall 1.00). Subject-less steps (29 sampled across both holdouts): 1 not executed, flagged correctly; no false flags.

DECISION INPUT. Adopt the v4 design (annotated ledger + per-part questions + subject-less question + chunked/halving map-reduce). Reject word-overlap name matching. Optional/approval-gated steps are a real residual error source (4 of 7 v5 errors on holdout 3 are approval-gated remediation steps or remediation credited to the control), but regex over free plan text is too brittle: better to have the planner mark steps optional/approval-gated structurally, or ask Jev one 'is this step required without user approval?' question per step. The remaining control false flags are the name mismatch between the request and the backend's label; no offline fix tried so far holds up.

LIMITS unchanged: one labeller (the builder, blind to scores), one task family, 16 fresh attempts. 90 attempts remain unlabelled for any further holdout.
ROUND 4 (2026-09-26; /home/drawal/rl/4dsr-offline: jev_v6.py, sample_r4.py, LABELING_RULES.md, labels4_a.txt (me), labels4_b.txt (independent subagent annotator, same written rules, blind to scores and to my labels), score_round4.py; ~$0.01 of Jev).

V6 = v4 x P(step required without user approval), one Jev question per step. It judged 284 of 1875 steps not required, including some required ones (holder listings, propose_fix) whose plans mention asking the user elsewhere.

FOURTH HOLDOUT: 8 attempts in no earlier sample, 96 pairs + 10 subject-less steps, stratified by v4.
- Inter-annotator agreement (me vs independent annotator): in_scope 0.97 raw, kappa 0.92; the scored label (in scope and not fully executed) 0.94 raw, kappa 0.85; 6 disagreements (open_finding called without a uid counted as executed or partial; 'for each matching identity'; 'for each right open the permission' credited to people or not). The labels are reliable enough to score against.
- On this sample v3 beat v4: vs consensus (90 pairs) v3 P 0.71 R 0.90, v4 P 0.65 R 0.83, v5 P 0.74 R 0.80, v6 P 0.79 R 0.65. v4's extra errors were mostly multi-part steps with an optional sub-part ('d. list_groups (optional)', 'd. Optionally show_properties') counted as required (5 of 7), plus one reasoning sub-part with a backticked field name (`permission_uid`) mistaken for a command (a rare v4 bug: 9 of 799 command parts across all plans).

POOLED, WITH ATTEMPT-CLUSTER BOOTSTRAP (correction to the V5 note's 'adopt the v4 design'):
- Holdouts 2+3+4 (24 attempts, 272 pairs, my labels; fresh for v3 and v4): v3 P 0.71 R 0.80 F1 0.75; v4 P 0.72 R 0.86 F1 0.78. v4 - v3: precision +0.01 [-0.06, +0.09], recall +0.06 [-0.06, +0.19], F1 +0.03 [-0.05, +0.12].
- Holdouts 3+4 (16 attempts; fresh for all versions): F1 v3 0.75, v4 0.78, v5 0.77, v6 0.71. v5 - v4 F1 -0.01 [-0.08, +0.04]; v6 - v4 -0.08 [-0.22, +0.03].
- So no version is shown to beat v3 at this sample size. The earlier 'v4 generalises, +12 points recall' rested on single 8-attempt samples; sample-to-sample swings are as large as the version differences. What is solid: the Jev execution check lands around precision 0.7-0.8, recall 0.8-0.9 on fresh attempts across all four versions; v6 buys precision (0.84-0.87) at a large recall cost (0.60-0.69); the control remains the weakest subject in every version.

NEXT, if pursued: (1) a larger pooled test, not more single rounds -- 82 attempts remain unlabelled; the independent annotator can label them in parallel with written rules (kappa 0.85 here). (2) Only then choose between v3's simplicity and v4/v5's extra machinery. (3) The optional-sub-part and field-name-part fixes are cheap and targeted, but were found on this round and would need testing on the remaining attempts.
LARGE TEST (2026-09-26; pre-registered in /home/drawal/rl/4dsr-offline/PREREG_large.md before sampling; sample_large.py, LABELING_RULES_v2.md, large_views/, large_labels/, score_large.py; jev_v7.py ~$0.16).

DESIGN. All 82 attempts in no earlier sample. v7 added before sampling = v4 + sub-steps count only if they name a real workflow command (vocabulary: every command any recorded run executed) and are not optional/approval-gated. Pairs stratified per attempt by the five versions' joint verdicts (out of scope 2, all flag 3, none flag 3, versions disagree up to 5): 910 pairs + 129 subject-less steps, estimates re-weighted by stratum size. Labels: 9 independent annotator subagents, one batch each, blind to scores, rules v2 (round-4 ambiguities settled in writing before labelling: conditional per-person steps in scope for all five people; per-item-a-person-holds steps belong to that person; optional sub-parts not required; no-uid open_finding does not count as opening). A 10th annotator re-labelled 8 attempts (88 pairs): kappa 1.00 (101/102 identical labels; transcript confirms it read only its own view, the rules and its own output). Caveat: same model and same rules for all annotators, so this is consistency, not an independent check of correctness; round 4 (me vs annotator) gave kappa 0.85.

RESULTS (weighted; 95% attempt-cluster bootstrap, 2000 resamples):
- F1: v3 0.75 [0.68, 0.80]; v4 0.81 [0.77, 0.85]; v5 0.83 [0.79, 0.87]; v6 0.78 [0.72, 0.82]; v7 0.82 [0.78, 0.86].
- P / R: v3 0.67/0.84; v4 0.74/0.89; v5 0.80/0.87; v6 0.86/0.70; v7 0.77/0.89.
- H1 v4 > v3: F1 +0.066 [+0.025, +0.112] -> DETECTED.
- H2 v7 > v4: F1 +0.011 [+0.001, +0.026] -> DETECTED (small).
- H3 v6 vs v4: precision +0.118 [+0.070, +0.166], recall -0.188 [-0.257, -0.134] -> DETECTED (trade-off as predicted).
- v5 vs v4 (no hypothesis): F1 +0.020 [+0.003, +0.041]. v7 vs v3: +0.077 [+0.037, +0.123].
- Exploratory, not pre-registered: v5 vs v7 F1 +0.009 [-0.008, +0.026] (v5 more precise +0.033, v7 more recall +0.021).
- By subject, F1 v3/v4/v5/v6/v7: people 0.84/0.87/0.89/0.80/0.88; permissions 0.53/0.61/0.61/0.66/0.64; control 0.62/0.72/0.76/0.75/0.73.
- Subject-less steps: 9 of 129 not executed; v4-v7 all flagged exactly those 9, no false flags.

READING. At 82 attempts the v4 machinery (annotated ledger, per-part questions, subject-less question, map/reduce) beats v3 by ~6-7 F1 points; the small-sample reversals in rounds 3-4 were noise, as the pooled CIs then suggested. v7 and v5 add ~1-2 points over v4; they are not distinguishable from each other. v7 is the simpler of the two (no regex step-skipping, no word-overlap names) with recall 0.89. v6's approval question is a precision/recall dial, not an improvement. Permissions remain the weakest subject (F1 0.61-0.66).

title: NoOpTraceSink does not stop offload evidence and nothing prunes without a sink: fix the docs and add a guarded prune on archive open
description:
Finding (PR 84 review). docs/observation_search.md, the WorkflowExecutionContext trace_sink docstring (workflow_execution_context.py ~L132: 'the code-level way to record nothing') and CHANGELOG ('an explicit tracing.NoOpTraceSink() records nothing') promise that NoOpTraceSink records nothing. It does not for offloading: build_tool_agent (observation_offloading/agent.py) opens state_paths.observability_db(workflow) via open_handle_archive regardless of the sink (RuntimeHandleArchive.__init__: 'whether or not a trace sink ever opened this database'), and record_context_clause / record_event also write through. Evidence (redacted by default), subject clauses (never redacted) and offload events (incl. search questions, reasoning, answers) reach disk. Pruning runs only at sink startup (observability/store.py SQLiteTraceSink start -> self.store.prune()), so with NoOpTraceSink the offload tables grow without bound. No test runs agent mode with NoOpTraceSink and asserts the DB stays untouched (existing NoOp tests use run_as_agent=False or only check sink identity). Not reproduced end to end (no working env in the review checkout); established by reading.

Decision (owner): make the docs true and bound the growth.
1. Docs: state that NoOpTraceSink stops spans and turn records but NOT offloading evidence, subjects or events, which are still written (redacted per FW_OFFLOAD_EVIDENCE_REDACTION) to the workflow's observability.sqlite3; point embedders at FASTWORKFLOW_STATE_ROOT for location. Fix all three places: docs/observation_search.md 'A program that embeds the library...' paragraph, WorkflowExecutionContext.__init__ docstring, CHANGELOG 3.4.0 entries.
2. Guarded prune: when the offload archive first opens a database, run ObservabilityStore.prune() at most ONCE per database path per process (build_tool_agent constructs a new RuntimeHandleArchive per agent build, so an unguarded prune would repeat on every build and add first-turn latency on a large DB). Failure to prune must log and never fail agent construction. For the normal path the sink-startup prune already ran, so this is a cheap no-op; deletion semantics are unchanged (same prune code).
3. Tests: agent-mode (or build_tool_agent-level) integration test with NoOpTraceSink asserting (a) evidence rows are written, matching the new docs, and (b) the prune runs once per path per process and not per agent build; a test that a prune failure does not stop the agent being built.

Open product question, deliberately not decided here: is 'record nothing' a promise fastWorkflow makes to embedders? If yes, a follow-up must make it true (option A: UnavailableHandleArchive when the caller explicitly opted out, covering all four write sites incl. the state.archive() temp-dir fallback, and exposing 'explicitly opted out' on the execution context since tracing.get_sink() returns None both for NoOp and for not-yet-bound; option B: an in-memory archive implementing the full contract).
close_reason: Docs corrected (observation_search.md, WorkflowExecutionContext docstrings, CHANGELOG): NoOpTraceSink stops spans/turn records, not offload evidence. open_handle_archive now prunes each database once per path per process (state.prune_once, cleared by reset_runtime_state; failure logged, archive still returned). Tests: tests/test_offload_noop_sink_prune.py (7). 'Record nothing' product question remains open as noted.

title: Roster nudge is brittle: false nudges without instance labels, and its wording overclaims; consider replacing with a task-completion evaluation
description:
fastworkflow/answer_coverage.py build_nudge / NUDGE_HEAD, called from fastWorkflowReAct at agent-selected finish (once per turn, >= NUDGE_MIN_ITERS_LEFT actions left, off with FW_EVAL_FINISH_REMINDERS=0).

(A) False nudges when a workflow declares no instance identity. 'Touched' means the named item appears in a recorded context clause (subject_corpus). A workflow whose context classes declare neither instance_label nor instance_label_attr records clauses that are the context name alone ('Account', 'Identity'). The haystack is then non-empty, so the 'no context clauses recorded' guard does not fire, yet no name can ever match: every person named in the request is reported untouched on every turn that names people, even when the agent opened each one. No test covers this (tests/test_answer_coverage.py builds clauses only from label-declaring workflows). Minimal fix: stay silent unless at least one recorded clause carries an instance label.

(B) Wording overclaims. The module's own rule is 'It never says data about the item does not exist'; NUDGE_HEAD tells the agent '...has not made the following named items of the request the subject of any command, so nothing about them has been retrieved'. The second clause is false whenever a name was retrieved as a row (find_identity <name>, a listing). Combined with (A) the agent can be told nothing about Alan Cooper was retrieved right after reading his portrait. Minimal fix: drop 'so nothing about them has been retrieved'.

Owner ruling (PR 84 review): even with both fixes the nudge remains brittle -- it depends on a regex over the request, on workflows declaring instance labels, and on 'was a subject' as a proxy for 'was covered'. The whole feature may be replaced by a more robust design that evaluates task completion against the task's requirements (the requirements the request actually states, checked against what the turn retrieved), rather than by entity presence. Treat (A)/(B) as stopgaps and scope the replacement before investing further in the regex extractor.
close_reason: Stopgaps landed: build_nudge stays silent when no recorded clause names an instance (reason 'no recorded clause names an instance'); NUDGE_HEAD no longer says 'so nothing about them has been retrieved'. subject_clauses/clause_names_instance added; build_nudge(clauses=) accepts a list. 3 tests in tests/test_answer_coverage.py. Replacement design tracked separately in fix-4dsr.

title: Study search_memory effectiveness on recorded trajectories; evaluate giving it neighbouring-step context
description:
Open question raised while reviewing PR 84: how effective is the current search_memory design (one archived observation + subject clause, bounded leading prefix sized from the search model's window)?

Research, not implementation:
1. Mine existing recorded trajectories (offload_events / offload_evidence in observability.sqlite3, and saved benchmark attempts) for every search_memory call. Classify outcomes: answered correctly, refused, answered from a truncated prefix, answered wrong, answered from the agent's premise, question actually needed a second observation (cross-observation join).
2. Measure how often the bounded-evidence truncation fired and whether answers degraded when it did.
3. Evaluate the proposed variant: hand search_memory a filtered view of the previous N (e.g. 5) steps. Two sub-variants: (a) thoughts included; (b) only neighbouring steps' context clauses and command arguments, no thoughts. Known counter-arguments from the current design: thoughts are model text, not evidence (the subject input was added to stop answers from the agent's unsupported premise); the subject clause already carries the one fact history supplied and survives cross-process resume; every byte of history comes out of the ~12 KB (reference) evidence budget.
4. Decide with data whether any variant is worth an experiment card.

Refs: docs/observation_search.md, fastworkflow/observation_offloading/search.py.
notes:
Correction to the framing above: search_memory ALREADY prefixes the current step's thought to the question (search.py: query = reasoning + question; agent.current_search_reasoning supplies it), and ObservationSearchSignature tells the model to treat that reasoning as context for the information need, never as evidence. So the variant to study is 'current step's thought only' (today) vs 'N neighbouring steps', not 'no reasoning' vs 'reasoning'. Also measure how often the agent's premise in that reasoning was adopted despite the instruction.

Evidence-bound question (raised in PR 84 review): today search_observation_max_bytes = 3/128 of the SEARCH model's window in bytes, floored at one 4 KB page (12 KB at 131k tokens; 4 KB on a 32k model, so a 40 KB listing is read as a ~3.8 KB prefix). The fraction only reproduces the removed result-handle paging geometry (3 x 4 KB); with paging gone the agent has no way past the prefix. Measure how often observation_bounded fired and whether those answers were refused or wrong.

Candidate designs to evaluate against the data:
(A) Window-minus-overhead: send as much evidence as fits the search model's window after instructions, question, reasoning and subject, with a safety margin (~2k tokens). Risks: per-call cost repeats on every search of the same listing; long-context recall; the 4 bytes/token estimate is optimistic for hex-uid tables, so the margin must absorb it or a real tokenizer is needed. Over-window already degrades to a typed observation.
(B) Chunked map-reduce: split the observation into overlapping chunks each <= 25% of the search window, search chunks in parallel with the same subject, then synthesise one answer; skip synthesis when the whole observation fits one chunk. Design points: chunk on row boundaries and repeat the header row in each chunk; overlap in rows, not bytes; aggregation questions (counts, 'all X') need the synthesiser to sum/merge rather than paraphrase; synthesis is model text over model text, so it must be told to cite chunk evidence and report gaps; cost scales with observation size; still one observation per search, so the one-observation rule holds.

Correction to the evidence-bound note above: 'with paging gone the agent has no way past the prefix' is wrong. The search_memory tool description (observation_offloading/agent.py scoped_search_memory) tells the agent that every search starts at byte zero, re-asking cannot reach the rest, and to re-run the producing command with a narrower filter or smaller page and search the NEW observation. The baseline to measure is therefore 'prefix + re-run with narrower filter' (costs a command; depends on the backend supporting filters/paging), and the trajectories should show how often agents actually took that path after a bounded read.
Related: fix-k6w3 applies the same split / parallel / synthesise design to answer-time rehydration when evidence exceeds the extraction budget. Build one shared helper for both.
Scope correction (Dhar, 2026-09-26): evaluate ONLY candidate (B) chunked map-reduce against the recorded data. Drop (A) window-minus-overhead and the neighbouring-step-context variants from this task.
FINDINGS (2026-09-26), chunked map-reduce only, per scope correction.

Data: every recorded search_memory event in 312 attempts / 1,435 searches, all live roles cerebras/gpt-oss-120b (131k window, 12,288 B bound):
- devreview-artifacts-20260919/gte-rerun-20260919-bundle (60 att, result handles still present)
- ido/evaluation/runs/gte-cme-pinned-ablation-20260920 arms T/B/R (180 att)
- ido/evaluation/runs/gte-list-owns-paging-20260920 (12 att)
- ido/evaluation/runs/gte-cleanup-candidate-20260923 arm C (60 att) = CURRENT design (result handles removed, list owns paging, portraits bounded ~4.1 KB)

1. observation_bounded fired 0 times in 1,435 searches. Largest observation searched: 5,435 B (arm C max 5,361 B; median 2,440; p99 4,627). No observation above 8 KB anywhere.
2. Chunked map-reduce with chunks <= 25% of the search window would need more than one chunk for 0 searches at 131k tokens AND 0 at 32k tokens. With synthesis skipped for single-chunk observations, (B) is byte-identical to today on 100% of the recorded data. It cannot move any metric measured on this workflow.
3. Why: the ido producers bound their own output (listings page themselves at ~3-4 KB with shown/remaining/filter=, portraits ~4.1 KB), so large text never reaches the archive. Chunking targets a size regime this workflow does not produce.
4. Where searches actually lose information (arm C, 312 answered + 13 incomplete), none of which chunking addresses:
   - 13 (4%) incomplete: completion limit hit on 'list all ... ids and labels' over 2-4 KB observations. One chunk each; chunking adds output, not less.
   - ~108 (35%) answers decline to reproduce a table (the signature's 'do not reproduce long tables' policy).
   - ~40 (13%) answers report an upstream page cut (the command's own first page; the missing rows were never archived).
5. Side observation, out of scope here: on a 32k-token search model the 4 KB floor would bound 59 of 327 arm-C searches, but that is a bound-size question (the dropped design A), not a chunking one; still 0 would need >1 chunk.

DECISION: no experiment card for chunked map-reduce. Revisit only if a workflow records search observations above ~25% of the search window (use observation_bytes in offload_events). fix-k6w3's shared-helper argument gets no support from the search side.
Caveat: one workflow (ido GTE, 12 tasks), one search model.
close_reason: Chunked map-reduce would be a no-op on all 1,435 recorded searches (0 bounded, max observation 5.4 KB vs 12 KB bound; 0 would need >1 chunk even at 32k). No experiment card. See notes.

comments.author: Dhar Rawal
comments.text: From fix-k6w3 research (2026-09-26, recorded IDO runs, 79 attempts): (1) Measured bytes/token on extract prompts is 2.74 median (2.33-3.20), not 4. Any window-minus-overhead sizing in design (A) should not assume 4 B/token for these uid-heavy observations. (2) fix-k6w3 finds the answer-rehydration budget binds in only 4/79 attempts, with 0 judged answer slots lost to the drop, and recommends not building the split/synthesise path. So the 'build one shared map-reduce helper for both' argument should not drive design (B); judge (B) on search_memory's own data. Details in fix-k6w3 notes.

title: WorkflowExecutionContext opens the observability sink itself when none was supplied
description: Recording is always on (FW_OBSERVABILITY removed), but a program that builds WorkflowExecutionContext directly gets NoOpTraceSink (workflow_execution_context.py ~113/163) while the agent still writes offload evidence into the DB, so nothing prunes it and no turn records exist. title: Replace an older-schema local observability DB on open instead of refusing it
description: The observability store was never published (last PyPI release 2.30.1 predates fastworkflow/observability/store.py, added in #82), so only developers' local DBs can carry an older schema. Today ObservabilityStore._ensure_schema (store.py ~1612-1633) refuses a populated DB with user_version < SCHEMA_VERSION, which silently degrades offloading. Decision (owner, 2026-09-24): on open, a populated OLDER-schema DB is deleted with its -wal/-shm and recreated fresh, with a logged warning. A NEWER-schema DB is still refused and never deleted. ReadOnlyObservabilityStore never deletes. Ships in PR #84.
close_reason: Implemented: ObservabilityStore._ensure_schema deletes a populated older-schema DB (-wal/-shm first, main last) and recreates it with a WARNING; refuses if deletion fails; newer-schema DB still refused and untouched; ReadOnlyObservabilityStore never deletes. Tests: test_replaces_an_older_populated_store, test_an_older_store_that_cannot_be_deleted_is_refused, test_refuses_newer_schema (bytes untouched), read-only never-deletes, archive older-DB replaced / newer-DB degrades. Targeted run 321 passed, 1 skipped.

title: Design: consolidate offload evidence sidecar into observability.sqlite3
description:
Design: move the offload evidence tables (observation_offload_handles, observation_subjects, observation_context_entries, observation_capture_policy, observation_seal_state) from the separate `<observability.sqlite3>.offload-handles.sqlite3` sidecar into `observability.sqlite3` itself. Needs a short design doc before code.

WHY. The sidecar is historical, not designed: it was born in 829450e ("Arm D" observation offloading) as an opt-in, relocatable experiment archive (FW_OFFLOAD_HANDLE_ARCHIVE, temp-file default in tests). 3.4.0 made offloading always-on and removed the override but kept the separate file, with no recorded rationale. Its real requirements do not need a separate file: synchronous persist-before-label (the store already has synchronous BEGIN IMMEDIATE writes; the evidence path must just bypass the droppable sink queue), existing when FW_OBSERVABILITY is off (means: create the DB when offloading needs it), and no-migration convenience (one v6->v7 migration).

WHAT THE SPLIT COSTS (found in a PR #84 server.py review): two paths for one store -> the canonical-vs-db_path mismatch, the equality guard and the workflow_offload_* key namespace in run_forget_channel/run_clear_conversations (the entire behavioural server.py change of PR #84); silent misses via non-canonical db_path, file symlink, or FASTWORKFLOW_STATE_ROOT mismatch; erasure that is atomic per file but not across files; two lifecycles (observability-off orphan sidecar); a DB copy/snapshot that silently omits its evidence.

EVALUATION.
Code: modest net reduction, estimated a few hundred lines of ~2,000 sidecar-related lines (estimate, to be measured in the design doc). Removed: server.py canonical-sweep blocks; store.py _offload_erasure hook plumbing (replaced by deletes inside the store's own transaction); erasure.py file plumbing -- sidecar_path/SIDECAR_SUFFIX, _connect, _compact (second VACUUM), file-exists early returns, per-file BEGIN/commit, .preserve sentinel helpers, structural table discovery (store owns the schema); archive.py ad-hoc 'gain columns on open' schema code moves into the store migration. Stays: preservation policy (scope classification by experiment_id), redaction + sealing + crash sweep, cache reclamation, FW_OFFLOAD_EVENTS filtering, UnavailableHandleArchive-style degrade.
Complexity: large reduction. One path, one transaction, one prune, one VACUUM, one backup unit; eliminates the path-mismatch bug class and cross-file partial erasure; 'erasure is complete or it has not happened' becomes literally true.
Flags/config: ~no reduction. FW_OFFLOAD_EVIDENCE_PRESERVATION, FW_OFFLOAD_EVIDENCE_REDACTION, FW_OFFLOAD_SEAL_GRACE_SECONDS are policy, not location, and stay; FW_OFFLOAD_EVENTS / FW_OFFLOAD_EVENT_BUFFER_MAX / FW_SEARCH_OBSERVATION_MAX_BYTES are unrelated. Only the file-based `<sidecar>.preserve` control goes (fold into PRESERVATION=all or redefine). A real flag reduction would come from a different change: record offload events in the DB and drop FW_OFFLOAD_EVENTS (also deletes _forget_events_file).
New costs / gating risks for the design doc: (1) schema v6->v7 + one-time import of existing sidecars; (2) ReadOnlyObservabilityStore on an older build rejects a newer-schema DB (IncompatibleObservabilityDB), whereas the sidecar left the main schema untouched; (3) write contention: the agent's synchronous evidence writes and the sink's writer thread share one WAL writer lock -- measure turn latency; (4) FW_OBSERVABILITY=0 would now still create observability.sqlite3 (evidence only) -- a documented-behaviour change; (5) sidecar-specific tests (test_offload_evidence_erasure, test_offload_seal_timing, test_offload_state_reclamation, test_offload_archive_unavailable) must be rewritten, not deleted, and any removal needs explicit user approval.

comments.author: Dhar Rawal
comments.text:
Refinements adopted (user, 2026-09-24) -- all ship in PR #84 with the consolidation:

R1. Evidence lives and dies with its turn. Key evidence rows by turn_key (like spans/artifacts); erase and prune via the store's existing turn-scoped DELETEs inside its own transaction. Experiment evidence IS deleted by Clear (matching clear_conversations, which already deletes the experiment records; store.py:5440-5446); forget_channel deletes that channel's evidence, experiment or not. Removes FW_OFFLOAD_EVIDENCE_PRESERVATION, the .preserve sentinel, scope_json classification (scope_experiment_id / is_experiment_scope / scope_is_erasable / scope_channel_id), preserved_scopes reporting, and effectively erasure.py. Drop store_identity/scope_json from evidence rows if nothing else needs them.
R2. Delete dead code: table observation_context_entries (the removed auto-navigation registry) with put_context_entry / list_context_entries (0 production callers, 1 test each), plus list_subjects and pending_aliases (0 callers). Rewrite the one test that exercises them.
R3. Collapse the evidence tables: capture-policy and seal/redaction state become columns on the handle row (they were separate tables only to avoid sidecar migrations, archive.py:366-368, 401). No 'unknown' pre-existing-row states: old sidecar evidence is deleted, not migrated. Keep observation_subjects only if a subject can exist without a handle row (archive.py:312-316); otherwise fold it in too.
R4. Redact at WRITE time, always, with a developer toggle to turn redaction off (FW_OFFLOAD_EVIDENCE_REDACTION=off -> raw bytes stored, row marked unredacted). With redaction on, raw bytes are held only in process memory for the live turn so in-flight reads (search_memory, rehydration) are exact; a turn resumed in a different process reads the redacted text (accepted). Removes the seal lifecycle: seal_state, seal_scope/_seal_*, sweep_unsealed, open-time sweep, owner_id, FW_OFFLOAD_SEAL_GRACE_SECONDS, and the raw-on-disk-during-a-turn exposure window.
R5. Remove FW_OFFLOAD_EVENTS and FW_OFFLOAD_EVENT_BUFFER_MAX: record offload events in a DB table (erased/pruned with the turn), deleting the plaintext events file and _forget_events_file. Remove FW_SEARCH_OBSERVATION_MAX_BYTES: the search bound is derived from the context budget only.

Resulting config surface for offload evidence: FW_OFFLOAD_EVIDENCE_REDACTION only (plus the context window input), down from six env vars + a sentinel file, with FW_OBSERVABILITY also gone.
Effect on children: fix-l4xr, fix-6ile, fix-ma7y, fix-5g7o become moot when this lands (their code disappears); fix-0xsb shrinks to the 'nothing to clear' message, since no evidence is preserved on Clear any more.
Docs/tests to rewrite in the PR: CHANGELOG 3.4.0 entry, docs/observation_search.md (retention/redaction/limits sections), docs/context_budget.md:62, README env table; sidecar/seal/preservation tests rewritten (approved), no test removed without explicit approval.

title: Erasure should report a missing sidecar instead of returning nothing
description: erasure.forget_channel / forget_all_channels (fastworkflow/observation_offloading/erasure.py ~515-517, ~556-558) return {} when the sidecar file does not exist, so callers cannot tell 'this workflow never offloaded' from 'erasure looked in the wrong place'. A PR #84 teaching review reproduced three silent misses that all present identically (no offload keys in the result, raw evidence still on disk): (1) run_forget_channel(non_canonical_db, ch) without workflow_path; (2) the store-side sweep when db_path is a symlink to the file; (3) a deletion script whose FASTWORKFLOW_STATE_ROOT differs from the server that wrote the evidence, so the 'canonical' path is computed under the wrong root (/tmp/pr84_demo_state_root.py: 1 row left, no offload keys). Agreed direction: return an explicit marker (e.g. {'sidecar_missing': 1}, surfacing as offload_sidecar_missing / workflow_offload_sidecar_missing) and log the path that was checked at INFO/WARNING, keeping the file uncreated. Absence is legitimate (a workflow that never offloaded), so this is information, not an error. Note: tests/test_offload_evidence_erasure.py::test_an_absent_sidecar_reports_nothing_rather_than_creating_one asserts no offload_* keys; changing that assertion needs explicit user approval per the testing rules. Consider pairing with fix-0xsb (UI message) so the UI can say 'no evidence file found'.
close_reason: Moot under fix-wys2: there is no second evidence file to be missing; forget/clear/prune report per-table offload_* counts from the store's own transaction. Legacy sidecar files are deleted on open (tests/test_offload_evidence_erasure.py LegacySidecarTests).

title: Offload sidecar cleanup must not depend on the main observability DB existing
description: Observation offloading always creates and fills <observability.sqlite3>.offload-handles.sqlite3 when the agent is built (docs/observation_search.md:513-517), but its cleanup paths hang off the main observability DB: (1) the chatbot UI Clear-conversations POST handler returns {"deleted": {}} early when the main DB file is absent (fastworkflow/run_chatbot/server.py:2306-2308), so run_clear_conversations and its canonical-sidecar sweep never run and the raw execute responses survive a 'clear'; (2) pruning is triggered only by sink install, so with FW_OBSERVABILITY off -- the DEFAULT for library embedders (observability_enabled(default_on=False), store.py:6323) -- the sidecar grows unpruned for the life of the deployment. Agreed fix (option D + warning, from a PR #84 teaching review): give the sidecar its own lifecycle -- prune it when the agent opens it, and have the Clear handler sweep the canonical sidecar even when the main DB is missing -- plus a one-time warning at agent construction when observability is off. Rejected: forcing observability always on (removes a documented switch, forces a trace DB on embedders) and raising when it is off (breaks every embedder by default). Needs an integration test: FW_OBSERVABILITY=0, run a turn, clear, assert sidecar rows gone.

title: Foreign-context routing hint conflicts with the INTENT_MISUNDERSTANDING_CLARIFICATION state it is shown in
description: wildcard.py (PR #84) appends the foreign_context_hint to the you_misunderstood message, and the same branch sets NLU_Pipeline_Stage to INTENT_MISUNDERSTANDING_CLARIFICATION. The body says 'enter one of these command names, otherwise type abort'; the hint says 'Enter it with <enter_command>. Then run <command> there.' Following the hint literally only works when the entering command belongs to the CURRENT context: in the clarification stage the reply is matched only against the current context's commands + CME, the known-name guard does not run, and an unmatched reply hits fix-v8pr (KeyError). The caller has to abort first, which the hint does not say. Options: have the hint say to abort first; or end command processing / reset the stage when a hint is given (the you_misunderstood list is not the useful recovery for a known foreign name); or make the clarification stage walk parents for a known name. Agent-mode path: _resolve_intent_misunderstanding -> clarification agent may pick the hinted command as clarified_cmd and run it in the clarification stage.
acceptance_criteria: Following the hint text literally, from a context that does not own the entering command, reaches the entering command (or the hint text says exactly what to do first); covered by an integration test.
