title: Archived attempt references list turns newest-first, reversing every archived run
description:
ObservabilityWorkspace.attempts() builds each attempt's turn_refs from ObservabilityStore.list_turns(), which documents itself as returning rows newest first (turn_key DESC). Every reference selection_api._workspace_attempts() derives from those refs therefore names an archived run's turns in REVERSE recorded order, while the same attempt read live (best_run.list_task_attempts) names them in order.

PRIORITY: P2. COST: low (one sort where turn_refs are built). RISK: medium -- the fix changes the derived ref_id of every archived reference, and review_pair_key is built from ref_ids, so any recorded comparison feedback anchored on an archived pair stops matching its pair. That is an owner call, not a worker call, which is why this is filed rather than fixed.

EVIDENCE (tests/test_consistency.py::TestSealedWorkspace::test_archived_turn_order_is_reversed_today_and_that_is_a_defect, which witnesses the current behaviour so this fails loudly when fixed): the same attempt seeded once and read twice --
  live   turn_keys [0232e5-a1-t1, 0232e5-a1-t2]
  sealed turn_keys [0232e5-a1-t2, 0232e5-a1-t1]

CONSEQUENCES, all on surfaces that already shipped:
* comparison.project_execution assigns turn_index in reference order, so an archived multi-turn run has its turns numbered backwards. A replan recorded in turn 2 is labelled [turn 1 replan].
* Anything reading the LAST turn reads the first. The new consistency route's final-answer metric compares an archived run's opening answer; observed 13 chars (an in-progress answer) where the live route correctly reads 35 (the completed one).
* The existing sealed /comparison route aligns two archived runs' steps in reverse, so its per-step alignment and its differences list are both reversed.

AFFECTED CODE: fastworkflow/observability/workspace.py ObservabilityWorkspace.attempts (turn_refs construction, ~line 612); consumed by fastworkflow/run_chatbot/selection_api.py _workspace_attempts.

ACCEPTANCE: an archived attempt's turn_refs are in the same order as the same attempt read live; the witness test above is rewritten to assert sealed_keys == live_keys; sealed /comparison alignment and the sealed consistency final-answer metric agree with the live ones for the same evidence; whatever is decided about already-recorded archived-pair feedback keys is recorded on this issue.
acceptance_criteria:
REVISED 2026-09-20 (consistency wave, root-assigned P2; low cost / medium risk,
so no owner gate). The fix is chronological CONTENT with frozen IDENTITY, not a
re-sort of the archived references:

1. Every reference, ref_id and review_pair_key ever filed is unchanged.
   ObservabilityWorkspace.attempts still builds turn_refs from list_turns, and
   an archived reference still names its turns newest-first. Nothing migrates

title: Compare repeated-run consistency in planning, execution and final answers
description:
Measure consistency between repeated attempts of the same task/setup, and show whether consistency improves across multiple-run distillation experiments. Extend the existing task Runs/Compare surfaces and structured read API, not a new dashboard or evaluation system. These are descriptive metrics for human/coding-agent judgment, with no upfront target, automatic winner selection or claim that consistency proves correctness. Chat streaming/final-answer artifacts stay first delivery priority; reproducibility remains deferred.

Initial metrics (cheap, derived from recorded evidence):
1. Planning similarity: cosine similarity between embeddings of recorded user-visible plan text, using one deterministic projection and the same embedding model/preprocessing for both sides. Preserve meaningful step order/content; exclude only volatile display identifiers/timestamps. Use the full recorded plan sequence for a multi-turn attempt, with boundaries explicit. Do not require hidden reasoning or treat absent plans as empty identical plans.
2. Final-answer similarity: cosine similarity of recorded final-answer text using the same comparison contract. Keep this separate from planning similarity and existing artifact comparison; similar wording is not proof of equivalent facts/artifacts or correctness.
3. Execution-step variation: count canonical executed steps from the existing execution ledger, including failed steps/retries/navigation consistently, without double-counting parent wrappers or open/close span updates. Report per-run counts and across-run mean, min/max and population standard deviation. For a run pair, show counts, signed count delta and explicitly labeled normalized step-count difference = 100 * abs(a-b) / max(a,b); both known zero gives 0%. Missing counts are unknown, not zero. Step-count similarity does not imply identical commands/order; links to the existing trace diff remain available.

Within a task/experiment: expose all-run pairwise planning/answer similarity summaries (mean, min/max and spread, with the spread formula documented) and step-count distribution, alongside selected-best-versus-each-other-run values. Best-run selection must not affect the all-run metrics. n=1 yields insufficient repeats rather than perfect consistency. Show contributing attempt IDs, eligible/missing pair counts and recorded statuses. Failed/incomplete attempts remain visible; include available evidence under an explicit rule rather than silently reporting only successful runs. Missing/withheld/truncated evidence is identified; do not present similarity of partial captures as full-output similarity.

Across experiments: align the same task and display baseline/current-winner versus candidate consistency metrics and deltas, together with each repeat count and evidence coverage. Do not pool different tasks or setup revisions silently. Different n can be displayed with denominators; this is descriptive comparison, not statistical significance. Metric definitions, embedding model/revision and text projection must match for a numeric delta; otherwise explain why that metric cannot be directly compared. Record these metric-computation identifiers as derived metadata, not a reproducibility snapshot project.

Reuse a suitable installed local embedding facility where available; no LLM judge or paid provider dependency. Compute derived vectors/metrics on demand and cache outside sealed source evidence by content/model/projection identity. Missing local model yields an actionable unavailable state rather than an implicit model download. Bound requests and pairwise work; any partial/sample calculation must be explicitly labeled with coverage, never presented as all-pairs.

UI: a compact Consistency section on the task Runs/Compare page; per-run rows show best-reference differences, summary shows all-run variation, and cross-experiment comparison shows changes. Clicking a pair opens the existing comparison to annotate it through Observations / Analysis, Conclusions, and Recommendations (see owner-confirmed enum contract below) and their established subcategories. No separate insight-review layer. Coding agents receive the same metric values, definitions, coverage and evidence references through the shared read API.

OWNER-CONFIRMED FEEDBACK CONTRACT (supersedes earlier three-question shorthand):
Categories and allowed subcategories, represented as API enum values:
- observations_analysis (UI: Observations / Analysis): observation, analysis.
- conclusions (UI: Conclusions): what_went_right, what_went_wrong.
- recommendations (UI: Recommendations): what_to_do, what_not_to_do.
The owner confirmed these six meanings explicitly in this implementation session. UI category/subcategory selectors and watermark guidance facilitate free-form human comments; the coding-agent recording API carries category and subcategory explicitly as enums and accepts arbitrary structured text within the comment. Validate category/subcategory pairing. No parsing headings to infer required metadata for NEW writes. Preserve existing historical text without rewriting frozen evidence; uncategorized legacy comments remain readable and visibly legacy/unclassified rather than guessing a new subcategory. Comparison comments can link both recorded executions/pass/step anchors through the same API. No separate insight schema, review layer, or mandatory verdict workflow.
acceptance_criteria: Real recorded/seeded attempts verify: n=1 is insufficient; identical nonempty text has cosine similarity approximately 1 with the selected local embedding implementation; known different vectors verify the cosine calculation independently of semantic thresholds; absent text is unknown. Step counts 2 and 4 produce delta +2, normalized difference 50%, mean 3 and population SD 1; both known zero produce 0% without division errors. Repeated span updates/wrappers do not inflate counts. Missing, failed and partially captured runs produce explicit coverage/status handling. Changing best run changes pair-reference rows but not all-run summaries. Two experiments show task-aligned metric deltas with n/coverage; incompatible metric/model/projection versions do not produce misleading deltas. UI/API parity and pair deep links are verified; annotations use the existing feedback API. No paid calls, automatic downloads or sealed-evidence mutation.
notes:
Triage: P2 / cost medium / risk medium. Useful follow-on to repeated-run comparison; basic math is cheap, with moderate integration effort for local embeddings, cache/coverage and UI/API parity. Main risk is confusing consistent behavior with correct behavior or comparing mismatched metric populations. No mandatory performance targets or winner gate.
Taxonomy corrected from owner clarification. Previous worked/went_wrong/should_change headings are legacy presentation, not the new API category enumeration.
Wave2 starts after accepted P1 commit78b5a2d. title: Nothing fails when the entire server layer skips
description: The full suite reports exit 0 with 3931 passed while 161 tests -- about 70% of all skips and effectively the whole FastAPI/server surface -- are gated on one untracked file. A gate that certifies coverage it does not have is the failure mode AGENTS.md warns about, wearing a friendlier face than a red run. PROPOSED: a session-level check that fails, or at minimum warns loudly at the end of the run, when a whole guarded surface skips. Lower-cost variant: assert a floor on the number of non-skipped tests per guarded module.

title: agent_runtime.py is the highest-risk new module and has the thinnest direct coverage
description:
PROBLEM
fastworkflow/agent_runtime.py is new, is the designated owner of a turn's archive,
result store and finished-scope cleanup, and replaces logic that was previously
scattered across state.py. It is the module in this refactor where a mistake costs the
most. It also has the least direct test contact of anything introduced.

WHAT ACTUALLY TOUCHES IT
`rg -ln "agent_runtime" tests/` returns ONE file: tests/test_offload_state_reclamation.py,
which imports build_turn_runtime at :30 and uses it at one call site, :311
(`agent.turn_runtime = build_turn_runtime(scope, archive=archive)`).

Everything else is reached only indirectly:
  - bind_scope        <- continuation.py:276 and :307
  - finish_scope      <- workflow_execution_context.py close path, continuation.py:272
  - get_result_store  <- result_handles/paging.py:379 (store())
  - scope             <- result_handles/paging.py:622 (current_scope())
  - emit              <- never (see the sibling dead-API bead)

WHY THIS IS MORE THAN A COVERAGE NUMBER
Two of the four intentional behavior deltas in this whole refactor live here or depend
on it (REVIEW-PACKET.md section 2):
  1. store() and current_scope() gained NEW highest-priority branches that consult the
     runtime. Neither branch existed at base, so neither is a "move" that the parity
     argument covers.
  2. TurnRuntime.get_result_store() MEMOIZES, where base re-resolved the archive path on
     every call. For agents built by build_tool_agent both resolve to the same object;
     they diverge only if a caller reassigns agent.observation_archive after
     construction. Nothing currently tests that divergence.
Indirect coverage through continuation/WEC/paging exercises the happy path of the
composition; it does not pin the contract of the object itself.

ON MEASURING COVERAGE - CORRECTION TO THE AUDIT NOTE
The audit reported that neither `coverage` nor `pytest_cov` was installed, so line
coverage could not be measured. A re-check makes that inconclusive rather than settled:
  - coverage 7.9.1 and pytest-cov 6.2.1 ARE importable from the interpreter on PATH
    (/home/drawal/miniconda3/bin/python, 3.12.2) and from /home/drawal/rl/fastworkflow/.venv.
  - But this worktree has no .venv of its own and `poetry env info --path` returns
    nothing, and the PATH interpreter cannot import fastworkflow (dspy 2.6.27 raises
    ImportError on `Module` from dspy.primitives.module at utils/react.py:11).
So the environment the audit measured in is not identified, and coverage tooling may
already be available in whichever interpreter actually runs the suite. Check that first -
installing may not be necessary.
acceptance_criteria: bind_scope, finish_scope, release_scope and get_result_store each have at least one direct test, including the memoization behavior of get_result_store; line coverage for agent_runtime.py is measured and recorded.

title: evidence_readers.subject_evidence re-implements answer_attribution.subject_index
description:
PROBLEM
The split left two independent implementations of the same rule - "which observations
belong to which subject, judged by the observation's clause".

    fastworkflow/evidence_readers.py:169-189
        subject_evidence() builds `by_subject` inline:
            by_subject = {
                entity.key: [item for item in evidence
                             if item.clause and writes(item.clause, forms[entity.key])]
                for entity in items
            }

    fastworkflow/answer_attribution.py:546
        subject_index() computes the same mapping.

Both are live:
  - subject_index is reached via check_attribution (answer_attribution.py:636:
    `subjects = subject_index(items, evidence, allow_segments=allow_segments)`)
  - evidence_readers.subject_evidence is reached from answer_attribution.py:599 and
    answer_coverage.py:669
Both are also in answer_attribution's __all__ (lines 744-745).

CONSEQUENCE
They are semantically identical today, so there is no live bug. The reason this still
earns a bead is what subject_index's own docstring says it is FOR: it exists so that the
forward evidence sentence and the after-the-fact attribution check apply one rule and
therefore "can never disagree". Two copies defeat exactly that guarantee. The copies can
now drift, and the failure mode when they do is the worst kind - a coverage claim and
its verification quietly disagreeing about what counted as evidence, with no exception
and no failing test.

This is the same defect class the cleanup pass already had to fix twice in this refactor
(the dead _segment_tail copy at answer_attribution.py:212 that a test was asserting
against while the live rule read the other copy, and the duplicated MAX_CURSOR_PAGE).
That is why P2 rather than P3: the pattern has a demonstrated record of producing real
defects in this specific change.

SUGGESTED SHAPE
Have subject_evidence call subject_index (or move subject_index into evidence_readers
and have answer_attribution re-export it), so the rule has one definition and both
directions read it.
acceptance_criteria: There is exactly one implementation of 'which observations belong to which subject'; both the forward evidence sentence and check_attribution reach it, so they cannot disagree by construction.

title: result_handles/paging.py still means 'everything not yet extracted' at ~2,550 lines
description:
PROBLEM
The module split moved six components out of the 3,705-line monolith, but what remains
in fastworkflow/result_handles/paging.py has no single named responsibility. It is
defined by subtraction: everything that was not extracted.

SIZE
2,548 lines as reported in REVIEW-PACKET.md section 1 (measured pre-cleanup); 2,572 in
the live post-cleanup tree. Either way that is ~68.8% of the original monolith still
sitting in one file.

MID-FILE MODULE-LEVEL IMPORTS
On top of the normal header import block, five module-level imports appear part-way
down the file. Verified with `ruff check --select E402` against the live tree:

    paging.py:248  from ...result_handles.models import ResultHandleSpec, SourceDescriptor
    paging.py:296  from ...result_handles.store import ResultHandleStore
    paging.py:759  from ...result_handles.cursors import (...)   # 6 names
    paging.py:767  from ...result_handles import cursors as _cursor_component
    paging.py:943  from ...result_handles.rendering import ResultPage, _assemble, _pack

(The packet cites these as lines 245/293/753/760/919; they shifted by a few lines in the
cleanup pass. 248 and 296 were reported as one finding each; 759 and 767 are adjacent
and were counted as one in the packet, hence "5 imports" vs ruff's 6 E402 findings.)

These are the full set of remaining ruff findings on the new package apart from one
F401 on the facade, and the packet records them as pre-existing/accepted.

CONSEQUENCE
Reviewability, NOT correctness. Nothing here is a behavior defect and nothing is
blocking. But a 2,500-line file whose boundary is "the leftovers" is the state the split
was performed to get out of, and the mid-file imports are a signal about which further
extractions are entangled - each one marks a point where a later component had to be
pulled in after code that uses it was already defined.

SUGGESTED NEXT STEP
Name the responsibilities still living in paging.py before extracting anything further;
the mid-file import positions are a reasonable map of the seams.
acceptance_criteria: paging.py has a stateable single responsibility that fits in one sentence without the word 'and'; the mid-file module-level imports are either hoisted or their cycle is documented in place.

title: Writer restart overwrites the predecessor's writer-health row: SQLiteTraceSink.close() and the heartbeat upsert counters from zero, so health_delta's max(0, after-before) hides drops across a restart
description: Found by the fix-485 implementer 2026-09-07. The fix-485 baseline row uses ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING, but close() force-persists the sink's own counters and the periodic heartbeat upserts them, so a second writer process (or a restart in the same process) resets the persisted row to its own counts. evidence_run's delta = max(0, after - before) then reads a smaller 'after' as zero drops. tests/test_evidence_run.py::test_reopening_a_store_does_not_reset_its_writer_health documents the current boundary. Candidates: monotone merge on upsert (never lower a counter), or per-writer-incarnation rows summed by health_snapshot, or invalidate any segment whose interval spans a writer restart (detectable from the pid/incarnation stamp). Related: fix-7de, fix-485.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-09-07 (awaiting review).

No schema change: writer_health is a diagnostics JSON blob (set_diagnostic), SCHEMA_VERSION stays 3. Confirmed before touching anything.

Merge: merge_writer_health() (observability_store.py:137 block) folds a writer's snapshot into the stored row. _HEALTH_MONOTONE_COUNTERS (records_dropped, spans_dropped, write_errors, busy_retries, refused_terminal_writes, sync_writes, sync_fallbacks, sync_write_ms_max, dropped_turn_keys_elided) take max(stored, incoming); the affected-turn-key lists are unioned under the existing _DROP_TURN_KEY_MAX cap with the overflow added to dropped_turn_keys_elided; last_error survives a writer that has not errored yet; everything else (gauges, the incarnation stamp) takes the newcomer's value. A FLOOR, not a sum, and it cannot be a sum: every persist carries the writer's cumulative total, so adding would re-count the same drop on every heartbeat. Consequence documented in the docstring: a successor's own smaller counts are invisible under a predecessor's larger ones, which is exactly what the incarnation guard covers.

Single write path: ObservabilityStore.merge_writer_health_row(conn, incoming) (:2680), called under the caller's BEGIN IMMEDIATE from _publish_baseline_health, _maybe_write_health (heartbeat + force) and therefore close(). fix-485's set_diagnostic_if_absent is deleted -- the merge does its job properly and for the two writes (heartbeat, close) where the clobbering actually happened.

Incarnation: SQLiteTraceSink._incarnation = {id: uuid4, pid, host, started_at, open} (:5341), carried in _health[WRITER_INCARNATION_FIELD] so it rides both the live health_snapshot() and the persisted row. close() (:5712) stamps a NEW dict with open=False before setting _stop (so the writer's exit write already says so) and then force-persists after the join -- guarded by _owns_its_db_file() so a sink recycled because its DB was deleted/replaced cannot resurrect or stamp the wrong file. That open flag is also what lets archive_to refuse a writer it cannot reach (fix-7de).

health_delta (:553) sets writer_restarted / writer_incarnation_before / writer_incarnation_after when BOTH snapshots carry a stamp and they differ. WriterHealthDelta.evidence_valid is False when restarted, and problems() emits the reason worst-first (right after incomparable). A snapshot with no stamp -- the in-process {} baseline evidence_run uses for a sink that appeared mid-run -- is not reported as a restart. evidence_run needed no change: the reason flows through delta.problems() into EvidenceRun.problems(), run.valid goes False, and the recorded segment lands with valid=0.

Tests (tests/test_evidence_run.py): test_reopening_a_store_does_not_reset_its_writer_health rewritten -- counters and turn keys still survive, the row is now re-stamped with the running writer, and the updated_at-equality assertion is gone (a re-stamp writes). Added test_counters_never_decrease_across_a_close_and_reopen (first writer drops 2 + a span, second drops 1: row stays 2, span counter untouched, turn-key lists unioned), test_a_writer_restart_inside_the_interval_invalidates_the_run (asserts the verbatim problem string), test_a_writer_restart_outside_the_interval_does_not (predecessor's drop is history in both snapshots, run stays valid).

Focused: 226 passed, 1 skipped. Wider observability sweep: 658 passed, 111 skipped. No commit made.
close_reason: Reviewed 2026-09-07. writer_health persisted through one merge path (merge_writer_health_row): monotone max on counters, union on turn-key lists under the cap, newcomer gauges; writer incarnation {id,pid,host,started_at,open} stamped on the row and in the live snapshot; close() re-stamps open=False and persists through the same merge, guarded by _owns_its_db_file; health_delta sets writer_restarted when stamps differ and evidence_run invalidates the segment with a verbatim reason. fix-485's set_diagnostic_if_absent superseded. No schema change (JSON diagnostics blob). Tests: counters never decrease across close/reopen; restart inside interval invalidates, outside does not. Orchestrator re-run passes.

title: External-driver experiment observability and review workspaces
description:
Context
FastWorkflow experiment capture currently runs only through the in-process ExperimentHarness. External HTTP drivers lack an exact declaration/store handshake, globally fenced claim and checkpoint identity, post-shutdown evidence sealing, and multi-store review workspace. run_chatbot opens only the default store.

Scope
Provide a driver-neutral lifecycle with exact attempt declarations and required evidence segments; persistent store identity; hashed one-use bootstrap capabilities, atomic labelled-conversation claim and cross-process epochs; versioned checkpoint propagation; WAL-free archive sealing; observability workspaces; and capability-authenticated review sidecar integration with fix-9eg. Preserve existing in-process harness and ordinary chatbot behavior.

Non-goals
Do not embed IDO vocabulary, replace the public HTTP path, treat channel IDs as capabilities, mutate sealed evidence, or make run_chatbot a score authority.
design: Generic mechanisms live in FastWorkflow; consumer semantics remain external. One startup owner migrates before readiness; controllers target explicit stores. A hashed bootstrap atomically claims the exact declaration under a global epoch. Epoch/server identity fences admission, commands, turns and every async trace envelope at persistence; stale records invalidate evidence. Sealed evidence is post-shutdown WAL-free archive. Formal review uses a separate versioned sidecar with per-rater capabilities and append-only revisions.
acceptance_criteria: On a release-shaped branch from freshly fetched upstream main, generic prerequisites and external support provide exact declarations, globally fenced public-path attempts, sealed workspaces, and authenticated review; IDO acceptance and required validation pass. Only after separate fix-rj2.13 owner approval, fix-rj2.12 submits a reviewed 3.3.0 PR to radiantlogicinc/main. No agent directly writes main, merges, tags, or publishes.

Owner permits reuse of ~/rl/fastworkflow-observability at implementation start. fix-rj2.11 ports generic prerequisites from fresh upstream main; 401e111 is reference-only. fix-rj2.13 is an independent human gate for fix-rj2.12. title: Test isolation: test_turn_and_cme_continuation leaks state that breaks test_run_chatbot_server's seeded_db fixture
description:
Running 'pytest tests/test_turn_and_cme_continuation.py tests/test_run_chatbot_server.py' produces 1 failure + 82 setup errors; each file alone passes. The errors are all 'assert conv_id == 1' in the seeded_db fixture (tests/test_run_chatbot_server.py:98), with conv_id climbing 2, 3, 4... across tests -- i.e. every test is minting into the SAME observability DB instead of its own tmp_path one, so a process-global sink or a FASTWORKFLOW_STATE_ROOT/workflow-id resolution is leaking between the two modules. The accompanying failure is TestReadOnlyViewer::test_viewer_does_not_create_a_missing_db.

VERIFIED PRE-EXISTING: reproduced identically on a clean tree (git stash of all fix-bn1 changes) -- 1 failed, 27 passed, 82 errors both before and after. Found while running a regression sweep for fix-bn1; filed rather than fixed because it is unrelated to that epic.

WHY IT MATTERS: 82 tests silently do not run whenever these two files share a process, and pytest-randomly is enabled by default in this repo, so which pairs land together varies run to run. A green CI line can mean 'those 82 were skipped by an ERROR', which is the failure mode the observability epic's own testing philosophy exists to avoid.
acceptance_criteria: Both files pass in either order in one pytest process, and seeded_db gets a genuinely per-test database.
notes:
ROOT CAUSE: state_paths._optional_env reads fastworkflow._env_vars BEFORE os.environ, and fastworkflow.init() REPLACES that dict wholesale (__init__.py:253). tests/test_turn_and_cme_continuation.py:32 calls init({'FASTWORKFLOW_STATE_ROOT': tmp_path/'workflow_contexts'}) and nothing ever restored it, so from that point every later test in the process resolved state_root() to that one dead tmp dir - silently overriding the OS variable conftest.isolate_state_root sets. Every test then minted conversations into ONE leaked observability.sqlite3, which is why test_run_chatbot_server's seeded_db fixture saw conv_id 2, 3, 4... instead of 1 (82 setup ERRORs + 1 failure).

CORRECTION to the original filing: pytest-randomly is NOT installed in this venv ('-p randomly' -> No module named randomly), so ordering is deterministic/alphabetical. That is why the full suite stayed green: test_run_chatbot_server sorts BEFORE the offender. The leak still poisons anything sorting after it; nothing currently depends on the root that late, so the blast radius today is latent rather than active.

FIX: conftest.isolate_state_root now snapshots and restores fastworkflow._env_vars around every test (rebinding, not mutating, because init() rebinds the module global). This keeps the documented 'the dict wins over the OS environment' behaviour INSIDE a test while making it impossible for that win to escape one. The offending fixture is left as-is - it legitimately wants its own root, and it is now safely scoped.

REGRESSION TEST: tests/test_state_isolation.py. test_a pins a root exactly as the offender does; test_b asserts it did not escape (verified: fails without the conftest restore, passes with it); test_c/test_d assert the root's CONTENTS are empty at setup - note the root's PATH is deliberately recycled between tests (the fixture rmtree's it, so mktemp hands out fw_state_root0 again), so 'unique path per test' is not the contract and asserting it would be a false invariant.
close_reason: Fixed: conftest.isolate_state_root now snapshots and restores fastworkflow._env_vars around every test. Root cause was state_paths._optional_env preferring _env_vars over os.environ combined with init() replacing that dict wholesale, so one test's state-root pin leaked to every later test in the process. Regression test in tests/test_state_isolation.py (verified to fail without the fix). Original pair goes from 1 failed/27 passed/82 errors to 110 passed in both orders.

title: pinned_span_count is resolved by the writer, not read by the producer on the turn thread
description:
RECONSTRUCTED 2026-08-29 from shipped code and tests. Landed in 3351f92 (merged 7a0340e) but was never filed as a bead; it is the citation at observability_store.py:640 that started this whole reconstruction. Filed retroactively and closed so it resolves.

THE PROBLEM. [DR43] wants pinned_span_count to be the trace's LIVE span count at the moment the pin is taken. The producer used to read it with its own sqlite3 connection -- a synchronous DB read on the TURN THREAD at the completion of every pinned run, stacked on top of the barrier waits the user is already paying for.

THE FIX. A sentinel, COUNT_LIVE_SPANS = "@fw.count-live-spans". A producer sets pinned_span_count to it and the WRITER resolves the column from the table inside the batch transaction it is already running, where the count is a free join. Costs the user nothing.

CORRECTNESS ARGUMENT, worth keeping: the pass rows are enqueued ahead of the run row and the record queue is FIFO, so they are already applied when the count runs; turn_key is unioned in so a run whose pass rows were lost still counts its own trace. Spans in the SAME batch are applied after the records, which leaves the count a slight UNDER-count -- deliberately the same conservative direction as the previous behaviour, so the pin never claims to protect more than it does.

WHERE IT LIVES: observability_store.py -- the sentinel and its rationale (~638-646), the docstring contract (~1814), and the resolution inside upsert_distillation_row (~1825).

TEST: tests/test_distillation_observability.py ~2706 -- "the pin costs the turn thread nothing" / "pinned_span_count is resolved by the WRITER".
close_reason: Closed

title: Retention pin classes partition on 'produced an insight', not on 'diverged'
description:
RECONSTRUCTED 2026-08-29 from shipped code and tests. Landed in 3351f92 (merged 7a0340e) but was never filed as a bead. Filed retroactively and closed so its citations resolve.

THE DISTINCTION. Section 10.3 defines two retention pin classes, and they partition on "produced an insight", NOT on "diverged". Those are different predicates: a run can AGREE and still carry an insight. The no-divergence class is time-limited (FW_OBS_DISTILL_NEGATIVE_PIN_DAYS, default 90) because a no-divergence run is contradiction evidence with a shelf life; an insight-producing run is pinned FOREVER and released only by the rejected-only arm.

WHY IT MATTERS, and it is forward-looking rather than a live bug: nothing produces an agreeing-run-with-an-insight today, because extraction is gated on divergence. But fix-sb8.11's counterfactual replay is PRECISELY an agreeing run that says something about an insight -- a replay that succeeds removes the divergence and still bears on the insight it was run to test. Had the pins partitioned on "diverged", replay evidence would have aged out on the 90-day negative clock, and the failure mode is silent evidence loss for the most interesting class of run in the epic.

WHERE IT LIVES: observability_store.py ~3326 (the two arms and the partition rationale) and ~3334 (the release query's comment spelling out that the two predicates differ).

TESTS: tests/test_observability_store.py ~975 ("allowed to release") and ~1558 ("the two section 10.3 pin classes partition on produced-an-insight").
close_reason: Closed

title: test_auto_spawn_defaults_to_unsigned_dev_jwt asserts a hard-coded port 8123 and fails whenever anything holds it
description:
CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL DESCRIPTION, 2026-08-29. It claimed "the busy-port fallback is currently only exercised by accident" and proposed building deliberate coverage for it. That is FALSE and would have sent the next reader off to write a test that already exists.

tests/test_run_chatbot_test_mode.py::TestSpawnDecision::test_busy_server_port_moves_to_a_free_one already covers the moved path deliberately and well: it binds a squatter socket on an ephemeral port, passes that as server_port, and asserts all three things that matter -- the chosen port differs from the requested one, server_url matches the port actually chosen, and server_note names the busy one.

So the real defect was much narrower than filed: ONE test hard-coded a port literal it did not need.

FIXED. test_auto_spawn_defaults_to_unsigned_dev_jwt's subject is JWT defaults (allow_unsigned_jwt, expect_encrypted_jwt, jwt_mode); the port was incidental scaffolding. It now takes a port that is genuinely free at that instant via a new module-level _an_unused_port() helper (bind to 127.0.0.1:0, read getsockname, close -- the same bind/close/rebind window _free_server_port itself lives with, and the mirror of the idiom the busy-port test already uses).

The port assertion is KEPT rather than dropped, because it is the only coverage of the happy path -- preferred port free, so the spawn uses it -- and a new assertion that server_note is None pins that a free port reports no move. Dropping it would have left only the moved path tested.

NEGATIVE CONTROL: with _free_server_port forced to always move (candidates reduced to ((0, True),)), the test fails. So the assertion still catches a real regression rather than passing vacuously against whatever port the code happens to return, which is the failure mode this kind of fix invites.

CHECKED AND LEFT ALONE: test_named_server_port_skips_spawn_and_exposes_the_url hard-codes 9000 the same way but is safe -- it runs the no_server=True path, which returns at server.py:540 and formats the URL verbatim with no port probe, so nothing can squat it.

ORIGINAL REPORT BELOW, for the record.
--------------------------------------------------------------------
The test passed server_port=8123 and asserted session["server_url"] ended in :8123. run_chatbot deliberately does NOT spawn onto a busy port -- _free_server_port (server.py:325) probes by binding and falls back to an ephemeral port -- so the assertion held only when 8123 happened to be free on the machine running the suite.

On this box it was not: a long-running `python -m fastworkflow.run_fastapi_mcp --workflow_path ido_workflow` (the IDO evaluation server, started 2026-08-28 14:05) holds 127.0.0.1:8123. Confirmed with ss -ltnp, and confirmed to fail identically at clean HEAD with all working-tree changes stashed, so it was never caused by a code change.

It also failed in the confusing direction: the message points at JWT/spawn behaviour when the real cause is a port.
acceptance_criteria: The test passes regardless of what is listening on 8123; the busy-port fallback is asserted deliberately rather than relied on being unexercised.
close_reason: Closed

title: AskUserSuspend escapes _execute_workflow_query with no finally, leaking an open fw.agent.tool_call span for the rest of the turn
description:
Found 2026-08-29 while surveying every span-close site for fix-ajv.19.

_execute_workflow_query (workflow_agent.py ~L215-280) opens an fw.agent.tool_call span and closes it in exactly three places: the success path at the end, an "except CommandCancelledError" branch, and an "except Exception" branch. There is no finally.

AskUserSuspend subclasses BaseException specifically so that "except Exception" does not swallow it (utils/react.py:21-27). The code KNOWS this -- the comment in the CommandCancelledError branch says so explicitly: "AskUserSuspend subclasses BaseException, so `except Exception` below never catches it either."

But nothing catches it here at all. So when a tool suspends via AskUserSuspend, the exception passes through this frame to the react loop (which catches it and returns a suspended sentinel), and the fw.agent.tool_call span opened at the top of this function is NEVER CLOSED. It leaks open onto the parenting stack for the remainder of the turn.

That is the same class of defect the sibling site guards against deliberately -- workflow_execution_context.py:1543-1552 exists precisely so "the span must close rather than leak onto the parenting stack for the rest of the turn".

CONSEQUENCE: every agent-mode ask_user leaves an open fw.agent.tool_call span. Subsequent spans in the turn parent under it, so the waterfall nests wrongly from the suspension onward, and the span never gets an end time or status.

SUGGESTED FIX: catch BaseException for the span-closing decision, or restructure as try/finally so no exception type can escape without closing. Whichever status mapping fix-ajv.19 settles on should apply here too -- this is a fourth site with the same question.

Note this is why fix-ajv.19's inventory matters: the AskUserSuspend handling is inconsistent across FOUR sites, not two, and this one does not merely mislabel the span, it loses it.
acceptance_criteria: An AskUserSuspend raised from an agent tool closes its fw.agent.tool_call span; no span remains open on the parenting stack after a suspension; test covers the agent-mode ask_user path.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-29 together with fix-ajv.19's shared mapping.

_execute_workflow_query's arm named only CommandCancelledError, and the comment beside it even observed that AskUserSuspend 'subclasses BaseException, so except Exception below never catches it either' -- and then nothing caught it there at all. It is now 'except BaseException as e' with three arms:
 - control signal (tracing.is_control_signal): close via the shared mapping, re-raise
 - any other non-Exception BaseException (KeyboardInterrupt, SystemExit): close the span so it cannot leak, but do NOT build a failure CommandOutput -- that is reserved for real command failures, and this frame must not dress an interpreter-level signal as one
 - ordinary Exception: unchanged, the existing failure-capture path

NEGATIVE CONTROL, and it showed the leak was worse than 'unclosed': with the old arm restored, the test's assertion fails as 'assert []' -- the fw.agent.tool_call span was never emitted to the sink AT ALL, because it is emitted on close. So an agent-mode ask_user did not merely leave a span open on the parenting stack, it lost the span entirely.

TEST: tests/test_command_executor_errors.py::test_the_agent_tool_span_is_closed_even_when_a_control_signal_escapes, parametrized over both control signals.
close_reason: Closed

title: AskUserSuspend closes its command span as ERROR in one layer and awaiting_user in another; suspensions render as failures in the trace UI
description:
Two layers close a span for the SAME control signal and disagree about its status, so a suspended ask_user renders as a red ERROR node in the chatbot trace waterfall.

THE DISAGREEMENT
workflow_execution_context.py:1543-1552 -- comment reads "CommandCancelledError/AskUserSuspend are control signals, not failures":
    status = STATUS_AWAITING_USER if isinstance(exc, (AskUserSuspend, CommandCancelledError)) else STATUS_ERROR

command_executor.py (error path of invoke_command):
    status = STATUS_CANCELLED if isinstance(exc, CommandCancelledError) else STATUS_ERROR

So for the same signal:
  CommandCancelledError -> awaiting_user (WEC)  vs  cancelled (CME)
  AskUserSuspend        -> awaiting_user (WEC)  vs  ERROR     (CME)

The fix-ajv.16 change made this visible rather than causing it: it introduced is_control_signal covering BOTH exceptions for the recording decision, while leaving the status ternary covering only one. The file now classifies the same exception two ways three lines apart.

USER-VISIBLE SYMPTOM, not theoretical
run_chatbot/static/index.html:1671 appends " . ERROR" to any span whose status is "error", and :1042 sets detail "error" from the same test. An ask_user suspension -- an ordinary, successful pause for input -- therefore renders as a failed node in the trace tree. index.html already renders awaiting_user correctly elsewhere (:803, :840, :2342, :2356 show "in progress" / "awaiting your reply"), so the status value it needs is one the UI already understands.

SUGGESTED FIX
Align command_executor's ternary with the WEC precedent, reusing the is_control_signal predicate that is already computed one line above:
    status = STATUS_AWAITING_USER if is_control_signal else STATUS_ERROR

OPEN DECISION, needs a human -- do not let the implementer pick silently
That alignment leaves STATUS_CANCELLED with no producer at this site. Two readings:
 (a) AWAITING_USER is correct for both, and CME's use of CANCELLED was always the outlier -> adopt the fix above and consider whether STATUS_CANCELLED has any remaining producer at all.
 (b) CANCELLED is the right value for a cancellation and AWAITING_USER for a suspension, and it is WEC that is wrong to collapse them -> then the fix is a three-way mapping in BOTH places, and WEC changes too.
The distinction is not cosmetic: a reader querying spans for cancelled-vs-suspended behaviour gets different answers depending on which layer closed the span, and today neither layer is authoritative.

TEST: a span closed for AskUserSuspend must not carry STATUS_ERROR; whichever mapping is chosen must be identical in command_executor.py and workflow_execution_context.py, pinned by a test that fails if one is changed without the other.
acceptance_criteria: AskUserSuspend no longer closes a command-execute span with STATUS_ERROR; command_executor.py and workflow_execution_context.py use one agreed mapping; a test fails if either is changed alone; the ask_user suspension no longer renders as an ERROR node in the chatbot waterfall.
notes:
COMPLETED 2026-08-29, and the taxonomy question is now settled with a reason rather than by majority vote.

DECISION: control signals close as STATUS_CANCELLED, not STATUS_AWAITING_USER. `awaiting_user` is a TURN-level state in this codebase -- the store's non-terminal turn status, and the only thing the SPA ever tests for (index.html:803/840/2342 all read turn.status; span.status is only ever tested for "error", at :1042 and :1671). NOTHING anywhere reads a SPAN status of awaiting_user. A span status describes that span's own outcome -- this dispatch was cut short -- while "we are waiting on a human" is recorded once, on the turn, where readers already look. That also makes WEC:1546, the lone awaiting_user producer, the site that was borrowing a turn-level word for a span nothing read.

SHIPPED: tracing.is_control_signal(exc) and tracing.status_for_dispatch_exception(exc) -- ONE mapping in ONE place, with deferred imports because both defining modules import tracing. All six sites now route through it:
  command_executor.py            (was: AskUserSuspend -> ERROR)
  workflow_execution_context.py x3, two of which had a separate `except CommandCancelledError` arm that left AskUserSuspend falling through to the BaseException arm and closing as ERROR -- collapsed into one arm
  workflow_agent.py              (fix-ajv.21, the leaked span)
  utils/react.py
This is stronger than the "a test fails if either is changed alone" this bead originally asked for: it removes the possibility of drift rather than detecting it.

TESTS: tests/test_command_executor_errors.py -- the helper's mapping as a unit test, an explicit pin that awaiting_user is never produced for a dispatch (so the taxonomy decision is not silently reverted), and the existing control-signal tests parametrized over both signals. Negative controls confirmed for both this and .21.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S ORIGINAL RECOMMENDATION, left here on purpose: option (a) was recommended on the strength of two sites and asserted that awaiting_user was right and CANCELLED was the outlier. The six-site survey showed the reverse -- CANCELLED was dominant at five of six. The shipped decision agrees with (a)'s instinct that ONE mapping is needed and with the survey's evidence about WHICH, which is not what (a) said.
close_reason: Closed

title: Scoring and arm comparison: pass@1 / pass^k over an experiment, baseline vs treatment
description:
What the container is FOR. With experiment_id/task_id/attempt on turns, these become GROUP BY queries instead of bespoke analysis scripts.

- per-task outcome across attempts; pass@1 and pass^k for the experiment
- comparison of an experiment against its baseline_experiment_id: per-task deltas, which tasks flipped in each direction, and how many flips are attributable to variance rather than the change
- a score is only reportable if the experiment status is 'complete'; an invalid or running experiment must refuse to render a headline number rather than render a provisional one

The pass^k / disjoint-pass-set subtlety matters here: an agent that passes each task often can still fail pass^k, so per-attempt outcomes must be retained rather than collapsed to a per-task rate at write time. Do not store only the aggregate.

This is the query layer fix-9eg.3 currently lacks a boundary for, and the same layer fix-sb8.10's corpus view needs. Build it once, against experiment_id, and let both consume it.
notes: Shipped in observability_store: experiment_scores (pass@1, pass^k, per-task, per-attempt) and compare_experiments. Scores computed against the DECLARED denominator, never surviving rows; no headline number unless status='complete'. Comparison refuses unless both complete, same declared shape, EQUAL task-id sets, and same capture profile/policy version. Answers the bead's variance question without claiming significance: _expected_flip_probability pools both arms per task and reports expected_flips_if_nothing_changed beside observed_flips, with the caveat rendered next to the number in the UI. Per-attempt outcomes are retained, never collapsed to a rate. This is the boundary fix-9eg.3 lacks.
close_reason: Closed

title: Chatbot UI: experiment browser (experiment -> task -> attempt), and the annotation panel
description:
The SPA already builds channel_id -> conversation_id -> [turns] for the debug rail (static/index.html ~L675-736). Experiment -> task -> attempt is the same three-level grouping over different keys, so this extends that code path rather than adding a second tree.

Views:
- experiment list: label, description excerpt, status, score, arm badge, created_at
- experiment detail: hypothesis and notes rendered prominently (the hypothesis is the point of the record), evidence-run validity, provenance
- task -> attempt drill-down, each attempt linking to its existing turn/trace views so no trace rendering is rewritten
- an INVALID experiment must be visually unmistakable; a run with dropped turn records has an unreconstructable denominator and must never look like a clean score

Annotation panel:
- notes editable inline
- hypothesis shown read-only after creation, with an explicit affordance explaining why (it is write-once by design, not a bug) - otherwise the first person to hit it files it as one
- creating an experiment from the UI must ask for the hypothesis BEFORE the run starts

Depends on fix-bn1.5 for data.
notes: Shipped in run_chatbot/static/index.html: Experiments rail button -> experiment list -> detail -> task -> attempt, drilling down inside #detail (the showCorpus precedent) rather than adding a second tree or a third top-level panel. Attempt rows link into the existing trace view via openTurnInDebug. Invalid experiments render an unmistakable .expInvalid block with the reason; hypothesis is read-only with the reason attached so nobody files it as a bug; notes editable inline via PATCH; baseline comparison rendered with the expected-flips-under-no-change caveat beside the number. api() now parses error bodies so the compare 409's per-problem reason reaches the operator. No innerHTML, no external URLs, one script tag, one file.

description:
Serve the stored records to the SPA and to scripts, following the existing handler conventions in fastworkflow/run_chatbot/server.py (parameterized SQL, store reads off the event loop, channel scoping).
