title: Experiment container: run and observe a task set as one measured object
description:
An experiment is a labelled set of tasks, each run one or more times, whose turns can be found, scored, and compared as a unit. No such object exists today.

WHAT EXISTS AND WHY IT IS NOT THIS

- observability.sqlite3 is three-level: channel -> conversation -> turn, with conversations PK (channel_id, conversation_id) and idx_turns_conv. /api/channels, /api/conversations?channel=, /api/turns?channel=&conversation= all ship, and the SPA already groups channel_id -> conversation_id -> [turns] (index.html ~L675). The READ shape generalises for free; the missing thing is the grouping dimension.
- fastworkflow/observability/evidence_run.py mints a run_id per measured run and asserts zero-drop, prune suppression, archival, provenance. But run_id lives ONLY in the bundle JSON EvidenceRun.as_record() writes. No column joins a turn back to the run it belonged to. That is the gap in one sentence.
- fix-9eg.3 aggregates per workflow over whatever turns are in the DB, with no experiment boundary to GROUP BY.
- fix-9eg.11-.15 (review rubric, assignment ingest, blinded mode, export) all begin from 'an assignment exists' and never say where the runs came from.
- fix-sb8.2 defines distillation_runs: one row per compared MESSAGE. That is a single trial, one level below this.

REJECTED: channel_id AS THE EXPERIMENT LABEL
The obvious mapping (channel = experiment, conversation = task) fails because channel_id is the live-session key, not a label:
1. It is the concurrency lease. Every FastAPI route runs under leased_session(channel_id); a second turn on the same channel gets 409 ChannelBusyError. Tasks in an experiment could never run in parallel.
2. It is the suspended-state key. SessionStateStore.load/save/clear(channel_id) holds the ask_user pending blob; all tasks would share one slot.
3. Topic uniquification is channel-scoped (_unique_topic_in_txn suffixes collisions across the channel), so repeating a task set inside one channel yields 'Task 3', 'Task 3 1', 'Task 3 2' - titles stop being join keys exactly when needed.
4. conversation_id is an INTEGER from a per-channel counter, so task identity would have to live in topic: LLM-generated AND uniquified, the worst available join key.
5. Two levels cannot express experiment -> task -> attempt, and repeats are what pass^k needs.
chat_session.py:127 already mints channel_id=f'cli:{timestamp}' - one channel per run. Channel is a session; this epic adds a labelling dimension beside it and leaves channel semantics untouched.

SHAPE
experiments(experiment_id PK, label, hypothesis, notes, arm, baseline_experiment_id, status, created_at, provenance_json)
conversations/turns += experiment_id, task_id, attempt (nullable; NULL = not part of an experiment)
index on (experiment_id, task_id, attempt)

hypothesis is WRITE-ONCE at creation and notes is freely editable, deliberately: one mutable description lets a predicted result be rewritten after seeing the outcome, which is the failure pre-registration exists to prevent.

arm + baseline_experiment_id exist for fix-sb8.11 (counterfactual replay), which otherwise has nowhere to record what it is the counterfactual OF.

SERVES THREE USES WITH ONE OBJECT
- an eval run: 15 tau2 hard tasks, 3 attempts each, scored pass^3
- a distillation sweep over a corpus (the level above fix-sb8.2s per-message run row)
- a controlled comparison: corpus C with insight #7 injected vs baseline C

Distillation is an INSTRUMENT, not an experiment - but it is run inside one. fix-sb8s own promotion bar ('how many turns support it, which turns contradict it, and whether applying it actually removes the divergence') is a paired A/B over a fixed task set, inexpressible without this container.

COORDINATION RISK - READ BEFORE STARTING
SCHEMA_VERSION lives in PRAGMA user_version, readers FAIL CLOSED on a forward version (IncompatibleObservabilityDB), and there is no numbered migration chain. fix-sb8.1 is already escalating a version-bump-as-compatibility-break for the distillation tables. This epic is a second schema change to the same DB. The two MUST share one Phase 0 and one version bump, or two mutually incompatible DB versions end up in flight.
notes: Code review completed to 100% in round 3: 8 lenses, 41 findings, every one independently verified by a refuting agent (24 upheld, 17 refuted, 0 agent failures). All 24 fixed. Most serious: complete_experiment compared a COUNT against the declared denominator instead of the declared SHAPE, so a resume with a changed task list was stamped 'complete' and experiment_scores returned pass@1=1.33 with reportable=True - reproduced before fixing. Also fixed: evidence gate discarded flush()'s durability bool (a dead writer certified itself zero-drop); _warm_routers warmed the wrong cache; a closed experiment accepted new attempts, overwriting quoted verdicts; segment invalidity was rewritable; capture-regime drift silently kept; migration guard keyed on 1 of 3 columns; experiment_id scrubbed on some routes and raw on others. Round 3 recorded in docs/experiment_container_design.md §13. Final: 660 tests pass.
close_reason: All 8 children shipped. Experiment container: schema (3 tables + 6 columns, additive, feature-marked), plumbing, harness, read API, chatbot UI, scoring/comparison, and 79 integration tests. Phase-0 gate at docs/experiment_container_design.md rev 2.

title: Serve an assignment's answers back for export
description:
The last link. Answers are stored per (turn, rater) by fix-9eg.10 and read by fix-9eg.9; this exposes them ASSIGNMENT-shaped rather than turn-shaped, which is what a consumer actually needs.

WHY TURN-SHAPED IS NOT ENOUGH: a consumer computing inter-rater agreement wants 'every answer in assignment X, by rater', not 240 separate per-turn lookups. And it needs to know which rows are still UNANSWERED, because an agreement figure computed over whatever happens to be finished silently describes the subset the reviewer got to first - which is not a random subset if they worked in order.

SHAPE: the assignment id, each row's turn, each rater's answers per question, and the unanswered set. Verbatim - no scoring, no agreement, no interpretation. Everything downstream of the raw answers belongs to whoever wrote the rubric.

DEPENDS ON fix-9eg.9 and fix-9eg.10.
acceptance_criteria: An assignment's answers export by assignment id, per rater, with unanswered rows identified; the response contains no interpretation of the answers.
notes: Implemented assignment-shaped answer export in commit 8a7d38c. Added token-gated GET /api/review/assignments/{id}/export using ReviewSidecar.export_assignment. Payload includes assignment_id, ordered rater_slots/questions/rows with each turn_ref, latest per-rater answer revisions, and explicit unanswered row/rater/question coordinates; no scoring or interpretation. Focused tests passed: 12 passed across test_review_sidecar.py, test_review_ingest.py, test_feedback_read_api.py, and test_review_export.py. Bead intentionally left open.
close_reason: GET /api/review/assignments/{id}/export on feat/experiment-observability-3.3 @ 8a7d38c. Assignment-shaped latest answers with unanswered coordinates; no interpretation. Independent tests 12 passed.

title: Ingest a review assignment into a chatbot session
description:
How a rubric reaches the server. Separated from the schema bead because the shape of the document and the way it arrives fail differently and will be got wrong independently.

TWO PLAUSIBLE PATHS, and the choice matters more than it looks:
 (a) A FILE IN THE WORKFLOW FOLDER, discovered like other workflow content. Fits the existing pattern and needs no new route. But it makes the assignment a property of the WORKFLOW rather than of a review session, so two raters working different assignments over the same workflow collide, and rotating an assignment means editing the tree under measurement - which for an evaluation consumer is exactly the thing that must not move.
 (b) A ROUTE that accepts an assignment and returns an id, with the review view addressed by that id. Assignments become session-scoped and disposable; several can coexist; nothing under the workflow folder changes.
(b) is the better fit for the first consumer and probably for any evaluation use. (a) may still be right for a workflow that ships a standing review rubric. Decide explicitly rather than by whichever is easier to wire.

WHATEVER IS CHOSEN: an assignment must be addressable after the fact, because a rater does not finish in one sitting and an adjudicator comes back to it days later.
acceptance_criteria: An assignment can be supplied, addressed by id afterwards, and two assignments over the same workflow do not interfere.
notes: Implemented path (b) in isolated worktree commit b001261: token-gated POST /api/review/assignments and GET /api/review/assignments/{assignment_id}, workspace-required, manifest-bound ReviewSidecar persistence, one-time capabilities only in POST response, focused coexistence/validation/sealed-evidence tests. Validation: 93 passed across test_review_ingest.py, test_review_sidecar.py, test_feedback_read_api.py, test_observability_workspace.py, and test_run_chatbot_server.py. Bead intentionally left open for orchestrator.
close_reason: Path (b): POST /api/review/assignments and GET by id on feat/experiment-observability-3.3 @ b001261. Workspace-required; two assignments coexist; invalid rubric 400; workflow tree and sealed archives untouched. Independent tests: ingest+sidecar+feedback+workspace 33 passed.

title: Consequence assessment carries almost no signal: reversibility and blast_radius are undeclarable in the manifest
description:
From fix-ajv.3. assess_consequence() takes effect_kind, reversibility, blast_radius
and decision_critical, but runtime_manifest's EffectContract declares ONLY `kind`.
There is nowhere for a workflow to state reversibility or blast radius, so both stay
"unknown" for every command, and per arch 6.6.1 unknown floors consequence at high.

Net effect: every command in every workflow is graded high or critical, so today's
consequence_class carries almost no discriminating signal - the only informative
field is effect_kind. That is the conservative direction and therefore safe, but it
means consequence-graded caution (FW-REQ-021 P1 clause 10, "consequence shall grade
evidence requirements continuously") has nothing to grade on yet.

TO CLOSE: extend EffectContract with reversibility and blast_radius, which is a
manifest schema decision (SUPPORTED_SCHEMA_VERSIONS is frozenset({1}), so it is a
schema bump, and the IDO generator writes these manifests).

Also unresolved: `decision_critical` - whether a downstream decision depends on the
result - is per arch 4.15 a property of the candidate action IN ITS BINDING, not of
the command definition, so it may not be declarable in a manifest at all.
notes:
2026-08-28 OWNER DECISION (Dhar): DEFERRED THROUGH G2B, not merely deferred. Do not close this before the G2B bundle is assembled. Same pairing argument as fix-ajv.10: landing declarable reversibility/blast_radius between the bundles would give G2B a non-degenerate consequence distribution that G2A lacks, making that axis unpairable. Safe windows are before G2A or after G2B, never between.

Consequence accepted, and it is a real scope reduction: arch 15.3 names the observed consequence-class distribution as a G2A product and the empirical answer to northstar Gaps 3-4. Phase 0 will NOT deliver it, and 19.6 thresholds have no empirical basis until G1W. This must be an approved omission recorded in ido-2l0.10, not a silent one.

Two supporting findings from the 2026-08-28 code review:
1. The degeneracy is doubly floored, so a partial fix buys nothing. read_only bases at 'low' (_EFFECT_BASE, decision_signals.py:353) but reversibility='unknown' floors to 'high' (:362) AND blast_radius='unknown' floors to 'high' (:416). Both fields must become declarable together.
2. Closing this would yield a DECLARED distribution, not an observed one — arch 15.3 asks for 'observed'. Combined with the already-recorded G1R read-only skew, the consequence axis stays weak either way, which is part of why the deferral costs less than it appears.

OPEN QUESTION to settle before anyone invests in the schema bump: is a read reversible? Intuitively yes (nothing changed), but assess_consequence's own docstring argues a read 'still has privacy impact' and disclosure cannot be undone. If reads count as irreversible, the floor fires regardless and even a fully-declared manifest leaves every read at 'high' — which would collapse the case for this bead entirely. Resolve that first; it is cheaper than 63 blast-radius judgements.

title: classifier-topk-margin is not computable: predict_single_sentence drops the top_k_scores predict_batch already computes
description:
From fix-ajv.4. FW-REQ-021 clause 1 names classifier top-k as a required uncertainty
signal, and decision_signals.classifier_topk_margin() exists to carry it, but the
margin cannot be emitted because the second-best probability never leaves the model
layer.

model_pipeline_training.predict_batch COMPUTES top_k_scores (:582) and RETURNS it
(:590). predict_single_sentence then DROPS it from its return dict (:676-682), so
predict_with_details (:409-416) has only the winning label's probability plus the
top-k label NAMES. There is no second-best probability to subtract.

TO CLOSE: propagate top_k_scores through predict_single_sentence's return dict and
into predict_with_details' details, then emit via classifier_topk_margin() at the
site in intent_detection.command_identity_uncertainty that is already commented for
it. Small change; it was out of scope only because that file was owned by another
agent. A second forward pass is NOT an acceptable alternative - that would be a real
performance change in a Phase 0 slice.
close_reason: top_k_scores propagated through predict_single_sentence to predict_with_details; classifier_topk_margin emitted at classifier tier

title: Cross-repo scope contract for workflow_content_hash file selection
description:
Follow-up to fix-oxr, found in review. The arch 7.1 RECIPE is now pinned on both
sides (fastworkflow canonical_content_hash and ido canonical_fingerprint agree
byte-for-byte, and tests/test_context_runtime_manifest.py carries a verbatim
transcription of ido's implementation as a drift detector). The SCOPE - which
files feed the recipe - has no such contract, and the two rules are structurally
different:

- ido excludes by a name list applied to the FIRST PATH SEGMENT ONLY
  (FINGERPRINT_EXCLUDED_TREES / FINGERPRINT_EXCLUDED_FILES in gen_ido_scaffold.py)
- fastworkflow excludes by dot-prefix plus name matching AT ANY DEPTH
  (workflow_content_entries in runtime_manifest.py)

They agree on the current ido tree (both select 134 files, same hash) but a
review enumerated 7 classes where they diverge, e.g. _commands/Insights/x.md,
_commands/__pycache__/y.py, nested ___command_info, and any dot-prefixed file
(ido has no dot rule at all). Latent rather than live today: ___convo_info and
___workflow_contexts hold .sqlite3 files, which the suffix filter drops anyway.

Two functions computing "the workflow fingerprint" with the same recipe and
different scopes is a trap, and verify_workflow_fingerprint now depends on them
agreeing - a divergence shows up as a healthy workflow failing strict startup
conformance.

Options: (a) transcribe ido's scope rule into the fastworkflow test beside
_ido_reference_fingerprint and assert scope equality on a synthetic tree
covering all 7 classes, then reconcile whichever side is wrong; (b) make the
scope part of the written recipe so both sides implement one rule. (a) first,
since it turns the divergence into a failing test rather than an argument.

Needs cross-repo agreement, so coordinate with the ido side rather than changing
one repo unilaterally.
notes:
=== CORE SIDE RESOLVED 28 Aug: option (a) implemented, option (b) rejected ===

MEASUREMENT (independent, not taken from the ido reply). Real ido tree: fw
workflow_content_entries and a transcription of ido _fingerprint_included both
select 134 files, identical set. Synthetic tree: 8 ido-only files across three
classes. Both reproduce the ido side's numbers exactly.

(b) REJECTED - scope-as-declared-data. Its stated premise is wrong: Insights is
not an ido name. fastworkflow/distillation.py:661 writes it and
utils/insights_loader.py:39 reads it. Every name in DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_TREES is a
fastWorkflow convention fastWorkflow itself writes, so core is naming its own
output, not learning a workflow's filenames. The coupling runs the other way -
ido hardcodes MODEL_DIRNAME="___command_info" and "Insights" - which is the
correct direction, since a generator targets a framework.

Second reason, independent of the first: (b) makes the check self-attesting. If
the manifest declares both the scope and the fingerprint, verification becomes
"hash the files you named and compare to the hash you gave me" - internally
consistent whether or not the scope is right. A generator declaring
suffixes=[".json"] by mistake yields a fingerprint no Python edit ever
invalidates, and it verifies forever. That is register item O3's harm class in
a new form: a provenance value attesting to less than it appears to. The
proposed zero-file floor catches only the degenerate case; a one-file scope is
equally vacuous and passes. It also contradicts the ido side's own answer that
the reader is normative - if the reader is normative the reader owns the rule,
and "independently recomputable" has to mean without trusting the artifact
under test.

WHAT LANDED INSTEAD, closing the same coupling structurally:
- FRAMEWORK_ARTIFACT_PREFIX = "___" in workflow_content_entries. The three
  artifact dirs are a class, not three names; a fourth would fold runtime state
  into identity until someone extended the list, and every generator
  transcribing that list would diverge until it did too. Verified a no-op on
  the live ido tree (still 134 files, declared fingerprint still verifies), so
  no hash moved.
- (a) as agreed: _ido_fingerprint_included / _ido_selection transcribed beside
  _ido_reference_fingerprint, plus set-comparison tests. Four agreement classes
  pass; three divergence classes are xfail(strict=True) keyed by the ido-side
  change that closes each, so each flips the suite red the moment ido adopts
  and the transcription is updated in the same change.
- Docstrings on both sides of the transcription state that it pins ido's FILTER
  and not its SELECTOR, per the ido side's correction: fingerprint_entries takes
  pending union declared-preserved, never a walk, and the invariant that these
  equal disk after replace_tree is unreachable from here. That assertion belongs
  on the ido side (ido-o1o).

G2A DEADLINE - answered by versioning rather than by hurrying.
WORKFLOW_SCOPE_RULE_VERSION=1 in runtime_manifest.py, recorded as
WorkflowProvenance.workflow_scope_rule_version. The ido side is right that
6.3 immutability means a scope change after G2A strands recorded bundle
identity, but "land it before G2A" only works once - the next scope change has
the same problem. With the version recorded, a bundle written under one rule and
read under another reports that the comparison cannot be made instead of
reporting a workflow that drifted. Deliberately not RuntimeProvenance.
schema_version: the record's shape and the selection rule move independently.
Note for the future: v1 denotes the rule INCLUDING the "___" prefix, since no
bundle was ever recorded under the pre-prefix rule.

AUTHORITATIVE TREE (asked by the ido side): /home/drawal/rl/fastworkflow, on
main. runtime_manifest.py, provenance.py and both test files exist only there
and are untracked work in progress. fastworkflow-hardening is a stale
feature-branch clone (feat/observability-hardening-24f-kw7) whose v3.2.0 work
already landed on main as PR #73; it has zero references to
canonical_content_hash, workflow_content_entries, workflow_content_hash or
DEFAULT_EXCLUDED_TREES. Pin against main; hardening will not grow a copy.

REMAINING, core side: remove the three xfail markers and update the
transcription when ido-o1o lands. The strict markers are the tracking
mechanism - no scheduling needed, the suite will say so.
close_reason:
Cross-repo scope contract closed. Both sides implement one rule, both pin it against the other, and the manifest can now carry the rule version that qualifies its fingerprint. Hash-neutral throughout: the live ido tree still selects 134 files and still declares sha256:326aec98..., so no recorded identity moved.

CORE SIDE. FRAMEWORK_ARTIFACT_PREFIX="___" closes the artifact-directory class structurally instead of by name list. Option (b), scope-as-declared-data, was rejected and the ido side conceded both premises: Insights is written by fastworkflow/distillation.py:661 and read by utils/insights_loader.py:39, so core was naming its own output and the coupling (b) targeted ran the other way; and (b) makes the check self-attesting, since a manifest declaring both the scope and the fingerprint verifies forever against whatever it named. Filed on their side as DISCARDED rather than deferred, with ido-jlj to write it into requirements 14 so it cannot be silently reopened.

THE XFAIL MECHANISM WAS WRONG AND THE MISTAKE IS THE INTERESTING PART. The three divergence classes were marked xfail(strict=True) on the reasoning that they would flip red when ido adopted the matching rules. They would not have. The test compared fastworkflow against a TRANSCRIPTION of ido's filter, and a copy diverges from its original the moment the original changes, so the xfails would have gone on passing-as-expected-failures while describing a divergence that no longer existed - the "test of a filter nobody runs" the marker's own reason string was written to prevent. Ido adopted the rules the same day and the markers noticed nothing. Found by the ido side, not by the suite.

FIXED BY IMPORTING RATHER THAN COPYING. gen_ido_scaffold turns out to be import-safe: 250 top-level nodes, one `if __name__` guard, 0.02s with its directory on sys.path. tests/test_context_runtime_manifest.py now loads it by path and checks the transcription against the real _fingerprint_included case by case, skipping when the sibling repo is absent. The transcription stays, so the tests run without ido, but it is no longer the drift detector - the import is. Ido runs the mirror against the real workflow_content_entries, so neither side waits for the other to notice.

SHARED CONTRACT. _SCOPE_CASES, 20 paths with the answer both sides owe, mirrored as ScopeContract.CLASSES in ido's tests/test_workflow_fingerprint.py. Diffed against the 19 they sent: strict superset, mine adds top-level ___command_info/m.json, none of theirs missing.

___notes.py IS IN SCOPE, deliberately. FRAMEWORK_ARTIFACT_PREFIX applies to directory segments only while the dot rule also applies to filenames. The framework creates ___ directories and has never created a ___ file, so extending the rule to filenames would close an empty class while opening a way to silently drop a command from workflow identity. Between the two directions of error that is the worse one: an over-included artifact file moves a hash that should not move, which is visible, and an under-included source file leaves a hash still when behavior changed, which is not. Recorded rather than left to be rediscovered.

MUTATION BLIND SPOT, found by ido and present here too. A disk-walk comparison that prunes excluded directories before the filter runs never asks the filter about paths underneath them, so a check deleted from the filter stays invisible. _ido_selection no longer prunes, and the transcription is also checked per-path with no walk between it and the assertion. It matters because the WRITER has no pruning: fingerprint_entries applies the filter to a flat dict of pending paths.

SCOPE RULE VERSION, and the defect in the first cut of it. RuntimeManifest.workflow_scope_rule_version is now modelled - it had to be, because extra="forbid" rejected the key by name and the ido generator was holding the value internally with a test asserting the rejection so it would go red the day the field landed. It did, and the emission landed in the same change. The first cut recorded only the READER's rule in provenance, which correctly labels workflow_source_hash and says nothing about declared_workflow_fingerprint - so a generator on an older rule would have had its fingerprint compared against a differently-selected tree and reported as drift, the exact failure the version exists to prevent. FingerprintVerification gained `incomparable` and WorkflowProvenance gained declared_scope_rule_version; fingerprint_verified is None rather than False in that case. Equal digests stay a pass whatever the versions say, since that means the two selections produced identical bytes and failing it would be the false alarm on a healthy workflow this bead was filed about.

VALIDATION. fastworkflow 174 passing in the two suites, zero xfail. ido 350 passing, 37 in the fingerprint suite including the flipped test and two added here (the version is never declared without a fingerprint; a declared fingerprint verifies end to end against the real reader). Live ido manifest carries workflow_scope_rule_version 1 and passes strict startup conformance.

MANIFEST UPDATED WITHOUT A DESTRUCTIVE REGENERATION. replace_tree moves ___command_info to a backup slot and deliberately does not restore it, so a full run would have left the ido workflow untrained. Instead the generator was run with --dry-run and replace_tree intercepted to capture its pending emission; the captured manifest differed from disk by exactly one line, the new field, with the fingerprint unchanged. Those bytes were written. Not a hand edit - the generator's own output - and the next real regeneration reproduces it.

title: Agent surface: documented schema, SQL recipes skill, JSON export, and README/design-doc updates
description:
SHIPPED IN FULL. All four deliverables landed in commit 3351f92 (merged as 7a0340e).

1. SQL RECIPES SKILL -- fastworkflow/skills_for_coding_fastworkflows/debug-workflow-conversations/reference.md, "### Distillation recipes" (~line 387), plus "### Distillation read API and HTTP surface" (~line 559). This is the location design-doc section 15 specified, following the fix-kw7.15 precedent.
2. DOCUMENTED SCHEMA -- design doc section 9 (Full DDL) and section 15, plus the HTTP-surface section above.
3. JSON EXPORT -- GET /api/distillation/export/<run_id> -> ObservabilityStore.export_distillation_run (run_chatbot/server.py ~1220).
4. README / DESIGN-DOC UPDATES -- README "Reviewing distillation" (~374); the [R24] reversal amendment in docs/fastworkflow_observability_studio_design.md (~416); docs/run_chatbot_cli_parity.md.

The shipped recipes are BETTER than the design doc's drafts: they carry the [DR54] corrections a Phase-0 reviewer caught. 9 'replay_of IS NULL' guards and 10 'comparable = 1' guards, which are the two filters whose absence made the flagship promotion query return support_runs = 3 where the answer was 1 -- a replay run counting as independent support for the very insight it was run to test, so a replay that FAILED to remove the cited divergence would have INCREASED that insight's support count. The section header states the fixture it was executed against (one comparable run, one non-comparable, one replay, one no-divergence, a run-level NULL-command_name divergence, and a NULL-command_name failed span), which is exactly [DR54]'s verification bar.

CORRECTION TO THIS BEAD'S 2026-08-29 "NARROWED" REVISION, which claimed only the skill remained. That was wrong, from two compounding errors:
 (a) the deliverable was searched for in .claude/skills/ (the continuity library) when section 15 names fastworkflow/skills_for_coding_fastworkflows/ (the skills packaged with the distribution). This repo has TWO skill trees and they are easy to conflate.
 (b) absence was then "confirmed" with `git show --stat 7a0340e`, which shows only the FIRST-PARENT diff of a merge commit and therefore omitted the file. An artifact of the command was read as evidence of absence.
The file's real history (`git log -- <path>`) shows 3351f92 added the section, and it is present in HEAD.
notes:
Findings 2026-08-27:

* A Redactor scrubs secrets at the SINK boundary before anything is persisted
  (observability_store.py ~L134-168, applied in upsert_span_rows and
  upsert_turn_row). A JSON export must go through stored rows, never around
  them — exporting from in-memory objects would bypass redaction and put
  secrets in a file meant to be shared with an extraction agent.
* The existing span catalog and SQL recipes to extend live at
  fastworkflow/skills_for_coding_fastworkflows/debug-workflow-conversations/
  reference.md (~L81-169 span catalog, L271 already notes that
  --generate_insights turns contain teacher AND student passes in one trace —
  update that line when separation lands).
* Cautionary precedent: ObservabilityStore.list_train_runs() exists with no
  HTTP route and no UI, so train metrics are effectively unreachable. Do not
  let the distillation tables end up the same way.
close_reason: Closed

title: Provenance-aware retention: never prune a trace an accepted insight cites
description:
Retention today exempts conversation rows and turn records but prunes spans
and artifacts ([R16]). Distillation inverts the usual value curve: the span
detail IS the evidence, and an insight can be reviewed months after the run
that produced it. Pruning the teacher trace an accepted insight cites would
silently break provenance and leave an unverifiable rule in a shipped file.

* Pin traces referenced by a distillation run that produced an accepted or
  unadjudicated insight.
* Decide and document what happens to traces behind rejected insights and
  no-divergence runs — those are the bulk of the volume and are the reasonable
  thing to prune, but no-divergence runs are also the contradiction set for
  future rules, so this is a real trade-off, not a default.
* Make the pin visible: a UI or query answer for 'why is this trace still
  here'.
notes:
Concrete retention behaviour found 2026-08-27 — the risk is
sharper than filed.

ObservabilityStore.prune (~L1094-1183) is exactly adverse to this epic:
* FW_OBS_RETENTION_DAYS, DEFAULT 30, deletes spans by start_ns and artifacts
  by turn_key horizon.
* FW_OBS_DB_MAX_BYTES, default 1 GiB including -wal, evicts OLDEST SPANS
  FIRST while over cap.
* Exempt: turns, conversations, conversation_counters, train_runs,
  diagnostics, feedback.
* prune runs automatically at SQLiteTraceSink startup.

So spans and artifacts — precisely the distillation evidence — are the only
things pruned, on a 30-day default, automatically, at every sink startup. An
insight older than a month currently loses the trace that justifies it with no
warning, and --generate_insights roughly triples span volume so the 1 GiB cap
arrives sooner. Pinning is not a nice-to-have; without it the provenance built
in fix-sb8.5 has a one-month shelf life.
close_reason: Closed

title: Corpus view: divergence rate over time, frequency by command/context/kind, per-insight support and contradiction counts
description:
One turn is an anecdote; skills and verifiers are extracted from patterns.

* Divergence rate over time — the signal for whether the student is actually
  improving as insights accumulate.
* Divergence frequency by command, by context, and by divergence kind: which
  commands does the student most often get wrong?
* Per-insight support count (runs exhibiting the pattern) and contradiction
  count (runs where the student did the right thing anyway, i.e. where the
  rule would have fired wrongly).
* Aggregate teacher-vs-student cost and latency, so the economic case for the
  student is visible.

These queries are the direct input to skill and verifier extraction, so they
must be available as SQL (task: agent surface) and not only as UI.
close_reason: Closed

title: Counterfactual replay: re-run the student against the stored teacher trace to test a candidate insight
description:
The bridge from insight to VERIFIER, and the strongest available form of
verification: an insight is a hypothesis, and the stored trace corpus is its
test set.

Given a stored run, re-run ONLY the student pass from the recorded entry state
with a candidate insight set injected, then diff against the STORED teacher
trace. Because the teacher trace is persisted, this costs one small-model run
instead of two — cheap enough to sweep the whole corpus.

Signal: did the cited divergence disappear? If yes the insight is validated;
if no it is decoration. Feed the answer back into the adjudication verdict.

This is what makes a stored (turn, teacher-trace) pair an executable test case:
the pair is the fixture and 'student now matches teacher on the cited
dimension' is the assertion — which is exactly the shape a planner verifier
needs.

Prerequisite on the stored record: enough to reconstruct pass entry — user
message, entry-state fingerprint and the state itself, and the insight set
that was live at the time (otherwise a replay silently tests a different
prompt than the original run used).
close_reason: Closed

title: Chatbot UI: side-by-side aligned teacher/student diff
description:
The comparison view proper, driven by the structured divergence record (not
recomputed in the browser).

* Two panes, rows aligned on the stored alignment, with unmatched rows gapped
  on the opposite side.
* Per-row diff kind styling, and parameter-level highlighting for
  same-command-different-params — 'step 3 used the wrong customer_id' must be
  visible without opening both spans.
* Jump to first divergence, and a divergences-only filter, so triage does not
  require scrolling a full trajectory.
* Click through from a diff row to either side's span detail.
* Non-material divergences (same end state, different path) visually demoted
  so they do not read as errors.
notes:
UI-implementation constraints found in the SPA survey
(2026-08-27). static/index.html is 2820 lines of vanilla JS, no framework, no
build step:

* NO innerHTML ANYWHERE, and it is test-enforced
  (assert b"innerHTML" not in server.index_html). All diff rendering,
  including parameter-level highlighting, must go through the existing el() /
  textContent helpers.
* The waterfall renders ONE level, direct children only, driven by a single
  state.path breadcrumb stack (buildTurnTree / renderWaterfall / descend). A
  two-pane aligned diff cannot reuse renderWaterfall as-is: it needs either
  two independent path stacks or a dedicated compare renderer. Budget for the
  latter.
* Reuse rather than reinvent: span colors are CSS vars in :root
  (--bar-turn, --bar-planner, --bar-tool, --bar-command, --bar-llm,
  --bar-human, --bar-other) mapped by spanCategory(), with the legend built
  inline at the end of each waterfall. Diff-state styling is additive to this,
  not a replacement.
* buildTurnTree already groups top-level spans into planning / execution /
  other PHASES — that grouping is the natural seam for a pass dimension.
* Inline scripts are covered by sha256 hashes in the CSP the server builds, so
  edits to the inline JS flow through that path; verify the page still loads
  under CSP after each change.
close_reason: Closed

title: Insight adjudication: verify each recommendation against its cited diff, and persist the verdict
description:
The verification surface. For each insight, show it beside (a) the divergence
records it cites, (b) the teacher/student trace excerpt at that point, (c) its
support count and any contradicting turns.

Persist a verdict per insight: supported | not-supported-by-cited-evidence |
overfit-to-single-turn | duplicate-of-existing | contradicted-by-other-turns,
with a free-text note and an actor.

title: Distillation observability: separated teacher/student traces, evidence-linked diffs, and insight verification
description:
Distillation (`fastworkflow run --generate_insights`) runs the SAME user
message twice — a teacher pass and a student pass — diffs them, and appends
two markdown files: `planning_agent_insights.md` ("what TO DO") and
`execution_agent_anti_patterns.md` ("what NOT to do"). Those two files are the
product. Everything that justifies them is currently thrown away.

Concretely, today:

* Both passes emit spans under the SAME trace_id (trace_id == turn_key), so a
  --generate_insights turn's waterfall is a ~2x interleaving with nothing
  marking pass boundaries (this is fix-kw7.11, now folded in here).
* The comparison inputs (teacher/student plans, teacher/student action lists,
  divergence summary) live in local variables in distill_message() and die
  with the call.
* compare_trajectories() reduces the diff to a PROSE STRING via set-difference
  over (command_name, params-json). Set semantics lose repeats, cannot express
  "same command, one wrong parameter", and cannot say whether the difference
  changed the end state or only the path.
* The extractor LLM call — the step that actually decides what the rule is —
  is unobserved: no record of the prompt, the existing_insights it deduped
  against, or the raw output.
* Emitted insights carry NO back-reference. They are numbered lines in a
  markdown file. Given rule #7 there is no way to find the turn it came from.
* Negative outcomes are invisible: "diverged but extractor returned EMPTY"
  (context-justified or duplicate) and "no divergence at all" are both
  unrecorded, and both are evidence.

So the artifacts cannot be verified against the evidence that produced them,
by a human or by an agent. That is the gap this epic closes.

SCOPE — record and review, not re-tune. This epic does not change extraction
prompts or insight quality heuristics. It makes the chain
teacher trace -> student trace -> aligned diff -> divergence record ->
extractor call -> emitted insight inspectable and falsifiable end to end, and
exposes it in the chatbot UI and to agents.

Motivating downstream use (Dhar): these recommendations are the raw material
for extracting SKILLS and VERIFIERS for the planner. That sets the bar. A rule
is only promotable to a skill if you can see how many turns support it, which
turns contradict it, and whether applying it actually removes the divergence.
Task 10 (counterfactual replay) is the mechanism that turns a stored
(turn, teacher-trace) pair into an executable verifier: replay the student with
the candidate insight injected and diff against the STORED teacher trace — one
small-model run, no teacher spend.

RELATIONSHIP TO EXISTING WORK
* Absorbs fix-kw7.11 (pass pollution of the live trace) as task 1.
* Reverses design-doc ruling [R24] ("insights distillation is explicitly out of
  Studio scope"). The doc must record the reversal and why.
* Overlaps fix-35m.3 (EXP-013), which already promises distillation isolation
  with "distinct invocation paths, accumulators, budgets, EVIDENCE STREAMS".
  35m.3 owns the isolation GUARANTEE (read-only surface check, separate
  budgets); this epic owns the RECORDING and REVIEW surface. The "evidence
  streams" phrase must be de-conflicted at Phase 0 so it is not built twice.
* Depends on the 3.2.0 observability platform (fix-kw7): spans/turns/artifacts
  tables, TraceSink, the chatbot SPA.

THE LOAD-BEARING DESIGN DECISION (Phase 0 gate)
`trace_id == turn_key` is assumed by root_span_id(), deterministic_span_id(),
GET /api/spans/{trace_id}, GET /api/turn/{turn_key}, and the turns PK. Giving
each pass its own viewable trace touches that invariant. Three candidates —
(a) derived per-pass trace ids plus a grouping row, (b) shared trace_id plus a
`pass` discriminator column and UI partitioning, (c) full logical turn keys per
pass. Each has different blast radius on replay, retention, and the turns
table. Decide by adversarial review before any code, exactly as fix-kw7.1 did
for the parent platform.

FIVE CAPABILITIES THIS MUST DELIVER
1. Separation — each pass independently viewable, still grouped as one run.
2. Alignment — a real sequence alignment with a divergence taxonomy and a
   materiality judgement (did the end state differ, or only the path?), not a
   prose summary. This is the piece most likely to be underestimated.
3. Comparability proof — state fingerprints at both pass entries, model
   identity per role, DSPy cache hit/miss, restore-succeeded assertion. A
   divergence is evidence of a student mistake ONLY if the passes started
   identical. Without this every diff is deniable. Rank this second, above UI.
4. Provenance — stable insight ids, bidirectional links insight <-> divergence
   <-> span, plus the negative decisions (EMPTY extractions, no-divergence
   turns).
5. Aggregation — one turn is an anecdote. Divergence rate over time, frequency
   by command/context/kind, per-insight support and contradiction counts.

RISKS
* Span volume roughly triples on --generate_insights runs.
* Retention currently prunes spans while exempting turn records. Pruning the
  teacher trace an accepted insight cites would silently break provenance.
  Provenance-aware retention is a task, not an afterthought.
design:
DESIGN NOTES (pre-Phase-0; the design doc + adversarial review own the final
answer — these are the constraints and candidate shapes the review starts from)

--- Current-state facts verified on the 3.2.0 tree (2026-08-27) ---

fastworkflow/distillation.py
  distill_message(): snapshot -> teacher pass -> snapshot teacher-final ->
  restore initial -> student pass -> compare_planning_traces() ->
  compare_trajectories() -> extract_*_insights() -> append_*_insights() ->
  restore teacher-final on any divergence. Returns TEACHER's CommandOutput.
  DistillationResult carries only two ints (counts). Nothing else survives.

  compare_trajectories() (L315-407) is set-difference over
  _action_signature() = (command_name, json.dumps(params, sort_keys=True)).
  Failure modes to fix in task 3: repeats collapse; a single differing param
  renders as two unrelated "only by X" entries; the ordering check only fires
  on the intersection; the fallback branch emits the literal string
  "Action sequences differ (unclassified difference)".

  snapshot_workflow_state() (L197) captures workflow._to_dict(),
  cme._to_dict(), len(conversation_history.messages). restore_workflow_state()
  (L209) writes those back and clears the action log. Nothing verifies the
  restore landed, and nothing outside those three fields is restored.

  _run_agent_pass() (L460) returns (command_output, trajectory, actions,
  planning_steps) — the trajectory dict is dspy ReAct's flat
  thought_N/tool_name_N/tool_args_N/observation_N shape.

fastworkflow/workflow_execution_context.py L1643: distillation is entered
  INSIDE the already-open logical turn, guarded on user_message_queue (CLI /
  Topology A only) — which is why both passes land under one trace_id.

fastworkflow/tracing.py: trace_id = turn_key (L141);
  root_span_id(turn_key) = deterministic_span_id(turn_key, "fw.turn", 0);
  start_span() parents to stack top else root_span_id(turn_key). Span columns:
  span_id, trace_id, parent_span_id, name, kind, channel_id, command_name,
  context, start_ns, end_ns, status, attributes. Kinds: internal|llm|
  human_wait|tool. Attribute values capped at FW_OBS_MAX_ATTR_BYTES (16384)
  with a lossy-and-counted envelope (truncated/original_length/sha256).

fastworkflow/observability/store.py L300-346: tables conversations,
  conversation_counters, turns, feedback, spans, artifacts, train_runs,
  diagnostics. Note `feedback` is the existing precedent for a mutable,
  turn-keyed, human-written verdict table — task 8 should follow its shape
  rather than invent one.

fastworkflow/run_chatbot/server.py: GET /api/meta, /api/session, /api/workflows,
  /api/browse, /api/health, /api/channels, /api/conversations, /api/turns,
  /api/turn/{turn_key}, /api/spans/{trace_id}, /api/artifact/{id};
  POST /api/select_workflow, /api/configure_env, /api/clear_conversations,
  /api/train. UI is a single 2820-line static/index.html.

Insight sinks: Insights/<workflow_name>/planning_agent_insights.md
  (entries "## N. text") and execution_agent_anti_patterns.md ("N. text"),
  written by _append_numbered_insights() which continues numbering by regex
  over the existing file. Those entry numbers are the only handle that exists
  today — task 4 should make the id stable and independent of file position,
  because renumbering or hand-editing the file must not orphan provenance.

--- Candidate shapes for the Phase 0 decision ---

Identity (pick one, argue the other two down):
 (a) Derived per-pass trace ids, e.g. trace_id = f"{turn_key}#teacher". Keeps
     one waterfall per pass for free; every reader that assumes
     trace_id == turn_key must be audited (spans read path, replay, retention,
     the artifacts join).
 (b) Shared trace_id + spans.pass column ('teacher'|'student'|'extract'|NULL).
     Smallest schema delta, closest to what fix-kw7.11 proposed; but parenting
     still interleaves, and every consumer must learn to partition.
 (c) Real per-pass logical turn keys with rows in `turns`. Most faithful — each
     pass genuinely is a turn — but doubles turn rows and pollutes the
     conversation ordinal sequence, which the chatbot's turn list reads.

Grouping row (needed under all three): a `distillation_runs` table keyed by the
user-visible turn, holding the two pass trace ids, per-role model identity,
both entry-state fingerprints, divergence booleans, counts, and timings.

Alignment (task 3): canonical step key + LCS/edit-script over the two action
sequences; per-pair classification identical | same-command-different-params |
param-value-only | extra-in-student | missing-in-student | reordered |
different-answer-same-actions; plus a materiality flag derived from the
post-pass state fingerprints (same end state reached by a different path is
NOT a mistake, and the current code cannot say so). Persist the STRUCTURED
record; render the prose summary from it for the extractor prompt, so the
extractor and the UI read the same source of truth.

Comparability (task 2): fingerprint = stable hash of (workflow context, cme
context, conversation-history tail). Record at teacher entry and student entry
and assert equal; surface a loud "passes did not start from identical state"
banner when they are not, because that invalidates every downstream claim.
Also record per-pass model id/params and per-LLM-call DSPy cache hit/miss — a
cache hit in one pass and a miss in the other is a silent confound.

Replay (task 10): the reason to store the teacher trace in full. Re-run only
the student against the STORED teacher trace with a candidate insight set
injected; the divergence-disappeared? answer is the verifier signal. Requires
the stored run to carry enough to reconstruct pass entry: user message, entry
fingerprint, and the insight set that was live at the time.

Non-goals: changing extractor prompts or insight wording; distillation for
Topology B / FastAPI (it is CLI-only by construction, guarded on
user_message_queue); multi-student (>2-way) comparison — leave the schema able
to grow to N passes but ship 2.
acceptance_criteria: 1. A --generate_insights turn yields two independently viewable traces (teacher, student) plus one grouping run record; neither waterfall interleaves the other. 2. Every emitted insight resolves, in one query and in one UI click, to the divergence record and the teacher/student span pair that justified it, and back again. 3. Divergences are stored as structured aligned pairs with a kind and a materiality flag, not a prose string. 4. Both pass-entry state fingerprints are recorded and compared; a run whose passes did not start identical is visibly flagged as non-comparable. 5. Negative outcomes are recorded: divergence-with-EMPTY-extraction, and no-divergence turns. 6. The extractor LLM call is a span with its prompt inputs and raw output. 7. An agent can answer 'which turns support insight X, and which contradict it' from documented SQL without scraping the UI. 8. A stored run can be replayed student-only against the stored teacher trace to test whether a candidate insight removes the divergence. 9. Retention cannot prune a trace that an accepted insight cites.
notes:
CODEBASE SURVEY, 2026-08-27 (two parallel explorations of the observability
store/span contract and of the chatbot SPA). Detailed findings are appended to
the affected children; three change the epic-level picture.

1. THE SCHEMA GATE IS FAIL-CLOSED, NOT DEGRADING. observability_store.py
   SCHEMA_VERSION = 1 in PRAGMA user_version; both the writable store (~L387)
   and the read-only viewer (~L1251) RAISE IncompatibleObservabilityDB when
   they meet a newer version, per ruling [R11]. Adding tables and bumping to 2
   therefore breaks older builds outright rather than degrading them, and
   there is no numbered migration chain to lean on (setup is idempotent CREATE
   TABLE IF NOT EXISTS plus one ad-hoc ALTER). fix-sb8.1 must decide whether
   the new tables justify a bump at all, or ship additive-only without one.

2. VERDICT WRITES COLLIDE WITH THE READ-ONLY VIEWER RULING [R12]. The chatbot
   opens ReadOnlyObservabilityStore per request and never writes the DB it
   inspects; do_POST refuses everything outside a four-route allowlist, and
   TestReadOnly enforces it. fix-sb8.9 (adjudication) needs an argued
   exception following the run_clear_conversations precedent, or verdicts move
   off the viewer entirely. Escalated to fix-sb8.1.

3. THE RETENTION RISK IS WORSE THAN FILED. prune deletes spans and artifacts
   ONLY — turns, conversations, feedback and train_runs are exempt — on a
   FW_OBS_RETENTION_DAYS default of 30, plus oldest-spans-first eviction above
   a 1 GiB cap, and it runs automatically at every sink startup. So the
   evidence behind an insight silently expires after a month by default, and
   --generate_insights roughly triples span volume. fix-sb8.13 is load-bearing
   for provenance, not cleanup.

Two findings that make tasks CHEAPER than filed: fw.llm.call already carries
model, usage, cost and cache_hit (dspy_logger.py ~L420-431), so the per-pass
cost rollup and the cache-confound detection are queries over existing data
rather than new instrumentation (fix-sb8.2, fix-sb8.3); and buildTurnTree in
the SPA already groups top-level spans into planning/execution/other phases,
which is the natural seam for a pass dimension (fix-sb8.7).

One that makes a task more expensive: the SPA forbids innerHTML and the ban is
test-enforced, and its waterfall renders one level of direct children off a
single breadcrumb stack — a two-pane aligned diff needs a dedicated renderer,
not a reuse of renderWaterfall (fix-sb8.8).

title: Progressive observability exploration: run hotspots to scoped aggregates
description:
Help humans and coding agents find expensive, slow or unsuccessful recorded activity and move directly into the existing comparison and feedback workflow. Deliver useful small slices first, then broaden the evidence population while retaining the same UI/API and evidence references.

Phase 1: scope the existing problem finder; expose expensive LLM calls within a run; summarize recorded command outcomes within a run; add recorded dispatch-duration summaries. These four leaves are P2 / low cost / low risk within their boundaries and include their validation.

Phase 2: explicitly selected runs of the same task/experiment; all recorded runs of that task; experiment-wide exploration with distinct task populations; recorded cross-experiment/workflow/version comparisons. Later estimates are provisional and must be reassessed after prerequisites land. The aggregate high cost describes combined remaining work, not each foundation leaf. The four foundation tasks were explicitly authorized and delivered; later expansion stages remain deferred. Any P2 leaf with cost OR risk high stays deferred for explicit owner approval.
design:
HUMAN UI
Keep Runs / Compare / Feedback. Answers and artifacts remain first in Compare. Add compact expandable command-outcome, command-duration and expensive-LLM-call sections independently for each side. Runs can offer Find problems within the explicitly supported current source. Clicking a number opens exact contributing calls/steps and existing trace/feedback navigation. No new analytics application or Insights layer.

Broaden scope progressively: This run -> Selected runs -> All runs of this task. Implement scope selectors only with their owning stage. Experiment-level views keep task populations distinguishable. Every view shows source/scope, examined population, unknown/missing coverage, and partial/complete state. Distinguish failed dispatches from runs with failures. Selecting an aggregate group opens contributing runs and supports explicit comparison with the best run; never manufacture a representative run or equate cheapest/fastest with best. Preserve source-switch/stale-response guards and teacher/student pass identity; shared legacy content stays shared.

CODING-AGENT API AND REUSABLE REDUCERS
Extend existing run/comparison reads and ExecutionRef/EvidenceAnchor conventions additively. Small shared reducers accept observations with explicit execution/run/turn/step/span identity, avoiding single-run assumptions while initially exposing one run. Later a bounded explicit reference list can use the same summary shape. No generic aggregation framework up front.

Each new derived summary carries requested/observed scope; metric definition/version/unit; counts/distributions and known/unknown/partial coverage; exact contributing evidence references; population completeness and continuation when relevant. Later contributor pagination must remain tied to the same observed result. UI and agents consume the same definitions and server results; retain compatibility for existing clients. Counts combine directly. Rates use combined numerators/denominators, never averaged percentages. Combined medians use underlying valid durations, never averaged per-run medians. Keep source identity and avoid silently normalizing command names or pooling workflow/version/task populations.

FEEDBACK
Keep existing task/run/pair/step targets and composer. Humans use free-form comments; agents can place structured analysis and scope/contributor references in comment text. Retain observations_analysis: observation|analysis; conclusions: what_went_right|what_went_wrong; recommendations: what_to_do|what_not_to_do. No aggregate-insight object, new category, mandatory verdict or automatic winner selection.

METRIC BOUNDARIES
A turn containing command X and a failure does not prove X failed: command summaries use canonical dispatch records. Distinguish completion, command response success and evaluator outcome. Missing cost is not zero; reuse canonical shared/nested response accounting. Dispatch durations are inclusive observations, not additive critical-path or human-wait-subtracted active time. Do not infer unrecorded retry rounds or context-instance identities; existing capture/identity gaps remain separate beads. Filter scope before aggregate/pagination and preserve the exact examined population for drill-down. Keyset scans avoid offset shifts but do not freeze a live store. The legacy attempt chip path's 10000-turn read must not become an assumed complete aggregate source.

FUTURE BOUNDARIES
Command-level allocation of LLM cost, exclusive/critical-path or active-time accounting, and instrumentation/identity repair require separately scoped and triaged work if later requested; they are not hidden prerequisites here. Reproducibility stays deferred under fix-nqv8. Stage-specific clarification/retry summaries use recorded signals and unknown coverage, never invented rates from missing evidence.

EXECUTION POLICY
This update changes planning only. Initial foundation tasks are open; duration depends on command outcome groups. Later stages are deferred pending prerequisites and re-triage, not automatically downgraded when foundations ship. A P2 leaf high in either cost or risk needs explicit owner approval. An epic's aggregate high cost does not impose that gate on its low-cost/low-risk leaves. File newly uncovered P3/P4 issues whose cost AND risk are medium-or-higher; adjacent low/low corrections follow the existing wave rule.
acceptance_criteria: Four bounded foundations work in existing UI/API with exact evidence drill-down and unchanged feedback taxonomy. Later stages preserve the shared summary contract, population/source identity and unknown coverage, and are re-triaged before implementation. Every task/sub-epic has priority/cost/risk recorded; high-cost or high-risk P2 leaves remain approval-gated. No automatic winner, required benchmark setup or evidence migration.
notes:
Triage (2026-09-19): priority=P2; cost=high; risk=medium. High effort for trustworthy aggregation; medium risk of misleading populations. Not a prerequisite for direct experiment comparison.
Owner clarified implementation gate: after P1 wave and eligible P2 wave, any P2 with EITHER high cost OR high risk requires explicit approval. This task has high cost and medium risk, so implementation is deferred pending that approval.
Decomposition investigation (2026-09-20; planning only, no implementation approval inferred):
Conclusion: a useful narrowed delivery can consist of low-cost/low-risk vertical slices; the FULL original experiment/cohort/version exploration cannot honestly be promised all low/low merely by splitting. Existing diagnosis.search_turns already provides scoped filtering, diagnostic marker facets, segmented continuation, counts_scope/basis and exact turn drill-down; comparison.project_execution already provides canonical steps, timing, per-turn LLM calls_detail, cost/usage coverage and immutable source references. The UI already displays marker counts and attempt cost chips, so do not create tasks to rebuild those.
Proposed slices (each includes shared human/agent semantics and focused real-component + relevant DOM validation, not separate uncosted integration work):
A. P2 / cost low / risk low: expose experiment/task/attempt scope controls in the existing turn finder for its CURRENT explicitly selected source. Reuse existing API filters, marker chips, scan continuation, stop/continue and partial-count labels. Reset scan/cursor on scope/source change. No automatic cross-source navigation or pooled store search. Add command filter only as a turn-membership filter, explicitly not a command-failure metric.
B. P2 / cost low / risk low: show recorded LLM calls ordered by known recorded cost inside each existing comparison side, using turns[].usage.calls_detail already on the wire. Keep unknown/shared-response calls visibly separate, retain cache/coverage labels and exact turn/span links; no cost allocation to commands, no cohort ranking, no new scan or source selection. Agents use the same existing per-call payload.
C. P2 / cost low / risk low, conditional on staying a small additive projection: one-run command outcome table, shown independently on each comparison side. Group existing canonical ExecutionStep rows by exact recorded command name; use recorded response_success true/false/unknown, retain conflict/unknown information and missing-evidence coverage, with exact member step references for drill-down. Shared pure reducer published additively through existing run/comparison routes; UI renders that payload. No SQL joins, command-name normalization, context inference, outcome quality score or writes. Unknown command names get a separate bucket. Do not count all failures in a turn as failures of every command in it.
D. P2 / cost low / risk low; depends on C: add count/min/median/max of known per-dispatch duration_ns to the same one-run command groups, plus timed/untimed counts and links to underlying dispatches. Label duration as recorded inclusive dispatch time; parent/child durations are not additive and this is not user-wait-subtracted active latency or critical-path time. No percentiles across experiments or new timing attribution.
A and B are independent; D depends only on C. Each slice must remain useful alone and include its own API/UI/drill-down/coverage acceptance where it introduces semantics. If implementation needs a new scanner, source router, persistence/cache subsystem, or attribution rules, stop and re-triage instead of retaining an artificial low estimate.
Residual original scope NOT covered by these four slices: experiment-wide command failure rates, pooling runs/tasks, exact contributors for aggregates across a changing live dataset, stage-specific clarification/retry rates when evidence is incomplete, cost allocation to commands, active-time accounting, cross-workflow/version comparisons, and fast large-corpus aggregate queries. These retain medium-or-higher cost/risk pending a separate design; broad cross-source/version cohorts retain the parent high-cost scope. Existing type-only context and retry-coverage gaps must not be silently solved or inferred here.
Concrete code evidence: diagnosis.py TurnQuery/search_turns/TurnSearchPage; index.html turnFindPath currently omits experiment/task/attempt though server turn_query_from_params accepts them; store.list_turns command predicate is any matching span in a TURN, not the same command_call_id as its failure; server.annotate_attempt_rows caps its legacy turn list at 10000, so do not use existing visible attempt chips as guaranteed complete experiment aggregates; comparison.py ExecutionStep and per-turn usage.calls_detail supply safer one-run inputs. Keyset continuation avoids offset shifts but is not a frozen snapshot of an actively changing store.
Validation of existing reusable contracts: .venv pytest tests/test_trace_diagnosis.py selected scope/facets/segmented-counts/record-only-failure/read-only tests: 7 passed, 103 deselected in 0.35s. Source audit only otherwise; no benchmark/experiment setup or historical-source writes.

title: Observability: live chat, answer artifacts, winners, diagnosis and feedback
description:
Owner-directed plan, 2026-09-19. Help humans and coding agents optimize workflows and the framework through a short loop: run an experiment; inspect it against the current winner; keep the winner, choose the candidate, or remain undecided. The first experiment automatically becomes current winner. Selection is a judgment supported by recorded evidence, not an automatic metric ranking.
Core scope, in owner delivery order: (1) stream agent-assistant interactions in chat and display artifacts alongside final answers; (2) lightweight setup reuse, persisted winner/history and candidate comparison; (3) execution/NLU highlights and consolidated task feedback. Independent tasks can proceed without artificial phase barriers. Existing capture, execution ledgers, benchmark versions, cost rollups, sealed workspaces and formal review remain foundations, not new build requirements.
No upfront measurable targets or difficult benchmark setup. Reproducibility (code/data/artifact snapshotting and restoration) is explicitly future work and must not block this epic. Supporting dashboards/training/retention/shared deployment are tracked separately. Release authorization gates remain separate and unchanged.
Human UI and coding-agent structured reads/actions must share semantics and stable store/experiment/task/attempt/turn/span references. Reuse existing stores, workspaces, benchmarks and APIs. Include focused real-component integration tests and relevant browser interaction checks; no paid experiments are required to implement this work. No mandatory upfront scores, numeric targets, rubric, hypothesis, pre-registration ceremony, or reproducibility snapshots.

Multiple-run optimization amendment (owner discussion, 2026-09-19):
Multiple-run optimization is part of the existing core: repeat the same task/setup n times within an experiment, explicitly select a best run for the task, compare each other run against it and record feedback through the established three categories/subcategories. Extend shared recorded-execution comparison to teacher/student passes with pass-aware references. Distillation lessons remain ordinary comments. Best-run selection never changes the experiment winner. First experiment still automatically becomes winner. Chat streaming and final-answer artifacts stay FIRST delivery priority; no new top-level distillation epic and no reproducibility expansion.

Repeated-run consistency follow-on: fix-9eg.17.5 adds cheap planning/final-answer cosine similarity and execution-step variation within a task and across experiments. Descriptive metrics support comparison and existing categorized feedback without automatic winner selection or upfront targets. Chat-first ordering remains unchanged.

OWNER-CONFIRMED FEEDBACK CONTRACT (supersedes earlier three-question shorthand):
Categories and allowed subcategories, represented as API enum values:
- observations_analysis (UI: Observations / Analysis): observation, analysis.
- conclusions (UI: Conclusions): what_went_right, what_went_wrong.
- recommendations (UI: Recommendations): what_to_do, what_not_to_do.
The owner confirmed these six meanings explicitly in this implementation session. UI category/subcategory selectors and watermark guidance facilitate free-form human comments; the coding-agent recording API carries category and subcategory explicitly as enums and accepts arbitrary structured text within the comment. Validate category/subcategory pairing. No parsing headings to infer required metadata for NEW writes. Preserve existing historical text without rewriting frozen evidence; uncategorized legacy comments remain readable and visibly legacy/unclassified rather than guessing a new subcategory. Comparison comments can link both recorded executions/pass/step anchors through the same API. No separate insight schema, review layer, or mandatory verdict workflow.
acceptance_criteria:
Live agent-assistant interactions appear during execution and artifacts appear alongside final answers, including restored conversations. First experiment automatically becomes current winner; candidates reuse setup without mandatory scores/targets/rubrics. Human and coding agent can compare, retain/promote/defer, inspect highlighted failures/navigation and read all task feedback. Core children complete; deferred/supporting work is not a completion gate.
Core also supports best-versus-other-run review and the same comparison/feedback surfaces for recorded teacher/student passes. Humans and coding agents use the same categories/subcategories and source anchors.
Repeated-run consistency summaries/deltas expose evidence coverage and are available in the existing task comparison UI and agent read API.

title: Chatbot picker: Train button (detached spawn + poll trained bool)
description:
Chatbot landing-page Train button for untrained workflows. Architecture is detached spawn + poll of a trained bool. Training must survive chatbot exit. No log scraping, no live stage label.

## Why this shape

Training can take an hour+. The user may quit the chatbot. A blocking POST dies with the process and cannot return a bool to a later session. In-memory spawn+poll is also insufficient: the next chatbot launch only sees disk + a live PID.

## In scope

- Train button next to untrained rows on the **candidate list** (left column of the picker).
- `POST /api/train {path}`: same host/origin + token gates as `select_workflow`.
  - Refuse bundled package examples (`source == "examples"` / path under the installed `fastworkflow/examples/`) — Rule 3: never train `fastworkflow/examples/*/___command_info` in place.
  - Refuse if env files cannot be autodetected (`_autodetect_env_files`). Point at the existing env-setup card; do not build a train-specific env UI.
  - Refuse if another train PID is alive (one at a time — BERT + this box's RAM).
  - Spawn `sys.executable -m fastworkflow.train <workflow> <env> <passwords>` with `start_new_session=True`.
  - Redirect stdout/stderr to a log file under the workflow **state dir** (`state_paths.workflow_state_dir`), not inherited stdio — inherited pipes SIGPIPE the child when the chatbot exits.
  - Write a pid file next to that log. Return immediately.
- Chatbot **shutdown must not terminate** the train process (unlike the FastAPI child).
- Poll existing `GET /api/workflows` (no new status endpoint). Add `training: bool` per row = pid file exists and `os.kill(pid, 0)` succeeds. Replace `_workflow_is_trained` (dir exists) with `is_workflow_trained()` — train creates `___command_info` immediately, so the dir check would flip to trained while models are still fitting.
- SPA: button on untrained local rows; `stopPropagation` so it does not also select. While `training`, show a static "Training…" (not parsed logs). Poll `/api/workflows` only while any row is `training`. On `trained: true`, show the trained tag. On death-without-trained, show a short error from the last POST or a generic "training failed — see the chatbot terminal / train log".
- Tests: spawn a **stub** Python process that writes a pid, sleeps, optionally writes a fake `threshold.json` layout — never call real `train_main`, never touch bundled example artifacts.

## Out of scope (effort squeezes — do not do these)

- Log scraping, tqdm/ANSI parsing, `"training <X>"` stage labels, log console in the SPA.
- In-process job table / Popen held on `ChatbotServer` / reader thread / PIPE.
- Reusing `publication_lock` as "train is running" — it is only held around publish-and-prune, not the hour of fitting.
- Changing `fastworkflow train` internals or adding `fw.train.*` spans.
- Train button on the **browse** pane (Use + tags stay as they are).
- Cancel/stop training, parallel trains, copy-bundled-example-then-train wizard, datasets-install UI.
- Disabling "Use"/select on untrained workflows.
- New design doc (additive picker affordance under the existing chatbot; T0).
- Windows-specific locking (fcntl already degrades; this machine is WSL).

## Files (expected)

- `fastworkflow/run_chatbot/launcher.py` — `plan_train_spawn` / `spawn_detached_train` / pid helpers (mirror `plan_server_spawn`; do not call `terminate_server` on train).
- `fastworkflow/run_chatbot/server.py` — POST allowlist, `/api/train`, `training` + real `trained` on `/api/workflows` and browse if cheap.
- `fastworkflow/run_chatbot/static/index.html` — button + poll.
- `tests/test_run_chatbot_server.py` (or a small sibling) — stub-process integration tests.

## Estimate after squeezes

~350–500 lines, about one day. Previous full estimate was 650–1100 (log scraping) then 450–650 (spawn+poll with an in-process manager). Dropping the job manager and browse-button is the remaining cut.
acceptance_criteria:
- Untrained local workflow on the picker candidate list shows a Train button; bundled package examples do not.
- Clicking Train starts `fastworkflow train` as a detached process and returns immediately.
- Exiting the chatbot does not stop that process (stdio redirected; shutdown does not SIGTERM it).
- Reloading the picker (same or new chatbot process) shows static "Training…" while the pid is alive, then the trained tag once `is_workflow_trained` is true.
- A second Train while one is running is refused.
- Missing env files reuse the existing env-setup path; no train-specific env UI.
- Tests cover spawn/refuse/poll against a stub process, not a real BERT train, and do not write into fastworkflow/examples/*/___command_info.
close_reason: Implemented detached spawn+poll Train button. pytest tests/test_run_chatbot_train.py tests/test_run_chatbot_server.py::TestPackaging tests/test_run_chatbot_server.py::TestControlPlane — 29 passed. Chatbot shutdown does not SIGTERM the train child; status is pid file + threshold.json check; bundled package examples refused.

title: Chatbot waterfall legend color chips float to top of page
description:
The span-type color chips in the debug-mode waterfall legend are not adjacent to their labels (turn, planner, tool call, etc.). They appear as a row of colored squares at the top of the page instead.

Root cause: legend chips reuse the `.wfBar` class, which is `position: absolute` so the waterfall bars can overlay `.wfTrack`. With no positioned ancestor, the chips escape the legend and pin to the initial containing block.

Fix: keep category color classes on the chips but do not treat them as absolutely-positioned bars; chips must sit inline next to the span-type labels they describe.

Verify in the live chatbot debug view: each legend label has its matching color square immediately to its left.
close_reason: Legend chips no longer reuse .wfBar (position:absolute). Category colors apply via .cat-* and .legend .chip is position:static. Verified: TestPackaging::test_legend_chips_sit_inline_with_labels passed; live debug view measured 7 chips adjacent to labels, 0 floating at viewport top.

comments.author: Dhar Rawal
comments.text:
UX REDESIGN (Dhar's direction, 2026-08-25): zero-setup chat.

Dhar's ruling: the chatbot must not require manual server start/connect; the channel is an implementation detail a single-user dev tool never exposes; no workflow argument should mean a picker UI. Implemented on the working tree:

1. AUTO-SPAWN + AUTO-CONNECT. `fastworkflow run_chatbot <wf>` spawns the FastAPI server automatically (loopback-only, --cors_loopback_only, terminated on exit incl. SIGTERM); the SPA polls /probes/readyz then /initialize's access_token and lands connected in the Chat tab. --no-server = trace viewer only; missing [server] extra degrades to viewer with the reason on /api/session and in the UI. Env files auto-detected (workflow dir -> bundled examples/ -> cwd) or via --env_file_path/--passwords_file_path.
2. R19 AMENDED (recorded in design doc §3.4): unsigned dev JWTs are the DEFAULT for the auto-spawned loopback server (chatbot mints its own tokens); --expect-encrypted-jwt restores signed mode; --start-server/--allow-unsigned-jwt kept as hidden no-op compat flags. Surviving invariants: 127.0.0.1-only bind, no UI path to wider bind, no wildcard CORS. CORS moved from exact-origin pin to loopback-origin regex (new run_fastapi_mcp --cors_loopback_only) because port forwarders (WSL/IDE) serve the page from a different local port.
3. CHANNEL HIDDEN. Chatbot server mints chatbot-<hex> per launch + user 'developer'; /api/session hands the SPA everything; Connect form deleted (Advanced panel remains for external servers: base URL + optional pasted JWT). 'New conversation' header button -> POST /new_conversation.
4. WORKFLOW PICKER. workflow_path now optional; token-gated control plane: GET /api/session|/api/workflows (bundled examples + 2-level cwd scan)|/api/browse (dirs only), POST /api/select_workflow (the ONLY HTTP write; observability data stays read-only); runtime workflow switching replaces the spawned server.
5. COSMETICS. Chat-first tab order, header status pill (server running/starting/viewer-only/error), segmented tabs, refreshed palette + dark theme, rounded chat bubbles + composer, picker card, better empty/error states, tabular-nums durations, reduced-motion-safe entry animation.

Tests: 70 chatbot tests green (incl. new: auto-spawn posture, signed-mode override, extra-missing degradation, control-plane auth/validation/405s, picker endpoints); 44 FastAPI regression green. Two OUTDATED tests updated with rationale: missing-DB-exits (now a normal cold start; maintenance commands still error) and main-refuses-unsigned-spawn (posture inverted by this ruling; plan_server_spawn's pure refusal logic + its tests unchanged). E2E verified live on examples/hello_world: auto-spawn banner, readyz->initialize->deterministic turn recorded in obs DB under the managed channel, forwarded-origin CORS preflight OK, SIGTERM stops both processes. Docs updated: README run_chatbot section, docs/run_chatbot_cli_parity.md, design doc §3.4 amendment.

comments.author: Dhar Rawal
comments.text: FOLLOW-UP (same session): live use surfaced two auto-spawn gaps — (1) a squatter on the default port 8000 (in Dhar's case, an orphaned test server from the review session) was silently mistaken for our spawn: uvicorn takes seconds to fail its bind, so the 1s liveness check passed and the chat connected to whatever was already answering; (2) a server dying mid-session left the UI claiming 'server running' and lost the typed message on the failed send.
