comments.author: Dhar Rawal
comments.text:
EPIC-LEVEL IMPLEMENTATION REVIEW (2026-08-25, Claude, reliability/latency/perf/functionality/UX pass; 3 parallel adversarial reviewers + orchestrator verification against the design doc + R1-R28 + Phase-7 I/C rulings).

VERDICT: Phases 1-6 sound; every §3.4 security invariant (R5/R18/R19/R22/R23) verified satisfied; emission sites complete per the §3.1 table, none missed/doubled (R28 verified per CommandTraceEvent constructor); [A39] channel scoping proven incl. byte-identical 404s; I8 distillation port fully correct. Phase 7 (fix-kw7.8) is ~40% done: steps 5+7 complete, store primitives exist but have ZERO production callers.

FIXED ON THE WORKING TREE THIS SESSION (with regression tests):
1. Ruling C2 (live aliasing bug): both mint sites now pass legacy_floor=get_last_conversation_id(); mint failures degrade to legacy reserve instead of failing /initialize or a turn; mint busy timeout cut 30s->FW_OBS_SYNC_WRITE_TIMEOUT_S (5s) so a wedged DB can't stall the event loop. Tests: TestMintingLegacyFloor.
2. Ruling I9 (live divergence bug): update_conversation_topic_summary now returns the STORED suffixed topic; the Phase-A mirror passes it. Tests in test_conversation_topic_labeling.py.
3. Ruling C1 (live erasure hole): run_chatbot --forget-channel now also deletes the legacy conversations/<channel_id>.sqlite3 (+wal/shm), with a path-traversal guard. Tests: TestForgetChannelLegacyErasure.
4. [R9] queued-window bug: resolve_logical_turn_key stamped the PREVIOUS turn's logical key onto an execution polled while QUEUED (pre_turn_key unset, current_turn_key never cleared); now guarded on ExecState.RUNNING. Test added.
5. Chatbot viewer was NOT read-only: it opened the DB read-write, created it if missing, and write-probed it on every launch; could not open a 0400 snapshot. New ReadOnlyObservabilityStore (mode=ro URI, no schema writes, refuse-newer kept); missing DB now serves empty views (test-mode cold start). Tests: TestReadOnlyViewer.
6. SIGTERM to the chatbot orphaned the spawned unsigned-JWT FastAPI server: SIGTERM handler added; child now spawned in its own process group and terminated via killpg; immediate-death poll after spawn; friendly EADDRINUSE/newer-schema launch errors; CSP hash extraction hardened (attribute-tolerant regex + launch assert).
7. Redaction gaps: failure_reason + conversation_summary/traces columns and label topic/summary now pass the [R20] redactor.
8. fw.command.execute attribute prep (params.model_dump) moved inside the never-raise boundary and gated on an open span; finalize_turn_for_observability early-outs when sink+metrics are no-op (CLI per-turn cost ~0 under FW_OBSERVABILITY=0).
9. Chatbot context filter moved server-side (parameterized LIKE, reaches rows beyond the 200-row page); list fetch errors now render an error state. Design doc §3.4 amended to record the loopback connect-src CSP exception.
10. Renames/docs: env template studio->run_chatbot; README --forget-channel 'everywhere' claim now true via fix 3.

REMAINING PHASE-7 SCOPE (amended implementation order steps 1(part),3,4,6): ack-returning sync-first emit_turn_record + pending-retry ring + breaker (I1/I6/C9 — reserve_turn_ordinal is currently dead code); §2.1 memory-column stamping (serialize_turn_result still hardcodes conversation_summary/traces NULL, so every store-side usable-rows read returns empty) + I5 baseline; last_completed_turn_key on WEC + feedback table wiring (I3/C4 — upsert_feedback dead); FastAPI switch of memory window/milestones/labeling/step-back/listings/dump to the store (I4/I7/I10/C7 — get_memory_window, count_usable_turns, conversation_summaries, conversation_label_state, newest_conversation_ids, get_last_completed_turn_key, list_conversation_summaries, dump_all_conversations all have zero callers; dump also still missing the legacy_stores_present marker); trim gating on ack (I2); shutdown finalizer re-scope (C5); §2.6 --include-conversations opt-in prune; TurnResult.ordinal stamping (resolves with sync emit); retirement of production conversation_store imports (C5, module+tests stay pending [DHAR]).

title: db_lookup rejects legal values absent from the candidate list, via the loose 0.2 difflib cutoff
description:
DatabaseValidator.fuzzy_match's final difflib stage uses cutoff=0.2 by default, where difflib's own default is 0.6. Combined with the rule that ANY non-empty suggestion list sets is_valid=False (signatures.py:638-641), a value that is legal but simply not in the candidate list gets rejected rather than passed through.

Measured in docs/FASTWORKFLOW_FUZZY_MATCH_DEFECTS.md: feeding real 32-character hex uids to a db_lookup field whose candidates were display names rejected 34 of 40 VALID uids.

Confirmed still loose after fix-86c, which did not touch this stage:
  fuzzy_match('Garisn', ['Aaron Garrison', 'Barry Jones'], suggest_threshold=0.0, threshold=0.2) suggests BOTH names
  the same call at threshold=0.6 suggests only 'Aaron Garrison'
Pinned by test_difflib_stage_suggests_when_levenshtein_finds_nothing in tests/test_fuzzy_match.py.

Deliberately left alone by fix-86c because raising the default changes acceptance behaviour for every existing workflow: fewer suggestions means fewer invalidations means values that are currently rejected would start passing through. That is probably the improvement we want, but it is an unmeasured behaviour change and it deserves its own measurement rather than riding along with a scoring fix.

Options to weigh:
1. Raise the default toward difflib's 0.6. Simplest; changes behaviour for existing callers.
2. Leave the default and document the workaround (decline with (False, None, []) for values the hook does not own). Already possible today; see fix-07b.
3. Separate 'suggest' from 'invalidate' so suggestions can be offered without failing validation. Largest change, and it touches a contract that the clarification flow depends on.

Decide with evidence, not taste: the 34-of-40 figure is from one external workflow, so it should be reproduced on an in-tree workflow before the default moves.
notes:
MEASURED AT SCALE 2026-08-20, post fix-86c. The fix looks measurably free, which the issue as filed did not establish.

Candidate-list SIZE is what drives this, and a small probe hides it: against 4 display names a 32-char uid produces NO suggestions at any cutoff, i.e. the 'no opinion' state, and looks already fixed. Against 1015 synthetic display names (matching the reported dataset size) with 40 valid 32-char hex uids:

  difflib cutoff=0.2 (current default):  23 of 40 valid uids REJECTED, 17 declined
  difflib cutoff=0.4:                     0 rejected, 40 declined
  difflib cutoff=0.6 (difflib's own):     0 rejected, 40 declined
  (0 wrongly auto-applied at any cutoff)

23/40 reproduces the reported 34/40 phenomenon on synthetic names, so the defect is real and survived fix-86c. With 1015 candidates, difflib's n=3 nearest always clear a 0.2 ratio, and any non-empty suggestion list sets is_valid=False (signatures.py:661-664).

TYPO RECALL IS UNAFFECTED BY THIS CUTOFF, which is the key result. The difflib stage is only reached when NO candidate is within suggest_threshold=0.7, so anything the Levenshtein stage already resolves never sees the cutoff:
  'Aaron Garrisen' -> (True, 'Aaron Garrison') at cutoff 0.2 AND at 0.6
  'Aaron Garri'    -> (True, 'Aaron Garrison')
  'Garrison'       -> 26 suggestions (correct ambiguity: 26 names share it)
Stage reached only for genuinely-unlike input: 'zzzz' and full uids go to difflib; 'Garrison', 'Garrisen', 'Ltd', 'Aaron', 'arrison' all resolve at Levenshtein.

So of the three options in the description, option 1 (raise the default) now has evidence behind it: 23 spurious rejections removed, no measured cost. Remaining work is to reproduce on an IN-TREE workflow with a large candidate list before moving the default, since both the 34/40 and this 23/40 come from name-shaped data and the interaction is with list size rather than with any workflow specific.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-20: difflib cutoff default raised 0.2 -> 0.6 (difflib's own default). Option 1 from the description, now with evidence on both sides.

IN-TREE CONFIRMATION, retail_data (379 names, 500 user_ids, 1000 order_ids, 500 emails, 50 product names, 591 item_ids), legal values fed to a field whose candidate list is a different domain:
  email   -> order_ids     cutoff 0.2: 40/40 REJECTED    0.4: 0    0.6: 0
  user_id -> product names cutoff 0.2: 30/40 REJECTED    0.4: 2    0.6: 0
  order_id-> product names all cutoffs: 0 rejected (list too small to clear the ratio)
  item_id -> names         all cutoffs: 0 rejected
Candidate-list SIZE is the driver: with ~1000 candidates difflib's n=3 nearest always clear a 0.2 ratio, and any non-empty suggestion list sets is_valid=False.

COST SIDE MEASURED, and it is the argument that decided it. Two findings:
1. The difflib stage contributes NOTHING to genuine near-miss recall, because anything recoverable is already caught by the Levenshtein stage at suggest_threshold=0.7. Identical at 0.2 and 0.6:
     'Aarav Andersen' -> matched 'Aarav Anderson'   'Aarav Andrsn' -> matched 'Aarav Anderson'
     'Yusuf Rossy'    -> matched 'Yusuf Rossi'
2. The suggestions the 0.2 cutoff produces are NOISE, so rejecting on them is a worse turn than passing the value through:
     'Bruce Wayne' -> ['Harper Ahmed', 'Isabella Taylor', 'Omar Hernandez', 'Yara Hernandez']
   Being told 'invalid, did you mean Harper Ahmed?' is not a better turn than letting business logic reject 'Bruce Wayne'.
The acknowledged trade is that genuine non-members now pass through as 'no opinion' rather than being rejected: for random 12-char noise against the name list, rejected 9/10 at 0.2 vs 3/10 at 0.6. Accepted, because the rejections it gives up are the noise-suggestion kind above.

Option 3 (separating 'suggest' from 'invalidate' so a hook can reject WITHOUT producing suggestions) is still the principled fix and is untouched -- the contract still has no way to say 'this is invalid and I have no suggestions'. Not filed separately; raise it if the pass-through becomes a problem in practice.

TESTS in tests/test_fuzzy_match.py::TestDefaultThresholds, against the real retail catalogues:
  test_absent_value_is_declined_rather_than_rejected  (32-char uid vs 379 names -> (False, None, []))
  test_loose_cutoff_would_reject_it_on_unrelated_suggestions  (same uid at threshold=0.2 -> suggestions, i.e. why the default moved)

NOTE the finding that came out of this measurement and dominates it: the auto_apply_threshold default of 0.7 was silently rewriting non-members to real records ('Batman' -> 'Fatima Nguyen'). Filed and fixed as fix-11r. The cutoff change here is second-order by comparison.
close_reason: Closed

title: fuzzy_match threshold does not gate the Levenshtein stage; split auto-apply from suggest
description:
DatabaseValidator.fuzzy_match accepts 'threshold' (utils/signatures.py:71) but only the third stage (difflib.get_close_matches) receives it. The Levenshtein stage that produces AUTO-APPLIED corrections is called with a literal:

    best_matches, _ = find_best_matches(value, key_values, threshold = 0.7)   # signatures.py:87

Consequences: (1) raising threshold cannot make matching stricter, because the stage that rewrites the parameter ignores it; (2) 0.7 is looser than find_best_matches' own default of 0.4, so the strictest-looking call site in the package is the most permissive. Verified: identical output at threshold 0.2 through 1.0.

Design note from review: tunability alone does NOT fix the reported case. 'Barry Jones' scores 0.375, so a 0.3 gate rejects it and falls through to suggestions, but 'Aaron Garrison' still scores 0.750 and still loses. It converts confidently-wrong into no-answer, and costs typo recall on short strings ('Ltd' vs 'Ltf' is 0.333).

The deeper issue is that ONE number does two jobs with very different costs: 'auto-apply this silently' and 'offer these as suggestions'. A loose threshold is right for suggesting and wrong for rewriting. Fix is to split them into separate, documented, caller-supplied parameters (auto_apply_threshold strict, suggest_threshold loose) rather than plumbing one value through.

Command-level tunability falls out for free: db_lookup is user code that calls fuzzy_match itself, so exposing the parameters IS per-command tunability. Do NOT add a json_schema_extra key for it — that would create a second control path competing with the hook for the same decision.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-20.

DatabaseValidator.fuzzy_match signature is now:
    fuzzy_match(value, key_values, threshold=0.2, suggest_threshold=0.7, auto_apply_threshold=0.7)

- threshold (unchanged name and default): difflib cutoff for the final suggestion-only stage.
- suggest_threshold: max Levenshtein distance at which a candidate is considered at all. This is the 0.7 that used to be a literal at signatures.py:87.
- auto_apply_threshold: max distance at which a UNIQUE match is reported as matched, i.e. silently written back by validate_parameters.

DEVIATION FROM THE ISSUE AS FILED, deliberate. The filed plan proposed a strict auto-apply default (0.15). Shipped it defaulting to 0.7 instead, i.e. equal to suggest_threshold and identical to today's behaviour. Reason: the measured evidence in docs/FASTWORKFLOW_FUZZY_MATCH_DEFECTS.md says the SCORING fix alone takes wrong answers from 56 to 0 across 1101 fragment queries with one-edit typo recall unchanged at 577/577. A strict auto-apply default would therefore be extra strictness that no measurement asks for, and it would cost typo recall: 'Garrisen' -> 'Aaron Garrison' is distance 0.125 and would stop auto-applying, and short strings suffer worst ('Ltd' vs 'Ltf' is 0.333). It would trade the fixed failure mode for the OTHER reported failure mode, the one that rejected 34 of 40 valid uids. So the knob ships as an affordance, not a behaviour change.

Confirmed the split does what the issue asked, on the patched tree:
  auto_apply_threshold=0.0 -> ('Garrisen') (False, None, ['Aaron Garrison'])   suggestion, no rewrite
  auto_apply_threshold=0.7 -> ('Garrisen') (True, 'Aaron Garrison', [])       today's behaviour
  suggest_threshold=0.0    -> ('Garrisen') (False, None, [both names])         stage now gated
A containing match still auto-applies at auto_apply_threshold=0.0, which is the intended semantics of 'exact or containing only'.

NO json_schema_extra key was added, per the review: db_lookup is user code that calls fuzzy_match itself, so exposing these parameters IS per-command tunability. A framework-level annotation would create a second control path competing with the hook for the same decision.

TESTS: test_auto_apply_threshold_downgrades_a_typo_to_a_suggestion, test_auto_apply_threshold_of_zero_still_applies_a_containing_match, test_suggest_threshold_gates_the_levenshtein_stage, test_difflib_stage_suggests_when_levenshtein_finds_nothing (which also pins how loose the 0.2 difflib default is: it suggests an unrelated name too).
close_reason: Closed

title: R13: /activate_conversation and cold session create hydrate whole conversations before windowing to 20 turns
description:
ADJACENT MEMORY DEFECT, found while reviewing gh-65. Not required for gh-65's goal,
but gh-65 proposes adding work to /activate_conversation without noticing that
activate is already the expensive endpoint.

gh-65 is careful to forbid full-conversation hydration on GET /conversations. Two
other paths already do it.

    __main__.py:1697   conv = runtime.conversation_store.get_conversation(request.conversation_id)
    __main__.py:1713-1715  restore_history_from_turns(conv["turns"][-MAX_CONVERSATION_TURNS_IN_MEMORY:])

get_conversation (conversation_store.py:187-191) goes through _hydrated ->
_read_turns -> list(...), which materializes EVERY turn record, and only then is
the list sliced to the newest 20. Same shape on cold session create:

    utils.py:517-527   conversation_store.get_conversation(conv_id_to_restore)
                       ... conversation["turns"][-MAX_CONVERSATION_TURNS_IN_MEMORY:]

At 450 KB turn payloads a 100-turn conversation is ~45 MB transiently resident,
per activate and per cold create of a reused channel. This is exactly the growth
the v3.0.x memory-bounds work removed from the save path, still present on the
restore path. It is also why MAX_CONVERSATION_TURNS_IN_MEMORY = 20 does not bound
what activate costs — it bounds only what activate KEEPS.

SCOPE (guiding principle 1: minimal and modular). Add a store method that yields
or returns only the last N turn records, using the machinery already there:
_iter_turn_records walks conv:{id}:turn:{index} one key at a time and
appended_turn_count gives the count, so reading indices
max(0, count-N)..count-1 needs no scan and no full materialization. Point both
call sites at it. Leave get_conversation for /admin/dump_all_conversations, which
genuinely wants everything.

NOTE the fallback at conversation_store.py / utils.py:519-521: when the last
conversation record is absent (the reserved-but-empty state right after a rotate)
create falls back to conv_id - 1. Preserve that behavior; a windowed reader must
still be able to report "no record" so the fallback triggers.

ACCEPTANCE.
- Activating or cold-restoring a long conversation reads at most
  MAX_CONVERSATION_TURNS_IN_MEMORY turn records.
- Peak RSS for those paths is independent of conversation length.
- The reserved-but-empty fallback on cold create still works.
- Measured, not asserted: include a before/after read count or RSS figure in the
  issue when it lands, per the repo's "if it isn't written with a number it didn't
  happen" rule.
close_reason: New ConversationStore.get_conversation_window(conv_id, max_turns) reads only the newest window's turn keys (count is on the record, turns are keyed by index, so no scan). Both restore paths point at it: _create_user_runtime and POST /activate_conversation. Returned turns are byte-identical to the old slice, so the load-bearing test counts deserializations - verified discriminating: 20 turn reads vs 100 for a slice implementation on a 100-turn conversation, same turns returned. None-for-missing-record contract preserved so the cold restore's conv_id-1 fallback still fires. 8 tests in new tests/test_conversation_window_reads.py; 183 pass across the affected suites.

title: R10: Add preview to ConversationSummary, denormalized at write time — read-time preview is O(all conversations x 450 KB)
description:
NICE-TO-HAVE. Only worth building after fix-dzs.5, because until "conversation
summary" carries real content on the deterministic and action paths, a preview of
it renders a constant string for the motivating workload.

WHAT gh-65 PROPOSES. Extend ConversationSummary (conversation_store.py:26-32,
returned by GET /conversations) with preview — the first ~200 characters of the
first turn's "conversation summary" — and optionally turn_count, so a picker is
usable while topic is blank. It correctly forbids hydrating whole conversations on
list, and correctly says list should "read turn 0 only ... and stop".

WHY THE READ-TIME VERSION IS NOT CHEAP. Two facts gh-65 misses.

1. list_conversations (conversation_store.py:207-229) iterates i in 1..
   last_conversation_id, builds a ConversationSummary for every conversation, and
   applies `limit` only AFTER sorting by updated_at. So a read-time preview would
   read turn 0 of EVERY conversation ever recorded for the channel in order to
   return 20.

2. KVStore stores each value as a single JSON TEXT row (kvstore.py:53-58), and a
   turn record is {"conversation summary", "conversation_traces", "feedback"}
   (conversation_history_io.py:13-20) with the 450 KB defect XML living inside
   conversation_traces. So extracting 200 characters means json.loads on 450 KB,
   once per conversation. Peak memory stays bounded because turns are read one at
   a time, but a channel with hundreds of conversations turns GET /conversations
   into hundreds of megabytes of JSON parsing per call.

That is the same class of cost the store's own docstring exists to keep out of the
process (conversation_store.py:377-384, on why get_conversation_summaries
projects instead of hydrating).

SCOPE. Denormalize. Compute preview once, when the first turn is appended
(append_conversation_turns, conversation_store.py:320-367 — it already has the
turn in hand and already writes the conv record), and store it on the conv:{i}
record. Then list_conversations stays exactly as cheap as it is today: one read
per conversation, no turn reads at all. turn_count is already there as
appended_turn_count and needs only to be surfaced.

Backfill is not required: preview is additive, older records simply have none, and
clients fall back to topic or to updated_at. Do not add a migration.

DOCUMENT WHAT BLANK MEANS, as gh-65 asks: a blank topic means no successful LLM
title yet — initialize-only, generation failed or timed out, perform_action-only,
or a pre-change record. It does NOT mean "only one turn elapsed".

OUT OF SCOPE (gh-65 agrees): no LLM on list, no ?ensure_topics=1 flag, no
background sweeper.

ACCEPTANCE.
- GET /conversations makes no LLM call and reads no turn records.
- Its cost does not grow with turn payload size.
- preview is present for conversations created after the change; absent, not
  wrong, for older ones.
- A picker can render every conversation from topic or preview alone.
notes:
DEFERRED 2026-08-13 after review with the developer. Research recorded so a future pickup does not redo it.

WHY DEFERRED, not rejected: nothing is blocked and no data is at risk, but the case is much weaker than when this was filed, and the performant design cannot serve the strongest remaining need.

1. UNBLOCKED but SHRUNK. fix-dzs.5 gave 'conversation summary' real content on the deterministic and action paths (it was a hardcoded constant), which was the blocker. But fix-dzs.6 then labels a conversation on its first chat turn, so the population of blank topics collapsed to: initialize-only channels, perform_action-only channels, transient generation failures, and pre-change records.

2. THE REAL CONSUMER IS AN LLM, NOT A UI. get_all_conversations and activate_conversation are both exposed as MCP tools (mcp_specific.py excludes seven operations; neither of these is among them). The flow is: agent lists conversations, picks one, calls activate_conversation. When topic AND summary are both blank the agent has nothing to discriminate on. This is a better justification than the 'UI picker' framing in the original GitHub issue - use it if this is revived.

3. A BLANK TOPIC IS NOT FUNCTIONALLY HARMFUL. Every production reference to topic: the uniqueness scan (_ensure_unique_topic), get_conversation_by_topic, the ConversationSummary display field, the blank placeholders, and the lazy-fill sentinel (get_conversation_label_state). get_conversation_by_topic has NO production caller - only its definition and two tests - and ActivateConversationRequest carries conversation_id: int. Topic is a display label plus a 'have I labeled this yet' flag.

4. PREVIEW CANNOT INHERIT A LENGTH BOUND. fix-dzs.5 bounded only the deterministic and action paths. The agent path is unbounded: with no actions the summary is the raw user message; with actions it is an LLM output whose signature asks for 'A multiline paragraph summary'. So preview must truncate AND collapse newlines itself.

5. turn_count IS FREE. appended_turn_count is already on the conv:{i} record that list_conversations already reads, so exposing it costs zero extra reads. If a cheap discriminator is ever wanted, this is the one to ship first.

6. THE BLOCKING PROBLEM. Denormalizing at write time - which is correct for performance, since read-time preview means a json.loads of a ~450 KB turn record per conversation, for every conversation, before the limit is applied - means preview is absent for every conversation that exists today. That is exactly the blank-topic population the feature is for. Serving it needs a lazy compute-and-write-back on read for records lacking a preview, which is more machinery than the value currently justifies.

REVIVE THIS IF: a client is observed choosing between multiple blank-topic conversations on one channel, or the MCP agent flow is seen failing to pick.
close_reason: Closed as won't-do-now to close the epic, NOT because the analysis was wrong. Full research is preserved in this issue's notes; read them before re-opening rather than re-deriving. Short version: fix-dzs.5 unblocked it but fix-dzs.6 then collapsed the population it serves (conversations are labeled on their first chat turn), a blank topic is not functionally harmful (get_conversation_by_topic has no production caller; activate takes a conversation_id), and write-time denormalization - the only performant design, since read-time preview means a json.loads of a ~450 KB turn record per conversation before the limit applies - cannot serve the pre-change records that are the strongest remaining case. REVIVE AS A NEW ISSUE IF: a client is observed choosing between multiple blank-topic conversations on one channel, or the MCP get_all_conversations -> activate_conversation flow is seen failing to pick. Cheapest first step if so: expose turn_count, which is already on the record list_conversations reads and therefore free.

title: import fastworkflow costs 7.2s, and it is the suite's real unit of cost
description:
MEASURED, and it replaces the long-tail theory that has been guiding test-performance thinking.

'import fastworkflow' takes 7.21s, reproducible to +/-0.01s across three runs, against ~0.00s for a bare interpreter. Decomposed with -X importtime:
  fastworkflow.chat_session                6.39s
    -> fastworkflow.model_pipeline_training 4.03s
       -> transformers auto_factory 1.83s, torch 1.23s, sklearn 0.93s
  litellm                                  1.56s
  dspy                                     0.79s

The chain is fastworkflow/__init__.py:309 -> chat_session -> chat_session.py:17, 'from fastworkflow.model_pipeline_training import CommandRouter'. Importing the PACKAGE unconditionally loads the entire training and model stack. Every fresh process pays it: every subprocess-spawning test, and every CLI invocation.

THE LONG-TAIL THEORY WAS WRONG. It looked like ~1650 tests averaging 1.25s each. Measured directly, the distribution is bimodal and most tests are 10-90ms: test_checkpoint_store.py runs 207 tests in 18.9s (0.09 s/test), and four other files run 202 tests in 10.25s of which ~7.2s is interpreter startup -- about 0.015 s/test of actual work. That is 409 tests, 24% of the suite, in roughly 30 seconds. The 1.25s average was an artifact of dividing a few very expensive tests across everything else.

It also explains the shape of the durations table: the cutoff sits at 7.11s and ten of the last fifteen entries are 7.1-7.7s. Those are fresh-process tests whose measured duration is almost entirely import; their bodies are near zero. The table was truncated exactly where that population begins.

PER-TEST FIXTURE OVERHEAD IS ESSENTIALLY ZERO -- the autouse conftest fixture early-returns unless a ChatWorker is alive, and fastworkflow.init is session-scoped at 0.34s once. So the previously-suspected fixture cost is not there.

DO: make the training/model import lazy so 'import fastworkflow' does not pull transformers, torch and sklearn. The win is per fresh process, which means CLI startup as well as the suite. Check what actually needs CommandRouter at import time in chat_session.py:17.
close_reason: Closed

title: A second request during a deferred agent turn gets a 500, not a 409
description:
PRODUCTION BUG, found via a test failure but not confined to tests. Discovered while diagnosing fix-j83.

workflow_execution_context.py:790-792 routes ANY message into _resume_agent_message whenever _awaiting_user is true. react.py:182 then raises a bare RuntimeError('No suspended ReAct state to resume') when _suspended is None.

Restoration is not the problem -- apply_serialized_state calls _ensure_agent_initialized() then import_suspended(react_blob), correctly. The desync arises afterwards: a deferred (202) agent turn CONSUMES _suspended while _awaiting_user is still set, and the next request re-enters the resume branch with nothing to resume.

REACHABLE IN PRODUCTION two ways: a client mixing /invoke_agent and /invoke_assistant on a channel that is awaiting user input, and any second request arriving while a deferred agent turn is still in flight. Both are ordinary client behaviour against a wait-or-defer API -- the second one especially, since 202 explicitly invites the client to come back.

The caller gets a 500, which reads as our internal error, when the honest answer is 409 (a turn is in progress) or a retry. Observed as 'assert 500 in (200, 202)' in test_session_not_found_errors.

FIX: _awaiting_user and the presence of _suspended must not be able to disagree -- either clear the flag when the trajectory is consumed, or treat 'awaiting but nothing suspended' as a recoverable state rather than a RuntimeError. The bare RuntimeError is also worth replacing with something the transport layer can map to a status.
notes:
Implemented: NoSuspendedAgentStateError (react.py) raised when resume has no trajectory; WEC._resume_agent_message checks export_suspended() before LLM work; turns._run_turn/run_owned_turn set http_status_on_error=409; _turn_json_response maps it to HTTP 409. Verified: test_clear_suspension_drops_stash, test_awaiting_user_without_suspended_raises_conflict, test_invoke_agent_while_awaiting_without_suspended_is_409.

OPEN QUESTION for user: on desync we return 409 but do NOT clear _awaiting_user / pending blob. Client stays stuck until cancel_pending/new_conversation. Alternative: clear desynced state when raising so a retry can start a fresh turn. Left uncleared to avoid inventing recovery policy.
close_reason: Closed

title: FastAPI test batch is flaky: live-LLM turns can legitimately return 202
description:
MEASURED, not suspected. Six runs of the seven FastAPI test files produced FOUR DIFFERENT failing test names: test_leading_slash_stripping, test_session_not_found_errors, test_post_feedback_endpoint, test_session_data_extracts_user_id_from_token, test_traces_include_raw_command. tests/test_fastapi_service.py passes 31/31 in ISOLATION every attempt.

CAUSE: these are live-LLM paths with 10-60s turn timeouts. /invoke_* is wait-or-defer, so a turn that does not finish inside the window correctly returns 202 -- and the assertions that follow depend on a completed turn. Under batch load, more turns miss their window. It is the same class as fix-wi3, which fixed ONE test by accepting {200, 202}; this is the pattern across the file.

WHY IT MATTERS BEYOND THE NOISE: four different names across six runs means anyone reading a CI failure here is told a different lie each time. The failing test name carries no information about the cause, which is the worst property a flaky test can have -- it sends the reader to the wrong file.

DO: audit the file for assertions that depend on a turn completing, and either accept the deferred outcome where the turn is incidental setup (as fix-wi3 did) or drive those paths deterministically instead of through a live provider. Prefer the second where the turn IS the subject.
notes:
CAUSE CORRECTED 2026-08-08 -- the mechanism on file is wrong, and acting on it would have fixed nothing.

I filed this as 'live-LLM turns can legitimately return 202 while later assertions assume completion'. That is not what is happening. test_session_not_found_errors is ALREADY 202-tolerant (commit 0a5a2c4 made it so, with a comment saying why) and it still failed -- on 'assert 500 in (200, 202)'. A 500, not a deferral.

THE REAL MECHANISM, two parts:

1. CROSS-RUN STATE POLLUTION. The suite leaves ___workflow_contexts/channel_session_state/nonexistent_user.pending.json in the working tree -- VERIFIED PRESENT: 5954 bytes, awaiting_user=true, carrying a full ReAct trajectory. It is gitignored (.gitignore:2 '___workflow_contexts*'), so it never shows in git status and persists indefinitely. The NEXT run restores it during session creation. That is a hidden cross-run dependency in a suite otherwise assumed hermetic, and it explains the signature nobody could explain: six runs producing FOUR DIFFERENT failing test names, because what fails depends on state the previous run left.

2. A SERVER-SIDE STATE DESYNC, which is the 500. workflow_execution_context.py:790-792 routes any message into _resume_agent_message whenever _awaiting_user is true, and react.py:182 raises a bare RuntimeError('No suspended ReAct state to resume') when _suspended is None. Restoration itself is correct -- apply_serialized_state calls _ensure_agent_initialized() then import_suspended(react_blob) -- so the desync arises afterwards, when a deferred (202) agent turn consumes _suspended while _awaiting_user is still set and the next request re-enters the resume branch.

WHY THIS MATTERS BEYOND THE TESTS: part 2 has a production analogue. A client mixing /invoke_agent and /invoke_assistant on a channel awaiting user input, or any second request arriving while a deferred agent turn is in flight, gets a 500 rather than a clean 409 or a retry. Filed separately.

REVISED SCOPE for this issue: make the suite hermetic -- the pending-state directory must not survive a run. The 202-tolerance work already done is fine and should stay, but it was treating a symptom.
Implemented hermetic SPEEDDICT for all FastAPI app_module fixtures via tests/fastapi_hermetic.py (tmp_path override + restore), matching checkpoint_integration. Removed leaked nonexistent_user.pending.json. Verified: after test_session_not_found_errors + topology_b, ___workflow_contexts/channel_session_state/ stays empty.
close_reason: Closed

title: Mitigate diskcache pickle RCE (CVE-2025-69872) — no upstream patch
description:
## Finding
- Locked: diskcache==5.6.3 (transitive via dspy); PyPI latest still 5.6.3
- Advisory: CVE-2025-69872 / GHSA-w8v5-vhqr-4h9v — default pickle serialization; attacker with write access to the cache directory gets RCE when the app reads cache. **No patched release** (pip-audit fix_versions: none).

## Reachability in fastWorkflow
- `run_fastapi_mcp` applies `dspy.configure_cache(enable_disk_cache=False, ...)` in `server_memory.py` (design decision in `docs/fastworkflow_memory_bounds_design.md`: disk cache off partly because pickle + 30GB default).
- CLI / other entrypoints may still leave DSPy disk cache enabled (`dspy_cache_utils.reset_dspy_cache_settings` re-enables it).
- Exploit requires filesystem write to the cache dir (local privilege / shared volume), not remote unauthenticated.

## Recommendation
1. **Do not expect a version bump** until upstream ships a non-pickle default or safe serializer.
2. Keep server disk-cache-off as the hard invariant; add a regression test if missing.
3. Consider disabling disk cache by default in CLI too, or document that cache dirs must be attacker-inaccessible.
4. Optional: pin a note / Dependabot dismiss with "risk accepted / mitigated" once security-tab access exists.
5. Watch dspy for `restrict_pickle=True` or alternate cache backends.

## Effort
Medium (policy + docs/tests; no clean package bump).
notes: Mitigated (no upstream patch): init() disables DSPy disk cache while preserving memory_max_entries; dspy_cache_utils.reset keeps disk off; server_memory already disk-off. pip-audit still reports diskcache==5.6.3 with fix=NONE.
close_reason: Closed

title: Escalation coverage floor counts core commands asymmetrically by visit order
description:
DISCOVERED FROM fix-k0i.34, which was scoped to SURFACING the budget numbers (done). This is the second half the surfacing made visible.

The coverage floor counts core commands differently depending on whether a context was first visited as an ANCESTOR (while computing another context's escalation candidates) or as a TRAINEE (being trained itself). The two paths do not agree on whether core commands count toward the floor.

CONSEQUENCE: when the floor binds, RENAMING A CONTEXT can change a SIBLING's training data -- because renaming changes alphabetical visit order, which changes which path visited it first. That is a spooky-action-at-a-distance defect: an author renames one context and a different context's model changes, with nothing in the diff to explain it.

Now diagnosable rather than invisible: fix-k0i.34 added the ESCALATION BUDGET table to the training report, so selected rows / own rows / budget / coverage floor are printed per context. Two runs that differ only by a rename can be diffed on those numbers.

FIX: in class_balance.py and the cache-fill in model_pipeline_training.py, make the count independent of visit order -- decide once whether core commands count toward the floor and apply it on both paths. Add a test that trains two workflows differing only by a context rename and asserts the sibling's selected escalation rows are identical.
close_reason:
Fixed, and the issue's own description was corrected in the process.

WHERE THEY DISAGREED: one shared dict, context_utterance_cache, written by two functions with different command sets. cache_ancestor_utterances used context_model.commands(), which EXCLUDES core commands (they are unioned in separately by command_routing.build). The trainee fill used crd.contexts[ctx] | core_cmds, which INCLUDES them. The single consumer, coverage_floor_of over group_ancestor_utterances, just counts cache entries, so the floor was whatever the first visitor happened to write.

CORRECTION TO THE ISSUE: it claimed renaming a context changes a SIBLING's training data. It cannot -- the trainee fill uses setdefault, so a context's entry is REPAIRED the moment that context is trained. The reachable case is ancestor -> descendant, and it hits every descendant at once. Sharper than stated, and in a different place than stated.

RESOLUTION: core commands count toward the floor on NEITHER path. Three reasons in order of weight: a core command is a label in every context so it is never an escalation target and has no coverage requirement to satisfy; every one of its rows is already local, so exclude removes them all and the coverage pass provably cannot deliver the row the floor claims -- the floor was making a promise the selection could not keep; and those rows are already inside own_row_count, so a row cannot be both the local data the ratio bounds and the ancestor data it is bounded against. Counting them would also have been symmetric but inflates the budget by 4 per ancestor context, a fitted constant the derivation does not justify.

Enforced at the SINGLE DERIVATION POINT (group_ancestor_utterances gained skip_commands) rather than by making both writers agree, so a future third writer is covered automatically. Matching is on the exact cache key, not the bare label -- bare-label matching would also silence a workflow command that merely shares a simple name with a core one.

MUTATION EVIDENCE, on real training rows rather than a reported number: with the asymmetry restored, Leaf selects 42 rows vs 38 across a single rename (floor 42 vs 38, raw candidates 132 vs 108) and picks up five extra inventory rows the renamed run does not. Its sibling Mint moves identically -- one rename, two other contexts' models changed. Fixed: both 31. On the real messaging_app_4, User's floor 9 vs 5 and raw 31 vs 7 became 5 and 7. 4 of 5 tests fail under the mutation; the fifth guards class_balance directly and is unaffected by the call site by design.

5 new tests, 8.2s, no LLM and no training -- the cheap deterministic shape asked for. Verified: skip_commands is at one derivation point and matches on exact cache key.

title: test_session_not_found_errors is latency-flaky against a real LLM
description:
tests/test_fastapi_service.py::test_session_not_found_errors posts to /invoke_agent with timeout_seconds=10 and asserts status 200. /invoke_agent is wait-or-defer: if the agent turn does not finish inside the wait window the endpoint correctly returns 202, so the assertion fails whenever the provider is slower than 10 seconds.

Measured 2026-08-06 on an unchanged tree, three consecutive isolated runs: pass in 12.4s, fail in 27.6s, fail in 30.7s. It also failed once in a full-suite run before any Release B work and passed in the next full-suite run, so this is provider latency, not a code regression.

The test is asserting the wrong thing for what it is named after. Its subject is "valid JWT for a channel with no session", i.e. the 404/500 behaviour of /perform_action; the two /invoke_* calls before it are incidental setup that happen to make real LLM calls.

Options, in preference order:
1. Assert on the set {200, 202} for the two /invoke_* calls, since both are correct outcomes of wait-or-defer and neither is what the test is checking. Smallest change, keeps all coverage.
2. Raise timeout_seconds so the wait window is comfortably above provider latency. Makes the suite slower and only moves the flake threshold.
3. Split the test so the session-not-found assertions do not depend on an agent turn at all.

Do NOT weaken this by deleting or skipping it - testing rules require explicit approval to remove coverage, and the /perform_action 500 assertion is genuine coverage worth keeping.
close_reason: Fixed by option 1 from the issue. The two /invoke_* calls now assert status in (200, 202) instead of == 200. They are incidental setup, not the subject: the test is about a valid JWT for a channel with no session, and /invoke_* is wait-or-defer, so 202 is a correct outcome whenever the provider is slower than the 10s wait window. The genuine coverage -- the /perform_action 500 assertion -- is untouched, and nothing was skipped or deleted. Verified: three isolated runs at 10.0s, 19.0s and 15.2s wall, all passing, spanning the window that previously produced pass 12.4s / fail 27.6s / fail 30.7s. Full suite 1303 passed, 14 skipped, 0 failed.

title: Implement serialization hooks for the five pinned bundled workflows
description:
Release B. Adjudicated 2026-08-05 (decision 18, re-evaluated under the modified decision 25). BLOCKED on fix-qyz: the hook mechanism must be designed and approved first.

Five bundled workflows assign a live command-context object and are therefore pinned - their sessions can never be evicted, and today they silently LOSE that context if they are evicted (measured; see fix-3vy). The decision is to make the bound unconditional across the bundled set by implementing the serialization hook for all five, not just the scaffold.

TARGETS (census from memory-bounds design section 1.4, corrected):
1. fastworkflow/examples/simple_workflow_template - _commands/startup.py:12 assigns a WorkItem tree as root context. Pins from the first turn. HIGHEST VALUE: this is the scaffold new workflows are copied from, so its hook doubles as the worked example every author starts from. Get this one right first and let the other four follow its shape.
2. fastworkflow/examples/messaging_app_2 - _commands/startup.py:42, root context, pins from the first turn.
3. tests/todo_list_workflow - _commands/startup.py:12 assigns TodoListManager. Pins from the first turn. Also the natural integration-test subject, since fix-3vy's reproduction already drives it.
4. fastworkflow/examples/messaging_app_4 - _commands/set_root_context.py:15. Pins only once set_root_context runs, so it exercises the "becomes pinned mid-session" path.
5. fastworkflow/examples/messaging_app_3 - _commands/initialize_user.py:46 assigns workflow.current_command_context (not root). Exercises the current-context-only path.

KNOWN DIFFICULTY - do not assume a to_dict one-liner. The simple_workflow_template WorkItem tree (application/workitem.py) holds: _parent back-references, so the object graph is CYCLIC; _child_pos, a Dict[WorkItem, int] keyed by object IDENTITY; and a shared _workflow_schema reference. WorkflowSchema already has to_dict/from_dict/to_json_file/from_json_file (workitem.py:150, :167, :241, :247), so the schema half exists; the live-tree half does not. A correct hook must rebuild the tree and re-establish both the parent links and the identity-keyed positions. Design section 11.1 states the rule this has to satisfy: identity-preserving structures either round-trip with identity preserved, or the session pins.

ACCEPTANCE:
- Each of the five round-trips through evict + rehydrate with the command context restored, verified by an integration test in the shape of fix-3vy's reproduction (assert root and current context survive, not merely that no exception was raised).
- Integration tests only, real workflows, no mocks; never train in or delete fastworkflow/examples/*/___command_info.
- A workflow that has NOT implemented the hook still pins and still warns (that behaviour belongs to fix-qyz; this issue must not weaken it).
close_reason: Serialization hooks for the five pinned bundled workflows.
