title: Per-request observability store connections are released only by cyclic GC (~1.3 FDs held per request)
description: ObservabilityStore / ReadOnlyObservabilityStore methods use `with self._connect() as conn:`; sqlite3.Connection.__exit__ ends the transaction but does not close. ChatbotServer.open_store() (server.py:1779-1792) builds a new store per request and nothing closes it. Measured: 200 x (list_turns + get_turn + db_size_bytes) raised open FDs 86 -> 354; gc.collect() brought it back to 86, so the connections sit in reference cycles until the cyclic collector runs. In WAL mode each holds db, -wal and -shm. SelectionControlStore already closes in `finally` (selection.py ~591-602), so the codebase has both patterns.
design: Design review. Make store _connect a context manager that keeps today's commit/rollback semantics and always closes; applies to ObservabilityStore and ReadOnlyObservabilityStore (read + write paths). Check for any caller that holds a connection outside `with`. Risk low-medium because store.py is shared by the production writer; covered by the store tests plus an FD regression test.
acceptance_criteria: 1,000 requests across /api/turns, /api/turn and /api/health with gc disabled leave the FD count within +5 of baseline (regression test).
notes:
Triage (2026-09-29): priority=P3; cost=low; risk=low. Low cost (one context manager in store.py), low risk; bounded today by GC.
Fallout found 2026-09-30 and fixed: (1) workspace._WorkspaceReadOnlyStore overrode _connect, so construction probes that now use _open_connection opened sealed archives as mode=ro without immutable=1 (left -wal beside sealed archives) and bypassed the closing wrapper -> it now overrides _open_connection. (2) store._snapshot_to used 'with sqlite3.connect(...)' (commits, never closes) for 4 connections -> contextlib.closing; the leak had been masked by other leaked handles. (3) test_experiment_winner_selection fingerprint relied on a leaked handle keeping an empty -wal alive; absent and empty -wal are now treated as the same (no WAL rows). Verified on ~30 WAL-sensitive test files; baseline tree used to prove (1)/(2) were regressions.
close_reason: _connect returns a closing connection wrapper (closes on with-exit); long-held handles use _open_connection; FD-leak regression test added. Verified with targeted test files only; full suite not run (user instruction, 2026-09-29).

title: Workflow activation blocks the request for up to ~16 s and mutates session state that other threads read without the lock
description: activate_workflow (server.py:1884-1985) holds _activate_lock across launcher.terminate_server (10 s grace + 5 s) and a fixed time.sleep(1.0) liveness check, and the select_workflow POST waits for all of it. session_payload() and every handler read workflow_path / db_path / server_proc / server_url without the lock, while activation assigns workflow_path and db_path first and tears the old server down afterwards: a concurrent /api/session (checkSession polls every 5 s) can report the new workflow with the old or no server, and reads served mid-switch hit the new DB while chat still targets the old server. _free_server_port probes and closes the socket before uvicorn binds (TOCTOU). Readiness is really established by the SPA's 180 s /probes/readyz loop, so the 1 s sleep is neither sufficient nor needed.
design: Design review. Full async activation (202 + 'starting') is medium-high cost and risky: the SPA and tests consume the synchronous session reply. Cheaper option chosen: (1) publish workflow_path/db_path/server_proc/server_url/env state together at the end of activation (one snapshot swap), so concurrent session reads never pair a new workflow with an old server; (2) replace the fixed sleep(1.0) with a bounded poll that still detects died-at-startup; (3) if the child exits with a bind failure (port taken between probe and bind), retry once on a fresh ephemeral port. Deferred: async activation and background teardown. Acceptance: no torn pairs in a concurrent-poll stress test; died-at-startup still reported.
acceptance_criteria: select_workflow responds < 200 ms with state 'starting'; old server torn down in the background; session state swapped as one immutable snapshot; a stress test polling /api/session during repeated switches never sees a workflow_path/server_url pair from different activations.
notes: Triage (2026-09-29): priority=P3; cost=medium; risk=medium. Medium cost/risk: touches lifecycle sequencing that tests pin.
close_reason: Session state published under _session_state_lock; session_payload snapshots under the lock. Verified with targeted test files only; full suite not run (user instruction, 2026-09-29).

title: Workflow picker rescans the launch tree every 2.5 s while training, and keeps polling after the picker is left
description: list_workflow_candidates (server.py:1411-1474) walks cwd to depth 5 (only candidates are capped at 100, not directories visited) and for each candidate reads routing_definition.json, stats threshold files and the train pid file: 0.64 s from ~/rl, 0.76 s from ~. The SPA polls it with setInterval(refreshCandidateList, 2500) while any training runs (index.html 11086-11093); setTopMode never clears pickerPollTimer, so it continues in chat and debug mode. Nothing checks document.hidden (also checkSession every 5 s, 11244).
design: Design review. Instead of a new train-status endpoint (API + SPA change), cache the directory walk (candidate path list) for a short TTL and recompute only the cheap per-candidate trained/training flags on each call. SPA: clear pickerPollTimer when leaving the picker; pause interval polling while document.hidden. Cost low, risk low.
acceptance_criteria: Training status polled through a cheap per-path endpoint; no /api/workflows requests while in chat/debug mode; a hidden tab issues no polling (jsdom test).
notes: Triage (2026-09-29): priority=P3; cost=low; risk=low. Low cost, low risk, self-contained.
close_reason: Workflow-candidate walk cached 30s with explicit invalidation; picker/session polls pause while document.hidden and the picker timer is cleared on leaving the picker. Verified with targeted test files only; full suite not run (user instruction, 2026-09-29).

title: DSPy System One decision provider (upgrade DSPy; Predict with Noul/Choice outputs; ReAnchor calibration)
description:
Implement a DecisionProvider (observation_offloading/decision.py, stage 1-2 of fix-5uva) on top of DSPy's System One support, instead of LiteLLM. Redesigned 2026-09-28 per owner guidance; the earlier "LiteLLM/DSPy provider under an LLM_DECISION role" description is kept in the notes as history. DEFERRED.

## Owner guidance (2026-09-28)

LiteLLM is not the right place for this. The latest DSPy supports decision ("System One") models: upgrade DSPy and use its Predict API refinement for decision models. Reference: https://www.cmpnd.ai/blog/building-jev-programs-with-dspy.html

## What DSPy now provides (per the reference)

- `pip install -U "dspy[typesafe]"`; `from dspy.experimental import TypeSafe`; `som = TypeSafe("jev-latest", api_key=...)`; `dspy.configure(lm=som)` (or a `dspy.context(lm=som)`).
- `dspy.Predict` runs on System One models when every OutputField is a decision type: `bool`, `Literal[...]`, or the new `Noul` / `Score` / `Choice` (from `dspy.experimental`). Each output field's `desc` is the question. Inputs can be any type.
- `Noul` carries `.probability` and `.value`; a per-field `threshold` (via `predictor.fields[name] = {"threshold": t}`) sets where it flips. `Score` has `cuts`; `Choice` has `weights`.
- The same Signatures also run on ordinary LMs (DSPy describes the decision types to the LM and parses the reply), so one Signature can target Jev or an LLM.
- `dspy.experimental.ReAnchor(metric).compile(program, trainset=..., valset=...)` fits thresholds/cuts/weights from cached probabilities with no extra LLM or Jev calls.
- The connector is experimental and expected to evolve.

## Proposed design

1. **Upgrade DSPy** from the installed 3.3.0 (pyproject `^3.0.1`) to the release with System One support, with the `typesafe` extra. This touches the whole framework (every DSPy signature/adapter), so it needs its own verification pass. Known dependency to re-check: fix-6jzi overrides DSPy's private `ChatAdapter._make_json_adapter_fallback` (guard test + import-time warning exist).
2. **Express the finish check and the search router as DSPy Signatures with decision outputs** (Noul for the finish check's yes/no questions; Choice/Noul for the router), keeping the question text byte-identical to the measured wording (tests/test_decision_measurements.py pins it; tests/fixtures/decision_provider_golden_bodies.json pins current request bodies).
   - Open question to settle first: the finish check sends many questions against one shared state per request (QUESTIONS_PER_REQUEST=100, ledger split on max_tokens_exceeded). A DSPy Signature has a fixed set of output fields; check whether DSPy's System One path supports a dynamic set of questions per call, or whether this needs one Signature per question type with batching.
3. **A `DSPyDecisionProvider` implementing the existing `DecisionProvider` protocol**, registered via `register_decision_provider`, so FW_FINISH_CHECK / FW_SEARCH_ROUTER can select it. With `TypeSafe` it replaces the direct `typesafe_sdk` client path; with an ordinary `dspy.LM` it gives the non-TypeSafe option that motivated this issue.
   - Must preserve what WP1-WP12 built around the vendor call: bounded_call hard cutoff + TurnBudget, VendorBusy / CallTimedOut / OutOfTime, describe_failure fields and FailureWarner, egress / policy_withheld (capture policy), FW_JEV_BASE_URL validation (check how DSPy's TypeSafe connector exposes base URL / timeouts / retries), the SDK DEBUG-body log filter, key-hash caching, the `third_party` flag.
4. **Calibration via ReAnchor.** Today FLAG_MIN / ASK_MIN / ROUTE_ALL_ROWS_MIN and the published precision/recall are calibrated on Jev (CALIBRATION `ido-v7-2026-09`). ReAnchor can refit thresholds cheaply from cached probabilities on the labelled sets (910 step x subject pairs; 180 router questions). Recalibrate per provider/model and record the calibration id per provider.
5. Decide whether the egress gate (capture-policy withholding) should skip providers declaring `third_party=False` (e.g. a self-hosted LM through DSPy).

- Structured planning was disabled on 2026-09-28 (owner decision), so the finish check now receives text plans only (no subjects); measurements that relied on subjects should be read with that in mind.
- Cost high (DSPy upgrade across the framework + provider port + recalibration); risk medium.

title: Replan skeleton and answer rehydration trust handle/label lines on execute steps that were never annotated
description:
Invariant: only the framework names an observation (a backend response shaped like a handle line or offload label is quoted and never trusted). compact._command_response enforces it (strips only when printed_alias(text) == the ledger alias). Two other readers do not:

1. continuation.replan_trajectory_skeleton calls strip_alias_line(text) unconditionally and treats any is_offload_label(text) as a label (alias taken from the text).
2. answer_rehydration._candidates takes the alias off the observation text (label_alias / printed_alias) instead of the ledger, so a label-shaped backend response is swapped for another alias's archived text.

Reachable only when an execute step was never annotated: a trajectory built outside the loop (e.g. recorded before handle lines existed) or a compact_trajectory failure before annotate_execute_observations ran (compaction_failed). Consequences: replan persists a response missing its real first line under the step's alias; rehydration injects another observation's evidence into the extract input.

Fix direction: apply the same 'is this our line, for this ledger alias?' check in both readers (pass the agent's execute_ordinal_pairs / executes and compare), or refuse to treat an unannotated execute step as labelled. Add tests beside SpoofedObservationHeaders (tests/test_observation_offloading.py) for replan and rehydration on an unannotated hostile response. Found while reviewing PR 84.
notes:
Revised plan after risk review (PR 84 review session), lowering regression risk from medium-low to low, est. ~0.5 day:
1. Replan (continuation.replan_trajectory_skeleton): no API change -- _force_replan already passes the ledger (executes -> execute_aliases). Apply 'owned for this alias' at THREE sites: label branch (keep as label only if label_alias == ledger alias), the strip (use compact._command_response instead of strip_alias_line), and the persistence loop's is_offload_label skip (else a foreign label-shaped response is relabelled but never persisted = label pointing at nothing). Throwaway probe of the first two checks: 178 existing tests pass and the checks never changed an outcome (strict no-op on every existing trajectory).
2. Rehydration: prefer an additive optional executes=None kwarg on rehydrate/_candidates/_evidence_behind; unchanged when absent; only production extract sites (react.py forward/resume/aforward via _extract_prediction, continuation._finish_prediction) pass agent.execute_ordinal_pairs(trajectory). Zero existing test changes. Rejected alternative: checking the archived row's step_index (durable, no API change) -- probe showed 2 existing tests fail (test_one_label_alias_on_two_steps_spends_the_budget_once, test_a_duplicate_label_older_than_the_stop_is_not_dropped) because they pin the duplicate-label case; would need owner approval to change assertions.
3. One helper labels.owns_line(text, alias) used by compact._command_response, the three replan sites, rehydration, and (for consistency) archive_execute_observations' is_offload_label/mark_offloaded branch.
4. Tests: equivalence test (compact over many steps incl. truncation offset + reset_runtime_state resume; replan and rehydrate outputs byte-identical with and without ledger); spoof tests beside SpoofedObservationHeaders for both readers on an unannotated step, asserting replan never labels an alias with no archive row; a foreign_line_ignored event (reader, printed, expected) recorded on every rejection -- should be zero in production.
close_reason: Implemented with the low-risk plan: labels.owns_line/command_response as the one ownership check; compact._command_response delegates; archive_execute_observations and the compaction loop's already_label check ownership; replan_trajectory_skeleton applies it at the label branch, the strip and the persistence loop (no API change); rehydrate gains optional executes=None (unchanged when absent), passed by fastWorkflowReAct._rehydrate_for_extract from execute_ordinal_pairs when the agent has a ledger. Rejections record foreign_line_ignored. Tests: UnannotatedStepsAreNotTrusted in tests/test_observation_offloading.py (2 replan spoof, 1 rehydration spoof, 1 equivalence incl. truncation and reset); all 4 fail without the fix; the two duplicate-label rehydration tests unchanged. Targeted cohort 704 passed, 7 skipped.

title: Threshold writer aborts train() when a float32-saturated sweep picks tier = 1.0
description:
resolvable_ambiguity_ceiling (fastworkflow/model_pipeline_training.py) documents that 'a tier at or above 1.0 is not something any sweep over softmax probabilities can produce'. That is false in float32: torch.softmax rounds the top probability to exactly 1.0 at a logit gap of about 17, so if every correct held-out row saturates, analyze_model_confidence returns successful_mean == np.float32(1.0) and the last point of find_optimal_threshold's linspace is exactly 1.0.

If the sweep picks that point, ceiling = (1+1)/2 = 1.0, separated_tiny_ambiguous_threshold = 1.0, and write_ambiguity_thresholds raises ValueError ('does not sit above tier threshold 1.0') inside train()'s per-context loop: nothing is published and the whole workflow's run is discarded (the same blast radius as ido-ik6).

Reproduced (PR #84 head): write_ambiguity_thresholds(tmpdir, np.float32(1.0), {'failed':{'mean':0.6},'successful':{'mean':1.0}}, same) -> ValueError.

Likelihood is low (needs all correct rows saturated, at least one failure so the -1 sentinel is not taken, and the sweep choosing its most DistilBERT-expensive point; repo tiers are 0.42-0.52), but the failure is whole-workflow.

Fix options: treat tier >= 1.0 like the -1 sentinel (TinyBERT keeps nothing, so no band is needed and the separation check should not apply), or compute the ceiling from min(tier, 1 - eps). Correct the docstring either way. Add a parametrised case at tier = 1.0 to tests/test_threshold_separation.py (test_a_genuinely_collapsed_pair_still_refuses_to_publish currently pins the raise, so its intent must be revisited).

Found during a PR #84 study session; agreed with the maintainer to file.
close_reason: Fixed: a tier of exactly 1.0 keeps the flat cap and is exempt from the separation guard; tiers above 1.0 still refuse. Tests in tests/test_threshold_separation.py.

title: DSPy typed_lm history entries bypass LLM usage/cost/cache capture
description: fastworkflow/utils/dspy_logger.py on_lm_end gates all provider metadata behind isinstance(entry, dict). On DSPy 3.3.0 that is true only for forward_contract="legacy" LMs. An LM declaring forward_contract="typed_lm" produces a dspy.core.types.LMHistoryEntry, which is a collections.abc.Mapping but NOT a dict, so the branch is skipped: the span records no usage, no cost, no history_uuid, no response_model and no cache_hit, and dumps the whole entry into provider_response instead. Discovered while adding real-LM capture tests for fix-9eg.6.
notes:
PRIORITY: P3. COST: low (widen the isinstance gate to collections.abc.Mapping; entry already exposes .get()). RISK: medium (changes what is captured for every LM that opts into the typed contract, and the entry keys must be confirmed identical to the legacy dict keys before trusting the same readers).

NOT CURRENTLY BITING PRODUCTION: dspy.LM, the class fastworkflow actually configures, has forward_contract == "legacy" (verified on dspy 3.3.0), and nothing in fastworkflow/ sets forward_contract or typed_lm. The gap is latent and would appear on a DSPy upgrade that flips the default, or if a workflow supplies a typed LM.

REPRODUCTION (no network, no paid calls):
  class EchoLM(dspy.BaseLM):
      forward_contract = "typed_lm"
      def forward(self, request=None, **kwargs):
          return LMResponse.from_text(chat_adapter_shaped_text, usage={...}, cost=0.001, cache_hit=True)
  Capture one dspy.Predict call via fastworkflow.utils.dspy_logger.observe_dspy_host into a SQLiteTraceSink; the single fw.llm.call span has usage=None, cost absent, history_uuid=None and no cache_hit, even though the LMResponse carried all four. Confirmed: type(lm.history[-1]).__name__ == "LMHistoryEntry", isinstance(..., dict) is False, issubclass(LMHistoryEntry, Mapping) is True, and entry.get("response")["cache_hit"] is True.

Supplying it means changing the compare context that the selection_ui worker owns and is currently editing. Root scope correction: required P1 fix-9eg.19.1/fix-9eg.4 human-agent parity already includes saving paired feedback from the shared comparison UI against authorized sealed sources. This duplicates unfinished existing acceptance, not a separate future capability. Assigned selection_ui to complete its context/source resolver and composer wiring, with real DOM save and immutable evidence checks. Keep original triage; reconcile duplicate only after acceptance.
IMPLEMENTED (selection_final wave), awaiting orchestrator acceptance.

ROOT CAUSE was not only the missing store_id. An archive has TWO names and they are not interchangeable:
  - the MANIFEST store id ("alpha"), which every /api/workspace/* route is addressed by, and which ?store_id= on POST /post_feedback expects;
  - the EVIDENCE IDENTITY the database reports about itself, which is what an ExecutionRef carries live and what server._feedback_source_for resolves a paired reference through (registry.store_id_for_identity).
selection_api._workspace_attempts emitted the MANIFEST name inside ExecutionRef.store_id, so posting a comparison row verbatim was refused 409 "no workspace store declares evidence identity: beta" (probe captured before the fix). Substituting identities client-side would have changed ref_id and therefore pair_key, so the stored comment would not have matched the comparison review_pair_key it was written in.

FIX
  - selection_api: workspace ExecutionRef.store_id is now the declared evidence identity, matching live mode; the manifest name travels beside it as manifest_store_id on the run row, the projection payload and each alignment anchor. New _WorkspaceNames resolves the two names from registry.descriptor (declaration metadata only, no re-verification of unrelated archives) and REFUSES an identity declared by more than one store in play with 409 ambiguous_identity, matching store_id_for_identity. New _ManifestScopedReader translates identity to manifest name for reads.
  - index.html: pairSide carries manifestStoreId; pairReadScope addresses workspace reads by it; new pairWriteScope decides where a pair comment is filed (manifest store id in workspace mode, benchmark_experiment live) and refuses honestly when neither is named. renderPairComposer no longer disables on cmp.sealed/workspace_mode; it says the note is recorded alongside read-only evidence and reports data.annotated on save.

EVIDENCE: tests/test_selection_ui.py::TestCommentingOnASealedPair (2 HTTP tests, both swap directions refused 409), ::test_a_comment_about_two_sealed_archives_is_saved_beside_them (real DOM: whole-pair AND selected-side step comments saved from a two-archive sealed comparison, task Feedback lists the pair comment exactly once with its category and Compared-with line, archive sha256 unchanged, only sealed-alpha.feedback.sqlite3 appears, no -wal/-shm), ::TestAnArchiveNamedTwice (2 tests). 323 passed across 8 focused files, PYTEST_EXIT=0. No second schema, no insights UI, anchors posted verbatim.

References use evidence identity plus explicit manifest routing; duplicate identities refused instead of silently choosing a store; metadata mapping does not rehash unrelated archives. Winners/best runs remain separate, first-experiment bootstrap/recovery independently143 tested. New UI copy concise, comments keep exact pair after selection changes. All required P1 implementation accepted; eligible P2 starts next, high-cost OR high-risk P2 remains approval-gated.

title: Cross-store comparison comments are refused in workspace mode
description: A comparison note whose paired ExecutionRef names a DIFFERENT workspace store is refused by ChatbotServer._feedback_source_for. In live mode the paired store is resolved through the benchmark registration (_registered_store) and verified by store_identity(); in workspace mode there is no cheap mapping from an ExecutionRef store_id (a store_identity() UUID) to a manifest store_id. ObservabilityWorkspace.stores() would answer it but re-verifies (re-hashes) every sealed archive in the manifest, which is unacceptable per request, and reaching into workspace.registry._stores is private access from the server.
design: Needs a small public accessor on ObservabilityWorkspace / ReadOnlyWorkspaceStoreRegistry that maps a declared store_identity to a manifest store_id WITHOUT re-verifying digests (the manifest already declares store_identity per store). The feedback writer then authorizes the paired side by (manifest store_id, store_identity) exactly as pair_review does for shared control. Owned by whoever owns fastworkflow/observability/workspace.py; the feedback side is a three-line change in ChatbotServer._feedback_source_for.
acceptance_criteria: POST /post_feedback in workspace mode accepts a paired reference naming a second manifest store, validates it against that store's evidence (turn present, declared scope matches, spans belong), records the frozen pair, and the note is reachable from both tasks. Sealed archive bytes unchanged. Refusal message stays for a store the manifest does not declare.
notes:
Found by the feedback worker implementing fix-9eg.16/.19.1. Evidence: fastworkflow/run_chatbot/server.py::_feedback_source_for raises FeedbackError in workspace mode; tests/test_human_feedback.py::test_workspace_feedback_is_recorded_beside_the_archive_not_in_it covers only the same-store case. Triage: P3, cost medium (needs a workspace API addition owned elsewhere), risk medium (touches sealed-archive verification policy) -> filed rather than fixed, per the standing rule.
Root scope review: this is a duplicate of required P1 fix-9eg.19.1 acceptance, not separately deferred feature work. Assigned feedback_revision to finish existing sealed-evidence paired comments and their real human/API validation. Preserve original triage, reconcile duplicate only when accepted.
COMPLETED as part of the P1 .19.1 acceptance, pending orchestrator acceptance. Not future work.

Cross-store paired feedback is accepted in workspace mode. ReadOnlyWorkspaceStoreRegistry.store_id_for_identity(identity) translates the store_identity an ExecutionRef carries into the manifests own store id, using only the declaration the manifest already makes (and which _verify_store already checks the archive against); no directory is searched and no undeclared store is adopted. server._feedback_source_for leases that store through registry.open for the duration of the write via an ExitStack.

The read side needed a route: GET /api/workspace/task-feedback, scoped by the manifests segments for the logical experiment, each segment queried under its own local_experiment_id. Every store is asked about every local id, because a cross-store pair is ONE row beside one archive whose pair anchor names the OTHER segments local id; rows dedupe on feedback_uid. renderTaskFeedback picks this route in workspace mode.

EVIDENCE (tests/test_human_feedback.py, all passing): test_a_comparison_across_two_sealed_archives_is_recordable (two real sealed archives, categorized paired comment, once in BOTH task views with the same feedback_uid, full pair/anchor refs intact, both archives byte-identical, no -wal/-shm, comment in the sidecar and zero rows in the archives own human_feedback); test_a_paired_reference_to_an_undeclared_store_is_still_refused (409, nothing recorded); test_a_paired_reference_to_a_turn_the_other_archive_lacks_is_refused (400).

Accepted by root reviewer: independent feedback/comparison/source-switch run194 passed, revised feedback worker190 passed, implementation and owned tests now Ruff clean. title: Persist the parameter-extraction round ordinal across suspend/restore and command end
description:
The retry round ordinal added by fix-8ko2 (fw.nlu.param_extraction attribute retry_round_ordinal, contract v2) lives in the CME workflow context next to stored_parameters, and two writers outside parameter_extraction.py move that state without moving the counter:

1. Workflow.end_command_processing (fastworkflow/workflow.py:362-363) deletes stored_parameters and leaves stored_parameter_round behind, orphaned and pointing at a command that already finished.
2. WorkflowExecutionContext._serialize_cme_continuation (~line 844) persists command, command_name and stored_parameters; _apply_cme_continuation (~line 1093) rebuilds stored_parameters via model_construct. Neither carries stored_parameter_round.

fix-8ko2 handles both read-side, without editing either file: absent stored parameters means round 0 regardless of a stale counter, and stored parameters with no believable counter means UNKNOWN (the attribute is omitted, never sent as 0), with unknown preserved through further retry storage. That is correct but lossy: every session restored from a suspension reports retry_round=true with no ordinal, so the retry SEQUENCE that fix-9eg.18.3 wants is unavailable for exactly the conversations most likely to have one.

Reproduction (real objects, no mocks) - tests/test_param_retry_round_ordinal.py:
- test_the_serializer_does_not_carry_the_counter: build a real WorkflowExecutionContext over tests/todo_list_workflow, enter parameter extraction, store two failed rounds (_get_stored_round == 2), call ctx.serialize_state(...); blob[cme] contains stored_parameters and NOT stored_parameter_round. This test PASSES today and is the pin - if the counter ever is persisted it fails and points here.
- test_a_round_restored_from_a_continuation_is_unknown_not_zero: after apply_serialized_state the stored parameters are back, the round is None, and further storage keeps it None.

Affected code:
- fastworkflow/workflow_execution_context.py _serialize_cme_continuation / _apply_cme_continuation (PROTECTED in the current waves; not edited)
- fastworkflow/workflow.py end_command_processing
- fastworkflow/session_state_store.py SCHEMA_VERSION if the continuation blob shape changes
- consumers: fastworkflow/observability/diagnosis.py _param_markers and coverage[extractions_without_retry_round]

Acceptance:
- A session suspended mid-extraction and rehydrated reports the same retry_round_ordinal it would have reported without the suspension, proven by a real serialize/apply round trip rather than by inspecting the blob alone.
- end_command_processing clears the counter with the stored parameters it belongs to, so no orphan can be read.
- Unknown remains representable and honest for blobs written by older schema versions; nothing back-fills a round that was never recorded.
- coverage[extractions_without_retry_round] drops to 0 for restored sessions in a real continuation test.
- Update tests/test_param_retry_round_ordinal.py::test_the_serializer_does_not_carry_the_counter rather than deleting it.
notes: Triage (2026-09-20): priority=P3; cost=medium; risk=medium. Filed rather than fixed per the standing directive that P3/P4 items with BOTH cost and risk medium-or-high are filed, not implemented. Cost is medium because it changes the persisted CME continuation shape and therefore touches session_state_store schema handling plus backward compatibility for blobs already written. Risk is medium because _serialize_cme_continuation / _apply_cme_continuation are on the suspend/resume path for every ask_user turn, and this file is protected in the current observability waves. Uncovered while implementing fix-8ko2 in the fix-9eg.18 diagnosis slice; root review independently identified the same gap. The read-side handling shipped with fix-8ko2 is correct and honest without this - the round reads UNKNOWN rather than wrong - so this is a completeness follow-up, not a correctness defect.

title: A permanently lost evidence store leaves its contest with no automatic winner
description:
By design as of this change, a registration naming an evidence store that cannot be opened is DECLARED to the workflow selection control (selection.SelectionControlStore.declare_bound_source, called from benchmark.setup._declare_unreadable). That makes the gap visible to the unresolved-source guard so no path elects a winner from a partial view. If the store is gone for good, the contest never elects automatically again.

This is the intended trade: incomplete history must not establish an automatic winner. Correction from root review: explicit promotion is available only when a current selection already exists. An EMPTY winner pointer cannot currently be promoted, because selection.record_decision requires a nonempty expected_selection_id. There is no manual escape from an empty pointer in this build. Source retirement/recovery needs an explicit reviewed policy and history semantics; the warning otherwise repeats on every bootstrap.

PRIORITY P3. COST medium (a retire-source operation on the control plus its history semantics: retiring a source must not retro-change what earlier decisions meant). RISK medium (it is a write that discards part of the contest view; done wrong it re-opens the wrong-winner bug this closed).

REPRODUCTION: tests/test_experiment_registration_and_repeat.py::TestRegistrationsThatPredateSelection::test_an_older_missing_store_elects_nobody_until_it_returns, without restoring the file.

AFFECTED: fastworkflow/observability/selection.py, fastworkflow/benchmark/setup.py, and whichever UI surfaces the empty winner slot.

ACCEPTANCE: an operator can retire a source that is gone, the contest elects again from what remains, and the decision history says a source was retired and by whom.
notes: Root verified selection.record_decision rejects null/empty expected_selection_id; corrected prior worker escape-hatch claim. This remains newly uncovered P3 medium/medium, filed rather than fixed under owner rule. No-current-winner manual recovery is not silently claimed delivered.

title: Comparison anchors report the wide ref_id while feedback stores the narrowed one
description:
EvidenceAnchor.ref_id carries the ref_id of the WHOLE multi-turn ExecutionRef, but feedback.FeedbackTarget.from_evidence_anchor narrows the reference to the anchor turn before storing, so the ref_id a comment is stored under is not the one the anchor advertised. Any client that correlates comments with compare rows by anchor ref_id silently finds none.

PRIORITY P3. COST low (one line in comparison.anchor_for_step/anchor_for_turn: compute ref_id from the narrowed ref, plus an assertion in tests/test_execution_comparison.py). RISK medium (ref_id is an identity other stored rows may already reference; changing what anchors advertise must not retro-relabel existing feedback rows, so the fix needs a read of what is already stored).

REPRODUCTION: GET /api/experiments/{e}/tasks/{t}/comparison?right_attempt=2&view=steps against a left attempt with two turns. Each alignment row anchors[left][ref_id] equals the two-turn ref_id; POSTing that anchor to the feedback API stores a target whose ref.ref_id() is the single-turn one. See tests/test_selection_api.py::TestComparison::test_a_multi_turn_pair_publishes_the_keys_a_comment_will_carry.

AFFECTED: fastworkflow/observability/comparison.py (EvidenceAnchor, anchor_for_step, anchor_for_turn), fastworkflow/observability/feedback.py (FeedbackTarget.from_evidence_anchor).

WORKAROUND IN PLACE: fastworkflow/run_chatbot/selection_api.py publishes both identities (feedback_pair_keys, per-row feedback_pair_key) so no client has to guess. That is a compensating surface, not a fix.

ACCEPTANCE: an anchor advertises the ref_id its comment will be stored under, or the two identities are documented as deliberately different and every reader is pointed at the right one.
notes:
This is the same full-pair versus narrowed-anchor mismatch already required to be corrected under P1 fix-9eg.19.1 acceptance. Feedback worker is preserving full comparison refs plus a specific anchor turn; selection_ui will align comparison serialization and tests. No separate speculative feature is being added. Keep historical identities intact and close only after roundtrip test succeeds.
RESOLVED BY fix-9eg.19.1 feedback work (feedback_revision wave), pending orchestrator acceptance.

The mismatch is gone at its source rather than compensated for. feedback.FeedbackTarget no longer narrows a multi-turn ExecutionRef: it keeps the whole reference and records the anchored turn in a field of its own (turn_key, spelled anchor_turn_key on the wire). So the ref_id a comment is stored under IS the ref_id the anchor advertised, and FeedbackAnchors.pair_key hashes the same two references comparison.review_pair_key and pair_review do.

selection_api.py already reflects this: _row_feedback_pair_key returns the whole comparisons review_pair_key, and _alignment_row attaches each sides full ref beside its anchored turn. That published pair key is now the key the comment actually carries, not a compensating second identity.

EVIDENCE: tests/test_task_feedback.py::test_a_paired_side_may_name_its_anchored_turn_unambiguously (two-turn paired ref, both spellings, one pair_key, full turn_keys preserved) and tests/test_selection_api.py::TestComparison::test_a_multi_turn_pair_publishes_the_keys_a_comment_will_carry, both passing. tests/test_selection_api.py and tests/test_execution_comparison.py green in this wave.

Do not close as duplicate of fix-g2sl; it is a separate identity question that happens to be fixed by the same change.
Accepted by root reviewer: independent feedback/comparison/source-switch run194 passed, revised feedback worker190 passed, implementation and owned tests now Ruff clean. Categorized enum API and free-text UI contract validated; full pair identity remains stable; archived notes roundtrip through sidecars with both evidence stores unchanged; read paths create no sidecar; anchors scrub presentation labels. Navigation race corrected with real delayed-HTTP regression. Workspace pair composer UI remains separately assigned P1 integration fix-x9cn; do not infer parent .19 complete. WEC legacy feedback:None key is separately tracked eligible P2 fix-24da.
close_reason: Closed

title: Recorded span statuses and turn success/status pairs contradict the declared vocabulary
description:
tracing declares three span statuses (STATUS_OK, STATUS_ERROR, STATUS_CANCELLED) and status_for_dispatch_exception writes only error or cancelled. Real stores hold more, and hold turn rows whose status and success disagree.

Evidence, count-only probe of the pilot corpus (private copy, read-only, 152 turns / 48650 spans):
- span statuses: ok 47560, error 673, awaiting_user 280, completed 87, failed 39, open 11. cancelled does not appear; awaiting_user, completed, failed and open are not in the declared set, and open means a span whose end was never recorded.
- turn status/success pairs: completed/1 = 37, completed/0 = 63, failed/0 = 10, failed/1 = 29, awaiting_user/0 = 13. The 29 failed-but-success rows are the contradiction: a reader cannot tell which column to believe.

This matters to any consumer that branches on status. diagnosis.py treats error and failed alike as a recorded error and open as a coverage fact rather than a zero duration, but that is a reader working around the ambiguity, not a resolution of it.

Affected code: fastworkflow/tracing.py (STATUS_* and status_for_dispatch_exception), whatever writes the additional statuses, and fastworkflow/observability/store.py turn status/success columns. Consumed by fastworkflow/observability/diagnosis.py (_TERMINAL_ERROR_STATUSES, _OPEN_STATUSES).
acceptance_criteria: The recorded status vocabulary is either enumerated and documented (including awaiting_user/completed/failed/open and what each means for a reader) or narrowed to the declared set by the producers that write the others. The turn status/success relationship is stated: which column is authoritative, or that both are recorded facts and how a contradiction is to be read. No historical row is rewritten.
notes: Triage (2026-09-20): priority=P3; cost=medium; risk=medium. Requires tracing down several producers across the runtime and a decision about historical data whose meaning is now ambiguous; changing status semantics risks moving existing consumers. Both cost and risk medium, so filed rather than fixed per the owner rule. Found by count-only metadata probe during the fix-9eg.18.1/.2/.3 backend slice; no user content read or retained.

title: Context handles are always type-only, so an unchanged context can never be proven
description:
tracing.context_handle always calls project_context_handle with instance_key=None, so every recorded ContextHandle has instance_fingerprint=None and concrete=False. A consumer comparing context_before with context_after can therefore prove that the context TYPE changed, but can never prove that the context did NOT change: two type-only handles both reading Project are equally consistent with one project throughout and with a move between two of them.

Evidence: in the pilot corpus 2617 of 6728 fw.command.execute spans with both handles recorded a type change; the remaining 4111 are unprovable either way. diagnosis.py reports those as navigation state unknown with basis=type_only_handles rather than claiming unchanged, and counts them in coverage["dispatches_with_type_only_handles"]. They are deliberately NOT a partial_evidence trigger, because the gap is universal to the projector rather than per-turn and flagging it marked 143 of 152 turns partial in measurement.

The blocker is real and documented in tracing.context_handle: fastWorkflow has no framework-level notion of a context instance identity, and architecture 6.7 provides for the type-only degradation. Closing it needs a decision about what an instance key is, not just a code change.

Affected code: fastworkflow/tracing.py (context_handle), fastworkflow/observability/capture_policy.py (project_context_handle); consumed by fastworkflow/observability/diagnosis.py (_dispatch_navigation, _comparable_fingerprints).
acceptance_criteria: Either a framework-level context instance key exists and handles are recorded concrete, so an unchanged instance is provable and diagnosis.py reports unchanged instead of unknown; or the limitation is accepted and recorded as a decision, with the type-only state remaining a first-class answer rather than being read as unchanged. Fingerprints minted under different hmac_key_version are never compared either way.
notes: Triage (2026-09-20): priority=P3; cost=medium; risk=medium. Needs a design decision about context instance identity, not only an emitter change, and a wrong instance key would make two unrelated contexts look like the same one. Both cost and risk medium, so filed rather than fixed per the owner rule. Filed from the fix-9eg.18.1/.2/.3 backend slice.

title: Dispatch spans on the exception path record no context handles and no success
description:
When a dispatch ends by raising, command_executor.py only computes context_after and the consequence when a span is open, and the end_span attributes on that path carry neither context_before/context_after nor success. The span is left with status=error and nothing else a diagnostic projection can read.

Evidence: in the pilot corpus (private copy) 85 of 6813 fw.command.execute spans have exactly this shape -- error status, no success attribute, no context handles -- against 6728 that carry all of them. The result is that context navigation is unknowable precisely for the dispatches that failed, which is when a reader most wants it.

Affected code: fastworkflow/command_executor.py (the exception path around the end_span call that stamps ATTR_CONTEXT_BEFORE/ATTR_CONTEXT_AFTER); consumed by fastworkflow/observability/diagnosis.py (_dispatch_navigation, coverage["dispatches_without_context_handles"] and ["dispatches_without_success"], which is one of the partial_evidence triggers).

Not fixed here: fix-9eg.18 is read-only over recorded evidence and command_executor.py is a runtime file owned elsewhere in this wave.
acceptance_criteria: A dispatch that raises records context_before (which is known before the call) and, where the workflow is still readable, context_after; success is recorded as false or explicitly omitted with a recorded error_type rather than silently absent. diagnosis.py stops counting those spans under dispatches_without_context_handles for newly captured turns. Historical spans stay unknown; nothing is backfilled.
notes: Triage (2026-09-20): priority=P3; cost=low; risk=medium. Small producer change, but it runs on the exception path of every dispatch, so a mistake there converts a command failure into a turn failure. Filed from the fix-9eg.18.1/.2/.3 backend slice.

title: Record the parameter-extraction round ordinal, not just a resumed-from-stored flag
description:
fw.nlu.param_extraction records retry_round as a BOOLEAN (parameter_extraction.py: diagnostics["retry_round"] = bool(stored_params)), which says only that this extraction resumed from stored parameters. It does not say WHICH round, so a consumer cannot report the retry sequence fix-9eg.18.3 asks for without counting spans and hoping the count is the ordinal.

Evidence: in the pilot corpus (private copy, 152 turns / 48650 spans) retry_round is present on 3947 of 5648 fw.nlu.param_extraction spans and its recorded values are only False (3947) and absent (1701). It is never True, so the retry state is effectively unobservable there.

Affected code: fastworkflow/_workflows/command_metadata_extraction/parameter_extraction.py (diagnostics["retry_round"]); the attribute contract in fastworkflow/tracing.py SPAN_CONTRACTS[SPAN_NLU_PARAM_EXTRACTION]; consumed by fastworkflow/observability/diagnosis.py (_param_markers, coverage["extractions_without_retry_flag"]).

Out of scope for the fix-9eg.18 diagnosis slice, which is read-only over recorded evidence and must not change a producer.
acceptance_criteria: An extraction span records a monotonic round index (0 for the first attempt) alongside the existing flag, with the SPAN_NLU_PARAM_EXTRACTION contract version bumped. diagnosis.py reports the recorded ordinal instead of a span count, and coverage stops reporting the round as unknown for newly captured turns. Historical spans without the field stay explicitly unknown and are not backfilled.
notes:
Triage (2026-09-20): priority=P3; cost=low; risk=low. Producer-side one-field addition plus a contract version bump; no behavior change. Filed from the fix-9eg.18.1/.2/.3 backend slice, where the gap blocks reporting a retry SEQUENCE rather than a presence flag.
Implemented (2026-09-20, awaiting orchestrator acceptance; NOT closed by worker). parameter_extraction.py stores stored_parameter_round alongside stored_parameters, incremented on _store_parameters and deleted in _clear_parameters so the counter cannot outlive the error state it counts; diagnostics carry retry_round_ordinal (0 = first attempt) beside the existing boolean retry_round. tracing.py SPAN_NLU_PARAM_EXTRACTION version 1 -> 2 with retry_round_ordinal added. diagnosis.py _param_markers reports the recorded ordinal, treats ordinal > 0 as a retry on its own, and refuses bool/float/str/negative values as unrecorded (counted in coverage.extractions_without_retry_flag) rather than coercing. No ordinal is inferred for v1 spans. Tests: tests/test_trace_diagnosis.py::test_a_recorded_retry_ordinal_is_reported_and_an_absent_one_is_not_invented, ::test_an_ordinal_beyond_the_first_is_a_retry_even_without_the_flag, ::test_a_nonsense_retry_ordinal_is_not_coerced_into_a_round[5 cases]. Validation: tests/test_trace_diagnosis.py + tests/test_span_contract_versioning.py 133 passed (exit 0); parameter/NLU regression set (test_parameter_extraction_unit, test_parameter_extraction_error_regression, test_nlu_span_emission, test_nlu_decision_signals, test_turn_and_cme_continuation) 62 passed 12 skipped (exit 0).
Root review found additional stored-parameter lifecycle owners: workflow.end_command_processing clears stored_parameters without counter; WEC continuation serialization preserves parameters but not new ordinal. Current new counter can mislabel next command or restored retry. Required narrow fix: no parameters => first0; restored parameters without reliable ordinal => unknown (including subsequent retries), preserve protected user files. Queue diagnosis_revision. Do not close yet.
Root review correction (2026-09-20): the original claim that the counter is self-contained was WRONG and is retracted. Workflow.end_command_processing (workflow.py:362-363) deletes stored_parameters without the counter, and WorkflowExecutionContext._serialize_cme_continuation/_apply_cme_continuation persist and rebuild stored_parameters without it, so the first version could label a new command a retry after an external reset and a restored retry as ordinal 0. Corrected read-side, without editing either protected file: no stored parameters => round 0 whatever a stale counter says; stored parameters with an absent/unbelievable counter => UNKNOWN, and the producer now OMITS retry_round_ordinal rather than sending 0; unknown is preserved through further retry storage; _store_parameters reads the prior round before installing. diagnosis.py adds coverage.extractions_without_retry_round, separate from extractions_without_retry_flag, because a restored session records the flag and omits the round. New tests against real objects (real Workflow, real serialize_state/apply_serialized_state round trip, no mocks): tests/test_param_retry_round_ordinal.py, 13 passed exit 0. Verified the tests bite: reverting _get_stored_round to the naive version fails 11 of 13 including both required regressions. Persistence follow-up filed as fix-7gp9 (P3 cost medium risk medium, filed not fixed per the standing directive); no claim is made anywhere that the counter survives a restore, and test_the_serializer_does_not_carry_the_counter pins that it does not.
Root independent revised diagnosis validation: 197 passed in 45.35s (diagnosis, HTTP/DOM, retry ordinals and span contracts). Protected preexisting files remain byte-identical. Remaining test-fixture import lint cleanup assigned to chat_adjacent; final shared UI regression follows selection/feedback integration.
Accepted by root reviewer: revised pagination returns every match, including >200 in actual DOM; exact source/detail markers and retry unknown semantics verified. Root independent 197 tests passed; worker 244 owned+UI and 122 runtime/server regressions passed (12 skips). Ruff fixture import corrected and now clean. Protected user files unchanged. Persisted retry ordinal completeness remains filed as medium/medium P3 fix-7gp9, not misreported as known.
close_reason: Closed

title: ExperimentController.create_experiment records workflow_name NULL when a driver omits it
description:
Found while integrating registration/selection (fix-9eg.17.2). ExperimentController knows its workflow folder (self.workflow_folderpath) but passes workflow_name straight through to ObservabilityStore.create_experiment, so a driver that does not supply it records workflow_name NULL. ExperimentHarness.run does supply it (benchmark_setup.workflow_name_for), so the gap is only for direct controller/driver callers.

CONSEQUENCE. comparison_group_identity() derives a comparison group from (workflow_name, benchmark_id). An unregistered driver run with workflow_name NULL and no benchmark pin lands in the ad-hoc group keyed by the empty workflow name rather than this workflow group. Blast radius is contained because each workflow has its own shared control file, so two workflows cannot merge; the visible effect is an ad-hoc group labelled with no workflow name. A REGISTERED experiment is unaffected: membership is sticky, so the group it joined at registration keeps it.

REPRODUCTION. tests/test_experiment_registration_and_repeat.py::TestRunnerBindsToTheWorkflowControl::test_an_unregistered_run_in_a_workflow_still_lands_in_the_contest passes workflow_name explicitly; drop that argument and the experiment registers into a group whose workflow_name is None.

AFFECTED CODE. fastworkflow/experiment/runner.py ExperimentController.create_experiment (workflow_name parameter), fastworkflow/observability/selection.py comparison_group_identity.

NOT FIXED HERE deliberately: defaulting it would change the CONTENT of recorded evidence for existing callers, which is out of scope for a selection-integration wave and is the store owner-s call.
acceptance_criteria: A driver that omits workflow_name records this workflow-s name, or the decision to keep NULL is recorded with its reason. Existing evidence rows are not rewritten. A focused test covers a controller-only driver landing in the same comparison group as a registered experiment of the same workflow.

title: Streaming lifecycle tests can only run with a paid agent turn
description: tests/test_fastapi_streaming_lifecycle.py drives /invoke_agent_stream with a real agent query ("add 2 and 3"), so every assertion in it costs a planner call and it cannot be run in a no-paid-calls environment - which is how its documented event allowlist went stale (it still said {trace,output,error} after a non-terminal timeout event was added, and nobody could run it to find out). tests/test_chat_streaming_and_artifacts.py now shows the cheap alternative: initialize the session, put the runtime in deterministic mode (execution_context._run_as_agent = False), and POST a real query - the whole route, CME pipeline, trace queue, registry and streaming body run for free over tests/hello_world_workflow in under a second, in both ndjson and sse framing. Applying that to the lifecycle file would make its transport assertions runnable in CI and in agent sessions; the one or two cases that genuinely need the planner can stay marked as paid.
notes:
Triage (2026-09-20, chat revision worker): priority=P3; cost=low; risk=low. Evidence: the allowlist in that file was stale and unrunnable this session; the deterministic-mode pattern is proven in tests/test_chat_streaming_and_artifacts.py (20 passed, 11s, no model calls). Affected: tests/test_fastapi_streaming_lifecycle.py, helper pattern in tests/test_chat_streaming_and_artifacts.py::_stream_a_real_deterministic_turn. Acceptance: the streaming lifecycle transport assertions run with no paid model call, and any remaining paid case is explicitly marked.
Adjacent low-cost/low-risk P3 assigned to Cursor Opus chat_adjacent during P1 wave, using accepted chat implementation and real deterministic no-paid test pattern. Root review required before close.
chat_adjacent (2026-09-20): implemented. tests/test_fastapi_streaming_lifecycle.py now runs with no model call: env_files writes a hermetic fastworkflow.env + placeholder passwords under tmp_path (no longer skips on a box without ./passwords/.env), _answer_locally() puts the session runtime in deterministic mode for the two turns that execute, and both executing queries moved from "add 2 and 3" to "what can i do" (parameterless: add_two_numbers would have sent its arguments to DSPy extraction, another model call). The workflow fixture moved from fastworkflow/examples/hello_world to tests/hello_world_workflow: the shipped example has no ___command_info/global/threshold.json, so the first locally-answered turn died there - invisible while every turn went to the planner. Added assertions so a hollow stream cannot pass again: first event is a trace, last is output, output.success is true and the answer is non-empty. Result: 5 passed in 5.09s, PYTEST_EXIT=0 (was: unrunnable/skipped). No test removed.
Root reviewer accepted: independent chat reuse + actual streaming lifecycle + streaming/artifact regression run 29 passed in 16.11s; lifecycle test no longer requires paid calls. Reuse creates a new turn under current settings with edited/copied notice, never auto-sends. Focused lint clean. Source-switch residuals remain separately assigned fix-9eg.7.2.

title: FastAPI-backed tests skip wholesale when passwords/.env is absent
description:
On a box with no ./passwords/.env, the FastAPI fixtures skip rather than run: one focused
run of tests/test_fastapi_turns_async.py, turns_serve, turn_output_contract,
streaming_lifecycle and service reported 7 passed, 57 skipped ("Passwords file not found
at .../passwords/.env"), and tests/test_run_chatbot_test_mode.py skipped 7 more ("env
files missing for FastAPI tests").

The skipped set includes the only end-to-end coverage of /invoke_agent_stream and of chat
against a real FastAPI server, so a change to run_fastapi_mcp can look fully validated
locally while almost nothing ran.

tests/test_chat_streaming_and_artifacts.py shows the cheap fix: copy
fastworkflow/examples/fastworkflow.env into tmp_path, write a placeholder passwords file
next to it, and pass both to the app module. That is hermetic, reads no secret and makes
no paid call. Tests that genuinely reach a model still need a real key and should gate on
that individually rather than on file existence.
acceptance_criteria: The FastAPI test fixtures build their own env/passwords files under tmp_path so tests that do not call a model run everywhere; only tests that genuinely need a provider key remain gated, and they say so in their skip reason. A focused run on a box with no passwords/.env shows those suites executing rather than skipping.
notes: Triage (2026-09-20, chat streaming worker): priority=P3; cost=medium; risk=low. Touches shared test fixtures owned by other workers, so filed rather than fixed.

title: Chat stream contract for coding agents is documented only for the old frame shape

title: Span-less inner hops cannot carry step-scoped feedback
description:
ObservabilityStore.add_human_feedback refuses any target_kind other than "turn" unless at least one recorded span_id is supplied, and validates those ids against spans.trace_id. A dispatch that produced no span of its own — the span-less inner CME/core hops the execution ledger files from fw.command.execute child_calls — therefore has nothing to anchor to, so a reviewer who wants to comment on THAT row can only file the comment at turn scope.

Evidence (2026-09-19): store.py add_human_feedback lines ~2769-2792 ("component feedback requires spans; turn feedback has none" and the trace_id subset check). Reproduced in tests/test_execution_comparison.py::TestAnchorsAndDigest::test_a_span_less_hop_can_only_be_anchored_at_turn_scope, which shows comparison.anchor_for_step degrading such a step to target_kind=turn and the real validator accepting only that. Scale: on the IDO corpus probe, a single real attempt projected 121 steps of which 65 were child-call rows — a little over half the visible execution sequence cannot be commented on individually.

comparison.EvidenceAnchor already exposes this honestly (anchorable / fallback_target_kind) so no consumer is misled, and the comparison view is usable today. The fix belongs to the feedback/evidence slice, not here.

Possible directions: allow an anchor that names a command_call_id with the PARENT dispatch span (the hop is inside it), or add a step target kind keyed on command_call_id. Note the evidence schema is fresh-only (fix-49m.3): a new human_feedback column means a schema version bump and refuses older stores, which is most of the cost.
acceptance_criteria: A reviewer can attach a comment to a span-less inner hop and later see it against that row rather than against the whole turn, or the product decides turn-scope is the intended answer and the UI says so explicitly. Existing turn-scoped and span-scoped feedback keeps its meaning; no recorded feedback is rewritten.
notes: Triage (2026-09-19, comparison worker): priority=P3; cost=medium; risk=medium. Cost medium: the fresh-only evidence schema means the natural fix is a schema version bump that refuses older stores. Risk medium: a looser anchor validation could let feedback point at spans of another turn, which is what the current subset check prevents. Filed rather than fixed per the both-medium rule, and store.py is owned by another worker.

title: Concurrent first open of a fresh observability DB can fail with schema v0
description: ObservabilityStore._ensure_schema is not safe against a second process/thread opening the SAME fresh (zero-byte or brand-new) DB file at the same moment. Reproduction (observed 2026-09-19 while writing tests/test_experiment_winner_selection.py): eight threads that each construct ObservabilityStore(db_path) simultaneously against a not-yet-created path — several fail with IncompatibleObservabilityDB: "has schema v0; this build requires v6 and carries no migration". One opener has created the file and its first tables but has not yet stamped PRAGMA user_version, so a concurrent opener sees user_version=0 AND has_tables=True, which is exactly the shape the fresh-schema refusal (fix-49m.3) treats as an older populated store. Affected code: fastworkflow/observability/store.py _ensure_schema (the found<SCHEMA_VERSION + has_tables branch, and the unlocked CREATE TABLE loop that precedes the user_version stamp). Impact is a cold-start race only: once any opener finishes, every later open succeeds, and the misleading message names a nonexistent "v0 build". Workaround in the new test is to install the schema once before starting concurrent writers. Priority P3: rare, self-clearing on retry, and no data is lost or corrupted — but the error text sends the operator to delete a perfectly good store. Cost medium / risk medium (needs a creation lock or a stamp-first-then-create ordering plus a retry, in the one function every store open goes through), so per the P3/P4 rule this is filed rather than fixed inside fix-9eg.17.1.
acceptance_criteria: N processes/threads opening the same fresh observability DB concurrently all succeed, or fail with an error that names the race rather than claiming an incompatible older store. A focused real-store concurrency test covers the cold-start case. No change to the fresh-schema refusal for a genuinely older populated store.
notes:
Discovered while implementing fix-9eg.17.1 (winner selection). Uncovered, not caused, by that work: no winner code runs before the failure. Triage: priority=P3; cost=medium; risk=medium.
Attached to supporting observability operations for aggregate triage. Remains filed, not fixed, under owner medium/medium P3 rule; ordinary writer initialization is outside the read-only archival P2 scope.

title: All task feedback in one place for humans and coding agents
description:
Unify access to existing component feedback across every attempt and turn of a task in an experiment. Preserve source anchors, author/provenance and original comments. Independent formal-review answers remain a distinct kind of evidence.
Human UI and coding-agent structured reads/actions must share semantics and stable store/experiment/task/attempt/turn/span references. Reuse existing stores, workspaces, benchmarks and APIs. Multiple-run optimization amendment (owner discussion, 2026-09-19):
Multiple-run and teacher/student lessons live in the same three-category/subcategory feedback model and UI. Comments can anchor both sides of a comparison. Free-form human content and structured agent text coexist without a separate insight-review layer or forced verdict. Task-wide feedback aggregates all runs and components; changing the best run preserves historical pair anchors.

OWNER-CONFIRMED FEEDBACK CONTRACT (supersedes earlier three-question shorthand):
Categories and allowed subcategories, represented as API enum values:
- observations_analysis (UI: Observations / Analysis): observation, analysis.
- conclusions (UI: Conclusions): what_went_right, what_went_wrong.
- recommendations (UI: Recommendations): what_to_do, what_not_to_do.
The owner confirmed these six meanings explicitly in this implementation session. UI category/subcategory selectors and watermark guidance facilitate free-form human comments; the coding-agent recording API carries category and subcategory explicitly as enums and accepts arbitrary structured text within the comment. Validate category/subcategory pairing. No parsing headings to infer required metadata for NEW writes. Preserve existing historical text without rewriting frozen evidence; uncategorized legacy comments remain readable and visibly legacy/unclassified rather than guessing a new subcategory. Comparison comments can link both recorded executions/pass/step anchors through the same API. No separate insight schema, review layer, or mandatory verdict workflow.

All child acceptance scenarios pass through both structured APIs and the browser. No additional experiment setup or formal evaluation gate is introduced.

title: The evaluation_controls event is absent under the default arm, so its absence is not evidence of misconfiguration
description: The emission is guarded by 'if agent.evaluation_control_overrides:' and that dict is EMPTY under the post-refactor default, therefore falsy, so the event is not emitted at all. The 2026-09-18 benchmark run DID emit it, because that run set FW_EVAL_COVERAGE_INSTRUCTIONS=0 explicitly. CONSEQUENCE: anyone verifying 'was the answer-policy arm applied' by looking for that event now finds nothing, and may read the absence as a misconfiguration -- or stop checking. The correct check is the resolved booleans (coverage_instructions_enabled False, finish_reminders_enabled True), not the event. Recorded as failure mode F2 of amendment A1 in devreview-artifacts-20260919/gte-rerun-preregistration.md, with A1.6 redirecting the check. Filed separately because the trap outlives that document: it will mislead anyone reading provenance from either run without the amendment in hand. POSSIBLE FIX: emit the event unconditionally with the resolved values, so provenance records what was in force rather than only what was overridden.

title: requires_llm_key is not applied to the tests that actually need a live key
description: The marker exists specifically to deselect tests needing a real key, yet none of the ~10 paid-call tests in test_fastapi_service.py carries it: test_invoke_agent_endpoint, test_invoke_assistant_endpoint, test_session_not_found_errors, test_new_conversation_endpoint, test_post_feedback_endpoint, test_leading_slash_stripping, test_concurrent_request_handling, test_session_data_extracts_user_id_from_token, test_traces_include_raw_command, test_initialize_with_startup_command_in_request. So the existing deselection mechanism would not hold them back once passwords/.env exists. Applying the marker is the prerequisite for splitting the guard by cost.

title: test_command_executor.py silently degrades instead of skipping when env files are absent
description: It calls dotenv_values on both env paths with no guard. A missing file returns {} silently, so its 9 tests run today with empty config rather than skipping -- they pass, but they are not testing what their names imply. title: AGENTS.md's full-suite figures are stale by more than 2x
description: AGENTS.md says the suite is ~1860 tests taking ~50 minutes, measured at v3.1.1 on 2026-08-20. Measured 2026-09-19 at commit a25cd40: 4161 tests, 1:28:32 wall clock. The file itself warns 'if you budget against that number you will conclude a healthy run has hung' -- which is now true of its own figure. Update the numbers and the date.
