title: DECISION for F4: the unsettled-terminal retry is unbounded over a handle lifetime
description: _reconcile returns without _settle_walk on countonly_error (paging.py:1765-1769) and on count-is-None (paging.py:1770-1773), so a transiently broken source re-fires the count once per fetch FOREVER. Within one fetch the purse bounds it; across fetches nothing does. So the 'exactly one reconciliation per walk' headline holds only on the happy path. Rev 4 measures this and elects to reproduce it as-is. The review's counter-point: the new contract is the moment when changing it would be free. OWNER DECISION REQUIRED before F4 (fix-iq53.2.8) implements the terminal callback. Not touched by the F1/F2 worker.
close_reason: OWNER RULING: reproduce the current behaviour as-is, and F4 did. _issue_terminal settles nothing when the adapter supplies no 'complete', so the retry re-fires exactly as measured -- Rev 4 elected this and the owner confirmed it. Recorded limitation, not a defect: the 'exactly one reconciliation per walk' headline holds on the happy path; against a transiently broken portal the real profile is unbounded reconciliations per handle lifetime, at one callback and zero batch reads each. F7 found a related post-F4 improvement that is now tested: a portal answering complete:false is a DECISION, so it settles and later fetches cost nothing, where old _reconcile retried forever. Revisit only if a broken-portal case is observed in practice.

title: No golden test on the result page header field set
description: rendering.py:51-78 builds the agent-visible page header and NOTHING in the suite asserts its field set or ordering. A field could be dropped and no test would fail. This is precisely how Rev 4's claim 'rendering.py: no change -- page format preserved' was asserted wrongly and survived review. Six tests added under AdapterBoundaryContractTests (tests/test_result_handles.py:1433) now cover filter_columns specifically, but the class of gap remains. PROPOSED FIX: golden-string test over _header for rows / partial / complete-zero / unsupported / over-budget.

title: state['start_offset'] is now a load-bearing cross-repository key with no contract
description: F1 turned a typed descriptor field with a default into an opaque key inside state. _origin_offset (paging.py:1484) is the only place in the package that reads state, and it reads exactly 'start_offset'. If IDO's I3 relation_source(...) does not pack the origin under that exact key, _origin_offset returns 0, the offset_origin_not_zero gate never fires, and a handle declared partway into a relation CLAIMS COMPLETENESS IT DOES NOT HAVE -- silently. That is the failure class the walk exists to prevent. PROPOSED FIX: name the key in I3's acceptance criteria (ido-0rk.2.1.3) and add an IDO-side assertion. FILE BEFORE I3 STARTS.
close_reason: Satisfied by IDO a7662ae. relation_source packs the origin under state['start_offset']; _terminal_reply reads it as its FIRST branch before any session is bound; two IDO tests pin it, one calling the callback with no session bound so a reply at all proves no query was attempted. The framework's duplicate backstop was then deleted in a25cd40, so the key has exactly one owner and the silent-completeness failure this issue warned about cannot occur. The boundary test now asserts the framework reads inside state in ZERO places, and was proven to bite by running it against the pre-deletion package.

title: Historical-store manifest is machine-local and silently re-baselines if deleted
description: The step-1 manifest at ~/.fastworkflow-historical-store-manifest/historical-store-manifest.json (135 KB, 451 stores) is the integrity anchor of the whole F5b acceptance bracket, but it lives outside both trees and is machine-local. Step 1 correctly refuses to OVERWRITE an existing manifest -- a manifest that re-baselined each run would record damage as the new truth -- but a DELETED manifest silently re-baselines on the next run, and nothing detects that. ACTION: copy the manifest into the review artifacts as durable evidence, and decide whether the anchor should live in-repo.

title: Eight pre-existing sidecars in the manifest will make any future read of four WAL stores fail step 6
description: The F5b step-1 manifest includes 8 sidecar files that already exist under evaluation/artifacts/ido-5uv-search/**. Including them is correct -- they are bytes in a frozen tree -- but it means any legitimate future read of those four WAL-mode stores changes an -shm and fails step 6 of the acceptance bracket. This is intended detection, not a defect. Filed so that whoever hits the failure knows it is informative rather than spurious, and so the team can decide whether to record a sanctioned-read exception.

title: file:{db_path}?mode=ro breaks on paths containing ? or #
description:
Affects fastworkflow/result_handles/store.py:849 and the precedent at fastworkflow/observability/store.py:5498 equally. Path.as_uri() is already used for exactly this in the same module at observability/store.py:5175 and :5204. F5b mirrored the existing precedent deliberately rather than diverging from it. Consequence: obscure failure or silently wrong path for an exotic directory name. Fix both sites together or neither.

Observability plan: fix both read-only URI construction sites using correctly encoded absolute file URIs. Preserve read-only behavior; do not reopen frozen evidence with a writer.
acceptance_criteria: Real stores under paths containing spaces, ?, # and Unicode open the intended DB through both readers without creating the wrong path or mutating evidence.
notes:
Triage (2026-09-19): priority=P3; cost=low; risk=medium. Small portable-store correctness fix; medium risk of reading wrong evidence. Existing parent retained.
Cross-reference (2026-09-19, setup/best-run integration wave): a THIRD site was introduced on feat/experiment-observability-3.3 and has been fixed correctly rather than mirroring the broken precedent — fastworkflow/observability/selection.py _read_only_uri(), used by control_mode_of(). It builds Path(os.path.abspath(path)).as_uri() + "?mode=ro". Use it as the reference implementation when fixing the two sites this bead owns. Regression coverage for the new site: tests/test_experiment_registration_and_repeat.py::TestControlPathEncoding (parametrized over roots containing #, ?, spaces and %). This bead is unchanged in scope: result_handles/store.py:849 and observability/store.py:5498 are still unfixed.

title: Quarantine or delete the invalid 720-test receipt at /tmp/fw-structural-validation
description:
PROBLEM
/tmp/fw-structural-validation records a 720-test run that certifies nothing that exists.
It is still on disk (confirmed present 2026-09-19) and has already been cited once as if
it validated a structural-only tree.

WHY IT IS INVALID - TWO INDEPENDENT REASONS
1. It describes a tree that no longer exists. Its recorded react.py hash is
   9a45a5ad..., which matches NEITHER base (07424d81...) NOR the live tree
   (9a3c9e1f...). Base react.py is the structural checkpoint's react.py, so a receipt
   with a third hash certifies some intermediate POLICY-CARRYING revision that was
   superseded. It is not evidence about the structural checkpoint and it is not evidence
   about the current policy residue either.
2. It did not even pass. Its own focused-initial.log shows `1 failed, 719 passed`.

CONSEQUENCE
The risk is purely that it gets cited again. It is the largest-looking test receipt in
the vicinity (720 tests), it sits in the obvious place, and the two things that
invalidate it are only visible if you open the log and compare a hash. The policy
residue in particular has NO valid receipt of any kind, which makes this the artifact
someone reaching for evidence will find first. REVIEW-PACKET.md section 3 already
carries a "Do not cite this receipt" warning; this bead is to remove the hazard rather
than rely on everyone reading the warning.

DO NOT CONFUSE WITH THE ADJACENT WORKTREES - LEAVE THESE ALONE
  - /tmp/fw-structural-review-candidate  KEEP until the full suite is green. It is the
    only tree the valid receipts actually describe. Remove with
    `git worktree remove --force` only after that.
  - /tmp/fw-g2e-v2-baseline              leave frozen
  - /tmp/fw-g2e-policy-ablation          leave frozen
acceptance_criteria: /tmp/fw-structural-validation is deleted, or renamed/annotated so it cannot be read as a passing receipt. /tmp/fw-structural-review-candidate is NOT touched until the full suite is green.

title: TurnRuntime.emit and its record_event field are dead on arrival
description:
PROBLEM
fastworkflow/agent_runtime.py is a brand-new 94-line module and ships with an unused
public method.

    agent_runtime.py:51-52   def emit(self, event): self.record_event(event)
    agent_runtime.py:45      record_event: Callable[[dict[str, Any]], None]
    agent_runtime.py:25      record_event=state.record_event   (in build_turn_runtime)

`rg -n "\.emit\(" fastworkflow/ tests/` returns nothing: emit() has zero callers
anywhere in the repo. `record_event` is a required (non-default) dataclass field that
every construction site must supply, and its only consumer is emit(). So the field
exists to feed a method nobody calls.

CONSEQUENCE
Small - roughly 2-4 of 94 lines - but it is dead API introduced at the moment the module
was created, in the module the epic designates as the new owner of turn lifecycle. A
required field with no live consumer is also a small tax on every future construction
site and a false signal to the next reader that events flow through TurnRuntime.

CORRECTION TO THE ORIGINAL AUDIT FINDING - PLEASE READ BEFORE ACTING
The audit (REVIEW-PACKET.md section 5, finding 11) also claimed that
"TurnRuntime.scope is written by bind_scope() and never read, so bind_scope is
currently inert". THAT PART DOES NOT REPRODUCE. `scope` IS read, and it is read on the
highest-priority branch of scope resolution:

    result_handles/paging.py:621-624   (inside current_scope())
        runtime = getattr(agent, "turn_runtime", None)
        runtime_scope = getattr(runtime, "scope", None)
        if isinstance(runtime_scope, RuntimeHandleScope):
            return runtime_scope

The plain-attribute grep the audit appears to have used misses it because the read goes
through `getattr(runtime, "scope", None)`. The packet's own section 2.1 describes this
branch correctly, so the packet contradicts itself on this point.

bind_scope (agent_runtime.py:48-49, called at continuation.py:276 and :307) is therefore
LIVE and load-bearing: it is what makes a rebound scope visible to handle filing. Do not
delete it. Scope this bead to emit/record_event only.
acceptance_criteria: emit() and record_event are either removed from TurnRuntime, or a caller exists that justifies them. TurnRuntime.scope and bind_scope are left alone - they are live.

title: Facade narrowing is wider than documented and partly masked by test rewrites
description:
PROBLEM
The module split is reported as losing no exported name, and that is true of `__all__`:
236 entries across 7 modules all resolve. But the modules lost a large number of
attributes that were reachable but not in `__all__`:

    fastworkflow.result_handles                  ~97 non-__all__ attributes lost
    observation_offloading.manifest               13
    answer_attribution                             4

CONSEQUENCE
No in-repo caller breaks today. The reason this is still worth a bead is the second
half: part of why nothing breaks is that the two test files which WOULD have broken were
rewritten to stop going through the facade.

    tests/test_result_handles.py:13
        from fastworkflow.result_handles import paging as result_handles
    tests/test_offload_state_reclamation.py:57
        from fastworkflow.result_handles import paging as result_handles

Both bind the name `result_handles` to the `paging` MODULE, so every `result_handles.X`
reference in those files now resolves against paging directly and the facade in
result_handles/__init__.py is never exercised by them.

WHY THAT MATTERS CONCRETELY
This same bypass already produced a real defect in the cleanup pass: MAX_CURSOR_PAGE was
duplicated in paging.py against common.py, the ENFORCED bound was cursors.py reading
common's copy, and the TESTED bound was paging's copy - the test could not see the
divergence because it was not looking through the facade. That one was found and fixed;
the bypass that hid it is still in place.

So the facade should not be treated as a proven-compatible surface. It is an unexercised
one. An external consumer doing `from fastworkflow import result_handles` and touching
any of the ~97 narrowed attributes would break, and no test in this repo would tell us.

SEVERITY
P3: no known caller is affected, and narrowing a facade is a legitimate outcome of a
split. The ask is to make the narrowing explicit and deliberate rather than incidental.
acceptance_criteria: The set of attributes lost from each narrowed facade is enumerated and either restored or consciously accepted in writing; at least one test exercises the bounds through the facade rather than through paging directly.

title: decode_cursor opens the result store before refusing an alias mismatch
description:
PROBLEM
`decode_cursor("O7/p2", alias="O9")` refuses correctly, but it creates and opens the
turn's SQLite archive on the way to the refusal.

WHERE (verified against the live post-cleanup tree)
fastworkflow/result_handles/paging.py:803-819 is the wrapper:

    815:  _parse_cursor_token(cursor)                     # grammar check - cheap, no I/O
    816:  selected_scope, store_ = _cursor_dependencies(scope, selected_store)
    817:  return _decode_cursor_impl(cursor, alias=alias, ...)

The alias mismatch is refused inside the implementation at
fastworkflow/result_handles/cursors.py:249-255. Line 816 runs first, and
`_cursor_dependencies` (paging.py:774, see its own docstring) calls `store()`, which
OPENS the turn's archive file - creating it if absent - and records the scope as an
owner of it via `_cache_namespace`.

So a well-formed token for the wrong handle still costs a ~61,440-byte SQLite file and
a scope registration before a refusal that never reads a row.

RELATION TO THE FIX ALREADY MADE
The malformed-token variant of this was a genuine defect and WAS fixed in the cleanup
pass: `_parse_cursor_token` was hoisted to line 815 precisely so a mistyped cursor is
refused without touching the filesystem (REVIEW-PACKET.md section 2.4). The alias
variant was left in deliberately.

WHY IT WAS DEFERRED (deliberate, not unknown)
Fixing it requires one of two things, both of which cost more than the defect:
  1. Duplicate the alias condition into `paging` so it can be checked before line 816 -
     which recreates the exact duplicated-cursor-grammar drift hazard that fix-iq53.1.5.1
     exists to remove; or
  2. Split `cursors.decode_cursor` into a parse/validate half and a resolve half so the
     wrapper can call them in order.
Option 2 is the honest fix if this is ever worth doing.

SEVERITY IS LOW BECAUSE IT IS NOT REACHABLE COLD
Unlike the malformed-token path, this one is in practice only reached from `fetch_page`,
by which point the store is already open - so the archive it "creates" almost always
already exists. That is why it is P3 and why it was not a blocker.
acceptance_criteria: decode_cursor('O7/p2', alias='O9') refuses without opening the archive and without registering scope ownership, and the alias condition still has exactly one definition.

title: observation_offloading: module-level _events list grows without bound in production
description:
Ultrareview nit on PR #84 (observation-offloading branch, 2026-09-14).

fastworkflow/observation_offloading/state.py declares a process-global _events list and record_event() appends to it unconditionally. Production callers fire several times per agent step: compact.py (compact_trajectory), continuation.py (_force_replan, forced_replan_wall), search.py (search_memory), agent.py (build_tool_agent), state.py (evict_hot_handles). Nothing in fastworkflow/ ever consumes or trims the list: snapshot_events() is only called from tests and reset_runtime_state() only from test setUp.

A long-lived run_fastapi_mcp server therefore leaks a few hundred bytes per agent step for the life of the process, pushing RSS up until restart.

Options: cap the list with a bounded deque (keep the last N for diagnostics), drop the in-memory list when FW_OFFLOAD_EVENTS file persistence is enabled, or expose a consumer that drains it. The tests rely on snapshot_events() returning every event within a test, so a cap must stay above what any single test records, or tests should switch to reading the FW_OFFLOAD_EVENTS file.

Related nit from the same review, worth fixing together: record_event holds the process-wide _lock across the FW_OFFLOAD_EVENTS disk write (state.py:96-115), so slow I/O stalls every hot-cache and handle operation on other threads.

title: Notice dwell and fade-out timings
description: Success notifications dwell 6s then vanish with no fade-out, which reads as lingering. Give success notices a 1.5s dwell plus a 0.5s fade, errors a 6s dwell plus a 6s fade, and extend the existing hover/focus pause so it also cancels a fade already in progress.

title: Picker offers every *.json in the current directory as a workspace manifest; offer only workspace.json or files that validate as a manifest
description: Pre-existing behaviour surfaced by fix-zns (2026-09-07): browse_directories lists any *.json in the current directory under workspace_manifests, so from /home/drawal/rl/ido the picker offers clarification_e2e.json, complex_task_results.json etc. as manifests. Restrict to files named workspace.json plus files whose top level carries the workspace manifest schema key (read at most the first KB), and label stray JSON as not-a-manifest or omit it. XS. Keep the one-level-down discovery from fix-zns unchanged.
notes:
Implemented on feat/experiment-observability-3.3 (worktree /home/drawal/rl/fastworkflow-observability).

ACCEPTANCE RULE for a *.json file in the browsed directory (server.py
_local_workspace_manifests, ~:1312, called from browse_directories ~:1384):
offered as a workspace manifest iff
  (a) its name is exactly workspace.json (case-insensitive) -- offered on the
      name alone, unread, so a manifest that fails validation is still
      reachable and reports why; or
  (b) _declares_workspace_schema(path) (~:1268): at most 4096 bytes are read;
      the prefix is json.loads-ed and, if it is a dict, its top-level
      "schema" (or legacy "schema_version") must equal WORKSPACE_SCHEMA
      ("fastworkflow-observability-workspace/1"); if the prefix is truncated
      or malformed, the prefix is scanned with a regex for that same
      key/value pair.
Anything else is OMITTED from workspace_manifests entirely (not labelled, not
offered). Any OSError answers False, so the picker always renders.
fix-zns one-level-down discovery (_nested_workspace_manifests) unchanged.

Real-path verification (read-only):
  /home/drawal/rl/ido                              -> offers NOTHING (was
      clarification_e2e.json, complex_task_results.json, ... )
  /home/drawal/rl/ido/evaluation/collections       -> offers exactly the
      exp029 trial: exp029-trial-3.3-lifecycle-2026-09-06 ->
      .../workspace/workspace.json
  .../exp029-trial-3.3-lifecycle-2026-09-06        -> offers only the nested
      workspace/workspace.json (cases.json, driver-state.json,
      seal-record.json, summary.json etc. all omitted)

Tests (tests/test_run_chatbot_zero_arg.py): fixture now also carries
workspace.json, a renamed manifest and a stray loose.json; the fix-zns
expectation that loose.json is offered was updated (that is the behaviour
this bead changes). New: omits stray JSON; offers workspace.json on its name
alone even when unparseable; offers a renamed manifest (schema and
schema_version); omits another schema and a merely-nested schema key; reads
at most the probe window (200 KB file with the key first is offered, same
file with the key last is not); skips a chmod 000 file without error; skips
undecodable bytes; /api/browse reflects the filter. 30 passed.

No index.html change: the SPA renders whatever the route offers.
No git commit/push. No schema change.
close_reason: Reviewed 2026-09-07. Picker offers a local *.json only if named workspace.json (unread) or its top-level schema key (<=4 KB probe) equals the workspace schema; everything else omitted; errors answer False. Verified read-only: /home/drawal/rl/ido offers nothing; evaluation/collections offers exactly the exp029 trial. fix-zns nested discovery unchanged. Orchestrator re-run: 256 passed across 7 suites (one transient collection error from a concurrent edit, clean on re-run).

title: run_chatbot /api/turns: per-turn cut-at-limit count issues one get_spans read per listed turn (~500/refresh); add a bulk span read
description: Introduced by fix-49m.6 (a): annotate_turn_rows calls store.get_spans per turn to count fw.llm.call spans cut at max_tokens; the rail requests 500 turns, so a large store pays ~500 small indexed queries per refresh. Acceptable for the localhost debug UI; fix is a bulk span read (or a per-turn aggregate column) on ObservabilityStore under [R12]. Measure before changing.
notes:
Implemented on feat/experiment-observability-3.3 (worktree /home/drawal/rl/fastworkflow-observability).

NEW READER (one, read-only, next to get_spans, [R12] -- no raw SQL in the server):
  ObservabilityStore.spans_for_turns(turn_keys: Iterable[str])
      -> dict[str, list[dict[str, Any]]]
  fastworkflow/observability/store.py:2689
  Same row shape and per-turn start_ns order as get_spans; every requested key
  present (-> [] when the store holds none); duplicates collapsed, blanks
  dropped; keys bound in chunks via the existing _chunked() helper (400/query),
  so SQLite s variable limit cannot be hit. ReadOnlyObservabilityStore inherits
  it (it subclasses ObservabilityStore).

  Archived twin: ObservabilityWorkspace.traces(store_id, logical_turn_keys)
  -> {logical_turn_key: spans}, fastworkflow/observability/workspace.py:700.
  trace() and traces() now share a new _scope_spans() helper (:673) so the
  single and bulk readers cannot drift; traces() opens the store once and
  refuses a blank store_id exactly as trace() does.

CALL SITES CONVERTED (fastworkflow/run_chatbot/server.py):
  - annotate_turn_rows (:169)             -- /api/turns, the rail
  - annotate_attempt_rows (:249)          -- per-attempt tallies/costs
  - annotate_workspace_attempts (:305)    -- workspace turn_refs, now one bulk
                                             read per store for ALL rows
  - annotate_projected_attempts (:359)    -- resolved_turns + resolved_sources
  New helper _workspace_span_cache (:270) groups (store_id, key) refs by store
  and issues one workspace.traces() per store.
  Untouched (single-turn reads, correctly one query): /api/turn/,
  /api/spans/, /api/workspace/turn|trace|spans, the review-sidecar reads.

MEASUREMENT (synthetic store, 500 turns x 10 spans = 5000 spans, 1.9 MB;
local, no model/network calls; ReadOnlyObservabilityStore + annotate_turn_rows
over a 500-turn page; SELECTs counted with sqlite3 set_trace_callback; 2 warm-
up passes then 7 timed passes each, medians):
  BEFORE (one get_spans per turn): 500 span queries, median 140.2 ms (min 132.8)
  AFTER  (one spans_for_turns)   :   2 span queries, median  49.1 ms (min  45.1)
  -> 250x fewer queries, 2.85x faster. (2 queries, not 1, because 500 keys is
  two 400-key chunks.) Stamps compared element-by-element across all 500 turns:
  identical.

EQUIVALENCE TESTS:
  tests/test_run_chatbot_ui_tier1.py TestBulkSpanStamping (new wide_db fixture,
  30 turns, every third cut at its cap): stamps identical to the pre-fix
  per-turn path for every turn; annotate_turn_rows makes exactly one bulk call
  and get_spans is monkeypatched to fail if a page reads per-turn; /api/turns
  answers the same tallies.
  tests/test_observability_store.py TestSpansForTurns: bulk == per-turn
  get_spans over 30 turns; 1 query for the page; unknown keys -> []; duplicate
  and blank keys collapsed; empty input reads nothing; 1200 keys chunk rather
  than raise; the writable store has it too.
  tests/test_observability_workspace.py
  test_bulk_traces_answer_exactly_what_the_per_turn_reader_answers: traces ==
  per-key trace over a sealed archive, scope stamps and attribute decoding

title: is_ask_user can collide with a named failure output
description:
Latent, found by both reviews of fix-ajv.16.

CommandOutput.is_ask_user is command_name == 'ask_user' (__init__.py:123). Since fix-ajv.16, a failure output carries the REAL ROUTED command name and success=False - exactly the pattern complete_ask_user_entry scans for.

Unreachable today: ask_user is a DSPy pseudo-command, never routed, so no routed name can equal it. But ROOT-CONTEXT COMMAND NAMES ARE UNQUALIFIED (the ido workflow has several at the root), so the guarantee rests on no workflow ever defining a root command called ask_user rather than on anything structural.

Cheap fix if it is ever worth one: make the ask_user marker a distinct field or a reserved prefix rather than a bare name comparison. Recording it now because fix-ajv.16 is what made it reachable in principle, and a reader of that change should be able to find this.
acceptance_criteria: ask_user identification does not depend on a command name a workflow could define.
notes:
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-29. The acceptance -- "ask_user identification does not depend on a command name a workflow could define" -- is met by a structural marker.

CommandOutput gains `ask_user_entry: Optional[bool] = None`, appended (not inserted) for the same section 12.2 reason as command_call_id: every existing constructor call and already-serialized record must keep validating. None means "written before this field existed" and defers to the old name comparison; True/False are authoritative. is_ask_user reads the field first.

Producers wired: the single CommandOutput producer (WorkflowExecutionContext.append_ask_user_entry) sets True; workflow_agent's failure output -- the one whose routed name could collide -- sets False explicitly.

FOUR consumers moved off the bare name, and two of them were worse than the bead recorded:
 - complete_ask_user_entry: scanned for name == "ask_user" AND success is False, which is byte-identical to a failed command called ask_user. It would have overwritten the error text with the user's answer and flipped success to True.
 - the two ask_user ATTEMPT COUNTERS: these feed tracing.deterministic_span_id(turn_key, SPAN_ASK_USER, attempt). A miscount does not just mislabel -- it makes two real ask_user spans collide on one span id.
 - the _note_agent_suspension dedup check.
observability_store._apply_capture_policy reads the marker with the same name fallback (it walks the model_dump()ed dict and cannot call the property), which also hardens the ask_user carve-out added by fix-ajv.18.

TESTS: tests/test_turn_result_capture.py::TestAskUserMarkerIsStructural, 5 cases including the legacy-record fallback and the two concrete harms. Negative control: reverting is_ask_user to the bare comparison fails 3 of them.

tests/test_public_shape_parity.py's COMMAND_OUTPUT_FIELDS pin updated -- that pin exists to force exactly this review, and the field is appended at the end.

title: Document the three-state db_lookup hook contract, including the 'no opinion' return
description:
The db_lookup hook has three meaningful return states, and only two of them are documented anywhere:

  (True, corrected_value, [])   -> framework overwrites the field with corrected_value (signatures.py:636-637)
  (False, None, [suggestions])  -> framework marks the field invalid and shows suggestions (signatures.py:638-641)
  (False, None, [])             -> framework does NEITHER: no rewrite, no invalidation

The third state is the load-bearing escape hatch and it is undocumented. Verified against signatures.py:636-641: an empty suggestion list hits neither branch, so it genuinely means 'no opinion, leave the extracted value alone'. That is what a *_uid field needs in order to accept a real uid whose candidate list holds display names -- without it, docs/FASTWORKFLOW_FUZZY_MATCH_DEFECTS.md measured 34 of 40 valid uids being rejected.

Also worth documenting in the same place: messaging_app_4's set_current_user returns fuzzy_match's matched LABEL directly, which is right for a field holding a name and wrong if the shape is copied onto a *_uid field, where it leaves a display name in the uid field and the command then queries the backend by display name.

Candidate homes: .claude/rules/command-authoring.md (which currently documents the hook as just 'db_lookup(workflow_snapshot, command) -> list[str]: # Optional', a signature that does not match the real one) and fastworkflow/docs/integrate-chat-agent/reference.md:171.

Deferred from fix-86c, which fixed the matching itself.
notes:
VERIFIED 2026-08-20. Both documented signatures are wrong in both arity and return type, not merely incomplete:

  .claude/rules/command-authoring.md:46
      db_lookup(workflow_snapshot, command) -> list[str]
  fastworkflow/docs/integrate-chat-agent/reference.md:171
      Optional hooks: db_lookup(workflow_snapshot, command), ...

  ACTUAL, per the framework's own call at utils/signatures.py:653-656
      db_lookup(workflow, field_name, field_value) -> tuple[bool, str | None, list[str]]

An author following either doc writes a 2-parameter hook, the framework passes 3 positional args, and the call raises TypeError. There is NO try/except around that call (contrast validate_extracted_parameters at :674-679, which is guarded), so it propagates out of validate_parameters. Loud and immediate rather than silent, so the severity stays low -- but it is a guaranteed first-run failure for anyone using the docs, and p3 assumes someone reads the messaging_app_4 example instead.

Should now also document the parameters fix-86c added: suggest_threshold and auto_apply_threshold on DatabaseValidator.fuzzy_match, and that per-command tuning is done by passing them from inside the hook rather than via json_schema_extra.

SEQUENCING: do this AFTER fix-63k, so the documented difflib cutoff default is the final one rather than needing a second edit.
IMPLEMENTED 2026-08-20.

.claude/rules/command-authoring.md
- Corrected the skeleton signature to db_lookup(workflow, field_name, field_value) -> tuple[bool, str | None, list[str]].
- Added a '## db_lookup' section: how to mark the field, the messaging_app_4 example, a three-state return TABLE (overwrite / fail-with-suggestions / no-opinion), the 34-of-40 uid figure and the decline pattern that fixes it, the label-vs-uid trap with the uid_of[label] mapping, per-command tuning by passing arguments (with the defaults and what each one costs), and the fact that the call is unguarded so exceptions propagate.

fastworkflow/docs/integrate-chat-agent/reference.md:171
- Corrected the same signature and summarised the three return states inline, keeping the terse bullet style of that file.

The tuning paragraph documents the post-fix-11r/fix-63k defaults (auto_apply_threshold 0.2, suggest_threshold 0.7, threshold 0.6), which is why this was sequenced last -- doing it first would have documented values that then changed.
