title: R9b: detect and report near-duplicate command capabilities
description:
ADDRESSES F14 (S3). Some workflows expose the same capability twice — on IDO, ControlsMonitor/list_findings and Directory/search_control_findings answer the same question. No amount of utterance engineering separates them. They present as PERMANENT BENCHMARK FAILURES and send developers chasing an unfixable defect.

DO (spec R9): after training, cluster label centroids and warn on near-duplicate commands, NAMING THE PAIR so the developer can merge, alias, or accept them.

The value here is diagnostic honesty: turning an unfixable-looking accuracy failure into a design observation the developer can act on.
notes:
R9b DELIVERED (reporting-only; no integration into the training path, by design). Near-duplicate defined operationally as a property of the TRAINING DATA rather than of the commands' meanings: two commands are near-duplicates when a classifier restricted to that pair, trained on their own utterances, cannot separate them. Implemented as leave-one-out balanced nearest-centroid accuracy in TF-IDF space with document frequency computed across ALL commands, which is what suppresses false positives on command families sharing boilerplate. Chance is 0.5 by construction, so the threshold is the coin-flip line, not a fitted constant. Evidence: on retail (19 commands, 79 pairs) zero duplicates and one low-severity overlap; minimum separability 0.56 and median 1.00 across 171 scored pairs. The positive-control workflow's deliberately duplicated pair scores 0.00 and is flagged; the hard negative in that workflow is not. Documented blind spot: it is a lexical instrument, so a duplicate pair with genuinely disjoint vocabulary is invisible -- covered instead by find_confusable_commands, which asks the trained router what it actually does via a predict_fn.
R9b SHIPPED, and the missing piece was the call site. duplicate_detection.py was complete and unit-tested but had NO caller anywhere in fastworkflow/ -- a developer had no way to run it, which is indistinguishable from the feature not existing. Now wired as `fastworkflow duplicates <workflow> [--json] [--fail-on-duplicates]`.

Wiring it surfaced two defects no unit test could have caught, which is the argument for insisting on call sites: (1) the scan needs fastworkflow.init() before the routing definition resolves -- it failed with "'NoneType' object has no attribute 'get_definition'"; (2) find_confusable_commands() requires a trained model's predict_fn, so it CANNOT run in a pre-training scan at all. The command therefore does the lexical scan only, which is the half that works before you have spent an afternoon training two commands no data separates.

--fail-on-duplicates gates on outright duplicates only. Overlapping and confusable pairs are frequently correct -- two commands SHOULD look similar when they do similar things -- and failing on them would teach developers to bypass the check. Verified discriminating: exits 1 on tests/duplicate_capability_workflow, exits 0 on retail (which has an overlapping pair and no duplicate). 5 CLI integration tests run the real binary in a subprocess, because the failure being guarded against is that the entry point is unreachable -- a test importing the function would have passed all through the period the command did not exist.
close_reason: Shipped and integrated; see notes

title: F11: shared encoder with per-context heads — cut 276 MB/context
description:
ADDRESSES F11 (S3). Each context directory holds a full DistilBERT copy PLUS a BERT-tiny (largemodel.pth, tinymodel.pth, two threshold files, a label encoder) — roughly 276 MB per context. 33 contexts -> 8.6 GB for a 160-command workflow.

A shared encoder with per-context classification heads would cut this by roughly two orders of magnitude, and would make selective retraining cheap: rewriting one context would touch a few MB of head weights instead of 276 MB.

DO:
- Evaluate and, if it holds up, implement a shared-encoder / per-context-head architecture.
- Measure the accuracy consequence on BOTH axes (R1) with a paired test — a shared encoder is a real modelling change, not a packaging change, and must clear the same bar as R7.

SCOPED AS P3 DELIBERATELY: it is a cost and ergonomics win that makes versioning (R4) and selective training (R5) cheaper, but neither depends on it. Do not let it block them.

VERIFY current cost: du -sh <workflow>/___command_info/*/ | sort -h | tail -5
notes:
RETIRED — NOT A LOSSLESS PACKAGING REFACTOR. One Tiny+Distil context is 287,342,019 bytes (274.0 MiB); 33 contexts are ~8.83 GiB. Frozen shared encoders plus per-context heads could reduce that to ~348 MiB (96.1%, 26x). But current training fine-tunes every encoder independently: sampled contexts shared 0/41 identical Tiny tensors and 0/104 Distil tensors, so existing artifacts cannot be split losslessly. Frozen shared encoders change the trained model and may reduce routing/escalation accuracy; joint multi-context training invalidates every head and defeats R5; adapters add major runtime/serialization/dependency complexity. R4/R5 already hardlink carried-forward contexts, reducing version duplication. Without a pre-registered five-seed non-inferiority experiment, storage savings do not justify this modeling redesign. Documented as spec M14; no replacement task created.

title: R30: Define user-facing vs developer-facing record projections
description:

design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar). (1) ONE RECORD, TWO READ-TIME VIEWS - a projection function beside the record reader (A21); no dual storage. (2) INTERNAL DETECTION: DERIVED FROM workflow_name (user decision; no schema flag). The predicate is centralized in EXACTLY ONE PLACE - the projection function - so future internal execution sources have a single update point; the accepted caveat (read side carries the name contract) documented there. (3) VIEW COMPOSITIONS: user view = non-internal executions (app commands + ask_user exchanges per A7) + answer, status, success, user_message, gallery payloads; failed executions show error MESSAGE never traceback. Developer view = full record incl. internal CME executions, raw parameters, tracebacks (A5), trajectory_ref (A37), refined_user_message (A36). title: R28: Reserve a trajectory slot in review records (roadmap: durable agent trajectory)
description:
FINDING: the DSPy ReAct trajectory (react_blob) is already serialized for suspends (workflow_execution_context.py:270) and discarded at completion. Persisting it into the review record (PayloadStore-offloaded) is nearly free and directly serves the externalize-trajectory roadmap item; the R1 event sequence gives trajectory entries a natural home. design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar) - PERSIST NOW. At every terminal write of an agent turn, the TurnSerializer (A21) offloads the ReAct trajectory to the turn-scoped PayloadStore (A8) and stamps TurnResult.trajectory_ref. title: R23: Completion-sequence atomicity and review-write failure semantics
description:
FINDING: offload -> put record -> clear pending -> return has undefined failure semantics. OPEN QUESTIONS: (1) review-write failure does NOT fail the turn (best-effort, loud log, monitored) - confirm and add the monitoring expectation; (2) crash-window analysis with R16 stable keys; (3) bound retries inside the per-session lock or move the write post-lock (ordinal still assigned in-lock per R18). See docs/turn_result_design_review.md R23.

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar). (1) WRITE FAILURE = BEST-EFFORT + LOUD TELEMETRY: bounded in-line retries, then the turn succeeds for the user regardless - by record-write time the command's side effects are committed; erroring would invite double-execution retries. Failure logged prominently; a MONITORING COUNTER is documented as a deployment alarm expectation (post-A1 stakes acknowledged: a lost write means the turn is missing from conversation history and post-restart memory - the gap is operator-visible by contract). (2) CRASH WINDOWS = BOUNDED LEAKS (stated): payloads under a recordless turn prefix are adopted idempotently by a retry (A22 stable key + A27 hashed leaves) or removed eventually by conversation-prefix retention (A12). (3) STALE-PENDING SAFETY NET (stated): order = record write -> pending clear; at restore, a pending blob whose turn key already has a record is stale and discarded - record-write wins always (blob carries its turn key per A22). (4) LOCK HOLD (stated): write stays in-lock with a tight retry budget (sub-ms/ms writes vs multi-second turns); post-lock writing noted as a permitted future optimization (A24 assigns the ordinal in-lock either way). Recorded in design doc Amendment A28 and review doc R23.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 with the post-A1 stakes shift and the double-execution trap): best-effort + loud telemetry, recommended option. The side-effects-already-committed argument was decisive.
close_reason: Finding finalized: best-effort record writes with alarm-contract telemetry, bounded crash leaks, stale-pending discard rule, in-lock writes; recorded in bead, review doc R23, design doc Amendment A28

MISSION (review, not implement): resolve the OPEN QUESTIONS collaboratively with the user, then finalize this finding into an unambiguous, detailed and complete issue description plus a design recommendation of matching quality. design: RESOLVED 2026-06-11 (with Dhar). (1) ARITY = LIST: CommandOutput.nested_turns: list[TurnResult] = [] (supersedes the singular nested_turn of design section 5.2) - empty in the common case, represents loops/fan-outs over sub-agents, never needs a record-schema break later. (2) NESTED SUSPENSION = ALWAYS ESCALATE: an inner agent's question bubbles up to become the TOP-LEVEL turn's suspension, generalizing the existing wildcard.py:61-71 escalation pattern. Consequence: a nested TurnResult attaches to its command ONLY WHEN COMPLETE; partial-inside-partial pending blobs never exist; all suspend/resume machinery (A19, A30) works unchanged at any nesting depth. Deliberately constrains future nested-agent designs to escalation-style clarification (also the simplest UX - one question stream). (3) STATED CONVENTIONS: nested user_message = the delegation instruction the parent command passed to the sub-agent; a SYNTHETIC TEST PRODUCER ships with the seam (R35 matrix) so the recursive serializer is never dead untested code; embedded-only revisit trigger named (p95 record size over ~256KB with real nested agents -> promote nested turns to references). Recorded in design doc Amendment A32 and review doc R12.
notes: Q and A (after ELI5 turn-within-a-turn): list arity + always-escalate, both recommended options. The escalation model's payoff: zero new suspension machinery at any nesting depth.

title: Add schema migration for serialized session state (schema_version)
description: serialize_state writes schema_version (currently 1) and apply_serialized_state only logs a warning on mismatch; there is no migration logic. If the serialized blob format evolves, existing pending blobs (disk JSON / Redis) will be misread or silently dropped. Add versioned migration: on load, detect schema_version and upgrade older blobs to the current shape (or explicitly discard with a clear policy).
acceptance_criteria: Loading an older-schema blob either migrates it to the current schema or is handled by an explicit documented policy; mismatch no longer silently warns; tests cover an older-version blob.
notes:
Surfaced during trajectory-serialization review. Related: fastworkflow/session_state_store.py (SCHEMA_VERSION), fastworkflow/workflow_execution_context.py apply_serialized_state.
PARTIALLY ADDRESSED 2026-08-06 (v2.27.x). The dangerous half is fixed; the migration machinery is deliberately not.

DONE - fail-closed on mismatch. apply_serialized_state() previously logged a warning and then fell through to apply every field, so a blob written by a future build would be HALF-restored onto a live session. It now raises session_state_store.IncompatibleSessionState having applied nothing, and the cold-create path in run_fastapi_mcp/utils.py catches it, clears the stale blob so it cannot re-raise on every subsequent cold create, and starts the session clean. Losing a suspended turn is recoverable by asking again; a partial restore is not.

Tests: tests/test_session_state_serialization.py::test_unreadable_schema_version_applies_nothing (parametrized over newer/older/0/None/string) asserts nothing was applied, plus test_readable_schema_version_still_applies so the first test is about the VERSION rather than about apply_serialized_state doing nothing at all. Mutation-checked: reverting the guard to warn-and-fall-through fails all 5 cases.

STILL OPEN - migration. There is only one schema version, so there is nothing to migrate FROM, and writing migration machinery now means designing against a format that does not exist. Pick this up when SCHEMA_VERSION 2 is actually defined; the policy question (upgrade in place vs discard) is then answerable rather than speculative. The fail-closed behaviour above is the correct default until then.
Closed as part of v3.0.0: SCHEMA_VERSION bumped 2→3 with no migrator (user accepted discard of old blobs along with SPEEDDICT→FASTWORKFLOW_STATE_ROOT relocation). Old pending blobs raise IncompatibleSessionState and the session starts clean.
close_reason: Closed

title: Restore full command-context navigation depth on rehydration
description: serialize_state captures only current_command_context_name (a string). On cold rehydration, startup is re-run which resets to the root context; if the user had navigated several levels deep into a nested context, that exact position is not reconstructed. apply_serialized_state only logs a debug warning when the rehydrated name differs from the saved one. Design a way to serialize and restore the navigation path/position (e.g. an ordered list of context identifiers + a workflow-specific restore hook) so deep navigation survives relocation.
acceptance_criteria: A session navigated N levels deep resumes at the same context after cold rehydration on a fresh process; covered by an integration test using a nested-context workflow.
notes: Surfaced during trajectory-serialization review. Related: fastworkflow/workflow_execution_context.py serialize_state/apply_serialized_state, tests/test_command_context_serialization_spike.py.
close_reason: Resolved by the serialization-hook locator mechanism in v2.26.0. serialize_state captured only current_command_context_name, so a nested position was lost on rehydration. The checkpoint now serializes one anchor and stores the other context slots as LOCATORS into it, with a serialize-time self-check that find_by_locator(anchor, get_locator(obj)) is obj. Verified by identity rather than equality in tests/test_workflow_serialization_hooks.py: restored.current_command_context is bug (a nested WorkItem), is laundry (a nested TodoList), and bob is chatroom.users[1]. Applies to workflows whose context class implements the hooks; one without them pins instead of losing the position.

The split saves only dict.get calls on an empty dict. Collapse into one 'probe when cacheable' loop and delete the false comment. No behaviour change. title: Decide: revisit ephemeral-only port and per-launch token for dev/test on remote boxes (fix-vf7, fix-cb5)
description:

Every restart changes the URL, so an open tab gets 401 on every call, and SSH/devcontainer port-forward rules must be redone per launch; a headless host still tries wslview/powershell/webbrowser. The target audience (product/dev/test) includes remote dev boxes.

Options: (a) keep as is; (b) opt-in env var for a fixed loopback port; (c) persist last port + token (0600, state dir) and reuse when free; (d) honour BROWSER=none / non-tty for the auto-open.

title: Write verbs read request bodies with no size cap; a negative Content-Length reads to EOF
description: do_POST / do_PUT / do_DELETE / do_PATCH each repeat `length = int(self.headers.get('Content-Length') or 0); json.loads(self.rfile.read(length) or b'{}')` (server.py 2338-2339, 2564-2565, 2600-2601, 2651-2652). -1 makes read(-1) block the handler thread until the client closes; a huge length allocates; chunked bodies silently parse as {}. configure_env_files caps content at 512 KB only after the whole body has been read. Token-gated loopback, hence P4, but it is one helper.
design: Design review: one _read_json_body(max_bytes=4 MiB) helper used by all write verbs: missing length on a body-required route -> 411, negative/non-numeric -> 400, oversize -> 413. Done with fix-hzux.2.
acceptance_criteria: One _read_json_body(max_bytes) helper: missing/negative/non-numeric length -> 411/400, over the cap -> 413; tests for -1, oversize, missing and chunked.
notes: Triage (2026-09-29): priority=P4; cost=low; risk=low. Low cost/risk; folds naturally into the route-table work.
close_reason: _read_json_body: 4 MiB cap (413), negative Content-Length 400, chunked 411. Raw-socket test helper now reads to Content-Length (was flaky). Verified with targeted test files only; full suite not run (user instruction, 2026-09-29).

title: Small follow-ups from the WP1-WP12 verification
description:
Found by the adversarial verifier on 2026-09-28; all low severity.
- jev_client._configured_timeout reads the SDK's private _config; if the SDK changes it silently falls back to cutoff+margin (safe) and the SDK contract test does not cover it. Add it to the contract test or read a public attribute.
- tests register a test model with litellm.register_model for the whole process and never remove it (unique name, harmless); consider a fixture that restores litellm.model_cost.
- scoped_search_memory docstring is labelled history but was edited in place; amend instead (owner rule on comments).
- Search-window rule: min(FW_MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS, search model metadata) applies only when LLM_OBSERVATION_SEARCH is set; with it unset the agent window (and FW_MODEL_CONTEXT_TOKENS) still wins outright. title: browser_validation discovers only top-level DOM tests, so a class-nested one is invisible
description: tests/browser_validation.py builds its required set from ast.Module.body, so only module-level functions are considered. A DOM test written as a method of a test class is never discovered: it skips itself without TEST_JSDOM_ROOT and the gate reports 'no browser checks were discovered at all' (or silently omits it when other files do have top-level ones), which is exactly the failure mode the gate exists to prevent.
design: Walk ClassDef bodies as well and emit the pytest node id as file::Class::method. The existing _jsdom_functions closure already handles helper reachability; it needs the same treatment applied per class scope.
acceptance_criteria: A DOM test written as a class method is discovered by the gate and a run in which it skipped is a failed run.
notes:
Observed while adding the training-history browser check (fix-9eg.2): the new DOM test was first written as TestTrainingHistoryInThePage::test_training_history_dom and 'python -m tests.browser_validation tests/test_training_history.py' answered 'required browser checks: 0'. Worked around inside the owned file by moving that test to module level, where the gate finds it (verified: required 1, executed and passed 1). No other test file in the repo currently has a class-nested DOM test, so nothing is hidden today. Not fixed here: tests/browser_validation.py is a new file owned by another wave worker, so this is reported as a cross-file item rather than edited. Triage: P4, cost low, risk low.
Root assigns eligible P2 pass capture and adjacent low/low gate/import followups to Cursor Opus. Shared-file edits serialized; no pushes. Protected owner behavior preserved; import cleanup limited to unused import or explicit re-export.
Implemented (Cursor Opus, root-assigned follow-up). tests/browser_validation.py now discovers browser checks written as methods. Discovery was split into scopes: _reaching() is the jsdom-reachability fixpoint for one scope, _called_names() follows plain calls plus attribute calls whose receiver is self, cls or the class itself (so a sibling helper is followed while something_else.run() is not mistaken for a local one), and _class_tails() recurses through nested classes emitting file::Class::method and file::Outer::Inner::method. A method reaches jsdom directly, through a module-level helper, or through a class helper at any depth. Over-discovery was treated as the unsafe direction and closed off: only classes pytest would actually collect are enrolled (default python_classes=Test*, and no class defining __init__), because requiring an uncollectable node id would read as 'never reported' and fail the gate for a check that does not exist. Outcome reading was the other half: a JUnit classname is one dotted field for module AND class, so _split_junit_classname() cuts it by finding the module on disk and, when the report came from a run rooted elsewhere, by the naming pytest itself relies on; without it tests.test_x.TestThing became the path tests/test_x/TestThing.py and every class-nested check read as never reported. Parametrised cases still fold onto their function with worst-outcome-wins, now under the class-qualified id. Tests (tests/test_browser_validation_gate.py, real pytest runs writing real JUnit reports, no mocks, and deliberately written AS class methods so the discovery they check is the discovery that finds them): method discovered with its class in the node id; sibling helper followed; helper reached through the class name followed; a method driving no DOM not enrolled; nested class addressed through both names; a non-Test class and a class with __init__ both excluded (parametrised); helpers never reported as checks; outcomes found under file::Class::method; the class never folded into the file path; a skipped method read as skipped; one parametrised case skipping or failing making the whole check skipped/failed; and end to end, the gate FAILING when a class-nested check skips -- the run that used to report success having executed no browser code. Results: tests/test_browser_validation_gate.py 25 passed PYTEST_EXIT=0; flake8 --select=F clean. No regression on the real suite: discovery before and after returns the identical 21 node ids (no class-nested DOM test exists in the suite today, so nothing was newly enrolled), and the full gate is required 21 / executed and passed 21, GATE_EXIT=0. No gate architecture beyond discovery and outcome mapping was touched. Pending root review.

description:

diagnosis.py reports them in coverage["unrecognized_span_names"] and counts the turn as partial_evidence rather than ignoring them, which is the honest handling but not an answer: the evidence may be load-bearing (fw.evidence.read looks like a tool-use record) or may be dead capture from a branch that never landed.

title: Two control sidecars now sit beside one evidence store
description:
Control metadata about an evidence store is now split across two sibling SQLite files with two independent schema versions and two independent identity bindings:

- <stem>.selection.sqlite3 (selection.py, CONTROL_SCHEMA_VERSION=1): winner pointer and selection history.
- <stem>.pairreview.sqlite3 (pair_review.py, PAIR_REVIEW_SCHEMA_VERSION=1): per-reviewer reviewed/not-reviewed progress for comparison pairs.

Both were written separately and deliberately — a worker must not write tables into another worker sidecar, and both are fresh-only so neither can adopt the other tables after the fact — but the result is two files to copy beside an archive, two chances for an identity mismatch, and two schema versions to keep straight. Nothing is broken: both bind to the same store_identity() and both degrade to unavailable on a read-only directory.

This is a consolidation question for whoever next touches control metadata, not a defect. If the answer is one sidecar, note that merging them is a fresh-schema break for both and that existing sidecars would have to be moved aside.
acceptance_criteria: Either the two sidecars are deliberately kept separate and that decision is written down where the next author will see it, or they are merged into one control DB with a single schema version and a documented move-aside path for existing files.
notes:
Triage (2026-09-19, comparison worker): priority=P4; cost=medium; risk=medium. Cost medium: merging is a fresh-schema break on two files with a migration story to write. Risk medium: a bad merge loses recorded winner decisions or review history, which are judgements nobody can reconstruct from evidence. Filed rather than fixed per the both-medium rule; selection.py is owned by another worker.
Duplication grew: pair_review.py now also mirrors selection.py control_mode (single/shared) plus an evidence_sources authorization table, because a comparison pair can span two evidence stores and a single-store binding could not record it. That is ~150 lines of the same schema/mode/source-authorization machinery in two files, on top of the two sibling sidecars already noted.
2026-10-04: subsumed by epic fix-10vj (owner decided one live evidence DB per workflow, zero sidecars, no legacy support). Implemented by fix-10vj.3; close this when fix-10vj.3 closes. The 'move-aside path' in the acceptance criteria no longer applies: owner decided no migration code; old files are deleted by hand in fix-10vj.7.
close_reason: Resolved by fix-10vj.3: both control sidecars replaced by control tables in the live DB.

SAFE FREE SUBSET IDENTIFIED: see the child issue.
PARTIAL VERIFICATION 2026-09-19, at zero cost. A throwaway placeholder passwords/.env (eight LITELLM_API_KEY_* names, every value the literal <PLACEHOLDER-NOT-A-REAL-KEY>, chosen because '<' is the repo's OWN _looks_like_real_key sentinel for 'no key present') unblocked the two NLU-free modules: test_fastapi_turns_async 0->4 passed, test_fastapi_turns_serve 1->6 passed. ALL NINE gated skips converted and ALL NINE PASSED, 10 passed / 0 skipped / exit 0 in 28s. ZERO EGRESS, enforced rather than observed: a pytest plugin loaded from outside both repos patched socket.connect/connect_ex/create_connection/getaddrinfo to allow only loopback and AF_UNIX and to record-and-refuse anything else, counting a DNS lookup for a provider host as egress. title: field_annotations_digest digests address-bearing text the prompt no longer shows
description:
DISCOVERED FROM fix-r4p. Latent, not live -- filed so the trip-wire is written down.

After fix-r4p the prompt's copy of the annotations block is address-stripped (_address_free) and the DIGESTED copy is not: field_annotations_digest still hashes the raw str(model_fields), which for a parameter model holding a non-JSON-native example contains ' at 0x...'.

So the two differ for exactly those models. Today this is safe in the only direction that matters -- the raw text is strictly MORE discriminating, so it can cost a cache miss but can never cause a stale hit -- and such a command never reaches a key anyway, because field_details raises first.

It goes live the day _canonicalize_unserialisable grows a case for such a type: then the command DOES reach a key, and its digest contains an address that changes every run, which is a permanent miss indistinguishable from a first run. That is precisely the defect fix-k0i.46 fixed in _canonical_digest.

Documented on compute_fingerprint rather than changed, because the change is untestable through any public path today. DO: when adding a case to _canonicalize_unserialisable, strip addresses from the digest input in the same change.
notes: Verified 2026-08-08: no code change. compute_fingerprint docstring (param_example_cache.py) already documents the latent asymmetry — prompt uses _address_free (fix-r4p), field_annotations_digest hashes raw str(model_fields); safe direction (miss not stale hit); command does not reach a key today because field_details raises in _canonicalize_unserialisable first. Trip-wire stands: when adding a case to _canonicalize_unserialisable, strip addresses from the digest input in the same change. Closing as documented-latent.
close_reason: Closed

title: DECIDED NOT TO FIX: PersonaHubSource pool code is deliberately outside the digest
description:
RECORDED SO IT IS NOT REDISCOVERED AS A BUG. Discovered during fix-6r5.

Editing PersonaHubSource.persona_at to read a different dataset column would change every workflow's personas and invalidate no cache entry. That is a real hole, and it is the same one fix-6r5 closed for app-supplied and domain-conditioned sources.

It is left open DELIBERATELY. active_persona_source_label() returns None for the default PersonaHub draw (decision D6). Giving that up means every cached utterance in every existing workflow is invalidated at once, and the default source has no configuration to condition on -- so the cost is certain and the benefit is hypothetical until someone actually edits persona_at.

If persona_at is ever edited in a way that changes which personas come back, the correct response is a deliberate one-time cache invalidation, not a permanent label. Anyone who rediscovers this should read it as a decision with a stated price rather than an oversight.

Filed as a task rather than a bug for that reason.
notes: Verified 2026-08-08: DECIDED NOT TO FIX stands. Code documents D6 — active_persona_source_label() returns None for PersonaHubSource (personas.py); pool-code digest applies only to app/domain sources (fix-6r5). Closing as wontfix/decided so rediscovery reads as a priced decision, not an oversight. No PersonaHub digest label added.
